# Editing menus from the remote (3c): implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Let the user add, remove, reorder and rename their tiles and submenus, and choose their icons, from the couch, with StreamFlex's own on-screen keyboard, shipping as v0.6.0.

**Architecture:** Four new pure modules carry the logic and are tested by CTest with no SDL: `osk.c` (the keyboard), `applist.c` (the app list), `iconmatch.c` (library matching) and `menuedit.c` (the menus as data, its operations, and how they are written back). `inidoc.c` and `config_save.c` gain the section and position primitives `menuedit.c` writes through. The SDL side adds the platform app scans on a background thread, icon plating, the live rebuild of the launcher's `Menu` and `Entry` lists, the new settings pages and pickers, and the hold-OK shortcut.

**Tech Stack:** C (MSVC `/W4 /WX` on Windows, gcc on Linux), SDL3 3.2.10+ / SDL3_image 3.2.4+ / SDL3_ttf 3.2.2+ (Windows: vcpkg SDL3 3.4.18, static), inih, CMake + CTest, COM (`shobjidl.h`) on Windows, Docker (the headless harness), Python 3 (`build-library.py`, the mutant driver, `check-smoke.py`), PowerShell 7.

**Spec:** `design/specs/2026-09-29-menu-editing-design.md`, amended for SDL3 by PR #61. Read it in full before any task; this plan argues from it. ## Global Constraints

- **Version floors** (port spec § 2): SDL3 **3.2.10**, SDL3_image **3.2.4**, SDL3_ttf **3.2.2**. Debian and the Pi build at the floor; Arch and Windows at the newest. Code that compiles only on 3.4 fails CI.
- **No OS keyboard, ever** (spec, "No OS keyboard, ever"): StreamFlex never calls `SDL_StartTextInput` or `SDL_StartTextInputWithProperties`, and has no `SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT` or `SDL_EVENT_TEXT_EDITING` handler. `make_window()` calls `SDL_StopTextInput()` on each window it creates.
- **Real-keyboard typing from key events only** (user, 2026-10-15): the character is `SDL_GetKeyFromScancode(scancode, mod & (SDL_KMOD_SHIFT | SDL_KMOD_CAPS | SDL_KMOD_MODE), false)`.
- **A config line is at most 199 bytes** (`INIDOC_MAX_LINE`; inih's 200-byte buffer) and a section name at most 49 (`INIDOC_MAX_SECTION`). An entry is `Key=title;icon;command`; no part may be empty (the parser's `strtok_r` skips empty tokens), a title may not contain `;`, and every written value passes `inidoc_check_in()`.
- **Section names match case-sensitively** (`MATCH` is `strcmp`), as the parser does. Reserved sections: General, Layout, Background, Titles, Highlight, Scroll Indicators, Clock, Screensaver, Hotkeys, Gamepad.
- **Hold-OK:** 0.8 s (`HOLD_OK_MS 800`), first press only, never on key repeat.
- **Platforms:** Windows, Debian trixie, Raspberry Pi OS trixie, Ubuntu 25.10+, Arch, Fedora. The headless harness is Linux only; Windows code is proven by the Windows CI leg and by qa-harness.
- **No manual test runs** (user, 2026-10-15): CI, the headless harness and qa-harness do the testing. Every hands-on row is a qa-harness row.
- **Smoke rows with every change** (todo Binding decision): Task 17 writes them; each task names its claims. The `smoke-coverage` check is required. The smoke target moves to v0.6.0 with the first results file (user, 2026-10-15).
- American spelling in every added line, file name and commit message (gray, color, canceled, dialog).
- One implementer per checkout. Commits by pathspec, never `git add -A`. Every git command uses `git -C C:/Users/jscha/source/repos/streamflex`. Branches come from `pwsh C:/Users/jscha/.claude/scripts/git-new-branch.ps1`. Never `cd`.
- The build's ledger is `C:/Users/jscha/source/repos/streamflex/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-menu-editing/progress.md` (git-ignored). Every result goes into it verbatim.
- Every Windows compile check runs both cl 19.44 (CI's) and 19.51. Every mutant has an unmutated control that passes.

## Plan rulings (the controller's, 2026-10-15, where the spec is silent)

These follow from the spec and the code; the user reviews them with the plan.

1. **OK acts on release in the launcher's menus.** The hold-OK shortcut needs it: a press that launched at once could not become a hold. A short press selects when OK is released; a hold of 0.8 s opens the tile's page and the release does nothing. Inside settings, OK still acts on press.
2. **An empty menu is shown, not refused.** Today `load_menu()` refuses a menu with no entries and the parser never creates a menu for a section with no lines. After 3c, every non-reserved section is a menu, empty or not; an empty one draws a centered note, *This menu is empty. Hold OK to add tiles.*, and holding OK on it opens its Tiles page. Back leaves it as usual.
3. **The menus model is built from the file, not from the live `Menu` list,** because a live `Entry` keeps neither its key nor its line's text, and its library icon name is replaced by a file path at load (`util.c:823-826`).
4. **Menu edits are saved by reconciling each section on a fresh read**, not by replaying a journal: the model knows each tile's line as it was read, and the save makes the section's entry lines match the model's order and content. A line removed or changed by hand meanwhile follows 3b's rules (a removal is skipped, a change becomes a new line), with the same notes.
5. **A structural change rebuilds the settings model.** The model is sized to the menus at open (`settings_create(names, count)`). Adding, removing or renaming a submenu remakes it, carrying every pending slot edit across by menu name.
6. **Names (drafted in Task 3):** two menu names that differ only in case clash (they would look like one menu on screen), though loading and finding match exactly as the parser does; a name may not contain `;` (it is also its tile's title) or `]`, nor start or end with a space. A menu may change its own name's case.
7. **Enter and Backspace while the keyboard is open (user, 2026-10-16, AskUserQuestion: "Remote keys until typing"):** many remotes send Enter for OK and Backspace for Back, so in a field Enter types the highlighted key and Backspace backs out, as everywhere else in settings, until a printing character from a real keyboard has been typed into that field; from then on in that field Enter is Done and Backspace deletes. Keypad Enter is always Done and Esc is always Back. This amends ruling 3 (approved 2026-10-15) and the spec's "Enter is Done … Backspace deletes" line, which this plan's PR rewords.
8. **Spec wording, corrected in the spec by this plan's PR:** `inidoc_value_ok()` becomes `inidoc_check_in()`, which exists; the field's text is drawn as settings text is (`draw_text()`'s cached texture), not as titles are.

## Review Focus

1. **A hand edit to `config.ini` between opening settings and saving** (a tile removed, a line changed, a section renamed or removed). Expect: the save succeeds; each edit whose target is gone is skipped or written as a new line, with 3b's notes; nothing else in the file moves. **One exception** (Fable review I1): a menu renamed in settings whose section the hand renamed or removed meanwhile fails the save (*[Games] was renamed or removed in config.ini meanwhile, so it cannot be renamed to Play*), as a name clash does, since its openers elsewhere already name the new name; nothing is written. Pinned in Task 2 (`test_inidoc`, `test_config_save` cases) and Task 3 (`test_menuedit` `apply` cases on a changed doc).
2. **A value that would break the line** (a title with `;`, an empty title, a line over 199 bytes, a title ending in a space before `;`, a section name with `]`, a name over 49 bytes, a reserved or existing name in another case). Expect: *Done* disabled with the reason in the caption; nothing written. Pinned in Task 3 (`test_menuedit` name and tile rules) and Task 5 (`test_osk` validators).
3. **A submenu opened from two menus, or the default menu's tile, or the menu settings was opened from, removed or renamed.** Expect: the confirm page offers *Remove only this tile* only when another opener exists; the default menu cannot be removed; a rename rewrites every exact `:submenu <Old>` and `DefaultMenu`; closing settings lands on the default menu when the origin is gone. Pinned in Task 3 and Task 4 (headless `f80-*` runs).
4. **An app scan that is slow, fails, or finds nothing, and settings closed while it runs.** Expect: *Finding apps… (N)* while it runs, the other Add options working, the thread joined before the list is freed, no leak under ASan. Pinned in Task 7 (the scan hook's delay and failure modes, the leak pass).
5. **Typing on a real keyboard that is not US** (Shift, AltGr, a dead key, Caps Lock) and keys that type nothing. Expect: the layout's character with Shift/Caps/AltGr; a dead key types its own character; masked keys, control characters, U+007F and U+FFFD insert nothing; arrows still move the highlight. Pinned in Task 5 (`test_osk` `osk_key_char`) and Task 12 (headless `xdotool type` with a German layout).

## Interfaces between tasks

Fixed here so tasks drafted and built apart agree. A task that needs a change to one of them stops and reports; it never renames one alone.

**Task 1, `src/inidoc.h`** (pure; every function returns false with `inidoc_why()` set on refusal):
```c
// Insert Key=value into `section` before the line `before` (an index from inidoc_list or inidoc_find_line), or
// after the section's last key when `before` is -1, as inidoc_list_add does. The section must exist.
bool inidoc_list_insert(IniDoc *doc, const char *section, int before, const char *key, const char *value);
// Move the key line `line` within its section to before `before`, or after the section's last key when -1.
// Comments and blank lines stay where they were.
bool inidoc_list_move(IniDoc *doc, int line, int before);
// Append "[section]" at the end of the file, after one blank line. Refuses an existing section or a bad name.
bool inidoc_add_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *section);
// Remove every "[section]" header of that name and every line up to the next header.
bool inidoc_remove_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *section);
// Rename every "[old_name]" header to "[new_name]". Refuses when new_name exists or is a bad name.
bool inidoc_rename_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *old_name, const char *new_name);
// The file's section names in order of first appearance, each once. Fills at most `max` and returns the
// total, as inidoc_list does, so (doc, NULL, 0) gives the count.
int inidoc_sections(const IniDoc *doc, const char **names, int max);
bool inidoc_has_section(const IniDoc *doc, const char *section);
```

**Task 2, `src/config_save.h`:**
```c
// Called on the fresh read, before `edits` and `lists` are applied. False fails the save with `result->why` set.
typedef bool (*ConfigDocEdit)(IniDoc *doc, void *context, ConfigSaveResult *result);
bool config_save_with(const char *loaded, const char *system_prefix, const char *user_config,
                      const ConfigEdit *edits, int count, const ConfigListEdit *lists, int list_count,
                      ConfigDocEdit doc_edit, void *context, ConfigSaveResult *result);
// config_save_all() becomes config_save_with(..., NULL, NULL, result).
void config_save_note(ConfigSaveResult *result, ConfigNoteKind kind, const char *text);   // Appends one note line
```
`ConfigNoteKind` gains `CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE` (a menu renamed or removed by hand meanwhile: that menu's edits are skipped). Also: `bool config_save_next_key(const IniDoc *doc, const char *section, const char *stem, char *out, size_t size, ConfigSaveResult *result);` (the one `<stem>N` numbering, shared with Task 3). **A slot edit placed `INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER` (a menu's own setting) whose section is gone is skipped with a `SECTION_GONE` note**, so a menu removed or renamed by hand never comes back empty; Tasks 4 and 10 keep placing menu settings that way.

**Task 3, `src/menuedit.h`** (pure; uses `alloc.h`):
```c
typedef struct {
    char *key;        // "Entry3"; NULL for a tile not yet written (numbered at save)
    char *title;
    char *icon;       // As the file has it: a library name or a path
    char *command;
    char *original;   // The line as read ("Entry3=Kodi;kodi;kodi"); NULL for a new or moved-in tile
} MenuTile;

typedef struct {
    char *name;
    char *original_name;   // The section as read; NULL for a new menu
    MenuTile *tiles;
    int count;
} MenuEditMenu;

typedef struct MenuEdit MenuEdit;

MenuEdit *menuedit_load(const IniDoc *doc, const char *default_menu);   // Every non-reserved section, in file order
MenuEdit *menuedit_copy(const MenuEdit *edit);                          // The snapshot Discard returns to
void menuedit_free(MenuEdit *edit);
int menuedit_count(const MenuEdit *edit);
const MenuEditMenu *menuedit_menu(const MenuEdit *edit, int m);
int menuedit_find(const MenuEdit *edit, const char *name);              // -1 when none
const char *menuedit_default(const MenuEdit *edit);
bool menuedit_changed(const MenuEdit *edit);

// Each returns NULL on success or the reason it refused, in a few words for the caption.
const char *menuedit_add(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int after, const char *title, const char *icon, const char *command);  // after: -1 = at the end
const char *menuedit_set(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int t, const char *title, const char *icon, const char *command);
const char *menuedit_remove(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int t);              // A submenu tile: see menuedit_remove_menu
const char *menuedit_move(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int from, int to);
const char *menuedit_move_to_menu(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int t, int to_menu);   // Appended at the end of to_menu
const char *menuedit_add_submenu(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int after, const char *name, const char *icon);
const char *menuedit_rename_menu(MenuEdit *edit, int m, const char *new_name);  // Rewrites each exact ":submenu <old>" and the default
const char *menuedit_remove_menu(MenuEdit *edit, int m, int t, bool with_tiles);   // t: the submenu tile in m
int menuedit_openers(const MenuEdit *edit, const char *name);           // Tiles whose command is exactly ":submenu <name>"
const char *menuedit_submenu_of(const MenuTile *tile);                  // The name after ":submenu ", or NULL

const char *menuedit_check_name(const MenuEdit *edit, const char *name, int except);   // Reserved, ']', too long, exists
const char *menuedit_check_tile(const char *title, const char *icon, const char *command);   // Empty part, ';' in title, line too long, inidoc_check
// Addition (fix pass 2, Fable review M2): what menuedit_set() would say, before it is asked: the tile weighed in its
// own line as read (inidoc_check_in(), its comment and spacing counted), and a new tile with its menu's new-tile key
// (weighed_key(), fix pass 3). Pages keeping Done grayed for an existing tile call it (Tasks 10a, 10b, 13b);
// menuedit_check_tile(), with no tile, is for a new one.
const char *menuedit_check_set(const MenuEdit *edit, int m, int t, const char *title, const char *icon, const char *command);
#define MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX 64

// Make `doc` (a fresh read) match `edit`: section renames, removals and additions first, then each menu's entry
// lines in the model's order, new tiles numbered "Entry<N>", then DefaultMenu when renamed. Notes go to `result`.
bool menuedit_apply(const MenuEdit *edit, IniDoc *doc, ConfigSaveResult *result);
```

**Task 4, `launcher.h` / `util.h`:**
```c
void menus_apply(const MenuEdit *edit);   // Rebuild the live Menu and Entry lists from the model; textures stale, layout recomputed
Menu *menu_for(const MenuEditMenu *menu); // The live Menu a model menu stands for, by Menu.section; NULL for a menu not yet applied
void resolve_entry_icon(Entry *entry, const char *menu_name);   // One entry's library name to its file; menu_name for the log line (30-backgrounds.sh:116 reads it)
void add_empty_menus(const char *config_text, size_t length);   // At load: a Menu for each non-reserved section the parser made none for
```
`Menu` gains `char *section` (the section it was built from; `settings_open()` resets it to `name`), which is how `menus_apply()` keeps a `Menu` across a rename and how `menu_for()` finds it. `make_menu()` sets it to the model menu's `original_name`, or NULL for a new menu; `menu_for()` matches by section, and a NULL-section menu by name; a rename never changes it.

In `settings.h` (pure): `SettingsState *settings_remodel(const SettingsState *old, const char *const *names, const char *const *old_names, int count);` (`old_names[i]` is the name menu `i` had in `old`, or NULL for a new one; slot values and their `entry` carried across by that name; the Default menu slot follows a rename; a pending value naming a removed menu goes back to its original). `SettingsState` is opaque, so the model is reached through `void settings_set_menus(SettingsState *state, MenuEdit *menus);` and `MenuEdit *settings_menus(const SettingsState *state);` (borrowed; the screen owns it).

In `settings_screen.h`: `bool settings_menus_changed(void);` — **Tasks 10, 11, 13 and 14 call it after every model change** (with no keyboard picker open); it runs `menus_apply()` and, when the menu list changed, `settings_remodel()` and the `menus[]` / `PickerHost.menus` refresh. A page about a removed menu closes; an open picker or browser closes as Back would.

Test hook `STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT` (Task 4) applies model operations at settings open, so removals and renames are pinned before any page can make them.

### Task 1: inidoc's section and position primitives

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/inidoc.h` (`:41-54`, the prototypes; `:45`, `inidoc_why()`'s comment)
- Modify: `src/inidoc.c` (`:38-50`, the reasons; `:547-572`, `add_section()`; new functions between `inidoc_list_remove()` `:837-851` and `inidoc_free()` `:853`)
- Modify: `tests/test_inidoc.c` (three tests before `main()` `:773`; `main()` `:773-800`)
- Modify: `tests/test_alloc.c` (one proof after `prove_bindings_reload()` `:810-839`; `main()` `:841-879`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `inidoc.c`'s own line model: `Line` (`text`, `length`, `eol`, `kind`, `name`, `section`), `classify_all()`, `insert_line()`, `remove_line()`, `find_header()`, `end_of_key()`, `has_continuations()`, `count_keys()`, `list_line_proven()`, `read_line()`, `find_chars_or_comment()`, `same_section()`, `section_name()`, `refuse()`.
- Produces, in `src/inidoc.h` (pure; each returns false with `inidoc_why()` set on refusal):
  ```c
  bool inidoc_list_insert(IniDoc *doc, const char *section, int before, const char *key, const char *value);
  bool inidoc_list_move(IniDoc *doc, int line, int before);
  bool inidoc_add_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *section);
  bool inidoc_remove_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *section);
  bool inidoc_rename_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *old_name, const char *new_name);
  bool inidoc_has_section(const IniDoc *doc, const char *section);    // Addition: Tasks 2 and 3 ask it
  int inidoc_sections(const IniDoc *doc, const char **names, int max);   // Fills at most max; returns how many there are
  ```

What each primitive settles, so Task 3 can lean on it:
- **Insert** goes directly before the key line `before`, so a comment just above that line ends up above the new one; `-1` is `inidoc_list_add()`'s place. The section must exist (a menu's section is made only by `inidoc_add_section()`). The new line is proven as `inidoc_list_add()` proves its own: one more key, reading as written, with no continuation; else it is taken back.
- **Move** moves the key line's own `Line` (its bytes, its ending) and nothing else. A line already in its place (no key of its section between it and the place) does not move, so a comment between two tiles never jumps. It refuses a key with continuation lines and a key with an empty name, and takes back any move that turns a key into a continuation (the key count proves it).
- **Add section** appends `[name]` after one blank line, sharing `add_section()`'s code through a new `append_header()`. **Remove section** takes every header of the name and every line up to the next header; when that runs to the end of the file, the blank lines just before the header go too, so add-then-remove gives the file back byte for byte. **Rename** rewrites the bytes between each header's brackets, keeping its spacing and any comment after it; every new line is made before any is put in.
- **A section name** is valid when it is 1 to 49 bytes (`INIDOC_MAX_SECTION`; inih keeps no more), holds no line break, and `[name]` reads back as exactly that name: no `]`, and no `;` after whitespace. Names compare as inih compares them: exactly, case included, on their first 49 bytes. Remove and rename copy the name first, since a caller may pass a name `inidoc_sections()` gave, which points into a header they replace.
- `inidoc_sections()` follows `inidoc_list()`: `(doc, NULL, 0)` gives the count.

```c
                            "[Games]\nEntry1=D;apps;:quit\n");
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, inidoc_find_line(doc, "Main", "Entry1=A;apps;:quit"), -1));
    static const char *const moved = "[Main]\nRows=2\nEntry3=C;apps;:quit\n; about B\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\n"
                                     "Entry1=A;apps;:quit\n\n[Games]\nEntry1=D;apps;:quit\n";
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), moved);

    // Already in place: before the next key though a comment lies between; after the last key (the next
    // key is another section's); before itself
    int c = inidoc_find_line(doc, "Main", "Entry3=C;apps;:quit");
    int b = inidoc_find_line(doc, "Main", "Entry2=B;apps;:quit");
    int a = inidoc_find_line(doc, "Main", "Entry1=A;apps;:quit");
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, c, b));
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, a, -1));
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, a, a));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), moved);
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "");

    // Down, before a later line
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, c, a));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Main]\nRows=2\n; about B\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\nEntry3=C;apps;:quit\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\n\n"
                            "[Games]\nEntry1=D;apps;:quit\n");
    inidoc_free(doc);

    // Refused: not a key line; a place in another section; a key with continuation lines (they would have
    // to move past the lines among them); a key with an empty name (the indented key after it would join
    // the key before it); and a place where the moved key would take the indented key after it as its
    // continuation, which is taken back. The file is as it was.
    static const char *const tangled = "[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\n  more\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\n=x\n"
                                       "  Entry3=C;apps;:quit\n[Games]\nEntry1=D;apps;:quit\n";
    doc = parse(tangled);
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 2, -1));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the line is not a key");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 99, -1));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the line is not a key");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 1, 99));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the line is not a key");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 3, -5));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the line is not a key");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 3, 7));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the line is not in that section");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 1, -1));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the line has indented lines after it, which config.ini reads with it");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 4, 1));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "it would change how other lines read");
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 3, 5));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "it would change how other lines read");
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), tangled);
    inidoc_free(doc);

    // The file's last line keeps having no line ending, whichever line ends up last
    doc = parse("[Main]\r\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\r\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit");
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, 2, 1));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Main]\r\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\r\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit");
    CHECK(inidoc_list_move(doc, 1, -1));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Main]\r\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\r\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit");
    inidoc_free(doc);

    // And a move taken back from the end, or to it, leaves the endings as they were
    static const char *const open_end = "[Main]\n=x\n  Entry1=A;apps;:quit\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit";
    doc = parse(open_end);
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 3, 2));                       // From the end: Entry1 would continue Entry2
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), open_end);
    CHECK(!inidoc_list_move(doc, 2, -1));                      // To the end: Entry1 would continue Entry2
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "it would change how other lines read");
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), open_end);
    inidoc_free(doc);
}

// A function to test whole sections: listed once each in the order first read; added at the end
// after a blank line; renamed at every header, the comment after one kept; removed with every line up
// to the next header (at the end of the file, the blank line before it too, so adding and removing
// gives the file back); and the names refused, by the rule that "[name]" must read back as that name
static void test_sections(void)
{
    IniDoc *doc = parse("; my launcher\n[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:submenu Games\n\n"
                        "[Games] ; mine\nEntry1=B;apps;:quit\n[Main]\nEntry2=C;apps;:quit\n");
    const char *names[8];
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, names, 8), 3);
    CHECK_STR(names[0], "General");
    CHECK_STR(names[1], "Main");
    CHECK_STR(names[2], "Games");
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, names, 1), 3);              // The count, though only one fits
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, NULL, 0), 3);
    CHECK(inidoc_has_section(doc, "Games"));
    CHECK(!inidoc_has_section(doc, "games"));                  // Names match exactly, case included

    CHECK(inidoc_add_section(doc, "Kids"));
    static const char *const added = "; my launcher\n[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:submenu Games\n\n"
                                     "[Games] ; mine\nEntry1=B;apps;:quit\n[Main]\nEntry2=C;apps;:quit\n\n[Kids]\n";
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), added);
    CHECK(!inidoc_add_section(doc, "Kids"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "a section of that name is there already");
    CHECK(!inidoc_add_section(doc, "a]b"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "config.ini would not read it back as that section's name");
    CHECK(!inidoc_add_section(doc, "a ;b"));                   // inih ends the header at a ';' after a space
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "config.ini would not read it back as that section's name");
    CHECK(!inidoc_add_section(doc, ""));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "config.ini would not read it back as that section's name");
    CHECK(!inidoc_add_section(doc, "a\nb"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "config.ini would not read it back as that section's name");
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), added);

    CHECK(inidoc_rename_section(doc, "Main", "Home"));
    CHECK(inidoc_rename_section(doc, "Games", "Play"));
    CHECK(inidoc_rename_section(doc, "Play", "play"));          // Another case is another name to inih
    CHECK(!inidoc_rename_section(doc, "play", "Home"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "a section of that name is there already");
    CHECK(!inidoc_rename_section(doc, "Nowhere", "Kids2"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the section is not there");
    CHECK(!inidoc_rename_section(doc, "play", "a]b"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "config.ini would not read it back as that section's name");
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "; my launcher\n[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[Home]\nEntry1=A;apps;:submenu Games\n\n"
                            "[play] ; mine\nEntry1=B;apps;:quit\n[Home]\nEntry2=C;apps;:quit\n\n[Kids]\n");
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, names, 8), 4);
    CHECK_STR(names[1], "Home");
    CHECK_STR(names[2], "play");

    CHECK(inidoc_remove_section(doc, "Kids"));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "; my launcher\n[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[Home]\nEntry1=A;apps;:submenu Games\n\n"
                            "[play] ; mine\nEntry1=B;apps;:quit\n[Home]\nEntry2=C;apps;:quit\n");
    CHECK(inidoc_remove_section(doc, "Home"));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "; my launcher\n[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[play] ; mine\nEntry1=B;apps;:quit\n");
    CHECK(!inidoc_remove_section(doc, "Home"));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the section is not there");
    inidoc_free(doc);

    // A file without a final newline keeps having none; a name may point into the document, as
    // inidoc_sections() gives it (the header it names goes, and ASan would see the name read after)
    doc = parse("[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit");
    CHECK(inidoc_add_section(doc, "Games"));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\n\n[Games]");
    CHECK(inidoc_remove_section(doc, "Games"));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit");
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, names, 8), 1);
    CHECK(inidoc_rename_section(doc, names[0], "Home"));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Home]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit");
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, names, 8), 1);
    CHECK(inidoc_remove_section(doc, names[0]));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "");
    inidoc_free(doc);
    // The same with a header left after the one removed, so the search for the next header runs and
    // reads the name (the case above empties the file, so nothing would read it)
    doc = parse("[Home]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\n[Games]\n");
    CHECK_INT(inidoc_sections(doc, names, 8), 2);
    CHECK(inidoc_remove_section(doc, names[0]));
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), "[Games]\n");
    inidoc_free(doc);

    // 49 bytes is the longest name inih keeps whole; a header's comment counts toward its line
    char name[64];
    char other[64];
    memset(name, 'M', INIDOC_MAX_SECTION);
    name[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION] = '\0';
    memset(other, 'N', INIDOC_MAX_SECTION);
    other[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION] = '\0';
    char text[256];
    char comment[160];
    memset(comment, 'c', 150);
    comment[150] = '\0';
    snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "[G] ;%s\n", comment);         // 155 bytes
    doc = parse(text);
    CHECK(inidoc_add_section(doc, name));
    CHECK(!inidoc_rename_section(doc, "G", other));             // 1 + 49 + 1 + 152 = 203
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the section's name is too long for one line of config.ini (199 bytes at most)");
    CHECK(inidoc_rename_section(doc, "G", "Games"));
    name[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION] = 'M';
    name[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION + 1] = '\0';
    CHECK(!inidoc_add_section(doc, name));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the section's name is too long for config.ini (49 bytes at most)");
    CHECK(!inidoc_rename_section(doc, "Games", name));
    CHECK_STR(inidoc_why(doc), "the section's name is too long for config.ini (49 bytes at most)");
    name[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION] = '\0';
    snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "[Games] ;%s\n\n[%s]\n", comment, name);
    CHECK_STR(written(doc), text);
    inidoc_free(doc);
}
```

```c
// A function to prove that the section edits fail cleanly: refused, saying "out of memory", with the
// document as it was before the call that failed; or done. Moving a line, removing a section and
// listing the sections allocate nothing, so they cannot fail for want of memory.
static void prove_section_edits(void)
{
    static const char *const text = "[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\n[Games] ; mine\nEntry1=C;apps;:quit\n";
    static const char *const after_insert = "[Main]\nEntry3=N;apps;:home\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\n"
                                            "[Games] ; mine\nEntry1=C;apps;:quit\n";
    static const char *const after_rename = "[Main]\nEntry3=N;apps;:home\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\n"
                                            "[Play] ; mine\nEntry1=C;apps;:quit\n";
    static const char *const done = "[Main]\nEntry3=N;apps;:home\nEntry1=A;apps;:quit\nEntry2=B;apps;:quit\n"
                                    "[Play] ; mine\nEntry1=C;apps;:quit\n\n[Kids]\n";
    for (int n = 1;; n++) {
        IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, strlen(text));
        arm(n);
        bool inserted = inidoc_list_insert(doc, "Main", 1, "Entry3", "N;apps;:home");
        bool renamed = inserted && inidoc_rename_section(doc, "Games", "Play");
        bool added = renamed && inidoc_add_section(doc, "Kids");
        disarm();
        char *out = text_of(doc);
        if (!failed)
            CHECK_RUN(added && out != NULL && strcmp(out, done) == 0, n);
        else {
            CHECK_RUN(strcmp(inidoc_why(doc), "out of memory") == 0, n);
            CHECK_RUN(out != NULL && strcmp(out, renamed ? after_rename : inserted ? after_insert : text) == 0, n);
        }
        alloc_free(out);
        inidoc_free(doc);
        runs = n;
        if (!no_leak(__LINE__, n) || !failed)
            break;
    }
    report("the section edits");

    IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, strlen(text));
    const char *names[4];
    arm(1);
    bool moved = inidoc_list_move(doc, 2, 1);
    bool removed = inidoc_remove_section(doc, "Games");
    int count = inidoc_sections(doc, names, 4);
    disarm();
    CHECK(moved && removed && count == 1 && !failed && calls == 0);
    inidoc_free(doc);
    no_leak(__LINE__, 1);
}
```

Replace `add_section()` (`:547-572`) with a shared `append_header()` and `add_section()` over it (the same allocations in the same order, so `test_alloc`'s `prove_set` sees no change):

```c
// A function to add a section's header at the end of the file, after a blank line unless the file
// already ends with one. When out of memory it takes back every line it added, and is false.
static bool append_header(IniDoc *doc, const char *header)
{
    int lines_before = doc->count;
    bool ok = true;
    if (doc->count > 0 && doc->lines[doc->count - 1].text[0] != '\0')
        ok = insert_line(doc, doc->count, "");
    ok = ok && insert_line(doc, doc->count, header);
    while (!ok && doc->count > lines_before)
        remove_line(doc, doc->count - 1);
    return ok;
}

// A function to add a missing section at the end, after a blank line, with the key's line in it
static bool add_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *text, const char *section, const char *key, const char *value)
{
    size_t header_size = strlen(section) + 3;
    if (header_size - 1 > INIDOC_MAX_LINE)
        return refuse(doc, SECTION_TOO_LONG);
    char *header = alloc_malloc(header_size);
    if (header == NULL)
        return refuse(doc, OUT_OF_MEMORY);
    snprintf(header, header_size, "[%s]", section);
    int lines_before = doc->count;
    bool ok = append_header(doc, header);
    alloc_free(header);
    if (!ok)
        return refuse(doc, OUT_OF_MEMORY);
    ok = try_place(doc, doc->count, text, section, key, value);

    // On failure take back every line added: the header and the blank line before it
    while (!ok && doc->count > lines_before)
        remove_line(doc, doc->count - 1);
    return ok;
}
```

After `inidoc_list_remove()` (`:851`), before `inidoc_free()`, add:

```c
// A function to insert a line into a list section before the key line `before` (an index from
// inidoc_list() or inidoc_find_line()), or after the section's last key when `before` is -1, as
// inidoc_list_add() places it. Unlike inidoc_list_add() it never makes the section: it must be there. A
// comment just above `before` ends up above the new line. Refused where the new line would change how
// another reads (before an indented key that follows a key with an empty name, which would become its
// continuation), with the file as it was.
bool inidoc_list_insert(IniDoc *doc, const char *section, int before, const char *key, const char *value)
{
    doc->why = "";
    if (find_header(doc, section) < 0)
        return refuse(doc, NO_SECTION);
    if (before == -1)
        return inidoc_list_add(doc, section, key, value);
    if (before < 0 || before >= doc->count || doc->lines[before].kind != LINE_KEY)
        return refuse(doc, NOT_A_KEY);
    if (!same_section(section_name(doc, doc->lines[before].section), section))
        return refuse(doc, NOT_IN_SECTION);
    const char *reason = inidoc_check(key, value);
    if (reason != NULL)
        return refuse(doc, reason);
    size_t size = strlen(key) + strlen(value) + 2;
    char *text = alloc_malloc(size);
    if (text == NULL)
        return refuse(doc, OUT_OF_MEMORY);
    snprintf(text, size, "%s=%s", key, value);
    int keys_before = count_keys(doc);
    bool inserted = insert_line(doc, before, text);
    alloc_free(text);
    if (!inserted)
        return refuse(doc, OUT_OF_MEMORY);
    if (!list_line_proven(doc, before, key, value, keys_before)) {
        remove_line(doc, before);
        return refuse(doc, NO_SAFE_PLACE);
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to tell whether a key line of a section lies strictly between two lines
static bool key_between(const IniDoc *doc, const char *section, int after, int before)
{
    for (int i = after + 1; i < before; i++) {
        const Line *line = &doc->lines[i];
        if (line->kind == LINE_KEY && same_section(section_name(doc, line->section), section))
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to move a line from one index to another, as it is: its text, its name, its value and its
// ending go with it. The file's last line keeps having no line ending when it had none: the line that
// leaves the end, or takes it, swaps endings with the one that takes or leaves it, so moving a line back
// puts every ending back. It allocates nothing, and leaves placing the lines to the caller.
static void shift_line(IniDoc *doc, int from, int to)
{
    int last = doc->count - 1;
    bool open_end = doc->lines[last].eol[0] == '\0';
    Line moving = doc->lines[from];
    if (from < to)
        memmove(&doc->lines[from], &doc->lines[from + 1], (size_t) (to - from) * sizeof(Line));
    else
        memmove(&doc->lines[to + 1], &doc->lines[to], (size_t) (from - to) * sizeof(Line));
    doc->lines[to] = moving;
    if (open_end && (from == last || to == last)) {
        int a = from == last ? to : last;
        int b = from == last ? last : last - 1;
        const char *eol = doc->lines[a].eol;
        doc->lines[a].eol = doc->lines[b].eol;
        doc->lines[b].eol = eol;
    }
}

// A function to move a key line within its section: to before the key line `before`, or after the
// section's last key and its continuation lines when `before` is -1. Comments and blank lines stay where
// they were, and a line already in its place (no key of its section between it and the place) does not
// move. Refused for a key with continuation lines (they would have to move with it, past the lines among
// them), a key with an empty name (the indented keys after it would join the key before it), and a place
// where it would change how a line reads, which is taken back. The key count proves that last: the line
// lands before a key, or after the last key's continuation lines, and leaves no continuation behind, so a
// line can only change by turning from a key into a continuation. It allocates nothing.
bool inidoc_list_move(IniDoc *doc, int line, int before)
{
    doc->why = "";
    if (line < 0 || line >= doc->count || doc->lines[line].kind != LINE_KEY)
        return refuse(doc, NOT_A_KEY);
    if (before != -1 && (before < 0 || before >= doc->count || doc->lines[before].kind != LINE_KEY))
        return refuse(doc, NOT_A_KEY);
    const char *section = section_name(doc, doc->lines[line].section);
    if (before != -1 && !same_section(section_name(doc, doc->lines[before].section), section))
        return refuse(doc, NOT_IN_SECTION);
    if (doc->lines[line].name[0] == '\0')
        return refuse(doc, NO_SAFE_PLACE);
    if (has_continuations(doc, line))
        return refuse(doc, HAS_CONTINUATIONS);
    if (before == line || (before == -1 ? !key_between(doc, section, line, doc->count)
                                        : line < before && !key_between(doc, section, line, before)))
        return true;
    int target = before;
    if (before == -1) {
        for (int i = 0; i < doc->count; i++) {
            const Line *other = &doc->lines[i];
            if (other->kind == LINE_KEY && same_section(section_name(doc, other->section), section))
                target = end_of_key(doc, i) + 1;
        }
    }
    int to = target > line ? target - 1 : target;
    int keys_before = count_keys(doc);
    shift_line(doc, line, to);
    classify_all(doc);
    if (count_keys(doc) != keys_before) {
        shift_line(doc, to, line);
        classify_all(doc);
        return refuse(doc, NO_SAFE_PLACE);
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to say why "[name]" would not read back as a header of exactly that name, or NULL when it
// would: inih keeps 49 bytes of a name, and ends a header at its first ']' or at a ';' after whitespace
static const char *section_name_problem(const char *name)
{
    size_t length = strlen(name);
    if (length > (size_t) INIDOC_MAX_SECTION)
        return SECTION_NAME_TOO_LONG;
    if (length == 0 || strchr(name, '\n') != NULL || strchr(name, '\r') != NULL ||
        find_chars_or_comment(name, 0, "]") != length)
        return NOT_A_SECTION_NAME;
    return NULL;
}

// A function to add an empty section at the end of the file, after a blank line, as inidoc_set() adds a
// missing one. Refused when the section is there already, or when its name would not read back as itself.
bool inidoc_add_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *section)
{
    doc->why = "";
    const char *reason = section_name_problem(section);
    if (reason != NULL)
        return refuse(doc, reason);
    if (find_header(doc, section) >= 0)
        return refuse(doc, SECTION_EXISTS);
    char header[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION + 3];
    snprintf(header, sizeof(header), "[%s]", section);
    if (!append_header(doc, header))
        return refuse(doc, OUT_OF_MEMORY);
    return true;
}

// A function to tell whether a line is a header of a section
static bool is_header_of(const IniDoc *doc, int i, const char *section)
{
    return doc->lines[i].kind == LINE_SECTION && same_section(doc->lines[i].name, section);
}

// A function to make a header's line again with a new name between its brackets, keeping its spacing
// and whatever follows the closing bracket (a comment); the reason it cannot, or NULL
static const char *renamed_header(const Line *line, const char *name, Line *out)
{
    size_t start = 0;
    while (is_space(line->text[start]))
        start++;
    size_t end = find_chars_or_comment(line->text, start + 1, "]");   // The bracket read_line() found
    size_t name_length = strlen(name);
    size_t length = start + 1 + name_length + (line->length - end);
    if (length > INIDOC_MAX_LINE)
        return SECTION_TOO_LONG;
    *out = *line;   // Keeps the line ending; read_line() replaces the name
    out->text = alloc_malloc(length + 1);
    if (out->text == NULL)
        return OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    memcpy(out->text, line->text, start + 1);
    memcpy(out->text + start + 1, name, name_length);
    memcpy(out->text + start + 1 + name_length, line->text + end, line->length - end);
    out->text[length] = '\0';
    out->length = length;
    if (!read_line(out)) {
        alloc_free(out->text);
        return OUT_OF_MEMORY;
    }
    return NULL;
}

// A function to rename a section: each of its headers is written again with the new name. Refused when
// no header has the old name, the new one would not read back as itself, or another section has it
// already (inih would read the two as one). Every new line is made before any is put in, so running out
// of memory changes nothing.
bool inidoc_rename_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *old_name, const char *new_name)
{
    doc->why = "";
    const char *reason = section_name_problem(new_name);
    if (reason != NULL)
        return refuse(doc, reason);

    // Copies, of the bytes inih compares: either name may point into a header this replaces
    char old_copy[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION + 1];
    char new_copy[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION + 1];
    snprintf(old_copy, sizeof(old_copy), "%s", old_name);
    snprintf(new_copy, sizeof(new_copy), "%s", new_name);
    if (find_header(doc, old_copy) < 0)
        return refuse(doc, NO_SECTION);
    if (!same_section(old_copy, new_copy) && find_header(doc, new_copy) >= 0)
        return refuse(doc, SECTION_EXISTS);
    int headers = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < doc->count; i++) {
        if (is_header_of(doc, i, old_copy))
            headers++;
    }
    Line *renamed = alloc_calloc((size_t) headers, sizeof(Line));
    if (renamed == NULL)
        return refuse(doc, OUT_OF_MEMORY);
    int made = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < doc->count && reason == NULL; i++) {
        if (is_header_of(doc, i, old_copy)) {
            reason = renamed_header(&doc->lines[i], new_copy, &renamed[made]);
            if (reason == NULL)
                made++;
        }
    }
    if (reason != NULL) {
        while (made > 0)
            free_line(&renamed[--made]);
        alloc_free(renamed);
        return refuse(doc, reason);
    }
    made = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < doc->count; i++) {
        if (is_header_of(doc, i, old_copy)) {
            free_line(&doc->lines[i]);
            doc->lines[i] = renamed[made++];
        }
    }
    alloc_free(renamed);
    classify_all(doc);
    return true;
}

// A function to remove a section: each of its headers and every line after one up to the next header,
// its comments and blank lines included. When that runs to the end of the file, the blank lines before
// the header go too, so a section added at the end and removed again leaves the file as it was. It
// allocates nothing.
bool inidoc_remove_section(IniDoc *doc, const char *section)
{
    doc->why = "";
    char name[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION + 1];   // A copy, of the bytes inih compares: `section` may point into a header this removes
    snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%s", section);
    int header = find_header(doc, name);
    if (header < 0)
        return refuse(doc, NO_SECTION);
    for (; header >= 0; header = find_header(doc, name)) {
        int end = header + 1;
        while (end < doc->count && doc->lines[end].kind != LINE_SECTION)
            end++;
        int start = header;
        while (end == doc->count && start > 0 && doc->lines[start - 1].length == 0)
            start--;
        for (int i = end - 1; i >= start; i--)
            remove_line(doc, i);
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to tell whether a section has a header in the file, matched as inih matches names
bool inidoc_has_section(const IniDoc *doc, const char *section)
{
    return find_header(doc, section) >= 0;
}

// A function to list the file's sections by name, in the order each is first read, each once (inih
// reads two headers of one name as one section), as inih gives the names: cut to 49 bytes. It fills at
// most `max` names, which point into the document until its next edit, and returns how many there are.
int inidoc_sections(const IniDoc *doc, const char **names, int max)
{
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < doc->count; i++) {
        bool first = doc->lines[i].kind == LINE_SECTION;
        for (int k = 0; first && k < i; k++)
            first = !is_header_of(doc, k, doc->lines[i].name);
        if (!first)
            continue;
        if (count < max)
            names[count] = doc->lines[i].name;
        count++;
    }
    return count;
}
```

- Produces, in `src/config_save.h`:
  ```c
  typedef enum { CONFIG_NOTE_CHANGED_MEANWHILE, CONFIG_NOTE_REMOVAL_SKIPPED, CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE } ConfigNoteKind;
  // Called on the fresh read, before `edits` and `lists` are applied. False fails the save with `result->why` set.
  typedef bool (*ConfigDocEdit)(IniDoc *doc, void *context, ConfigSaveResult *result);
  bool config_save_with(const char *loaded, const char *system_prefix, const char *user_config,
                        const ConfigEdit *edits, int count, const ConfigListEdit *lists, int list_count,
                        ConfigDocEdit doc_edit, void *context, ConfigSaveResult *result);
  void config_save_note(ConfigSaveResult *result, ConfigNoteKind kind, const char *text);   // Appends one note line
  // Addition: <stem>N one above the section's highest, so Task 3 numbers EntryN as 3b numbers HotkeyN
  bool config_save_next_key(const IniDoc *doc, const char *section, const char *stem, char *out, size_t size,
                            ConfigSaveResult *result);
  ```
  `config_save_all()` becomes `config_save_with(..., NULL, NULL, result)`; its signature and every caller (`settings_screen.c:933`, `:936`) are unchanged.

What changes in how a save behaves:
- The notes gather straight into `result` (they were in a local `SaveNotes` copied over on success), so a callback's `config_save_note()` lines come first, then the single-key edits', then the list edits'. A save that fails empties them, as before: it made nothing.
- `config_save_note()` ignores an empty text. Every note then takes at least one byte, and two with its line break, which keeps `note_kinds` (`CONFIG_SAVE_NOTES_SIZE / 2` entries) from overflowing under a public caller.
- **A menu's own setting whose menu is gone is skipped.** A `ConfigEdit` placed `INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER` (that is a menu's slot: `settings_screen.c:920` places only those so) with a value, whose section the fresh read does not have, is skipped with a `CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE` note, `[Games] is not there any more, so its Rows change is skipped`. Today it would make the section again, which after 3c (plan ruling 2) shows as a new empty menu. Review Focus 1: a hand edit's removal or rename of a menu wins.

```c
// What the document callback in these tests does
typedef struct {
    bool refuse;   // Note something, then fail the save
    int calls;
} DocEditTest;

// A document callback: a note, then a section added (an edit that sets a key in it shows the callback ran
// first), or a refusal
static bool edit_doc(IniDoc *doc, void *context, ConfigSaveResult *result)
{
    DocEditTest *test = context;
    test->calls++;
    config_save_note(result, CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE, "[Games] is not there any more, so the changes to that menu are skipped");
    if (test->refuse) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "the menus cannot be written: a test said no");
        return false;
    }
    if (!inidoc_add_section(doc, "Kids")) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "%s", inidoc_why(doc));
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to test a save through a document callback: it runs once, on the fresh read (a hand edit
// made meanwhile included), before the single-key edits (one sets a key in the section it adds) and the
// list edits; its notes come first; and when it fails, the save fails with its reason, the file and its
// backup are as before, and no note is left
static void test_save_with_a_document_callback(void)
{
    reset(CONFIG, ORIGINAL);
    const char *meanwhile =
        "; my launcher\n[Layout]\nRows=1\nMaxButtons=4 ; the old name\n\n[Games]\nIconSize=128\nEntry1=One;apps;:quit\n"
        "[Hotkeys]\nHotkey1=#4000003A;:quit\n";
    CHECK(fileio_write_all(CONFIG, meanwhile, strlen(meanwhile)));
    ConfigEdit edit = { "Kids", "Rows", NULL, "3", INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER };
    ConfigListEdit gone = { CONFIG_LIST_REMOVE, "Hotkeys", "Hotkey2=#4000003B;:home", NULL, false, NULL };
    DocEditTest test = { false, 0 };
    ConfigSaveResult result;
    CHECK(config_save_with(CONFIG, NULL, NULL, &edit, 1, &gone, 1, edit_doc, &test, &result));
    CHECK_INT(test.calls, 1);
    CHECK(holds(CONFIG,
        "; my launcher\n[Layout]\nRows=1\nMaxButtons=4 ; the old name\n\n[Games]\nIconSize=128\nEntry1=One;apps;:quit\n"
        "[Hotkeys]\nHotkey1=#4000003A;:quit\n\n[Kids]\nRows=3\n"));
    CHECK(holds(CONFIG ".bak", meanwhile));
    CHECK_INT(result.note_count, 2);
    CHECK_INT(result.note_kinds[0], CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE);
    CHECK_INT(result.note_kinds[1], CONFIG_NOTE_REMOVAL_SKIPPED);
    CHECK_STR(result.notes, "[Games] is not there any more, so the changes to that menu are skipped\n"
                            "'Hotkey2=#4000003B;:home' is not there any more, so its removal is skipped");

    reset(CONFIG, ORIGINAL);
    test.refuse = true;
    CHECK(!config_save_with(CONFIG, NULL, NULL, &edit, 1, NULL, 0, edit_doc, &test, &result));
    CHECK_STR(result.why, "the menus cannot be written: a test said no");
    CHECK(holds(CONFIG, ORIGINAL));
    CHECK(!fileio_exists(CONFIG ".bak"));
    CHECK_STR(result.notes, "");
    CHECK_INT(result.note_count, 0);
}

// A function to test a menu's own setting (placed under its header) whose menu a hand edit renamed or
// removed meanwhile: it is skipped with a note, rather than making the section again as an empty menu.
// A removal there has nothing to do and says nothing; a setting outside the menus still makes its section.
static void test_setting_of_a_gone_menu_is_skipped(void)
{
    reset(CONFIG, ORIGINAL);
    ConfigEdit edits[] = {
        { "Games", "Rows", NULL, "3", INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER },
        { "Movies", "Columns", NULL, "5", INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER },
        { "Movies", "IconSize", NULL, NULL, INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER },
        { "Background", "Mode", NULL, "Image", INIDOC_AFTER_LAST_KEY }
    };
    ConfigSaveResult result;
    CHECK(config_save(CONFIG, NULL, NULL, edits, 4, &result));
    CHECK(holds(CONFIG,
        "; my launcher\n[Layout]\nRows=1\nMaxButtons=4 ; the old name\n\n[Games]\nRows=3\nIconSize=128\n"
        "Entry1=One;apps;:quit\n\n[Background]\nMode=Image\n"));
    CHECK_INT(result.note_count, 1);
    CHECK_INT(result.note_kinds[0], CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE);
    CHECK_STR(result.notes, "[Movies] is not there any more, so its Columns change is skipped");
}

// A function to test adding notes by hand, as a document callback does: one line each, an empty one
// adding nothing, and none past the end of the buffer, so every note counted has its line
static void test_save_note(void)
{
    ConfigSaveResult result;
    memset(&result, 0, sizeof(result));
    config_save_note(&result, CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE, "first");
    config_save_note(&result, CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE, "");
    config_save_note(&result, CONFIG_NOTE_CHANGED_MEANWHILE, "second");
    CHECK_STR(result.notes, "first\nsecond");
    CHECK_INT(result.note_count, 2);
    CHECK_INT(result.note_kinds[1], CONFIG_NOTE_CHANGED_MEANWHILE);

    // Each "x" takes two bytes with its break: 505 more fit in the 1023 after "first\nsecond", and the
    // 506th finds room for its break alone, so it has no line and no kind
    for (int i = 0; i < 600; i++)
        config_save_note(&result, CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE, "x");
    CHECK_INT((int) strlen(result.notes), (int) sizeof(result.notes) - 1);
    CHECK(result.notes[sizeof(result.notes) - 2] == '\n');
    CHECK_INT(result.note_count, 507);
}
```

```c
{

// A function to prove that a save through a document callback fails cleanly: refused with memory's

static void prove_config_save_with(void)
{

        runs = n;

    }
    report("saving through a document callback");
}
```

In `src/config_save.c`, replace `apply_edits()` (`:26-49`) with:

```c
// A function to apply the edits to a config's text; false (with the reason) when one cannot be written.
// A key and its older alias never both survive an edit: the alias alone is edited in its place,
// and beside the key it is removed, so the file never holds two lines for one setting. A menu's own
// setting (placed under its header) whose section a hand edit renamed or removed meanwhile is skipped,
// with a note: setting it would make the section again, which the launcher shows as an empty menu.
static bool apply_edits(IniDoc *doc, const ConfigEdit *edits, int count, ConfigSaveResult *result)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const ConfigEdit *edit = &edits[i];
        const char *key = edit->key;
        if (edit->value != NULL && edit->placement == INIDOC_UNDER_HEADER && !inidoc_has_section(doc, edit->section)) {
            char note[CONFIG_SAVE_NOTES_SIZE];
            snprintf(note, sizeof(note), "[%s] is not there any more, so its %s change is skipped", edit->section, key);
            config_save_note(result, CONFIG_NOTE_SECTION_GONE, note);
            continue;
        }
        if (edit->alias != NULL && inidoc_get(doc, edit->section, edit->alias) != NULL) {
            if (inidoc_get(doc, edit->section, key) == NULL && edit->value != NULL)
                key = edit->alias;
            else
                inidoc_remove(doc, edit->section, edit->alias);
        }
        if (edit->value == NULL)
            inidoc_remove(doc, edit->section, key);
        else if (!inidoc_set(doc, edit->section, key, edit->value, edit->placement)) {
            snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "the %s value in [%s] cannot be written: %s",
                key, edit->section, inidoc_why(doc));
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
```

Replace `:110-128` (`SaveNotes` and `add_note()`) with:

```c
// A function to add a note of a kind to a save's notes, one per line; one that does not fit is cut
// short, and one with no room left at all adds no line, and so no kind
static void add_note(ConfigSaveResult *result, ConfigNoteKind kind, const char *format, const char *line)
{
    size_t size = sizeof(result->notes);
    size_t used = strlen(result->notes);
    if (used > 0 && used + 1 < size)
        result->notes[used++] = '\n';
    if (used + 1 < size)
        result->note_kinds[result->note_count++] = kind;
    snprintf(result->notes + used, size - used, format, line);
}

// A function to add one note line of a kind, in the words a document callback chooses. An empty one
// adds nothing: each line then takes two bytes at least with its break, as `note_kinds` is sized for.
void config_save_note(ConfigSaveResult *result, ConfigNoteKind kind, const char *text)
{
    if (text[0] == '\0')
        return;
    add_note(result, kind, "%s", text);
}

// A function to take back a failed save's notes: it made nothing, so nothing was skipped
static void drop_notes(ConfigSaveResult *result)
{
    result->notes[0] = '\0';
    memset(result->note_kinds, 0, sizeof(result->note_kinds));
    result->note_count = 0;
}
```

Replace `apply_list_edits()` (`:209-259`) with:

```c
// A function to apply the list edits to the fresh file: changes and removals first, found by the line
// each had when settings opened, then the additions. A line a hand edit changed or removed meanwhile
// takes its change as a new line, and its removal is skipped; both say so in the result's notes. A
// removal inidoc refuses (a key with an empty name) fails the save with its reason, as a line that cannot
// be written does.
static bool apply_list_edits(IniDoc *doc, const ConfigListEdit *lists, int count, ConfigSaveResult *result)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const ConfigListEdit *edit = &lists[i];
        if (edit->op == CONFIG_LIST_ADD)
            continue;
        int line = inidoc_find_line(doc, edit->section, edit->original);
        if (edit->op == CONFIG_LIST_REMOVE) {
            if (line < 0)
                add_note(result, CONFIG_NOTE_REMOVAL_SKIPPED, "'%s' is not there any more, so its removal is skipped",
                         edit->original);
            else if (!inidoc_list_remove(doc, line)) {
                snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "the line '%s' in [%s] cannot be removed: %s", edit->original,
                    edit->section, inidoc_why(doc));
                return false;
            }
            continue;
        }
        if (line < 0) {
            add_note(result, CONFIG_NOTE_CHANGED_MEANWHILE, "'%s' changed meanwhile, so its change is written as a new line",
                     edit->original);
            if (!add_list_line(doc, edit, result))
                return false;
            continue;
        }
        // A numbered set keeps the line's own key: its number is already the line's
        const char *key = edit->key;
        char own[INIDOC_MAX_LINE + 1];
        if (edit->numbered) {
            if (!line_key(doc, edit->section, line, own, sizeof(own), result))
                return false;
            key = own;
        }
        if (!inidoc_list_set(doc, line, key, edit->value)) {
            snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "the %s value in [%s] cannot be written: %s", key,
                edit->section, inidoc_why(doc));
            return false;
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (lists[i].op == CONFIG_LIST_ADD && !add_list_line(doc, &lists[i], result))
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}
```

Replace `config_save_all()` (`:268-353`) with:

```c
// A function to save the settings screen's changes and list edits, with no document callback
bool config_save_all(const char *loaded, const char *system_prefix, const char *user_config,
                     const ConfigEdit *edits, int count, const ConfigListEdit *lists, int list_count,
                     ConfigSaveResult *result)
{
    return config_save_with(loaded, system_prefix, user_config, edits, count, lists, list_count, NULL, NULL, result);
}

// A function to save the settings screen's changes. `loaded` is the file the launcher read.
// When it cannot be written but lies under `system_prefix` (the packaged copy on Linux), the
// save goes to `user_config` instead, which the launcher searches first; pass NULL for both
// where there is no such fallback (Windows). On the fresh read, `doc_edit` (NULL for none) makes its
// changes first (menuedit_apply() writes the menus so, and a menu's settings then find its section by
// its new name), then the single-key edits, then the list edits. What they could not make as asked
// reaches `result->notes`, which a save that fails leaves empty, since it makes nothing.
bool config_save_with(const char *loaded, const char *system_prefix, const char *user_config,
                      const ConfigEdit *edits, int count, const ConfigListEdit *lists, int list_count,
                      ConfigDocEdit doc_edit, void *context, ConfigSaveResult *result)
{
    memset(result, 0, sizeof(*result));
    char source[CONFIG_SAVE_PATH_MAX];
    if (!fileio_real_path(loaded, source, sizeof(source))) {
        snprintf(result->path, sizeof(result->path), "%s", loaded);
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "%s", fileio_last_error());
        return false;
    }
    snprintf(result->path, sizeof(result->path), "%s", source);

    if (!fileio_is_writable(source)) {
        if (system_prefix == NULL || user_config == NULL || !starts_with(source, system_prefix)) {
            snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "%s", fileio_last_error());
            return false;
        }
        if (!use_user_config(user_config, source, sizeof(source), result))
            return false;
    }

    // Read the file as it is on disk now, so a change made meanwhile by hand survives
    size_t length = 0;
    char *text = fileio_read_all(source, &length);
    if (text == NULL) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "could not read %.300s: %s", source, fileio_last_error());
        return false;
    }
    IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, length);
    alloc_free(text);
    if (doc == NULL) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "out of memory");
        return false;
    }
    if ((doc_edit != NULL && !doc_edit(doc, context, result)) || !apply_edits(doc, edits, count, result) ||
        !apply_list_edits(doc, lists, list_count, result)) {
        inidoc_free(doc);
        drop_notes(result);
        return false;
    }
    char *output = inidoc_serialize(doc, &length);
    inidoc_free(doc);
    if (output == NULL) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "out of memory");
        drop_notes(result);
        return false;
    }

    // Keep the file as it was, then write the new one beside it and swap it in whole. A file that
    // cannot be looked up (out of memory, say) is never taken for one that is not there, which
    // would replace it without a backup.
    bool present = fileio_present(result->path);
    bool ok = true;
    if (!present && strcmp(fileio_last_error(), "not found") != 0) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "could not look for %.300s: %s", result->path, fileio_last_error());
        ok = false;
    }
    ok = ok && (!present || keep_backup(result));
    char temporary[CONFIG_SAVE_PATH_MAX + 4];
    snprintf(temporary, sizeof(temporary), "%s.tmp", result->path);
    if (ok && !fileio_write_all(temporary, output, length)) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "could not write %.300s: %s", temporary, fileio_last_error());
        ok = false;
    }
    else if (ok && !fileio_replace(temporary, result->path)) {
        snprintf(result->why, sizeof(result->why), "could not replace the file: %s", fileio_last_error());
        ok = false;
    }
    if (!ok) {
        fileio_remove(temporary);
        drop_notes(result);
    }
    else
        snprintf(result->warning, sizeof(result->warning), "%s", fileio_last_warning());
    alloc_free(output);
    return ok;
}
```

### Task 3: The menus model (`src/menuedit.c`)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/menuedit.h`, `src/menuedit.c`
- Create: `tests/test_menuedit.c`
- Modify: `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (a block after the `config_save` test, `:53-58`; `menuedit.c` in `test_alloc`'s sources, `:112-117`)
- Modify: `tests/test_alloc.c` (`#include "menuedit.h"` after `:17`; three proofs after Task 2's `prove_config_save_with()`; `main()`)

The launcher does not build `menuedit.c` yet: Task 4 adds it to `src/CMakeLists.txt` `SOURCES` with its first caller. Task 18 adds it to `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s pure-module list.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 1's `inidoc_sections()`, `inidoc_has_section()`, `inidoc_add_section()`, `inidoc_remove_section()`, `inidoc_rename_section()`, `inidoc_list_insert()`, `inidoc_list_move()`, with `inidoc_list()`, `inidoc_find_line()`, `inidoc_list_set()`, `inidoc_list_remove()`, `inidoc_get()`, `inidoc_set()`, `inidoc_why()`, and `inidoc_parse()`, `inidoc_check_in()`, `inidoc_free()` (a tile weighed in its own line); Task 2's `config_save_note()`, `config_save_next_key()`, `ConfigSaveResult`, `CONFIG_NOTE_*`; `fileio_lower()`; `launcher_config.h`'s `SETTING_ROWS`, `SETTING_COLUMNS`, `SETTING_ICON_SIZE`, `SETTING_DEFAULT_MENU`.
- Produces: `src/menuedit.h`, exactly the skeleton's Task 3 block (Step 3 below), plus one addition: `const char *menuedit_check_set(const MenuEdit *edit, int m, int t, const char *title, const char *icon, const char *command);`, `menuedit_set()`'s reason before it is asked (fix pass 2, M2), for the pages that keep *Done* grayed for an existing tile.

**Decisions this task makes** (where the spec and the skeleton leave room; each is pinned by a test):
- **Load mirrors the parser**: every section `inidoc_sections()` lists whose name is not exactly a reserved one (`MATCH` is `strcmp`, so `[general]` is a menu), in file order, an empty section included (ruling 2). A tile is a line the parser makes an entry of: not `Rows`/`Columns`/`IconSize` with a value holding no `;`; the title and the icon each end at a `;` with any `;` before them skipped (`strtok_r`'s way, `util.c:263-300`), the command is the rest; fewer than three parts, or exactly `:select`, is no tile. Keys before the first header are not a menu: inih reads them as a section named `""`, as it reads keys under an empty `[]` header, and a menu by that name could be neither opened (`:submenu ` with no name) nor saved. `inidoc_sections()` lists no name for the keys before the first header, and the load skips a `""` name from `[]`; Task 4's load drops the menu the parser makes of either, so the live menus and the model agree. The icon is kept as the file has it (no `clean_path()`). **One case the model does not mirror, documented rather than handled** (it takes a hand edit that indents an entry line): an indented key line right after an entry is a continuation line to inidoc, which does not list it and keeps it with the line above, while inih makes a tile of it, titled with its whole text (`Entry2=Plex`). The model has no tile for it. Removing the tile above it removes both lines (`inidoc_list_remove()` takes continuation lines with their key), and moving the tile above it fails the save with inidoc's reason (`inidoc_list_move()` refuses a key with continuation lines). The file stays one inih reads either way.
- **A tile whose line has no key** (`=Title;icon;command`, a tile to the parser) is loaded with the key `""`. It can be changed in place, but removing it, moving it to another menu, or removing it with a submenu is refused (*Its line in config.ini has no key, so it can't be removed or moved*), since inidoc refuses to remove or move such a line (the indented lines after it would join the key before it). Moving any tile within its menu is refused too (*A line in this menu has no key in config.ini, so its tiles can't be moved*), since putting the tiles in the model's order can move that line; and removing a submenu that such a tile opens elsewhere is refused (*A tile that opens it has no key in config.ini, so it can't be removed*).
- **Names find exactly, clash in any case.** `menuedit_find()` is `strcmp`, as the parser matches. `menuedit_check_name()` refuses a name that equals a reserved or an existing menu's name ignoring ASCII case: `Games` and `games` would be two menus to inih, but two menus that read the same on screen, and a reserved name in another case (`general`) would be a menu that reads as settings to anyone opening `config.ini`. A menu may change its own name's case (`except`).
- **A name** is 1 to 49 bytes, with no `]`, no `;` (it doubles as its tile's title, which cannot hold one), no line break, and no space at either end (`:submenu Name ` would end with a space, which config.ini drops).
- **A tile** has three non-empty parts; no `;` in the title or the icon; no space at either end of any part (a title ending in a space before `;` is read as a comment by inih: Review Focus 2); no `;` after a space in the command; not `:select`; and its line, `key=title;icon;command`, at most 199 bytes, weighed with the tile's own key, or for a tile not yet numbered with `Entry99999`, or in a menu a hand edit numbered past that, with `Entry` and one digit more than its longest number (`Entry100000` gives `Entry9999999`: the save numbers new tiles one above the highest), whether the new tile is being added, changed (`menuedit_set()`, `menuedit_check_set()`) or rewritten by a rename. These rules are `inidoc_check()`'s for this shape of line, so a value that passes them always passes it (a test proves it over a grid of parts). **A tile read from the file is weighed in its own line too**, as `inidoc_list_set()` will write it there: `inidoc_check_in()` on a document of that line alone (under a header `[S]`), so the line's spacing and any comment after its value count toward its 199 bytes (Global Constraints: every written value passes `inidoc_check_in()`). `menuedit_check_set()` (an addition to the skeleton's block) gives that answer before an edit, for a page's *Done*; `menuedit_check_tile()`, with no tile, cannot. `MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX` is the keyboard's limit (Task 5); `menuedit_check_tile()` does not hold a hand-written longer title to it, so such a tile stays editable.
- **Removing a submenu tile** goes through `menuedit_remove_menu()`; `menuedit_remove()` refuses a tile that opens a menu the model has (`It opens a submenu`), and treats one whose menu is gone as any tile. `with_tiles = false` (*Remove only this tile*) is refused unless another tile opens the menu. `with_tiles = true` removes the menu with its tiles and every tile anywhere that opens it (none would open anything); it does not follow the submenus that menu opens. The default menu is never removed.
- **Renaming** rewrites every tile whose command is exactly `:submenu <Old>` to `:submenu <New>`, and its title to `New` when the title was exactly `Old` (a title of its own stays); and the model's default. A rename any opener's line has no room for is refused with that reason. The file's `:submenu Old` lines that the model never read (a hand edit's, meanwhile) and hotkey or gamepad bindings to `:submenu Old` are not rewritten: the spec names entries, and the model knows only the ones it read.
- **Moving to another menu** gives the tile a new key there (`key` and `original` NULL), so its line is weighed as a new tile's in that menu (`Entry99999`, or the longer key above); moving a tile into the menu it opens is refused.
- **`menuedit_apply()`** (ruling 4), on the fresh read: (1) removes the sections of menus the model removed (one already gone: skipped, `SECTION_GONE` note); (2) finds each menu whose section as read is gone (renamed or removed by hand): all its edits are skipped, with a `SECTION_GONE` note when it had any; **but one the model renamed fails the save** (*[Games] was renamed or removed in config.ini meanwhile, so it cannot be renamed to Play*), as a clash does: its openers in other menus already open it by its new name, which no section would have; (3) fails the save when a menu renamed or added by the model takes a name a hand edit gave a section meanwhile (merging into it would join two menus), unless a renamed menu gives that name up; (4) renames each renamed section straight to its new name when no section holds that name, and otherwise through a name of its own, `StreamFlex renaming <N>` (the first in neither the file nor the model's names), then to its new name once the others have moved, so names that swap or follow on never meet, and a header whose comment has room for the new name but not the 21-byte temporary one is still renamed; (5) adds new menus' sections at the end; (6) reconciles each changed menu's section; (7) points `DefaultMenu` at a renamed menu's new name only when the file still names its old one.
- **Reconciling a section:** the lines of tiles the model no longer holds are removed, found by their text as read (a line read twice and held once loses one; one already gone: `REMOVAL_SKIPPED` note). Each tile finds its line by its text as read, the first not yet found. A changed tile is written into its own line with its own key (spacing and comment kept); one whose line is gone is written as a new line (`CHANGED_MEANWHILE` note); an unchanged tile whose line is gone stays gone, silently, as an unchanged binding does in 3b. **Only when the model moved a tile it read** are the tiles with lines put in the model's order, moving only them, each before the line in the place it should hold, so a hand edit's order of a menu the model did not reorder survives, and lines added by hand stay where they are. New tiles are written in the model's order, each before the next tile in the model's order that has a line, else after the section's last key, numbered `Entry<N>` one above the section's highest `Entry` number at that moment (`config_save_next_key()`), so numbers ascend in the model's order. `Rows`, `Columns` and `IconSize` setting lines are never listed, set, moved or removed. A menu the model did not change is not touched.
