```c
// A function to free a menu's entries: their textures, while the renderer that made them exists
// (`textures`), their text, and the menu's index of them
static void free_entries(Menu *menu, bool textures)
{
    Entry *entry = menu->first_entry;
    while (entry != NULL) {
        Entry *next = entry->next;
        if (textures) {
            if (entry->icon != NULL)
                SDL_DestroyTexture(entry->icon);
            if (entry->icon_selected != NULL)
                SDL_DestroyTexture(entry->icon_selected);
            if (entry->title_texture != NULL)
                SDL_DestroyTexture(entry->title_texture);
        }
        free(entry->title);
        free(entry->icon_path);
        free(entry->icon_selected_path);
        free(entry->cmd);
        free(entry);
        entry = next;
    }
    free(menu->items);
    menu->first_entry = NULL;
    menu->items = NULL;
    menu->num_entries = 0;
}

// A function to free a menu: its entries (free_entries()), its names, and itself
static void free_menu(Menu *menu, bool textures)
{
    free_entries(menu, textures);
    free(menu->name);
    free(menu->section);
    free(menu);
}

// A function to make an empty menu for a menus model's menu the launcher has none for. Its section is
// the one the model read it from: a menu Discard puts back, or one the hand-edit catch-up reads from
// config.ini, is then found by menu_for() at the next change, not made again (losing its place). A menu
// made in settings was read from none, so it has none, and menu_for() finds it by its name; a section
// of its name would let a new menu named as a renamed one was take that menu's Menu.
static Menu *make_menu(const MenuEditMenu *from)
{
    Menu *menu = calloc(1, sizeof(Menu));
    if (menu == NULL || (menu->name = strdup(from->name)) == NULL ||
        (from->original_name != NULL && (menu->section = strdup(from->original_name)) == NULL))
        log_fatal("Could not allocate the menu '%s'", from->name);
    return menu;
}

// A function to give a menu the entries of a menus model's menu, as the parser makes them from its
// lines: the icon as written (quotes round a path taken off), its selected icon beside it when there is
// one, then a library name pointed at its file
static void make_entries(Menu *menu, const MenuEditMenu *from)
{
    Entry *previous = NULL;
    for (int t = 0; t < from->count; t++) {
        const MenuTile *tile = &from->tiles[t];
        Entry *entry = calloc(1, sizeof(Entry));
        if (entry == NULL || (entry->title = strdup(tile->title)) == NULL ||
            (entry->icon_path = strdup(tile->icon)) == NULL || (entry->cmd = strdup(tile->command)) == NULL)
            log_fatal("Could not allocate the entries of menu '%s'", from->name);
        clean_path(entry->icon_path);
        entry->icon_selected_path = selected_path(entry->icon_path);
        resolve_entry_icon(entry, from->name);
        entry->previous = previous;
        if (previous == NULL)
            menu->first_entry = entry;
        else
            previous->next = entry;
        previous = entry;
        menu->num_entries++;
    }
    if (menu->num_entries == 0)
        return;
    menu->items = malloc(menu->num_entries * sizeof(Entry*));
    if (menu->items == NULL)
        log_fatal("Could not allocate the entries of menu '%s'", from->name);
    Entry *entry = menu->first_entry;
    for (unsigned int i = 0; i < menu->num_entries; i++, entry = entry->next)
        menu->items[i] = entry;
}

// A function to find the live menu a menus model's menu stands for: the one read from the section the
// model read it from, or, for a menu made in settings (read from none), the one made for it under its
// name. NULL when there is none: the model's menu is new to the launcher.
Menu *menu_for(const MenuEditMenu *from)
{
    for (Menu *menu = config.first_menu; menu != NULL; menu = menu->next) {
        bool same = from->original_name != NULL ? menu->section != NULL && MATCH(menu->section, from->original_name)
                                                : menu->section == NULL && MATCH(menu->name, from->name);
        if (same)
            return menu;
    }
    return NULL;
}

// A function to rebuild the launcher's menus from the menus model after a change to it (spec "Saving and
// applying"): each live menu the model still has is kept, renamed when it was, with its grid settings,
// its place and its back link; one the model has no more goes, every pointer to it first; one the model
// made is made. Every menu's entries are made again from the model's tiles, as the parser makes them,
// and its textures are marked stale; the menu on show (while settings are open, the preview's) is laid
// out again at once, and the others when next shown. The default menu follows its menu through a rename;
// were that menu gone, the model's default (the file's DefaultMenu, through its renames) takes its place.
void menus_apply(const MenuEdit *edit)
{
    int count = menuedit_count(edit);
    Menu **list = calloc((size_t) (count > 0 ? count : 1), sizeof(Menu*));
    if (list == NULL)
        log_fatal("Could not allocate the menus");
    int kept = 0;
    for (int m = 0; m < count; m++) {
        list[m] = menu_for(menuedit_menu(edit, m));
        if (list[m] != NULL)
            kept++;
    }

    // The menus the model has no more: every pointer to one let go of, then each freed with its textures
    int gone = 0;
    Menu *menu = config.first_menu;
    while (menu != NULL) {
        Menu *next = menu->next;
        bool keep = false;
        for (int m = 0; m < count && !keep; m++)
            keep = list[m] == menu;
        if (!keep) {
            log_debug("Menus: '%s' is gone", menu->name);
            for (int m = 0; m < count; m++) {
                if (list[m] != NULL && list[m]->back == menu)
                    list[m]->back = NULL;
            }
            if (current_menu == menu)
                current_menu = NULL;
            if (default_menu == menu)
                default_menu = NULL;
            free_menu(menu, true);
            gone++;
        }
        menu = next;
    }

    // The model's menus, in its order: made, renamed, and given their entries again
    for (int m = 0; m < count; m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *from = menuedit_menu(edit, m);
        if (list[m] == NULL) {
            list[m] = make_menu(from);
            log_debug("Menus: '%s' is new", from->name);
        }
        else if (!MATCH(list[m]->name, from->name)) {
            // Its section stays the one read: the model's original_name, which menu_for() matches it by
            log_debug("Menus: '%s' is now '%s'", list[m]->name, from->name);
            free(list[m]->name);
            list[m]->name = strdup(from->name);
            if (list[m]->name == NULL)
                log_fatal("Could not allocate the menu '%s'", from->name);
        }
        free_entries(list[m], true);
        make_entries(list[m], from);
        list[m]->rendered_size = 0;
        list[m]->next = NULL;
        if (m > 0)
            list[m - 1]->next = list[m];
    }
    config.first_menu = count > 0 ? list[0] : NULL;
    config.num_menus = (size_t) count;

    if (default_menu == NULL) {
        const char *name = menuedit_default(edit);
        for (int m = 0; m < count && default_menu == NULL; m++) {
            if (name != NULL && MATCH(list[m]->name, name))
                default_menu = list[m];
        }
        if (default_menu == NULL && count > 0)
            default_menu = list[0];
        if (default_menu != NULL)
            log_error("Menus: the default menu is gone, so '%s' is the default menu now", default_menu->name);
    }
    if (default_menu != NULL && (config.default_menu == NULL || !MATCH(config.default_menu, default_menu->name))) {
        free(config.default_menu);
        config.default_menu = strdup(default_menu->name);
    }
    if (current_menu == NULL)
        current_menu = default_menu;
    current_entry = NULL;   // Its entry is gone; laying the menu out finds the new one
    if (current_menu != NULL)
        apply_layout(current_menu);
    log_debug("Menus: the launcher's menus were made again from the menus model: %i menu(s), %i kept, %i new, %i gone",
        count, kept, count - kept, gone);
    free(list);
}
```

```c
// A function to show in the preview the menu the page is about: a menu being edited or highlighted,
// else the one settings opened over. An empty menu shows too, with its note (plan ruling 2). In the
// Menus list the preview waits for the cursor to rest (settings_draw() switches it), so moving down the
// list never waits for the icons of every menu on the way.
static void follow_preview(void)
{
    int index = settings_preview_menu(model);
    Menu *want = index >= 0 && index < menu_count ? menus[index] : origin;
    preview_wanted = NULL;
    if (want == current_menu)

    if (settings_page(model) == SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS) {
        preview_wanted = want;
        preview_asked = ticks_ms();
    }
    else
        show_preview(want);
}
```

```c
// A function to load the bindings from config.ini as it is now (`doc`; NULL when it could not be read),
// whose lines the save finds again by their text. Bindings that cannot be read (the file gone, or out
// of memory) leave the binding pages out, and say so.
static void load_bindings(const IniDoc *doc)
{
    static const char *const skip[] = { SETTING_GAMEPAD_ENABLED, SETTING_GAMEPAD_DEVICE, SETTING_GAMEPAD_MAPPINGS_FILE, NULL };
#ifdef _WIN32
    bindings = bindings_create(true, gamepad_running());
#else
    bindings = bindings_create(false, gamepad_running());
#endif
    bool loaded = bindings != NULL && doc != NULL && load_section(doc, "Hotkeys", NULL, BINDINGS_KEYBOARD) &&
                  load_section(doc, "Gamepad", skip, BINDINGS_GAMEPAD);
    if (!loaded) {
        log_error("Settings: the bindings could not be read from %s, so the binding pages are left out", config.config_path);
        bindings_free(bindings);
        bindings = NULL;
        return;
    }
    settings_set_bindings(model, bindings, pickers_key_name);
}

// A function to load the menus model from config.ini as it is now (`doc`), as the bindings are: a live
// Entry keeps neither its key nor its line (plan ruling 3). Each live menu is taken as read from the
// section of its name, as config.ini reads after any save (menu_for()). Menus that cannot be read leave
// the menus model out, and say so. So does a config.ini whose every menu was removed by hand since
// StreamFlex started: the launcher cannot show no menu (menus_apply() would leave current_menu with none to
// draw), so it keeps its own, and the hand-edit catch-up does not run.
static void load_menus(const IniDoc *doc)
{
    for (int m = 0; m < menu_count; m++) {
        free(menus[m]->section);
        menus[m]->section = strdup(menus[m]->name);
    }
    menu_edit = doc != NULL ? menuedit_load(doc, config.default_menu) : NULL;
    if (menu_edit == NULL) {
        log_error("Settings: the menus could not be read from %s, so they cannot be edited", config.config_path);
        return;
    }
    if (menuedit_count(menu_edit) == 0) {
        log_error("Settings: %s has no menus now (edited by hand since StreamFlex started), so the launcher keeps "
                  "its menus, and they cannot be edited", config.config_path);
        menuedit_free(menu_edit);
        menu_edit = NULL;
        return;
    }
    settings_set_menus(model, menu_edit);
    log_debug("Menus: read %i menu(s) from %s", menuedit_count(menu_edit), config.config_path);
}

// A function to tell whether the menus model and the launcher's menus are the same menus by name, in the
// same order, as they are unless config.ini's menus were edited by hand since StreamFlex started
static bool menus_in_step(void)
{
    if (menuedit_count(menu_edit) != menu_count)
        return false;
    for (int m = 0; m < menu_count; m++) {
        if (strcmp(menuedit_menu(menu_edit, m)->name, menus[m]->name) != 0)
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}
```

After `begin_pickers()` (`:1724`) add:

```c
// A function to put the menus model into the launcher after a change to it, and the settings with it
// (plan ruling 5). The launcher's menus are rebuilt from it (menus_apply()). When a menu came, went, was
// renamed or moved, the settings model is made again over the menus as they are now first, every unsaved
// change carried across by the menu's name (settings_remodel()), and then the screen's list of menus, the
// pickers' and the menu settings opened over follow: one now gone gives way to the default menu, which
// closing settings then shows (Review Focus 3). A picker or the folder browser open on the old model's
// slots closes first, as Back would close it. False, with nothing changed in the launcher, when out of
// memory, or when the model holds no menu (the launcher cannot show none): the change stays in the menus
// model alone.
bool settings_menus_changed(void)
{
    if (model == NULL || menu_edit == NULL)
        return false;
    int count = menuedit_count(menu_edit);
    if (count == 0) {
        log_error("Settings: the menus model holds no menu, so the launcher keeps its menus");
        return false;
    }
    size_t room = (size_t) (count > 0 ? count : 1);
    const char **names = calloc(room, sizeof(char*));
    const char **old_names = calloc(room, sizeof(char*));
    Menu **now = calloc(room, sizeof(Menu*));

    // Each menu of the model, the live menu it stands for, and that menu's place and name in the settings
    // model: any menu new, gone, renamed or moved makes the settings model again
    bool remake = count != menu_count;
    int origin_at = -1;
    for (int m = 0; names != NULL && old_names != NULL && m < count; m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *menu = menuedit_menu(menu_edit, m);
        Menu *live = menu_for(menu);
        int was = -1;
        for (int k = 0; live != NULL && k < menu_count && was < 0; k++) {
            if (menus[k] == live)
                was = k;
        }
        names[m] = menu->name;
        old_names[m] = was >= 0 ? menus[was]->name : NULL;
        if (live != NULL && live == origin)
            origin_at = m;
        remake = remake || was != m || strcmp(old_names[m], names[m]) != 0;
    }
    SettingsState *remade = NULL;
    if (names != NULL && old_names != NULL && now != NULL && remake) {
        if (pickers_active())
            pickers_cancel();
        if (browser != NULL)
            close_browser();
        remade = settings_remodel(model, names, old_names, count);
    }
    if (names == NULL || old_names == NULL || now == NULL || (remake && remade == NULL)) {
        free(names);
        free(old_names);
        free(now);
        log_error("Settings: out of memory, so the menus cannot change");
        return false;
    }

    menus_apply(menu_edit);
    if (remade != NULL) {
        int m = 0;
        for (Menu *menu = config.first_menu; menu != NULL && m < count; menu = menu->next)
            now[m++] = menu;
        settings_free(model);
        model = remade;
        free(menus);
        menus = now;
        now = NULL;
        menu_count = count;
        origin = origin_at >= 0 ? menus[origin_at] : default_menu;
        preview_wanted = NULL;
        begin_pickers();
        log_debug("Settings: the menus changed, so their settings were made again over %i menu(s)", count);
    }
    free(now);
    free(names);
    free(old_names);
    return true;
}

#ifdef STREAMFLEX_TEST_HOOKS
// A function only the headless harness builds: remove a submenu with its tiles, as its confirm page does,
// through the first tile that opens it; the reason it could not, or NULL
static const char *test_remove_menu(const char *name)
{
    for (int m = 0; m < menuedit_count(menu_edit); m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *menu = menuedit_menu(menu_edit, m);
        for (int t = 0; t < menu->count; t++) {
            const char *opens = menuedit_submenu_of(&menu->tiles[t]);
            if (opens != NULL && strcmp(opens, name) == 0)
                return menuedit_remove_menu(menu_edit, m, t, true);
        }
    }
    return "No tile opens that menu";
}

// A function only the headless harness builds: add a tile, written title;icon;command, at a menu's end
static const char *test_add_tile(const char *name, char *tile)
{
    int m = menuedit_find(menu_edit, name);
    char *icon = strchr(tile, ';');
    char *command = icon != NULL ? strchr(icon + 1, ';') : NULL;
    if (m < 0)
        return "No such menu";
    if (command == NULL)
        return "The tile is not title;icon;command";
    *icon++ = '\0';
    *command++ = '\0';
    return menuedit_add(menu_edit, m, -1, tile, icon, command);
}

// A function only the headless harness builds: STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT makes one change to the menus
// model as settings open, as the Tiles pages make one, and puts it into the launcher, so a check can
// watch the live rebuild: "remove-menu <name>", "rename-menu <old>=<new>", or
// "add-tile <menu>=<title>;<icon>;<command>"
static void test_menu_edit(void)
{
    const char *given = getenv("STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT");
    if (given == NULL || menu_edit == NULL)
        return;
    char text[256];
    snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%s", given);
    char *name = strchr(text, ' ');
    char *value = name != NULL ? strchr(name, '=') : NULL;
    const char *why = "it is not an edit the hook knows";
    if (name != NULL) {
        *name++ = '\0';
        if (value != NULL)
            *value++ = '\0';
        int m = menuedit_find(menu_edit, name);
        if (strcmp(text, "remove-menu") == 0)
            why = test_remove_menu(name);
        else if (strcmp(text, "rename-menu") == 0 && value != NULL)
            why = m < 0 ? "No such menu" : menuedit_rename_menu(menu_edit, m, value);
        else if (strcmp(text, "add-tile") == 0 && value != NULL)
            why = test_add_tile(name, value);
    }
    if (why == NULL && !settings_menus_changed())
        why = "the settings could not follow it";
    if (why == NULL)
        log_debug("Test hook: the menu edit '%s' was made", given);
    else
        log_debug("Test hook: the menu edit '%s' was refused: %s", given, why);
}
#endif
```

```bash
# The menus as 3c shows and rebuilds them (plan rulings 2 and 5): a section with no lines is a menu of
# its own, shown empty with a note, and the launcher's menus follow the settings' menus model as it
# changes. The Tiles pages that change the model come later; STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT makes one change
# as settings open, so the rebuild is watched now. Nothing here saves: the menus model is written only by
# the Tiles pages' save, so each config that opens settings must come back unchanged.
# Not timing-sensitive: every key waits for its frame, and every result is read from the log's lines and their order, never from a clock

# A header alone ([Kids]) and a section of only a comment ([Notes]) are menus, listed where their sections
# are, though the parser saw no line of either. Kids opens with its note and no highlight, OK there
# selects nothing, Back leaves it, and Main's next tile still runs.
run_keys f80-empty Return Return BackSpace Right Return
ok=1
log=$out/f80-empty.log
[ "$(grep -o '^Menu Name: .*' "$log" | tr '\n' ,)" = "Menu Name: Kids,Menu Name: Main,Menu Name: Notes," ] \
    && grep -A1 '^Menu Name: Kids' "$log" | grep -qx 'Number of Entries: 0' \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Notes' has no lines, so it is shown empty" "$log" \
    && in_range "$log" "Loading menu 'Kids'" "Loading menu 'Main'" "Menu 'Kids' is empty, so it shows the note: This menu is empty. Hold OK to add tiles." \
    && in_range "$log" "Loading menu 'Kids'" "Loading menu 'Main'" "Empty menu note: rendered" \
    && in_range "$log" "Loading menu 'Kids'" "Loading menu 'Main'" "Menu 'Kids' is empty: there is no tile to select" \
    && grep -qx 'Title: Bye' "$log" && ran_clean f80-empty && ok=0
result "menus live: a section with no lines is an empty menu in its place, shown with its note, and Back leaves it (exit $(cat "$out/f80-empty.code"))" $ok
grep -E "^Menu Name|Loading menu|is empty|Empty menu note|^Title:" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# DefaultMenu may name a menu with no lines: StreamFlex starts on it, with its note, where it stopped before
run_quick f80-default-empty
ok=1
log=$out/f80-default-empty.log
grep -q "Loading menu 'Kids'" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Kids' is empty, so it shows the note: This menu is empty. Hold OK to add tiles." "$log" \

    && ! grep -q "Menus: the launcher's menus were made again" "$log" \
    && sed -n '/^Settings closed/,$p' "$log" | grep -qx 'Title: Bye' && ran_clean f80-stray && ok=0
result "menus live: keys before the first section make no menu, and settings open rebuilds nothing (exit $(cat "$out/f80-stray.code"))" $ok
grep -E "^Config:|^Menu Name|Menus:|Settings (opened|closed)|^Title:" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A menu config.ini gained by hand while StreamFlex runs: settings open reads it (the catch-up makes its
# menu, from its section), and the next change keeps that menu, never freeing it and making it again
# (make_menu() gives it the section it was read from, which menu_for() finds it by; Discard's restored
# menus take the same path)
f80_hand_add() { printf '\n[Kids]\nEntry1=Cartoons;apps;:home\n' >> "$cfg"; }
cfg=$(writable_config f80-caught-up)
STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT='add-tile Main=Two;apps;:home' CFG=$cfg run_keys f80-caught-up +f80_hand_add Menu BackSpace Return
ok=1
log=$out/f80-caught-up.log
grep -q "Menus: config.ini's menus are not the launcher's" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Test hook: the menu edit 'add-tile Main=Two;apps;:home' was made" "$log" \
    && [ "$(grep -c "^Menus: 'Kids' is new$" "$log")" = 1 ] && ! grep -q "^Menus: 'Kids' is gone$" "$log" \
    && precedes "$log" "Menus: the launcher's menus were made again from the menus model: 2 menu(s), 1 kept, 1 new, 0 gone" \
                       "Menus: the launcher's menus were made again from the menus model: 2 menu(s), 2 kept, 0 new, 0 gone" \
    && sed -n '/^Settings closed/,$p' "$log" | grep -qx 'Title: Bye' && ran_clean f80-caught-up && ok=0
result "menus live: a menu read by settings open is kept by the next change, not made again (exit $(cat "$out/f80-caught-up.code"))" $ok
grep -E "Menus:|Test hook: the menu edit|Settings (opened|closed)|^Title:" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# Every menu removed from config.ini by hand while StreamFlex runs: the launcher cannot show no menu, so
# settings open says so and keeps the launcher's menus (no catch-up, no rebuild), and Main's tile still runs
f80_hand_empty() { printf '[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n' > "$cfg"; }
cfg=$(writable_config f80-no-menus)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f80-no-menus +f80_hand_empty Menu BackSpace Return
ok=1
log=$out/f80-no-menus.log
grep -q "has no menus now (edited by hand since StreamFlex started), so the launcher keeps its menus, and they cannot be edited" "$log" \
    && ! grep -q "Menus: config.ini's menus are not the launcher's" "$log" \
    && ! grep -q "Menus: the launcher's menus were made again" "$log" \
    && sed -n '/^Settings closed/,$p' "$log" | grep -qx 'Title: Bye' && ran_clean f80-no-menus && ok=0
result "menus live: a config.ini left with no menu by hand keeps the launcher's menus at settings open (exit $(cat "$out/f80-no-menus.code"))" $ok
grep -E "Settings: .*has no menus|Menus:|Settings (opened|closed)|^Title:" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'
```

### Task 5: The keyboard model (`src/osk.c`)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/osk.h`, `src/osk.c`
- Create: `tests/test_osk.c`
- Modify: `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (a block after Task 3's `menuedit` test; `osk.c` in `test_alloc`'s sources, after Task 3's `menuedit.c`)
- Modify: `tests/test_alloc.c` (`#include "osk.h"` after Task 3's `#include "menuedit.h"`; one proof after Task 4's `prove_settings_remodel()`; `main()`)

The launcher does not build `osk.c` yet: Task 12 adds it to `src/CMakeLists.txt` `SOURCES` with its first caller (the keyboard on screen). Task 18 adds it to `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s pure-module list.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `alloc.h`. The tests use Task 3's `menuedit_check_tile()`, `menuedit_check_name()`, `menuedit_load()`, `MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX` as the validators the pages will give (Review Focus 2).
- Produces: `src/osk.h`, exactly the skeleton's Task 5 block (Step 3), plus `#define OSK_SCANCODE_MASK (1u << 30)` (SDL3's `SDLK_SCANCODE_MASK`, which the pure module cannot include; Task 12 checks the two agree with an `SDL_COMPILE_TIME_ASSERT`, as `settings_pickers.c:40-41` does for its key codes). `osk.c` steps through UTF-8 itself: `utf8.h` has no character step (it has `utf8_length`, `utf8_truncate`, `utf8_shorten`), so `osk.c` does not include it.

**Decisions this task makes** (the spec leaves room; each is pinned by a test):
- **Geometry.** Keys have widths in key units, and every row is centered on its page's widest row; Up and Down go to the key whose center is nearest the center of the key left, the left one of two as near; Left and Right wrap within the row; Up from the top row and Down from the bottom row do nothing. Task 12 draws the keys by the same rule. Every page has five rows, the bottom row last, so a page change keeps the highlight on the bottom key pressed.
- **QWERTY:** the number row `1`-`0`, then `q`-`p`, `a`-`l`, `z`-`m`, every key 1 wide. Shift leaves the digits as they are (the ?123 page has the symbols).
- **ABC:** the 7-column alphabetical grid, `a`-`g`, `h`-`n`, `o`-`u`, `v`-`z`, keys 1.5 wide; the last row is filled to seven with `-` and `.`, which titles use often (`ES-DE`, `Dr. Who`), so the grid keeps its columns.
- **?123:** `1`-`0`; `! @ # $ % ^ & * ( )`; `- _ = + [ ] { } ; :`; `' " , . / ? \ | ~ < >`. It is the same over either layout. `;` is there: a command may hold one, and a title's validator refuses it.
- **àé:** exactly the spec's 31, in its order, four rows of 8, 8, 8 and 7: `à á â ä ã å æ ç` / `è é ê ë ì í î ï` / `ñ ò ó ô ö õ ø œ` / `ù ú û ü ý ÿ ß`. Shift gives each capital (Ÿ U+0178, Œ U+0152); `ß` has none.
- **The bottom row**, 12 units: *ABC* (1.5; it names the layout it switches to, *QWERTY* on the ABC layout), *?123* (1.5), *àé* (1), *Shift* (1.5), *Space* (2), *⌫* (1), *◀* (1), *▶* (1), *Done* (1.5). The ?123 and àé keys read *abc* on their own page and go back to the letters; the layout key switches the layout and shows its letters from any page.
- **Shift** cycles off, one-shot, caps lock, off. A one-shot Shift ends when an on-screen key or Space types something; `osk_insert()` (the real keyboard, with a Shift of its own) leaves it as it is.
- **The text.** The cursor starts at the end. `max_bytes` counts bytes; an insert that would pass it changes nothing. A text longer than `max_bytes` to begin with (written by hand) stays whole and can be shortened. `osk_insert()` takes only well-formed UTF-8 with no control character (below U+0020, or U+007F).
- **Back.** With the text as it opened, Back cancels at once, even after typing and deleting back to it; after a change the first Back answers `OSK_ASKED`, a second cancels, and any other command between them ends the question.
- **`osk_key_char()`** refuses exactly what the spec names (a masked keycode, below U+0020, U+007F, U+FFFD), and also what is no character at all: a surrogate, or a value past U+10FFFF. U+0080 to U+009F are not named by the spec, and type.
- **Results.** A highlight move, a cursor move, and a Shift, layout or page change answer `OSK_MOVED`; a change to the text `OSK_CHANGED`; anything refused (a full field, the cursor at an end, Done disabled, Up at the top) `OSK_NONE`.

Create `tests/test_osk.c`:

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "check.h"
#include "osk.h"
#include "menuedit.h"

#define BOTTOM 4                      // The bottom row, on every page
#define ACCENTS "\xC3\xA0\xC3\xA9"    // The accents key's label
#define ERASE "\xE2\x8C\xAB"          // U+232B
#define LEFT "\xE2\x97\x80"           // U+25C0
#define RIGHT "\xE2\x96\xB6"          // U+25B6

// A function to join a row's keys' texts, or their shifted forms, as typing each in turn gives them
static const char *row_text(const Osk *osk, int row, bool shifted)
{
    static char text[128];
    text[0] = '\0';
    for (int c = 0; c < osk_row_length(osk, row); c++) {
        const OskKey *key = osk_key(osk, row, c);
        const char *typed = shifted && key->shifted != NULL ? key->shifted : key->text;
        size_t used = strlen(text);
        snprintf(text + used, sizeof(text) - used, "%s", typed != NULL ? typed : "");
    }
    return text;
}

// A function to join a row's labels, between bars
static const char *row_labels(const Osk *osk, int row)
{
    static char text[128];
    text[0] = '\0';
    for (int c = 0; c < osk_row_length(osk, row); c++) {
        size_t used = strlen(text);
        snprintf(text + used, sizeof(text) - used, c == 0 ? "%s" : "|%s", osk_key(osk, row, c)->label);
    }
    return text;
}

// A function to tell whether the highlight is on a key
static bool highlighted(const Osk *osk, int row, int column)
{
    int r = -1;
    int c = -1;
    osk_highlight(osk, &r, &c);
    return r == row && c == column;
}

// A function to move the highlight to a key with the remote's arrows, as a user would: down to the
// bottom row, up to the key's row, then along it; false when it never got there
static bool go(Osk *osk, int row, int column)
{
    while (osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN) == OSK_MOVED)
        continue;
    int r = 0;
    int c = 0;
    osk_highlight(osk, &r, &c);
    for (; r > row; osk_highlight(osk, &r, &c))
        osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    for (int i = 0; i < 16 && c != column; i++, osk_highlight(osk, &r, &c))
        osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    return highlighted(osk, row, column);
}

// A function to test the QWERTY layout: the number row, three rows of letters, and the bottom row,
// with the highlight starting on q
static void test_qwerty(void)
{
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title for Kodi", "", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK(osk != NULL);
    CHECK_STR(osk_label(osk), "Title for Kodi");
    CHECK_INT(osk_layout(osk), OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_LETTERS);
    CHECK_INT(osk_rows(osk), 5);
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 0, false), "1234567890");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 0, true), "1234567890");             // Shift leaves the digits as they are
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 1, false), "qwertyuiop");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 1, true), "QWERTYUIOP");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 2, false), "asdfghjkl");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, false), "zxcvbnm");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, true), "ZXCVBNM");
    CHECK_STR(row_labels(osk, BOTTOM), "ABC|?123|" ACCENTS "|Shift|Space|" ERASE "|" LEFT "|" RIGHT "|Done");
    static const OskKeyKind kinds[] = { OSK_KEY_LAYOUT, OSK_KEY_SYMBOLS, OSK_KEY_ACCENTS, OSK_KEY_SHIFT, OSK_KEY_SPACE,
                                        OSK_KEY_BACKSPACE, OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT, OSK_KEY_CURSOR_RIGHT, OSK_KEY_DONE };
    CHECK_INT(osk_row_length(osk, BOTTOM), 9);
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++)
        CHECK_INT(osk_key(osk, BOTTOM, i)->kind, kinds[i]);
    CHECK_INT(osk_key(osk, 1, 0)->kind, OSK_KEY_CHAR);
    CHECK(osk_key(osk, BOTTOM, 9) == NULL);
    CHECK(osk_key(osk, 5, 0) == NULL);
    CHECK(osk_key(osk, -1, 0) == NULL);
    CHECK(osk_key(osk, 0, -1) == NULL);
    CHECK_INT(osk_row_length(osk, 5), 0);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 1, 0));                                // On q
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "");
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 0);
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A function to test the other layouts and pages: the ABC grid, ?123 and the accents, each one press
// away on the bottom row, whose keys say where they go
static void test_layouts_and_pages(void)
{
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Name", "", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_ABC);
    CHECK_INT(osk_layout(osk), OSK_ABC);
    CHECK_INT(osk_rows(osk), 5);
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 0, false), "abcdefg");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 1, false), "hijklmn");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 2, false), "opqrstu");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, false), "vwxyz-.");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, true), "VWXYZ-.");
    CHECK_STR(row_labels(osk, BOTTOM), "QWERTY|?123|" ACCENTS "|Shift|Space|" ERASE "|" LEFT "|" RIGHT "|Done");
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 0, 0));                                // On a

    // The layout key: QWERTY's letters, the highlight still on the key
    CHECK(go(osk, BOTTOM, 0));
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_layout(osk), OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_LETTERS);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 0));
    CHECK_STR(osk_key(osk, BOTTOM, 0)->label, "ABC");

    // ?123: digits and symbols, its key reading abc, and pressed again, the letters
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_SYMBOLS);
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 0, false), "1234567890");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 1, false), "!@#$%^&*()");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 2, false), "-_=+[]{};:");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, false), "'\",./?\\|~<>");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, true), "'\",./?\\|~<>");
    CHECK_STR(row_labels(osk, BOTTOM), "ABC|abc|" ACCENTS "|Shift|Space|" ERASE "|" LEFT "|" RIGHT "|Done");
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_LETTERS);
    CHECK_STR(osk_key(osk, BOTTOM, 1)->label, "?123");

    // The accents, from ?123 straight: exactly the spec's 31, in its order, with their capitals
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS);
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 0, false), "\xC3\xA0\xC3\xA1\xC3\xA2\xC3\xA4\xC3\xA3\xC3\xA5\xC3\xA6\xC3\xA7");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 1, false), "\xC3\xA8\xC3\xA9\xC3\xAA\xC3\xAB\xC3\xAC\xC3\xAD\xC3\xAE\xC3\xAF");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 2, false), "\xC3\xB1\xC3\xB2\xC3\xB3\xC3\xB4\xC3\xB6\xC3\xB5\xC3\xB8\xC5\x93");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, false), "\xC3\xB9\xC3\xBA\xC3\xBB\xC3\xBC\xC3\xBD\xC3\xBF\xC3\x9F");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 0, true), "\xC3\x80\xC3\x81\xC3\x82\xC3\x84\xC3\x83\xC3\x85\xC3\x86\xC3\x87");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 1, true), "\xC3\x88\xC3\x89\xC3\x8A\xC3\x8B\xC3\x8C\xC3\x8D\xC3\x8E\xC3\x8F");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 2, true), "\xC3\x91\xC3\x92\xC3\x93\xC3\x94\xC3\x96\xC3\x95\xC3\x98\xC5\x92");
    CHECK_STR(row_text(osk, 3, true), "\xC3\x99\xC3\x9A\xC3\x9B\xC3\x9C\xC3\x9D\xC5\xB8\xC3\x9F");
    CHECK_STR(row_labels(osk, BOTTOM), "ABC|?123|abc|Shift|Space|" ERASE "|" LEFT "|" RIGHT "|Done");

    // The layout key from a page: the other layout's letters
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_layout(osk), OSK_ABC);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_LETTERS);
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A function to test moving the highlight: Up and Down to the nearest key by its center, the left one of
// two as near, across rows of different widths; Left and Right wrapping within a row; nothing past the
// top or the bottom
static void test_moves(void)
{
    // QWERTY, every row centered on the 12-unit bottom row: q at 1.5, a at 2.0, z at 3.0, ?123 at 2.25,
    // the accents key at 3.5, Shift at 4.75, Space at 6.5, the left arrow at 9.0, Done at 11.25
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title", "", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 2, 0));                                // q to a
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 0));                                // z
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 2));                           // The accents key (3.5) is nearer than ?123 (2.25)
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN), OSK_NONE);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 2));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 0));                                // A tie, z (3.0) or x (4.0) from 3.5: the left one
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 2, 1));                                // s (3.0), straight above z
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 1, 1));                                // A tie, w (2.5) or e (3.5): w
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 1, 0));                                // q

    // Along a row, wrapping at either end
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 1, 9));                                // p
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 1, 0));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);

    // Down the right-hand side from p (10.5): l (10.0), m (9.0), the left arrow (9.0)
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 2, 8));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 6));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 6));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 8));                           // Done
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 6));                                // m, the nearest to Done (11.25)
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 6));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 0));                           // The bottom row wraps too

    // From Space (6.5), as near v (6.0) as b (7.0): v; then up the middle to the top, where Up does nothing
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 4));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 3));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 2, 4));                                // g (6.0)
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 1, 4));                                // A tie, t (5.5) or y (6.5): t
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 0, 4));                                // 5
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_UP), OSK_NONE);
    osk_free(osk);

    // The ABC grid, 10.5 units wide on the 12-unit bottom row: . (10.5) is nearer the right arrow (10.0)
    // than Done (11.25), and from Space (6.5), y (6.0) is nearer than z (7.5)
    osk = osk_create("Title", "", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_ABC);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 0));                                // a, h, o, v: one column
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 6));                                // .
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 7));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 3));
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A function to test Shift: one-shot, twice for caps lock, a third time off; ended by typing a key or
// Space, and on the accents page too; left as it is by a real keyboard's text
static void test_shift(void)
{
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title", "", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_CHANGED);            // q
    CHECK(go(osk, BOTTOM, 3));                                   // Shift
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK(osk_shift(osk) && !osk_caps(osk));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, 3, 2));                               // c (5.0), the nearest to Shift (4.75)
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "qC");
    CHECK(!osk_shift(osk));                                      // One shot
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "qCc");

    // Twice: caps lock, until Shift is pressed again
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    CHECK(highlighted(osk, BOTTOM, 3));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK(osk_caps(osk) && !osk_shift(osk));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_UP);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "qCcCC");
    CHECK(osk_caps(osk));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_DOWN);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK(!osk_caps(osk) && !osk_shift(osk));

    // A digit has no capital, and the one-shot ends with it as with any key; Space (the pad's Y) ends it too
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK(go(osk, 0, 0));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "qCcCC1");
    CHECK(!osk_shift(osk));
    CHECK(go(osk, BOTTOM, 3));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_SPACE), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK(!osk_shift(osk));

    // On the accents page: a capital E acute
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_INT(osk_page(osk), OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS);
    CHECK(osk_shift(osk));                                       // A page change is no key typed
    CHECK(go(osk, 1, 1));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "qCcCC1 \xC3\x89");

    // A real keyboard's text leaves the on-screen Shift as it is: that keyboard has its own
    CHECK(go(osk, BOTTOM, 3));
    osk_command(osk, OSK_OK);
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, "x"), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK(osk_shift(osk));
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A function to test editing UTF-8 at the cursor: whole characters at a time, inserted, deleted and
// stepped over, the cursor always on a character's first byte; what is not a character, or is a control
// character, is refused
static void test_editing(void)
{
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title", "Kodi", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 4);                               // At the end
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, "\xC3\xA9"), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "Kodi\xC3\xA9");
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 6);
    CHECK(go(osk, BOTTOM, 6));                                   // The left arrow
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 4);                               // Over e acute's two bytes at once
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, "\xF0\x9F\x98\x80"), OSK_CHANGED);   // U+1F600, four bytes, in the middle
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "Kodi\xF0\x9F\x98\x80\xC3\xA9");
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 8);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE), OSK_CHANGED);     // The pad's X: the whole character
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "Kodi\xC3\xA9");
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 4);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);                                 // The right arrow
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_cursor(osk), 6);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_NONE);               // At the end already
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_LEFT);                                  // The erase key
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "Kodi");
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "");
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_NONE);               // Nothing left to erase
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE), OSK_NONE);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT);                                 // The left arrow
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_NONE);

    // Not inserted: nothing; a lone lead or continuation byte; a control character; U+007F; a surrogate;
    // an overlong form; past U+10FFFF
    static const char *const bad[] = { "", "\xC3", "\x80", "a\tb", "\x7F", "\xED\xA0\x80", "\xC0\xAF", "\xF4\x90\x80\x80" };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(bad) / sizeof(bad[0]); i++)
        CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, bad[i]), OSK_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, NULL), OSK_NONE);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "");
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A function to test the field's byte limit: an insert past it changes nothing, from a key or Space or a
// real keyboard; a text longer than the limit to begin with stays whole and can be shortened
static void test_limit(void)
{
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title", "abcd", 5, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, "\xC3\xA9"), OSK_NONE);           // 4 + 2 > 5
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, "e"), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_NONE);               // q: full
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_SPACE), OSK_NONE);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "abcde");
    osk_free(osk);

    osk = osk_create("Title", "abcdefgh", 5, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "abcdefgh");
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, "x"), OSK_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "abcdefg");
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A tile's other parts, for its title's validator, as the tile's page gives them
typedef struct {
    const char *icon;
    const char *command;
} TileParts;

// The title field's validator: the tile's rules, with its other parts
static const char *check_title(const char *text, void *context)
{
    const TileParts *parts = context;
    return menuedit_check_tile(text, parts->icon, parts->command);
}

// A new submenu's name field's validator
static const char *check_name(const char *text, void *context)
{
    return menuedit_check_name(context, text, -1);
}

// A function to erase every character before the cursor
static void erase_all(Osk *osk)
{
    while (osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE) == OSK_CHANGED)
        continue;
}

// A function to test the validators the fields are given (Review Focus 2): Done is disabled while one
// says why, by its key, the pad's Start and Enter alike, and enabled again once the text is fixed
static void test_validators(void)
{
    TileParts parts = { "kodi", "kodi" };
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title for Kodi", "Kodi", MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX, check_title, &parts, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK(osk_why(osk) == NULL);
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, ";"), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "A title can't contain ;");
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_DONE), OSK_NONE);             // The pad's Start, and Enter
    CHECK(go(osk, BOTTOM, 8));
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_NONE);               // The Done key
    osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE);
    CHECK_INT(osk_insert(osk, " "), OSK_CHANGED);
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "A title can't start or end with a space");   // "Kodi ;" would begin a comment
    osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE);
    CHECK(osk_why(osk) == NULL);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_OK), OSK_FINISHED);
    erase_all(osk);
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "Type a title");
    osk_free(osk);

    // The title fits the field, but not the line beside the command: Entry99999= and Kodi;kodi; and 178
    // bytes of command are 199
    char command[200];
    memset(command, 'c', 178);
    command[178] = '\0';
    parts.command = command;
    osk = osk_create("Title for Kodi", "Kodi", MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX, check_title, &parts, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK(osk_why(osk) == NULL);
    osk_insert(osk, "x");
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "It's too long for one line of config.ini (199 bytes)");
    osk_free(osk);

    // A new submenu's name: an existing menu in another case, a reserved name, ']', and 50 bytes
    static const char *const text = "[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n[Main]\nEntry1=Games;games;:submenu Games\n"
                                    "[Games]\nEntry1=Retro;retro;retroarch\n";
    IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, strlen(text));
    MenuEdit *edit = menuedit_load(doc, "Main");
    inidoc_free(doc);
    CHECK(edit != NULL);
    osk = osk_create("Name of the new submenu", "", 64, check_name, edit, OSK_ABC);
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "Type a name");
    osk_insert(osk, "games");
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "There's already a menu with that name");
    erase_all(osk);
    osk_insert(osk, "Clock");
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "That name is kept for settings");
    erase_all(osk);
    osk_insert(osk, "Kids]");
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "A name can't contain ]");
    erase_all(osk);
    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++)
        osk_insert(osk, "K");
    CHECK_STR(osk_why(osk), "A name can be 49 bytes at most");
    erase_all(osk);
    osk_insert(osk, "Kids");
    CHECK(osk_why(osk) == NULL);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_DONE), OSK_FINISHED);
    osk_free(osk);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}

// A function to test Back: with the text as it opened it cancels at once; after a change it asks first,
// and the second Back cancels; anything else between ends the question, and a text changed back to how
// it opened cancels at once again
static void test_back(void)
{
    Osk *osk = osk_create("Title", "Kodi", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    CHECK(!osk_asking(osk));
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACK), OSK_CANCELED);
    osk_free(osk);

    osk = osk_create("Title", "Kodi", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    osk_insert(osk, "x");
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACK), OSK_ASKED);
    CHECK(osk_asking(osk));
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACK), OSK_CANCELED);
    osk_free(osk);

    osk = osk_create("Title", "Kodi", 64, NULL, NULL, OSK_QWERTY);
    osk_insert(osk, "x");
    osk_command(osk, OSK_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_RIGHT), OSK_MOVED);
    CHECK(!osk_asking(osk));
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACK), OSK_ASKED);
    osk_command(osk, OSK_BACKSPACE);
    CHECK(!osk_asking(osk));
    CHECK_STR(osk_text(osk), "Kodi");
    CHECK_INT(osk_command(osk, OSK_BACK), OSK_CANCELED);
    osk_free(osk);
}

// A function to test the real-keyboard rule (Review Focus 5): a key's character, with Shift, Caps Lock
// and AltGr already applied by SDL_GetKeyFromScancode(), as UTF-8; nothing for a key that types nothing
static void test_key_char(void)
{
    char out[5];
    CHECK(osk_key_char('a', out));
    CHECK_STR(out, "a");
    CHECK(osk_key_char('A', out));
    CHECK_STR(out, "A");
    CHECK(osk_key_char(' ', out));
    CHECK_STR(out, " ");
    CHECK(osk_key_char('^', out));                               // A dead key types its own character
    CHECK_STR(out, "^");
    CHECK(osk_key_char(0xE9, out));                              // e acute, on a French keyboard
    CHECK_STR(out, "\xC3\xA9");
    CHECK(osk_key_char(0xDF, out));                              // sharp s, on a German one
    CHECK_STR(out, "\xC3\x9F");
    CHECK(osk_key_char(0x20AC, out));                            // The euro sign, AltGr+E there
    CHECK_STR(out, "\xE2\x82\xAC");
    CHECK(osk_key_char(0x3B1, out));                             // Greek alpha
    CHECK_STR(out, "\xCE\xB1");
    CHECK(osk_key_char(0x1F600, out));
    CHECK_STR(out, "\xF0\x9F\x98\x80");

    // Nothing: SDLK_LEFT and SDLK_F1 (masked), the mask alone, Enter, Backspace, Tab, Esc, NUL, U+001F,
    // Delete (U+007F), SDL's U+FFFD for a key that types several code points, surrogates, past U+10FFFF
    static const unsigned int nothing[] = { 0x40000050, 0x4000003A, OSK_SCANCODE_MASK, 0x0D, 0x08, 0x09, 0x1B, 0x00,
                                            0x1F, 0x7F, 0xFFFD, 0xD800, 0xDFFF, 0x110000 };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(nothing) / sizeof(nothing[0]); i++) {
        CHECK(!osk_key_char(nothing[i], out));
        CHECK_STR(out, "");
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    test_qwerty();
    test_layouts_and_pages();
    test_moves();
    test_shift();
    test_editing();
    test_limit();
    test_validators();
    test_back();
    test_key_char();
    return check_report();
}
```

```c
// The on-screen keyboard's model (spec "The on-screen keyboard"): its layouts as data tables, which the
// overlay's keyboard can reuse; the highlight's moves between keys; Shift and caps lock; and the text it
// edits, UTF-8 with the cursor on character boundaries, held to a byte limit and to a validator that says
// why Done is disabled. Also the rule a real keyboard's key types by. settings_pickers.c draws it.
// Pure: no SDL, no globals; memory comes from alloc.h.
#ifndef OSK_H
#define OSK_H

#include <stdbool.h>

// SDL3's SDLK_SCANCODE_MASK: a keycode with it set names a key that types nothing (an arrow, F1)
#define OSK_SCANCODE_MASK (1u << 30)

typedef enum { OSK_QWERTY, OSK_ABC } OskLayout;   // The remembered choice; ?123 and àé are pages over either
typedef enum { OSK_PAGE_LETTERS, OSK_PAGE_SYMBOLS, OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS } OskPage;
typedef enum {
    OSK_KEY_CHAR, OSK_KEY_LAYOUT, OSK_KEY_SYMBOLS, OSK_KEY_ACCENTS, OSK_KEY_SHIFT, OSK_KEY_SPACE,
    OSK_KEY_BACKSPACE, OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT, OSK_KEY_CURSOR_RIGHT, OSK_KEY_DONE
} OskKeyKind;
// A key `width` units wide. A row's keys sit end to end, and every row is centered on its page's widest:
// Up and Down go to the key whose center is nearest, the left one of two as near, and the keys are drawn
// where that puts them. `text` is what a character key types, `shifted` what it types with Shift or caps
// lock (NULL: the same); `label` is what the key shows.
typedef struct { OskKeyKind kind; const char *label; const char *text; const char *shifted; float width; } OskKey;
typedef enum { OSK_UP, OSK_DOWN, OSK_LEFT, OSK_RIGHT, OSK_OK, OSK_BACK, OSK_BACKSPACE, OSK_SPACE, OSK_DONE } OskCommand;
typedef enum { OSK_NONE, OSK_MOVED, OSK_CHANGED, OSK_FINISHED, OSK_CANCELED, OSK_ASKED } OskResult;   // ASKED: "Back again to discard"
typedef const char *(*OskCheck)(const char *text, void *context);   // Why Done is disabled, or NULL

typedef struct Osk Osk;
Osk *osk_create(const char *label, const char *initial, int max_bytes, OskCheck check, void *context, OskLayout layout);
void osk_free(Osk *osk);
OskResult osk_command(Osk *osk, OskCommand command);
OskResult osk_insert(Osk *osk, const char *utf8);
bool osk_key_char(unsigned int keycode, char out[5]);   // The real-keyboard rule: false for masked, control, U+007F, U+FFFD
const char *osk_text(const Osk *osk);
int osk_cursor(const Osk *osk);                          // A byte offset on a character boundary
const char *osk_label(const Osk *osk);
const char *osk_why(const Osk *osk);                     // NULL when Done is enabled
OskLayout osk_layout(const Osk *osk);
OskPage osk_page(const Osk *osk);
bool osk_shift(const Osk *osk);
bool osk_caps(const Osk *osk);
int osk_rows(const Osk *osk);
int osk_row_length(const Osk *osk, int row);
const OskKey *osk_key(const Osk *osk, int row, int column);   // NULL off the page; good until the next command
void osk_highlight(const Osk *osk, int *row, int *column);
bool osk_asking(const Osk *osk);                         // "Back again to discard" is showing

#endif
```

The comment on `OskLayout` holds the skeleton's `àé`: the header is UTF-8, as every source is. If cl 19.44 or 19.51 warns C4819 on it (Step 6), write `?123 and the accents` instead, in the header only.

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "osk.h"
#include "alloc.h"

#define BOTTOM_ROW 4                   // Every page has four rows of characters, then the bottom row
#define BOTTOM_KEYS 9
#define KEY(text, shifted) { OSK_KEY_CHAR, text, text, shifted, 1.0F }
#define WIDE(text, shifted) { OSK_KEY_CHAR, text, text, shifted, 1.5F }   // The ABC grid's: seven fill its row
#define ROW(keys) { keys, (int) (sizeof(keys) / sizeof(keys[0])) }
#define LETTERS_LABEL "abc"            // The ?123 and accents keys on their own page: back to the letters
#define ACCENTS_LABEL "\xC3\xA0\xC3\xA9"   // a grave, e acute
#define BACKSPACE_LABEL "\xE2\x8C\xAB"     // U+232B, erase to the left
#define LEFT_LABEL "\xE2\x97\x80"          // U+25C0, the text cursor left
#define RIGHT_LABEL "\xE2\x96\xB6"         // U+25B6, the text cursor right

// A row of a page's keys
typedef struct {
    const OskKey *keys;
    int count;
} OskRow;

static const OskKey DIGITS[] = { KEY("1", NULL), KEY("2", NULL), KEY("3", NULL), KEY("4", NULL), KEY("5", NULL),
    KEY("6", NULL), KEY("7", NULL), KEY("8", NULL), KEY("9", NULL), KEY("0", NULL) };
static const OskKey QWERTY_TOP[] = { KEY("q", "Q"), KEY("w", "W"), KEY("e", "E"), KEY("r", "R"), KEY("t", "T"),
    KEY("y", "Y"), KEY("u", "U"), KEY("i", "I"), KEY("o", "O"), KEY("p", "P") };
static const OskKey QWERTY_MIDDLE[] = { KEY("a", "A"), KEY("s", "S"), KEY("d", "D"), KEY("f", "F"), KEY("g", "G"),
    KEY("h", "H"), KEY("j", "J"), KEY("k", "K"), KEY("l", "L") };
static const OskKey QWERTY_LOW[] = { KEY("z", "Z"), KEY("x", "X"), KEY("c", "C"), KEY("v", "V"), KEY("b", "B"),
    KEY("n", "N"), KEY("m", "M") };

static const OskKey ABC_1[] = { WIDE("a", "A"), WIDE("b", "B"), WIDE("c", "C"), WIDE("d", "D"), WIDE("e", "E"),
    WIDE("f", "F"), WIDE("g", "G") };
static const OskKey ABC_2[] = { WIDE("h", "H"), WIDE("i", "I"), WIDE("j", "J"), WIDE("k", "K"), WIDE("l", "L"),
    WIDE("m", "M"), WIDE("n", "N") };
static const OskKey ABC_3[] = { WIDE("o", "O"), WIDE("p", "P"), WIDE("q", "Q"), WIDE("r", "R"), WIDE("s", "S"),
    WIDE("t", "T"), WIDE("u", "U") };
static const OskKey ABC_4[] = { WIDE("v", "V"), WIDE("w", "W"), WIDE("x", "X"), WIDE("y", "Y"), WIDE("z", "Z"),
    WIDE("-", NULL), WIDE(".", NULL) };

static const OskKey SYMBOLS_1[] = { KEY("!", NULL), KEY("@", NULL), KEY("#", NULL), KEY("$", NULL), KEY("%", NULL),
    KEY("^", NULL), KEY("&", NULL), KEY("*", NULL), KEY("(", NULL), KEY(")", NULL) };
static const OskKey SYMBOLS_2[] = { KEY("-", NULL), KEY("_", NULL), KEY("=", NULL), KEY("+", NULL), KEY("[", NULL),
    KEY("]", NULL), KEY("{", NULL), KEY("}", NULL), KEY(";", NULL), KEY(":", NULL) };
static const OskKey SYMBOLS_3[] = { KEY("'", NULL), KEY("\"", NULL), KEY(",", NULL), KEY(".", NULL), KEY("/", NULL),
    KEY("?", NULL), KEY("\\", NULL), KEY("|", NULL), KEY("~", NULL), KEY("<", NULL), KEY(">", NULL) };

// The accents page (spec): the a's and c cedilla; the e's and i's; n tilde, the o's and the oe ligature;
// the u's, the y's and sharp s, which has no capital
static const OskKey ACCENTS_1[] = { KEY("\xC3\xA0", "\xC3\x80"), KEY("\xC3\xA1", "\xC3\x81"), KEY("\xC3\xA2", "\xC3\x82"),
    KEY("\xC3\xA4", "\xC3\x84"), KEY("\xC3\xA3", "\xC3\x83"), KEY("\xC3\xA5", "\xC3\x85"), KEY("\xC3\xA6", "\xC3\x86"),
    KEY("\xC3\xA7", "\xC3\x87") };
static const OskKey ACCENTS_2[] = { KEY("\xC3\xA8", "\xC3\x88"), KEY("\xC3\xA9", "\xC3\x89"), KEY("\xC3\xAA", "\xC3\x8A"),
    KEY("\xC3\xAB", "\xC3\x8B"), KEY("\xC3\xAC", "\xC3\x8C"), KEY("\xC3\xAD", "\xC3\x8D"), KEY("\xC3\xAE", "\xC3\x8E"),
    KEY("\xC3\xAF", "\xC3\x8F") };
static const OskKey ACCENTS_3[] = { KEY("\xC3\xB1", "\xC3\x91"), KEY("\xC3\xB2", "\xC3\x92"), KEY("\xC3\xB3", "\xC3\x93"),
    KEY("\xC3\xB4", "\xC3\x94"), KEY("\xC3\xB6", "\xC3\x96"), KEY("\xC3\xB5", "\xC3\x95"), KEY("\xC3\xB8", "\xC3\x98"),
    KEY("\xC5\x93", "\xC5\x92") };
static const OskKey ACCENTS_4[] = { KEY("\xC3\xB9", "\xC3\x99"), KEY("\xC3\xBA", "\xC3\x9A"), KEY("\xC3\xBB", "\xC3\x9B"),
    KEY("\xC3\xBC", "\xC3\x9C"), KEY("\xC3\xBD", "\xC3\x9D"), KEY("\xC3\xBF", "\xC5\xB8"), KEY("\xC3\x9F", NULL) };

static const OskRow QWERTY_ROWS[BOTTOM_ROW] = { ROW(DIGITS), ROW(QWERTY_TOP), ROW(QWERTY_MIDDLE), ROW(QWERTY_LOW) };
static const OskRow ABC_ROWS[BOTTOM_ROW] = { ROW(ABC_1), ROW(ABC_2), ROW(ABC_3), ROW(ABC_4) };
static const OskRow SYMBOL_ROWS[BOTTOM_ROW] = { ROW(DIGITS), ROW(SYMBOLS_1), ROW(SYMBOLS_2), ROW(SYMBOLS_3) };
static const OskRow ACCENT_ROWS[BOTTOM_ROW] = { ROW(ACCENTS_1), ROW(ACCENTS_2), ROW(ACCENTS_3), ROW(ACCENTS_4) };

// The bottom row, every page's; label_bottom() labels its first three keys for the layout and the page
static const OskKey BOTTOM[BOTTOM_KEYS] = {
    { OSK_KEY_LAYOUT, "ABC", NULL, NULL, 1.5F },
    { OSK_KEY_SYMBOLS, "?123", NULL, NULL, 1.5F },
    { OSK_KEY_ACCENTS, ACCENTS_LABEL, NULL, NULL, 1.0F },
    { OSK_KEY_SHIFT, "Shift", NULL, NULL, 1.5F },
    { OSK_KEY_SPACE, "Space", " ", NULL, 2.0F },
    { OSK_KEY_BACKSPACE, BACKSPACE_LABEL, NULL, NULL, 1.0F },
    { OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT, LEFT_LABEL, NULL, NULL, 1.0F },
    { OSK_KEY_CURSOR_RIGHT, RIGHT_LABEL, NULL, NULL, 1.0F },
    { OSK_KEY_DONE, "Done", NULL, NULL, 1.5F }
};

struct Osk {
    char *label;
    char *initial;              // The text it opened with: Back cancels at once while the text is that again
    char *text;                 // Room for max_bytes, or for the text it opened with when that is longer
    size_t max_bytes;
    size_t cursor;              // A byte offset on a character's first byte, or the end
    OskCheck check;
    void *context;
    OskLayout layout;
    OskPage page;
    bool shift;                 // One-shot: the next key typed is shifted, then it goes off
    bool caps;                  // Caps lock: every key typed is shifted until Shift is pressed again
    bool asking;                // "Back again to discard" is showing
    int row;                    // The highlighted key
    int column;
    OskKey bottom[BOTTOM_KEYS]; // The bottom row, labeled for the layout and the page on show
};

// A function to label the bottom row for the layout and the page on show: the layout key names the layout
// it switches to, and the ?123 and accents keys read "abc" on their own page, where they go back to the
// letters
static void label_bottom(Osk *osk)
{
    memcpy(osk->bottom, BOTTOM, sizeof(BOTTOM));
    osk->bottom[0].label = osk->layout == OSK_QWERTY ? "ABC" : "QWERTY";
    osk->bottom[1].label = osk->page == OSK_PAGE_SYMBOLS ? LETTERS_LABEL : "?123";
    osk->bottom[2].label = osk->page == OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS ? LETTERS_LABEL : ACCENTS_LABEL;
}

// A function to give a row of the page on show
static OskRow row_of(const Osk *osk, int row)
{
    if (row == BOTTOM_ROW)
        return (OskRow) { osk->bottom, BOTTOM_KEYS };
    const OskRow *rows = osk->page == OSK_PAGE_SYMBOLS ? SYMBOL_ROWS
                       : osk->page == OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS ? ACCENT_ROWS
                       : osk->layout == OSK_ABC ? ABC_ROWS : QWERTY_ROWS;
    return rows[row];
}

// A function to measure a row: its keys' widths, end to end
static float row_width(OskRow row)
{
    float width = 0.0F;
    for (int c = 0; c < row.count; c++)
        width += row.keys[c].width;
    return width;
}

// A function to find a key's center, in key widths from the keyboard's left edge: every row is centered
// on the page's widest
static float key_center(const Osk *osk, int row, int column)
{
    float widest = 0.0F;
    for (int r = 0; r <= BOTTOM_ROW; r++) {
        float width = row_width(row_of(osk, r));
        if (width > widest)
            widest = width;
    }
    OskRow keys = row_of(osk, row);
    float x = (widest - row_width(keys)) / 2.0F;
    for (int c = 0; c < column; c++)
        x += keys.keys[c].width;
    return x + keys.keys[column].width / 2.0F;
}

// A function to find the key in a row whose center is nearest a point; the left one of two as near
static int nearest(const Osk *osk, int row, float x)
{
    int best = 0;
    float best_distance = 0.0F;
    for (int c = 0; c < row_of(osk, row).count; c++) {
        float distance = key_center(osk, row, c) - x;
        if (distance < 0.0F)
            distance = -distance;
        if (c == 0 || distance < best_distance) {
            best = c;
            best_distance = distance;
        }
    }
    return best;
}

// A function to tell a byte that continues a UTF-8 character
static bool continues(char c)
{
    return ((unsigned char) c & 0xC0) == 0x80;
}

// A function to step back from a byte offset to the first byte of the character before it
static size_t previous_character(const char *text, size_t at)
{
    do {
        at--;
    } while (at > 0 && continues(text[at]));
    return at;
}

// A function to step from a byte offset past the character there
static size_t next_character(const char *text, size_t at)
{
    do {
        at++;
    } while (text[at] != '\0' && continues(text[at]));
    return at;
}

// A function to tell whether a text is UTF-8 that types something: well formed (no stray continuation
// byte, no character cut short, overlong, a surrogate or past U+10FFFF) and with no control character
static bool typeable(const char *text)
{
    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *) text;
    if (*p == '\0')
        return false;
    while (*p != '\0') {
        unsigned int c = *p;
        int more = c < 0x80 ? 0 : c >= 0xC2 && c <= 0xDF ? 1 : c >= 0xE0 && c <= 0xEF ? 2 : c >= 0xF0 && c <= 0xF4 ? 3 : -1;
        if (more < 0 || c < 0x20 || c == 0x7F)
            return false;
        unsigned int code = more == 0 ? c : c & (0x3Fu >> more);
        p++;
        for (int i = 0; i < more; i++, p++) {
            if ((*p & 0xC0) != 0x80)
                return false;
            code = (code << 6) | (*p & 0x3Fu);
        }
        if ((more == 2 && (code < 0x800 || (code >= 0xD800 && code <= 0xDFFF))) ||
            (more == 3 && (code < 0x10000 || code > 0x10FFFF)))
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to put text in at the cursor, the cursor after it; false, with nothing changed, when the
// field would hold more than its limit
static bool insert(Osk *osk, const char *text, size_t length)
{
    size_t used = strlen(osk->text);
    if (length == 0 || used + length > osk->max_bytes)
        return false;
    memmove(osk->text + osk->cursor + length, osk->text + osk->cursor, used - osk->cursor + 1);
    memcpy(osk->text + osk->cursor, text, length);
    osk->cursor += length;
    return true;
}

// A function to take out the character before the cursor, all of it; false at the start
static bool delete_before(Osk *osk)
{
    if (osk->cursor == 0)
        return false;
    size_t start = previous_character(osk->text, osk->cursor);
    memmove(osk->text + start, osk->text + osk->cursor, strlen(osk->text + osk->cursor) + 1);
    osk->cursor = start;
    return true;
}

// A function to move the cursor a character left (direction -1) or right; false at either end
static bool step_cursor(Osk *osk, int direction)
{
    if (direction < 0 ? osk->cursor == 0 : osk->text[osk->cursor] == '\0')
        return false;
    osk->cursor = direction < 0 ? previous_character(osk->text, osk->cursor) : next_character(osk->text, osk->cursor);
    return true;
}

// A function to type text at the cursor as the keyboard's own keys type it: a one-shot Shift ends once
// something is typed
static OskResult type(Osk *osk, const char *text)
{
    if (!insert(osk, text, strlen(text)))
        return OSK_NONE;
    osk->shift = false;
    return OSK_CHANGED;
}

// A function to finish, when the validator lets Done: nothing while it says why not
static OskResult finish(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk_why(osk) == NULL ? OSK_FINISHED : OSK_NONE;
}

// A function to answer Back: with the text as it opened, it cancels at once; after a change, the first
// Back asks ("Back again to discard"), and a second, with nothing between, cancels
static OskResult back(Osk *osk)
{
    if (strcmp(osk->text, osk->initial) == 0 || osk->asking) {
        osk->asking = false;
        return OSK_CANCELED;
    }
    osk->asking = true;
    return OSK_ASKED;
}

// A function to move the highlight a row up (-1) or down, to the key nearest the one it leaves; there is
// no row past the top or the bottom
static OskResult move_row(Osk *osk, int direction)
{
    int to = osk->row + direction;
    if (to < 0 || to > BOTTOM_ROW)
        return OSK_NONE;
    osk->column = nearest(osk, to, key_center(osk, osk->row, osk->column));
    osk->row = to;
    return OSK_MOVED;
}

// A function to press a key, as OK on the highlighted one does
static OskResult press(Osk *osk, const OskKey *key)
{
    switch (key->kind) {
        case OSK_KEY_CHAR:
            return type(osk, (osk->shift || osk->caps) && key->shifted != NULL ? key->shifted : key->text);
        case OSK_KEY_SPACE:
            return type(osk, " ");
        case OSK_KEY_BACKSPACE:
            return delete_before(osk) ? OSK_CHANGED : OSK_NONE;
        case OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT:
            return step_cursor(osk, -1) ? OSK_MOVED : OSK_NONE;
        case OSK_KEY_CURSOR_RIGHT:
            return step_cursor(osk, 1) ? OSK_MOVED : OSK_NONE;
        case OSK_KEY_DONE:
            return finish(osk);
        case OSK_KEY_SHIFT:
            // Off, then one-shot, then caps lock, then off again
            if (osk->caps)
                osk->caps = false;
            else if (osk->shift) {
                osk->shift = false;
                osk->caps = true;
            }
            else
                osk->shift = true;
            return OSK_MOVED;
        case OSK_KEY_LAYOUT:
            osk->layout = osk->layout == OSK_QWERTY ? OSK_ABC : OSK_QWERTY;
            osk->page = OSK_PAGE_LETTERS;
            break;
        case OSK_KEY_SYMBOLS:
            osk->page = osk->page == OSK_PAGE_SYMBOLS ? OSK_PAGE_LETTERS : OSK_PAGE_SYMBOLS;
            break;
        case OSK_KEY_ACCENTS:
            osk->page = osk->page == OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS ? OSK_PAGE_LETTERS : OSK_PAGE_ACCENTS;
            break;
    }

    // Another layout or page: the bottom row is labeled again, and the highlight stays on its key
    label_bottom(osk);
    int length = row_of(osk, osk->row).count;
    if (osk->column >= length)
        osk->column = length - 1;
    return OSK_MOVED;
}

// A function to open the keyboard on a field: its label, the text it holds, its limit in bytes (a longer
// text, written by hand, is kept whole and can be shortened), and its validator (NULL: Done is always
// enabled) with what it needs. The cursor starts at the end, the highlight on the first letter.
Osk *osk_create(const char *label, const char *initial, int max_bytes, OskCheck check, void *context, OskLayout layout)
{
    if (label == NULL)
        label = "";
    if (initial == NULL)
        initial = "";
    Osk *osk = alloc_calloc(1, sizeof(Osk));
    if (osk == NULL)
        return NULL;
    size_t length = strlen(initial);
    osk->max_bytes = max_bytes > 0 ? (size_t) max_bytes : 0;
    osk->label = alloc_strdup(label);
    osk->initial = alloc_strdup(initial);
    osk->text = alloc_malloc((length > osk->max_bytes ? length : osk->max_bytes) + 1);
    if (osk->label == NULL || osk->initial == NULL || osk->text == NULL) {
        osk_free(osk);
        return NULL;
    }
    memcpy(osk->text, initial, length + 1);
    osk->cursor = length;
    osk->check = check;
    osk->context = context;
    osk->layout = layout == OSK_ABC ? OSK_ABC : OSK_QWERTY;
    osk->page = OSK_PAGE_LETTERS;
    osk->row = osk->layout == OSK_QWERTY ? 1 : 0;   // q, or a
    osk->column = 0;
    label_bottom(osk);
    return osk;
}

// A function to free the keyboard
void osk_free(Osk *osk)
{
    if (osk == NULL)
        return;
    alloc_free(osk->label);
    alloc_free(osk->initial);
    alloc_free(osk->text);
    alloc_free(osk);
}

// A function to act on a command: the remote's arrows, OK and Back, and the pad's shortcuts, X for
// backspace, Y for space and Start for Done (Enter on a real keyboard is Done too)
OskResult osk_command(Osk *osk, OskCommand command)
{
    if (command != OSK_BACK)
        osk->asking = false;
    switch (command) {
        case OSK_UP:
            return move_row(osk, -1);
        case OSK_DOWN:
            return move_row(osk, 1);
        case OSK_LEFT:
        case OSK_RIGHT: {
            int length = row_of(osk, osk->row).count;
            osk->column = (osk->column + (command == OSK_RIGHT ? 1 : length - 1)) % length;
            return OSK_MOVED;
        }
        case OSK_OK:
            return press(osk, &row_of(osk, osk->row).keys[osk->column]);
        case OSK_BACK:
            return back(osk);
        case OSK_BACKSPACE:
            return delete_before(osk) ? OSK_CHANGED : OSK_NONE;
        case OSK_SPACE:
            return type(osk, " ");
        case OSK_DONE:
            return finish(osk);
    }
    return OSK_NONE;
}

// A function to put in what a real keyboard's key typed (osk_key_char()), at the cursor: only UTF-8 that
// types something, and only within the limit. An on-screen Shift stays as it is: that keyboard has its own.
OskResult osk_insert(Osk *osk, const char *utf8)
{
    osk->asking = false;
    if (utf8 == NULL || !typeable(utf8))
        return OSK_NONE;
    return insert(osk, utf8, strlen(utf8)) ? OSK_CHANGED : OSK_NONE;
}

// A function to give the character a real keyboard's key types, as UTF-8 in `out` (spec, "A real keyboard
// types into the field"): `keycode` is SDL_GetKeyFromScancode()'s, with Shift, Caps Lock and AltGr applied.
// False, with `out` empty, for a key that types nothing: a keycode with SDLK_SCANCODE_MASK set, a control
// character below U+0020, U+007F, U+FFFD (SDL's keycode for a key that types several code points), and
// what is no character at all (a surrogate, or past U+10FFFF).
bool osk_key_char(unsigned int keycode, char out[5])
{
    out[0] = '\0';
    if ((keycode & OSK_SCANCODE_MASK) != 0 || keycode < 0x20 || keycode == 0x7F || keycode == 0xFFFD ||
        (keycode >= 0xD800 && keycode <= 0xDFFF) || keycode > 0x10FFFF)
        return false;
    if (keycode < 0x80) {
        out[0] = (char) keycode;
        out[1] = '\0';
    }
    else if (keycode < 0x800) {
        out[0] = (char) (0xC0 | (keycode >> 6));
        out[1] = (char) (0x80 | (keycode & 0x3F));
        out[2] = '\0';
    }
    else if (keycode < 0x10000) {
        out[0] = (char) (0xE0 | (keycode >> 12));
        out[1] = (char) (0x80 | ((keycode >> 6) & 0x3F));
        out[2] = (char) (0x80 | (keycode & 0x3F));
        out[3] = '\0';
    }
    else {
        out[0] = (char) (0xF0 | (keycode >> 18));
        out[1] = (char) (0x80 | ((keycode >> 12) & 0x3F));
        out[2] = (char) (0x80 | ((keycode >> 6) & 0x3F));
        out[3] = (char) (0x80 | (keycode & 0x3F));
        out[4] = '\0';
    }
    return true;
}

const char *osk_text(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->text;
}

int osk_cursor(const Osk *osk)
{
    return (int) osk->cursor;
}

const char *osk_label(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->label;
}

// A function to say why Done is disabled: the validator's reason for the text now, or NULL
const char *osk_why(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->check != NULL ? osk->check(osk->text, osk->context) : NULL;
}

OskLayout osk_layout(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->layout;
}

OskPage osk_page(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->page;
}

bool osk_shift(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->shift;
}

bool osk_caps(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->caps;
}

int osk_rows(const Osk *osk)
{
    (void) osk;
    return BOTTOM_ROW + 1;
}

int osk_row_length(const Osk *osk, int row)
{
    return row >= 0 && row <= BOTTOM_ROW ? row_of(osk, row).count : 0;
}

const OskKey *osk_key(const Osk *osk, int row, int column)
{
    if (row < 0 || row > BOTTOM_ROW)
        return NULL;
    OskRow keys = row_of(osk, row);
    return column >= 0 && column < keys.count ? &keys.keys[column] : NULL;
}

void osk_highlight(const Osk *osk, int *row, int *column)
{
    *row = osk->row;
    *column = osk->column;
}

bool osk_asking(const Osk *osk)
{
    return osk->asking;
}
```
