The launcher builds `iconmatch.c` from this task on (fix pass R7): Step 4 adds it to `src/CMakeLists.txt` `SOURCES` where it is written, so Task 10b's app list, its first caller, and Task 13b's Icon page find it linked. Until then nothing calls it; its functions are public, so no compiler warns. Task 18 adds it to `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s pure-module list.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `library_load()` and its manifest; `libtools.read_sections()`, `libtools.BRANDS_INI` in Python.
- Produces, exactly the skeleton's Task 6 block, plus `#define ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX 256` (the most of a name compared):
  ```c
  typedef struct { const char *name; const char *title; const char *group; const char *const *match; int match_count; } LibraryInfo;
  int library_count(void);
  const LibraryInfo *library_info(int index);   // Manifest order
  void iconmatch_normalize(const char *name, char *out, size_t size);   // Lower case, no punctuation, vendor words dropped
  int iconmatch_find(const char *app_name, const LibraryInfo *icons, int count);   // Index, or -1
  ```
  `library_info(0)` is the first of `library_count()` entries in one array, so `iconmatch_find(name, library_info(0), library_count())` searches the library, as Tasks 10b and 13b call it.

**Decisions this task makes** (each pinned by a test):
- **What the library lists:** the icons `library_load()` kept (a rejected one is not listed), in the manifest's order; each with its title (its name when the manifest gives none), its group (`""` when none) and its aliases. A repeated `title` or `group` keeps the first, as `file` does; a repeated `match` adds to it.
- **`match =` is one comma-separated key**, `match = xbmc, kodi media center`: `libtools.read_sections()` refuses a key written twice in a section, and `check-library.py` reads the manifest with it. Each alias is trimmed; an empty one is skipped.
- **Normalizing** (`iconmatch_normalize()`): ASCII letters lower-cased; letters and digits make words, joined by one space; every other ASCII character breaks a word (`ES-DE` is `es de`, `Steam (Runtime)` is `steam runtime`, `Disney+` is `disney`); an apostrophe, `'` or U+2019, is dropped within its word (`Assassin's` is `assassins`); the registered, copyright and trade mark signs break a word too; every other non-ASCII byte is kept as it is, so other scripts' letters match themselves (not lower-cased: only ASCII is). Cut at `size`, both sides alike.
- **Vendor words**, dropped from an app's name as whole words only: the spec's Microsoft, Google, Mozilla, Apple and Valve, and Amazon and NVIDIA, which head the library's own brands as their apps install (*Amazon Prime Video*, *NVIDIA GeForce NOW*).
- **Two passes.** An app's name is compared as it is first, then without its vendor words; an icon's name, title and aliases always keep theirs. So *Apple Music* is Apple Music, never the generic Music, and *Google TV* takes no icon, though *Apple TV* without its vendor would read *tv*. The first match in the manifest's order wins; none is -1, and the caller falls back to `LIBRARY_FALLBACK_ICON`.
- **The aliases live in one table in `build-library.py`** (`MATCH`, keyed by icon name, generic and brand alike), not in `brands.ini`: `import-brand.py` rewrites `brands.ini` in a fixed key order (`libtools.BRAND_KEYS`), and one table keeps every alias in one place. `BRAND_KEYS` is unchanged. `build-library.py` refuses an alias for no icon, one not written as `iconmatch.c` compares it (lower-case words of a-z and 0-9, one space apart), and one that is another icon's name, title or alias, which would make the first icon take the other's apps.
- **The aliases**, each with why (fourteen icons; the spec's own example, `edge` getting *microsoft edge*, has no icon to go on: the library has no Edge):

  | Icon | Aliases | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | `settings` | `control panel`, `system settings` | Windows' Control Panel, KDE's System Settings: settings by another name |
  | `folder` | `file explorer`, `files` | Windows' and GNOME's file managers |
  | `terminal` | `windows terminal`, `gnome terminal`, `command prompt` | The terminals as Windows and GNOME list them |
  | `hbo-max` | `max` | The service's name from 2023 to 2025 |
  | `prime-video` | `prime video for windows` | The Microsoft Store app's display name |
  | `peacock` | `peacock tv` | Its Store and Linux name |
  | `tubi` | `tubi tv` | Its older app name |
  | `plex` | `plex htpc`, `plex media player`, `plex media server` | Plex's desktop apps and its server |
  | `jellyfin` | `jellyfin media player` | Jellyfin's desktop client |
  | `kodi` | `xbmc` | Kodi's name until 2014, still on old desktop entries |
  | `vlc` | `vlc media player` | Its name in the Start menu and its desktop entry |
  | `steam` | `steam runtime` | Linux's *Steam (Runtime)* desktop entry |
  | `es-de` | `emulationstation desktop edition`, `emulationstation de` | ES-DE's full name, in its desktop entry |
  | `moonlight` | `moonlight game streaming` | Its desktop entry's name |

```c
// A function to test normalizing an app's name: lower case, punctuation a break between words, an

static void test_normalize(void)
{

    CHECK_STR(normalized("Valve Hammer Editor", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "hammer editor");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("Microsoft Edge\xC2\xAE", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "edge");        // The registered sign

    CHECK_STR(normalized("Steam (Runtime)", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "steam runtime");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("Disney+", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "disney");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("ES-DE", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "es de");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("  VLC   media player  ", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "vlc media player");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("Assassin's Creed", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "assassins creed");

    CHECK_STR(normalized("Pok\xC3\xA9mon", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "pok\xC3\xA9mon");   // Other letters stay as they are
    CHECK_STR(normalized("Googleplex", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "googleplex");           // A vendor only as a whole word
    CHECK_STR(normalized("Microsoft", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("", ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "");
    CHECK_STR(normalized(NULL, ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX), "");
    CHECK_STR(normalized("Google Chrome", 6), "chrom");                             // Cut to the room given
}

// A function to test finding an app's icon: by name, title or alias, the app's name as it is first and
// without its vendor second, the icon's side always as it is; the first in the manifest's order; -1 for
// none, where the caller falls back to the library's apps icon
static void test_find(void)
{
    CHECK_INT(found("Apple Music"), 2);                          // Not Music: as it is, first
    CHECK_INT(found("Music"), 0);
    CHECK_INT(found("Amazon Music"), 4);
    CHECK_INT(found("Amazon Prime Video"), 5);                   // Without its vendor
    CHECK_INT(found("Prime Video for Windows"), 5);              // An alias
    CHECK_INT(found("Google Chrome"), 6);
    CHECK_INT(found("chrome"), 6);                               // The icon's name
    CHECK_INT(found("XBMC"), 7);
    CHECK_INT(found("Max"), 8);
    CHECK_INT(found("EmulationStation Desktop Edition"), 9);
    CHECK_INT(found("ES-DE"), 9);
    CHECK_INT(found("Disney+"), 10);                             // The title, "disney"
    CHECK_INT(found("Disney Plus"), 10);                         // The name, "disney plus"
    CHECK_INT(found("TV Shows"), 1);
    CHECK_INT(found("Google TV"), -1);                           // Apple TV keeps its vendor: never "tv"
    CHECK_INT(found("Mozilla Firefox"), -1);                     // No icon: the apps fallback is the caller's
    CHECK_INT(found("Microsoft"), -1);                           // Nothing left to compare
    CHECK_INT(found(""), -1);
    CHECK_INT(found(NULL), -1);
    CHECK_INT(iconmatch_find("Kodi", ICONS, 0), -1);
    CHECK_INT(iconmatch_find("Kodi", NULL, 0), -1);
}

// A function to find a loaded icon by its name; -1 when the library has none of that name
static int index_of(const char *name)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < library_count(); i++) {
        if (strcmp(library_info(i)->name, name) == 0)
            return i;
    }
    return -1;
}

// A function to test the shipped manifest, as build-library.py writes it: the names apps install under
// find their icons through its titles and match = aliases, an app the library has no icon for finds
// none, and every icon's title and alias finds that icon, never one before it
static void test_shipped_library(void)
{
    CHECK(library_load(LIBRARY_ROOT) > 0);
    int count = library_count();
    const LibraryInfo *icons = library_info(0);
    static const struct { const char *app; const char *icon; } cases[] = {
        { "Google Chrome", "chrome" }, { "Apple Music", "apple-music" }, { "Apple TV", "apple-tv" },
        { "Amazon Prime Video", "prime-video" }, { "Prime Video for Windows", "prime-video" }, { "Max", "hbo-max" },
        { "Disney+", "disney-plus" }, { "Peacock TV", "peacock" }, { "Tubi TV", "tubi" }, { "Plex HTPC", "plex" },
        { "Plex Media Server", "plex" }, { "Jellyfin Media Player", "jellyfin" }, { "XBMC", "kodi" },
        { "VLC media player", "vlc" }, { "Steam (Runtime)", "steam" }, { "NVIDIA GeForce NOW", "geforce-now" },
        { "Moonlight Game Streaming", "moonlight" }, { "EmulationStation Desktop Edition", "es-de" },
        { "Windows Terminal", "terminal" }, { "Command Prompt", "terminal" }, { "File Explorer", "folder" },
        { "Files", "folder" }, { "Control Panel", "settings" }, { "System Settings", "settings" },
        { "Photos", "photos" }, { "Mozilla Firefox", NULL }, { "Microsoft Edge", NULL }, { "Google TV", NULL }
    };
    for (size_t c = 0; c < sizeof(cases) / sizeof(cases[0]); c++) {
        int expected = cases[c].icon != NULL ? index_of(cases[c].icon) : -1;
        int got = iconmatch_find(cases[c].app, icons, count);
        if (got != expected)
            fprintf(stderr, "  '%s' found %s, expected %s\n", cases[c].app, got >= 0 ? icons[got].name : "none",
                    cases[c].icon != NULL ? cases[c].icon : "none");
        CHECK(cases[c].icon == NULL || expected >= 0);
        CHECK_INT(got, expected);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (iconmatch_find(icons[i].title, icons, count) != i)
            fprintf(stderr, "  the title '%s' does not find [%s]\n", icons[i].title, icons[i].name);
        CHECK_INT(iconmatch_find(icons[i].title, icons, count), i);
        for (int a = 0; a < icons[i].match_count; a++)
            CHECK_INT(iconmatch_find(icons[i].match[a], icons, count), i);
    }
    library_free();
}

int main(void)
{
    test_normalize();
    test_find();
    test_shipped_library();
    return check_report();
}
```

```c
// A function to add an icon's match = aliases: a comma-separated list, each alias trimmed of spaces and an
// empty one skipped; a repeated match key adds to them. Out of memory, an alias is left out.
static void add_aliases(LibraryIcon *icon, const char *value)
{
    const char *part = value;
    while (*part != '\0') {
        size_t length = strcspn(part, ",");
        const char *start = part;
        const char *end = part + length;
        while (start < end && isspace((unsigned char) *start))
            start++;
        while (end > start && isspace((unsigned char) end[-1]))
            end--;
        if (end > start) {
            char **grown = realloc(icon->match, (size_t) (icon->match_count + 1) * sizeof(char*));
            if (grown != NULL)
                icon->match = grown;
            char *alias = grown != NULL ? malloc((size_t) (end - start) + 1) : NULL;
            if (alias != NULL) {
                memcpy(alias, start, (size_t) (end - start));
                alias[end - start] = '\0';
                icon->match[icon->match_count++] = alias;
            }
        }
        part += length;
        if (*part == ',')
            part++;
    }
}

// The inih handler. inih reports keys, not section headers, so a change of section name marks a new
// section. A repeated section keeps the first; a repeated 'file', 'title' or 'group' keeps the first, and a
// repeated 'match' adds to it. A section with no keys at all never reaches this handler (inih's default
// build has no header callback, and Linux uses the system library), so it is skipped without the "has no
// 'file'" warning. build-library.py never writes one.
static int handler(void *user, const char *section, const char *key, const char *value)
{
    (void) user;
    if (parsing == NULL || strcmp(parsing, section)) {
        free(parsing);
        parsing = strdup(section);
        target = -1;
        if (!library_is_name(section))
            warn("Icon library: [%s] is not a valid icon name (a-z, 0-9 and '-', up to %i characters), skipping it",
                section, LIBRARY_NAME_MAX);
        else if (find_icon(section) >= 0)
            warn("Icon library: [%s] appears twice, keeping the first", section);
        else
            target = add_icon(section);
    }
    if (target < 0)
        return 1;
    LibraryIcon *icon = &icons[target];
    if (!strcmp(key, "file")) {
        if (icon->file != NULL)
            warn("Icon library: [%s] has 'file' twice, keeping the first", section);
        else
            icon->file = strdup(value);
    }
    else if (!strcmp(key, "title") && icon->title == NULL)
        icon->title = strdup(value);
    else if (!strcmp(key, "group") && icon->group == NULL)
        icon->group = strdup(value);
    else if (!strcmp(key, "match"))
        add_aliases(icon, value);
    return 1;
}
```

```c
// allocation, so tests/test_iconmatch.c builds it with the library alone.
#ifndef ICONMATCH_H
#define ICONMATCH_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include "library.h"

void iconmatch_normalize(const char *name, char *out, size_t size);   // Lower case, no punctuation, vendor words dropped
```

Create `src/iconmatch.c`:

```c
// An app's name and each library icon's name, title and match = aliases are compared normalized: in lower
// case, with punctuation dropped. The app's name is tried as it is first, then with its vendor's name
// dropped ("Google Chrome" is Chrome); an icon's side always keeps its vendor words, so "Apple TV" never
// stands for any "TV".
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "iconmatch.h"

// The words that name an app's maker rather than the app: the spec's five, and the two in front of the
// library's own brands as their apps install ("Amazon Prime Video", "NVIDIA GeForce NOW"). Whole words
// only: "Googleplex" keeps its name.
static const char *const VENDORS[] = { "microsoft", "google", "mozilla", "apple", "valve", "amazon", "nvidia" };

// A function to tell how many bytes at `p` are an apostrophe (' or U+2019), which a name drops within its
// word ("Assassin's" is "assassins"); 0 for none
static size_t apostrophe(const char *p)
{
    if (*p == '\'')
        return 1;
    if (strncmp(p, "\xE2\x80\x99", 3) == 0)
        return 3;
    return 0;
}

// A function to tell how many bytes at `p` are a sign that ends a word though it is not ASCII: the
// registered, copyright and trade mark signs ("Microsoft Edge(R)"); 0 for none
static size_t mark(const char *p)
{
    static const char *const MARKS[] = { "\xC2\xAE", "\xC2\xA9", "\xE2\x84\xA2" };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(MARKS) / sizeof(MARKS[0]); i++) {
        size_t length = strlen(MARKS[i]);
        if (strncmp(p, MARKS[i], length) == 0)
            return length;
    }
    return 0;
}

// A function to tell whether a word names a vendor
static bool vendor(const char *word)
{
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(VENDORS) / sizeof(VENDORS[0]); i++) {
        if (strcmp(word, VENDORS[i]) == 0)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to add a word to a normalized name, after a space when one is there already, as much of it as
// fits
static void add_word(char *out, size_t size, size_t *used, const char *word, size_t length)
{
    if (length == 0)
        return;
    if (*used > 0) {
        if (*used + 1 >= size)
            return;
        out[(*used)++] = ' ';
    }
    size_t room = size - 1 - *used;
    size_t take = length < room ? length : room;
    memcpy(out + *used, word, take);
    *used += take;
    out[*used] = '\0';
}

// A function to normalize a name: ASCII letters in lower case (other letters stay as they are), words of
// letters and digits joined by one space, every other ASCII character and the signs mark() knows a break
// between words, an apostrophe dropped within its word; with `drop_vendors`, a vendor's name left out.
// Cut at `size`, both sides alike.
static void normalize(const char *name, char *out, size_t size, bool drop_vendors)
{
    if (size == 0)
        return;
    out[0] = '\0';
    size_t used = 0;
    char word[ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX];
    size_t length = 0;
    const char *p = name;
    for (;;) {
        size_t skip = apostrophe(p);
        if (skip > 0) {
            p += skip;
            continue;
        }
        unsigned char c = (unsigned char) *p;
        size_t ends = c != '\0' ? mark(p) : 0;
        bool letter = ends == 0 && ((c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c >= 0x80);
        if (letter) {
            if (length + 1 < sizeof(word))
                word[length++] = (char) (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' ? c - 'A' + 'a' : c);
            p++;
            continue;
        }
        word[length] = '\0';
        if (!drop_vendors || !vendor(word))
            add_word(out, size, &used, word, length);
        length = 0;
        if (c == '\0')
            break;
        p += ends > 0 ? ends : 1;
    }
}

// A function to normalize an app's name as iconmatch_find() compares it once its vendor's name is dropped
void iconmatch_normalize(const char *name, char *out, size_t size)
{
    normalize(name != NULL ? name : "", out, size, true);
}

// A function to tell whether an icon's name, title or one of its aliases normalizes to `key`; the icon's
// side keeps its vendor words
static bool matches(const LibraryInfo *icon, const char *key)
{
    char other[ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX];
    normalize(icon->name, other, sizeof(other), false);
    if (strcmp(other, key) == 0)
        return true;
    if (icon->title != NULL) {
        normalize(icon->title, other, sizeof(other), false);
        if (strcmp(other, key) == 0)
            return true;
    }
    for (int a = 0; a < icon->match_count; a++) {
        normalize(icon->match[a], other, sizeof(other), false);
        if (strcmp(other, key) == 0)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to find the library icon an app's name stands for: the first in the manifest's order whose
// name, title or alias is the app's name, normalized; failing that, the first that is the app's name
// without its vendor's ("Google Chrome" is Chrome, while "Apple Music" stays Apple Music, never Music).
// -1 for none: the caller falls back to the library's apps icon (LIBRARY_FALLBACK_ICON).
int iconmatch_find(const char *app_name, const LibraryInfo *icons, int count)
{
    if (app_name == NULL)
        return -1;
    char key[ICONMATCH_KEY_MAX];
    for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
        normalize(app_name, key, sizeof(key), pass == 1);
        for (int i = 0; key[0] != '\0' && i < count; i++) {
            if (matches(&icons[i], key))
                return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}
```

```python
    "steam": ("steam runtime",),                                # Linux's "Steam (Runtime)" desktop entry
    "es-de": ("emulationstation desktop edition", "emulationstation de"),
    "moonlight": ("moonlight game streaming",),
}
ALIAS_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+( [a-z0-9]+)*$")


def normalized(text):
    """A name as src/iconmatch.c compares an icon's: lower case, apostrophes dropped, every other mark a break
    between words (the library's names and titles are ASCII)."""
    text = text.lower().replace("'", "").replace("\u2019", "")
    return " ".join(re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", text).split())


def match_lines(name):
    """The manifest's match = line for an icon, or none."""
    return [f"match = {', '.join(MATCH[name])}"] if name in MATCH else []


def match_problems(icons, match=None):
    """icons: [(name, title)] in manifest order. Each MATCH key must name an icon, and each alias must be written
    as iconmatch.c compares it and be no other icon's name, title or alias: iconmatch.c takes the first icon in
    the manifest's order that has it, so the other icon would lose its apps."""
    match = MATCH if match is None else match
    problems, taken = [], {}
    for name, title in icons:
        for text in (name, title):
            taken.setdefault(normalized(text), name)
    names = {name for name, _title in icons}
    for name, aliases in match.items():
        if name not in names:
            problems.append(f"MATCH '{name}': no icon has that name")
        for alias in aliases:
            if not ALIAS_RE.match(alias):
                problems.append(f"MATCH '{name}': alias '{alias}' is not lower case words of a-z and 0-9, one space apart")
            elif taken.get(alias, name) != name:
                problems.append(f"MATCH '{name}': alias '{alias}' is already {taken[alias]}'s")
            else:
                taken[alias] = name
    return problems
```

**Decisions this task makes** (where the spec and the skeleton leave room; each is pinned by a test):
- **Sort:** by name, ASCII letters compared in either case alike and every other byte by its value, so UTF-8 sorts by code point and a character is never split (`É` sorts after `Z`, and is not folded to `é`). Ties go to the exact bytes of the name (`Kodi` before `kodi`), then the command, so the order is total and the same on every run.
- **Duplicate:** the same name in any ASCII case **and** the same command, byte for byte. Two installs of one app (a `.deb` and a Flatpak) have different commands and both stay. One `.desktop` file found twice is not a duplicate case at all: the Linux scan reads each **desktop file ID** once (the path below its applications folder, `/` written `-`, as the Desktop Entry Specification defines it), the first folder's file winning, so a user's copy in `~/.local/share/applications` with `Hidden=true` or `NoDisplay=true` hides the system's app, as every desktop's menu does.
- **Left out** (`applist_add()` refuses): a name holding one of the words `uninstall`, `uninstaller`, `uninstallation`, `readme`, `help`, `documentation` (a word is a run of ASCII letters and digits, matched in any case), or the two words `read me`; a command whose last name (after its last `/` or `\`, a closing `"` dropped) starts with `unins` (`unins000.exe`, `uninstall-foo.desktop`) or ends with `.txt`, `.pdf`, `.htm`, `.html`, `.chm`, `.rtf`, `.md` or `.url` (a Start menu shortcut to a document); a command holding `://` (a web link); an empty name or command. `Helpdesk` and `Read Mentor` stay: only whole words count.
- **Filter:** a case-insensitive substring of the name, folded as the sort folds (ASCII only); an empty or NULL query matches every app; the indexes are into the sorted list, in its order; it returns how many match and fills at most `max`, as `inidoc_list()` does.
- **A `.desktop` file is an app** when its `[Desktop Entry]` group (any other group's keys are ignored) has `Type=Application`, a non-empty `Exec` (`unix.c:146-150` launches nothing without one), a name, and none of `NoDisplay`, `Hidden` and `Terminal` true (`true`, or `1` as GLib reads it). A `Terminal=true` app (`htop`, `vim`) is left out because `unix.c:122-154` runs its `Exec` through `sh -c` with no terminal, so its tile would show nothing. Keys take spaces around `=`; the first of a repeated key counts; `#` lines and CR line ends are read as the specification says. The name is `Name[<locale>]` for the best of `ll_CC@MOD`, `ll_CC`, `ll@MOD`, `ll` (the encoding dropped), wherever it stands in the file, else `Name`; an empty localized name gives way to `Name`. The locale is the first non-empty of `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES` and `LANG`, POSIX's order for messages; `C` and `POSIX` have no localized names. Escapes `\s \n \t \r \\` are read, the three line-breaking ones as a space (a tile's title is one line), and spaces at either end dropped. The command written is the `.desktop` path; a path holding `;` is refused, since `unix.c:127` cuts the command at the first `;` (`DELIMITER_ACTION`). `Icon=` is kept as written (empty: none); Task 9 resolves it.
- **The Linux folders**, in the order their files shadow later ones' (`applist_data_dirs()`, then `/applications` on each): `$XDG_DATA_HOME` when absolute, else `~/.local/share`; each absolute entry of `$XDG_DATA_DIRS`, or `/usr/local/share:/usr/share` when it is unset or empty; then `~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share`, `/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share` and `/var/lib/snapd/desktop`. Each folder once (a trailing `/` dropped), so a Flatpak export `$XDG_DATA_DIRS` already names keeps its place there. Subfolders are read four deep, hidden files skipped, regular files only (`fileio_list()`'s `is_file`), so a pipe named `x.desktop` never holds the thread. A folder that is not there holds no apps; the scan **fails** only when no folder could be listed and at least one that is there could not be (`The apps could not be listed: <folder>: <reason>`). It finds **nothing** when it read its folders and kept no app (`No apps were found`). Out of memory it lets the list go (`Out of memory while listing the apps`), as the font list does: a short list would misstate the apps, and the next visit lists them anew. A folder at any depth that cannot be listed because memory ran out (`fileio_last_error()` is fileio's `out of memory`) counts as out of memory too; a subfolder that cannot be listed for another reason (no permission) holds no apps, as a top folder does while another top folder lists.
- **The thread** is `fontscan.c`'s shape: everything it needs read on the main thread first (the folders, the locale, the hooks), nothing logged on it, `done` set last, and `appscan_poll()` waits for it once `done` reads 1 so its writes are safe to read on any CPU. It sorts the list before it ends. `appscan_free()` sets a stop flag the thread reads between files (and through the harness's delay) before it joins, so closing settings mid-scan returns at once on Linux.
- **At most once per settings visit, from the first *Add › App ›* (Known integration work 4, fix pass R1):** `settings_apps_start()` starts it (Task 10b's *App ›* calls it; once this visit has a scan, a list or a reason, it does nothing), `settings_draw()` polls it each frame, and `free_screen()` stops it and frees the list, so a visit's list is gone when settings close, the next visit lists the apps anew, and a scan under way is joined before anything it fills is freed. A visit that never opens *App ›* walks no folder and starts no COM enumeration. The scan is this task's alone: Task 10b reads the list through `settings_apps()` and builds no scan of its own.
- **On Windows until Task 8** the thread lists nothing and says why: `appscan.c` is in `SOURCES` on every platform from this task, so the Windows build compiles and links it under `/W4 /WX` now, and Task 8 replaces the one function `list_apps()` with the AppsFolder scan. No Windows build ships between the two commits.
- **Check 81 is Task 10b's:** no key path reaches *Add › App ›*, and so `settings_apps_start()`, before Task 10b builds the page, so this task's proof is its unit tests (`test_applist`, `prove_applist()`), the Windows check and the launcher's build. The scan's folders, rules, failures, the stop and join at close and (in the leak pass) no leak are proven by Task 10b's check 81, with the fixtures and log lines this task's code gives it; *Finding apps… (N)* is Task 10b's too (check 82).

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "check.h"
#include "applist.h"

// A function to read a .desktop file's text, as the scan reads each file: 1 an app, 0 skipped, -1 out of
// memory (which only test_alloc can make)
static int parse(const char *path, const char *text, const char *lang, AppItem *out)
{
    return applist_parse_desktop(path, text, strlen(text), lang, out);
}

// A function to read a .desktop text's name in a locale; "(skipped)" when it is not read as an app
static const char *name_in(const char *text, const char *lang)
{
    static char name[128];
    AppItem item;
    if (parse("/usr/share/applications/x.desktop", text, lang, &item) != 1)
        return "(skipped)";
    snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%s", item.name);
    applist_item_clear(&item);
    return name;
}

// A function to give an app's name in a list, or "" past its end
static const char *name_at(const AppList *list, int index)
{
    const AppItem *item = applist_item(list, index);
    return item != NULL ? item->name : "";
}

// A function to give an app's command in a list, or "" past its end
static const char *command_at(const AppList *list, int index)
{
    const AppItem *item = applist_item(list, index);
    return item != NULL ? item->command : "";
}

// A function to test reading a .desktop file: its name, its path as the command, its Icon= value; keys
// as the Desktop Entry Specification reads them (spaces around '=', CRLF line ends, comments, the first
// of a key repeated, another group's keys left out, escapes read); and the item cleared after
static void test_parse(void)
{
    AppItem item;
    CHECK_INT(parse("/usr/share/applications/kodi.desktop",
                    "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Kodi\nIcon=kodi\nExec=kodi\n", "en_US.UTF-8", &item), 1);
    CHECK_STR(item.name, "Kodi");
    CHECK_STR(item.command, "/usr/share/applications/kodi.desktop");
    CHECK_STR(item.icon, "kodi");
    applist_item_clear(&item);
    CHECK(item.name == NULL && item.command == NULL && item.icon == NULL);

    CHECK_INT(parse("/opt/mc.desktop", "# a comment\r\n[Desktop Entry]\r\nType = Application\r\nName = Media\\sCenter\\t2\r\n"
                    "Name=Second\r\nExec = mc %U\r\nIcon = /opt/mc/icon.png\r\n[Desktop Action play]\r\nName=Play\r\nIcon=play\r\n",
                    "C", &item), 1);
    CHECK_STR(item.name, "Media Center 2");
    CHECK_STR(item.icon, "/opt/mc/icon.png");
    applist_item_clear(&item);

    // A backslash written twice is one; spaces at either end go; an empty Icon= is no icon; NoDisplay,
    // Hidden and Terminal false keep the app
    CHECK_INT(parse("/a.desktop", "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=  Back\\\\slash  \nIcon=\nExec=a\n"
                    "NoDisplay=false\nHidden=false\nTerminal=false\n", "C", &item), 1);
    CHECK_STR(item.name, "Back\\slash");
    CHECK(item.icon == NULL);
    applist_item_clear(&item);

// or as 1), run in a terminal (Terminal, which unix.c has none for), not an application (Link,

// [Desktop Entry], an empty file, and a path holding ';', which
// unix.c's start_process() would cut there. Each is 0 (skipped, never -1: nothing ran short) and leaves

static void test_skipped(void)
{
    static const char *const skipped[] = {
        "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=A\nExec=a\nNoDisplay=true\n",
        "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=A\nExec=a\nHidden=true\n",
        "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=A\nExec=a\nHidden=1\n",

        "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=A\n",
        "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=A\nExec=\n",

        "[Desktop Action new]\nType=Application\nName=A\nExec=a\n",
        "Type=Application\nName=A\nExec=a\n",
        "",
        NULL
    };
    AppItem item;
    for (int i = 0; skipped[i] != NULL; i++) {

// A function to test the localized name: the best of ll_CC@MOD, ll_CC, ll@MOD and ll, the encoding

// the first of a key repeated; an empty localized name giving way to Name; and a file with a localized
// name alone, an app only in that locale
static void test_localized(void)
{
    static const char *const gimp = "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nExec=gimp\nName=GIMP\nName[de]=GIMP (de)\n"
        "Name[de_DE]=GIMP Bildbearbeitung\nName[de@euro]=GIMP (de, euro)\nName[de_DE@euro]=GIMP (de_DE, euro)\n"
        "Name[fr]=GIMP (fr)\n";
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "de_DE.UTF-8@euro"), "GIMP (de_DE, euro)");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "de_DE.UTF-8"), "GIMP Bildbearbeitung");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "de_DE"), "GIMP Bildbearbeitung");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "de_AT.UTF-8@euro"), "GIMP (de, euro)");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "de_AT.UTF-8"), "GIMP (de)");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "de"), "GIMP (de)");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "fr_CA.UTF-8"), "GIMP (fr)");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "ja_JP.UTF-8"), "GIMP");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "C.UTF-8"), "GIMP");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "C"), "GIMP");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, "POSIX"), "GIMP");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, ""), "GIMP");
    CHECK_STR(name_in(gimp, NULL), "GIMP");

    CHECK_STR(name_in("[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nExec=k\nName[de_DE]=Kodi DE\nName[de]=Kodi de\nName=Kodi\n",
                      "de_DE.UTF-8"), "Kodi DE");
    CHECK_STR(name_in("[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nExec=k\nName=Kodi\nName[de]=Erste\nName[de]=Zweite\n", "de_DE"),
              "Erste");
    CHECK_STR(name_in("[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nExec=k\nName=Kodi\nName[de]=\n", "de_DE"), "Kodi");
    CHECK_STR(name_in("[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nExec=k\nName[de]=Nur deutsch\n", "de_DE"), "Nur deutsch");
    CHECK_STR(name_in("[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nExec=k\nName[de]=Nur deutsch\n", "en_US"), "(skipped)");
}

// A function to test the list: what is left out (uninstallers, help and readme entries, documents, web
// links), one app found twice, the order (letters in either case alike, then the exact bytes, then the
// command; other bytes by value), and an index past either end
static void test_list(void)
{
    AppList *list = applist_create();
    CHECK(list != NULL);
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "Steam", "/a/steam.desktop", "steam"));
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "kodi", "/a/kodi.desktop", NULL));
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "\xC3\x89" "cran", "/a/ecran.desktop", "ecran"));
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "Kodi", "/b/kodi.desktop", "kodi"));            // Another command: another install
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "KODI", "/a/kodi.desktop", "x"));             // The same app, its name in another case
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "Alpha", "/a/alpha.desktop", NULL));
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "", "/a/x.desktop", NULL));
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "X", "", NULL));

    static const char *const left_out[] = {
        "Uninstall Foo", "Foo Uninstaller", "Foo uninstallation", "Foo Readme", "Read Me First", "README", "Foo Help",
        "GNOME Help", "Documentation (PDF)", NULL
    };
    for (int i = 0; left_out[i] != NULL; i++)
        CHECK(!applist_add(list, left_out[i], "/a/x.desktop", NULL));
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "Helpdesk", "/a/helpdesk.desktop", NULL));     // Words, not parts of them
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "Read Mentor", "/a/mentor.desktop", NULL));
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "Foo", "explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\\{7C5A40EF-A0FB-4BFC-874A-C0F2E0B9FA8E}\\Foo\\unins000.exe", "x"));
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "Foo notes",
                       "explorer.exe \"shell:AppsFolder\\{6D809377-6AF0-444B-8957-A3773F02200E}\\Foo App\\notes.TXT\"", "x"));
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "Foo website", "explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\\https://foo.example/", "x"));
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "Foo remover", "/usr/share/applications/uninstall-foo.desktop", NULL));
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "Calculator", "explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\\Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App",
                      "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"));
    CHECK(!applist_failed(list));
    CHECK_INT(applist_count(list), 8);

    applist_sort(list);
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 0), "Alpha");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 1), "Calculator");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 2), "Helpdesk");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 3), "Kodi");
    CHECK_STR(command_at(list, 3), "/b/kodi.desktop");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 4), "kodi");
    CHECK_STR(command_at(list, 4), "/a/kodi.desktop");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 5), "Read Mentor");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 6), "Steam");
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 7), "\xC3\x89" "cran");
    CHECK_STR(applist_item(list, 6)->icon, "steam");
    CHECK(applist_item(list, 8) == NULL);
    CHECK(applist_item(list, -1) == NULL);

    // The same name and command twice, the second's icon not kept
    CHECK(!applist_add(list, "Steam", "/a/steam.desktop", "other"));
    CHECK_STR(applist_item(list, 6)->icon, "steam");
    applist_free(list);
    applist_free(NULL);

    // Sorting an empty list, or a list of one, is fine
    list = applist_create();
    applist_sort(list);
    CHECK_INT(applist_count(list), 0);
    CHECK(applist_add(list, "One", "/a/one.desktop", NULL));
    applist_sort(list);
    CHECK_STR(name_at(list, 0), "One");
    applist_free(list);
}

// A function to test the filter: a substring of the name, ASCII letters in either case alike and other
// bytes as they are, in the list's order; all apps for an empty or no query; the count beyond `max`
static void test_filter(void)
{
    AppList *list = applist_create();
    static const char *const names[] = { "Alpha", "Calculator", "Helpdesk", "Kodi", "kodi", "Read Mentor", "Steam",
                                         "\xC3\x89" "cran", NULL };
    for (int i = 0; names[i] != NULL; i++) {
        char command[32];
        snprintf(command, sizeof(command), "/a/%d.desktop", i);
        CHECK(applist_add(list, names[i], command, NULL));
    }
    applist_sort(list);
    int indexes[8];
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "KO", indexes, 8), 2);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[0], 3);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[1], 4);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "e", indexes, 8), 3);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[0], 2);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[1], 5);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[2], 6);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "e", indexes, 1), 3);    // How many, though only one fits
    CHECK_INT(indexes[0], 2);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "e", NULL, 0), 3);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "\xC3\x89" "cr", indexes, 8), 1);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[0], 7);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "\xC3\xA9" "cr", indexes, 8), 0);   // é is not É: only ASCII letters fold
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "xyz", indexes, 8), 0);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, "", indexes, 8), 8);
    CHECK_INT(applist_filter(list, NULL, indexes, 8), 8);
    CHECK_INT(indexes[7], 7);
    applist_free(list);
}

// A function to test the data folders the Linux scan reads applications/ in: XDG_DATA_HOME (else
// ~/.local/share), each of XDG_DATA_DIRS in its order (else /usr/local/share and /usr/share), then the
// Flatpak exports and Snap's; each once, a trailing '/' dropped, a relative or empty entry ignored; and
// the folders that do not fit left out
static void test_data_dirs(void)
{
    char text[512];
    const char *dirs[8];
    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs(NULL, NULL, "/home/u", text, sizeof(text), dirs, 8), 6);
    CHECK_STR(dirs[0], "/home/u/.local/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[1], "/usr/local/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[2], "/usr/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[3], "/home/u/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[4], "/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[5], "/var/lib/snapd/desktop");

    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs("/data/", "/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share:/usr/share/:relative::/usr/share", "/home/u/",
                                text, sizeof(text), dirs, 8), 5);
    CHECK_STR(dirs[0], "/data");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[1], "/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[2], "/usr/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[3], "/home/u/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share");
    CHECK_STR(dirs[4], "/var/lib/snapd/desktop");

    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs("relative", "", "/home/u", text, sizeof(text), dirs, 8), 6);
    CHECK_STR(dirs[0], "/home/u/.local/share");
    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs(NULL, NULL, NULL, text, sizeof(text), dirs, 8), 4);
    CHECK_STR(dirs[0], "/usr/local/share");
    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs(NULL, NULL, "", text, sizeof(text), dirs, 8), 4);

    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs(NULL, NULL, "/home/u", text, sizeof(text), dirs, 2), 2);
    CHECK_STR(dirs[1], "/usr/local/share");
    CHECK_INT(applist_data_dirs(NULL, NULL, "/home/u", text, 20, dirs, 8), 1);   // "/home/u/.local/share" needs 21
    CHECK_STR(dirs[0], "/usr/local/share");
}

int main(void)
{
    test_parse();
    test_skipped();
    test_localized();
    test_list();
    test_filter();
    test_data_dirs();
    return check_report();
}
```

```c
// A function to prove that the app list fails cleanly: a .desktop file read short of memory says so (-1,
// never 0, which would read as a file that is no app) with nothing left allocated; an add short of memory
// is refused, the list keeps the apps added before it and says it is short; or all is done, 71 apps, the
// list growing past its first block
static void prove_applist(void)
{
    static const char *const desktop = "[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Kodi\nName[de]=Kodi DE\nIcon=kodi\nExec=kodi\n";
    int short_reads = 0;
    for (int n = 1;; n++) {
        AppItem item = { NULL, NULL, NULL };
        int added = 0;
        arm(n);
        AppList *list = applist_create();
        int got = list != NULL ? applist_parse_desktop("/a/kodi.desktop", desktop, strlen(desktop), "de_DE", &item) : 0;
        bool parsed = got == 1;
        bool adding = parsed && applist_add(list, item.name, item.command, item.icon);
        added += adding ? 1 : 0;
        for (int i = 0; adding && i < 70; i++) {
            char name[16];
            snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "App %d", i);
            adding = applist_add(list, name, "/a/x.desktop", NULL);
            added += adding ? 1 : 0;
        }
        disarm();
        if (!failed)
            CHECK_RUN(added == 71 && applist_count(list) == 71 && !applist_failed(list) &&
                      strcmp(applist_item(list, 0)->name, "Kodi DE") == 0, n);
        else {
            CHECK_RUN(added < 71, n);
            CHECK_RUN(list == NULL || applist_count(list) == added, n);
            CHECK_RUN(list == NULL || !parsed || applist_failed(list), n);
            CHECK_RUN(list == NULL || got != 0, n);
            CHECK_RUN(got != -1 || (item.name == NULL && item.command == NULL && item.icon == NULL), n);
            short_reads += got == -1 ? 1 : 0;
        }
        if (parsed)
            applist_item_clear(&item);
        applist_free(list);
        runs = n;
        if (!no_leak(__LINE__, n) || !failed)
            break;
    }
    CHECK(short_reads > 0);   // An allocation of the read's own failed in some run, so the -1 was met
    report("the app list");
}
```

```c
// The installed apps the settings' Add > App page lists (spec "Installed apps"): a pure list the platform
// scans fill on their thread (appscan.c), and the rules every platform shares: which entries are no app
// to launch (uninstallers, help and readme shortcuts, documents, web links), which are one app found
// twice, the order, and the filter the keyboard types into. For Linux it also reads a .desktop file's
// entry and names the data folders apps and their icons are found in. Pure: no SDL, no globals; memory
// comes from alloc.h.
#ifndef APPLIST_H
#define APPLIST_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>

typedef struct { char *name; char *command; char *icon; } AppItem;   // icon: Linux Icon= value; Windows the app ID
typedef struct AppList AppList;

AppList *applist_create(void);
void applist_free(AppList *list);
bool applist_add(AppList *list, const char *name, const char *command, const char *icon);   // false when filtered or a duplicate
void applist_sort(AppList *list);
int applist_count(const AppList *list);
const AppItem *applist_item(const AppList *list, int index);
int applist_filter(const AppList *list, const char *query, int *indexes, int max);
int applist_parse_desktop(const char *path, const char *text, size_t length, const char *lang, AppItem *out);  // 1 an app, 0 skipped, -1 out of memory
bool applist_failed(const AppList *list);   // An add ran out of memory, so the list is short
void applist_item_clear(AppItem *item);     // Frees what applist_parse_desktop() filled in
// The data folders apps (in applications/) and their icons are found in, in the order a file in one
// shadows the same file in a later one: XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_DATA_DIRS, the Flatpak exports, Snap's. They
// are packed into `buffer`; fills at most `max` and returns how many it filled.
int applist_data_dirs(const char *data_home, const char *data_dirs, const char *home, char *buffer, size_t size,
                      const char **dirs, int max);

#endif
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The list**

Create `src/applist.c`:

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "applist.h"
#include "alloc.h"
#include "fileio.h"

#define FIRST_CAPACITY 64
#define LOCALES 4          // ll_CC@MODIFIER, ll_CC, ll@MODIFIER, ll
#define LOCALE_BYTES 64
#define PART_BYTES 16      // The longest language, country or modifier a locale's name is read with
#define WORD_BYTES 32
#define DIR_BYTES 4096

struct AppList {
    AppItem *items;
    int count;
    int capacity;
    bool failed;   // An add ran out of memory: an app is missing
};

// A run of a .desktop file's text, not yet copied: a key, or its value
typedef struct {
    const char *text;   // NULL when the key was not there
    size_t length;
} Slice;

// The data folders being gathered by applist_data_dirs()
typedef struct {
    char *buffer;
    size_t size;
    size_t used;
    const char **dirs;
    int max;
    int count;
} DirList;

// The words that mark an entry as no app to launch from a TV: an uninstaller, or a help or readme
// shortcut (spec "Installed apps"). A name holding one of them as a word is left out, and "read me" too.
static const char *const SKIP_WORDS[] = { "uninstall", "uninstaller", "uninstallation", "readme", "help", "documentation", NULL };

// The ends of a command's last name that open a document, not an app: a Start menu shortcut to a readme,
// a license or a manual
static const char *const DOCUMENT_ENDS[] = { ".txt", ".pdf", ".htm", ".html", ".chm", ".rtf", ".md", ".url", NULL };

// A function to tell whether a byte belongs to a word: an ASCII letter or digit
static bool is_word_byte(char c)
{
    return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9');
}

// A function to compare two texts as the list sorts and matches names: ASCII letters in either case alike,
// every other byte by its value, so UTF-8 sorts by code point and no character is split
static int compare_text(const char *a, const char *b)
{
    for (;; a++, b++) {
        int x = fileio_lower(*a);
        int y = fileio_lower(*b);
        if (x != y || x == 0)
            return x - y;
    }
}

// A function to tell whether a name holds one of SKIP_WORDS as a word (a run of ASCII letters and digits,
// matched in either case), or "read" then "me"
static bool has_skip_word(const char *name)
{
    char previous[WORD_BYTES] = "";
    const char *p = name;
    for (;;) {
        while (*p != '\0' && !is_word_byte(*p))
            p++;
        if (*p == '\0')
            return false;
        char word[WORD_BYTES];
        size_t length = 0;
        for (; is_word_byte(*p); p++) {
            if (length + 1 < sizeof(word))
                word[length++] = (char) fileio_lower(*p);
        }
        word[length] = '\0';
        for (int i = 0; SKIP_WORDS[i] != NULL; i++) {
            if (strcmp(word, SKIP_WORDS[i]) == 0)
                return true;
        }
        if (strcmp(previous, "read") == 0 && strcmp(word, "me") == 0)
            return true;
        memcpy(previous, word, length + 1);
    }
}

// A function to tell whether a command opens no app: a web link, or a last name (after its last '/' or
// '\', a closing quote dropped) that is an uninstaller's (unins000.exe, uninstall-foo.desktop) or a
// document's
static bool opens_no_app(const char *command)
{
    if (strstr(command, "://") != NULL)
        return true;
    const char *last = command;
    for (const char *p = command; *p != '\0'; p++) {
        if (fileio_is_separator(*p))
            last = p + 1;
    }
    char name[256];
    size_t length = 0;
    for (; last[length] != '\0' && length + 1 < sizeof(name); length++)
        name[length] = (char) fileio_lower(last[length]);
    if (length > 0 && name[length - 1] == '"')
        length--;
    name[length] = '\0';
    if (strncmp(name, "unins", 5) == 0)
        return true;
    for (int i = 0; DOCUMENT_ENDS[i] != NULL; i++) {
        size_t end = strlen(DOCUMENT_ENDS[i]);
        if (length > end && strcmp(name + length - end, DOCUMENT_ENDS[i]) == 0)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to make an empty list of apps; NULL when out of memory
AppList *applist_create(void)
{
    return alloc_calloc(1, sizeof(AppList));
}

// A function to free what an item holds, leaving it empty
void applist_item_clear(AppItem *item)
{
    alloc_free(item->name);
    alloc_free(item->command);
    alloc_free(item->icon);
    item->name = NULL;
    item->command = NULL;
    item->icon = NULL;
}

// A function to free a list and its apps
void applist_free(AppList *list)
{
    if (list == NULL)
        return;
    for (int i = 0; i < list->count; i++)
        applist_item_clear(&list->items[i]);
    alloc_free(list->items);
    alloc_free(list);
}

// A function to add an app: its name, the command its tile runs, and its icon (Linux: the Icon= value;
// Windows: the app ID). False for an app left out (see SKIP_WORDS and opens_no_app()), one already listed
// (the same name in either case, the same command), and one that ran out of memory, which leaves the
// list as it was and marks it as failed.
bool applist_add(AppList *list, const char *name, const char *command, const char *icon)
{
    if (name == NULL || name[0] == '\0' || command == NULL || command[0] == '\0' || has_skip_word(name) ||
        opens_no_app(command))
        return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < list->count; i++) {
        if (compare_text(list->items[i].name, name) == 0 && strcmp(list->items[i].command, command) == 0)
            return false;
    }
    if (list->count == list->capacity) {
        int capacity = list->capacity > 0 ? list->capacity * 2 : FIRST_CAPACITY;
        AppItem *items = alloc_realloc(list->items, (size_t) capacity * sizeof(AppItem));
        if (items == NULL) {
            list->failed = true;
            return false;
        }
        list->items = items;
        list->capacity = capacity;
    }
    AppItem item = { alloc_strdup(name), alloc_strdup(command), icon != NULL ? alloc_strdup(icon) : NULL };
    if (item.name == NULL || item.command == NULL || (icon != NULL && item.icon == NULL)) {
        applist_item_clear(&item);
        list->failed = true;
        return false;
    }
    list->items[list->count++] = item;
    return true;
}

// A function to tell whether an add ran out of memory, so an app is missing
bool applist_failed(const AppList *list)
{
    return list->failed;
}

// A function to order two apps: by name as compare_text() reads it, then its exact bytes, then the command
static int compare_items(const void *a, const void *b)
{
    const AppItem *x = a;
    const AppItem *y = b;
    int order = compare_text(x->name, y->name);
    if (order == 0)
        order = strcmp(x->name, y->name);
    if (order == 0)
        order = strcmp(x->command, y->command);
    return order;
}

// A function to put the apps in order: alphabetical, the same order on every run
void applist_sort(AppList *list)
{
    if (list->count > 1)
        qsort(list->items, (size_t) list->count, sizeof(AppItem), compare_items);
}

// A function to count the apps
int applist_count(const AppList *list)
{
    return list->count;
}

// A function to get an app; NULL past either end of the list
const AppItem *applist_item(const AppList *list, int index)
{
    return index >= 0 && index < list->count ? &list->items[index] : NULL;
}

// A function to tell whether a text holds a query, ASCII letters in either case alike
static bool contains_folded(const char *text, const char *query)
{
    size_t length = strlen(query);
    for (const char *at = text; *at != '\0'; at++) {
        size_t k = 0;
        while (k < length && at[k] != '\0' && fileio_lower(at[k]) == fileio_lower(query[k]))
            k++;
        if (k == length)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to find the apps whose name holds a query (the keyboard's filter), in the list's order: it
// fills at most `max` indexes and returns how many match. An empty or NULL query matches every app.
int applist_filter(const AppList *list, const char *query, int *indexes, int max)
{
    int total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < list->count; i++) {
        if (query != NULL && query[0] != '\0' && !contains_folded(list->items[i].name, query))
            continue;
        if (total < max)
            indexes[total] = i;
        total++;
    }
    return total;
}

// A function to tell whether a run of text is exactly a string
static bool slice_is(Slice slice, const char *text)
{
    return slice.text != NULL && slice.length == strlen(text) && memcmp(slice.text, text, slice.length) == 0;
}

// A function to read a boolean as the Desktop Entry Specification writes one: "true" ("1" read as well,
// as GLib reads it)
static bool slice_true(Slice slice)
{
    return slice_is(slice, "true") || slice_is(slice, "1");
}

// A function to keep a key's value unless an earlier line had the key: the first counts
static void keep_first(Slice *kept, Slice value)
{
    if (kept->text == NULL)
        *kept = value;
}

// A function to list the locales a Name[...] key is matched against, best first, from a POSIX locale name
// (ll_CC.ENCODING@MODIFIER): ll_CC@MODIFIER, ll_CC, ll@MODIFIER, ll, each only when the name has its
// parts, as the Desktop Entry Specification orders them. C and POSIX, and a name with a part too long to
// be one, have none.
static int locale_candidates(const char *lang, char out[][LOCALE_BYTES])
{
    if (lang == NULL)
        return 0;
    size_t language = strcspn(lang, "_.@");
    const char *country = lang[language] == '_' ? lang + language + 1 : NULL;
    size_t country_length = country != NULL ? strcspn(country, ".@") : 0;
    const char *at = strchr(lang, '@');
    const char *modifier = at != NULL && at[1] != '\0' ? at + 1 : NULL;
    if (language == 0 || language >= PART_BYTES || country_length >= PART_BYTES ||
        (modifier != NULL && strlen(modifier) >= PART_BYTES))
        return 0;
    if ((language == 1 && lang[0] == 'C') || (language == 5 && strncmp(lang, "POSIX", 5) == 0))
        return 0;
    int count = 0;
    int l = (int) language;
    int c = (int) country_length;
    if (country_length > 0 && modifier != NULL)
        snprintf(out[count++], LOCALE_BYTES, "%.*s_%.*s@%s", l, lang, c, country, modifier);
    if (country_length > 0)
        snprintf(out[count++], LOCALE_BYTES, "%.*s_%.*s", l, lang, c, country);
    if (modifier != NULL)
        snprintf(out[count++], LOCALE_BYTES, "%.*s@%s", l, lang, modifier);
    snprintf(out[count++], LOCALE_BYTES, "%.*s", l, lang);
    return count;
}

// A function to rank a key against the locales: its place among them for a Name[<locale>] key that names
// one, else `count`, which ranks below every one
static int locale_rank(Slice key, char locales[][LOCALE_BYTES], int count)
{
    if (key.length < 7 || memcmp(key.text, "Name[", 5) != 0 || key.text[key.length - 1] != ']')
        return count;
    Slice locale = { key.text + 5, key.length - 6 };
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (slice_is(locale, locales[i]))
            return i;
    }
    return count;
}

// A function to copy a string value with the Desktop Entry Specification's escapes read (\s \n \t \r and
// \\; the three that would break a tile's one line read as a space), and the spaces at either end
// dropped; NULL when out of memory
static char *unescaped(Slice value)
{
    char *out = alloc_malloc(value.length + 1);
    if (out == NULL)
        return NULL;
    size_t n = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < value.length; i++) {
        char c = value.text[i];
        if (c == '\\' && i + 1 < value.length) {
            char next = value.text[i + 1];
            if (next == 's' || next == 'n' || next == 't' || next == 'r') {
                c = ' ';
                i++;
            }
            else if (next == '\\')
                i++;
        }
        out[n++] = c;
    }
    while (n > 0 && out[n - 1] == ' ')
        n--;
    size_t start = 0;
    while (start < n && out[start] == ' ')
        start++;
    memmove(out, out + start, n - start);
    out[n - start] = '\0';
    return out;
}

// A function to read a .desktop file's entry as an app for the list (spec "Installed apps"). It is one
// when its [Desktop Entry] group has Type=Application, a non-empty Exec (unix.c's start_process() runs
// nothing without one), a name, and none of NoDisplay, Hidden and Terminal true (start_process() runs
// Exec with no terminal, so a terminal app would show nothing). Its name is the Name[] of the best
// locale `lang` gives (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES or LANG's value), else Name; its command is the file's path,
// which StreamFlex launches; its icon is the Icon= value, NULL when none. A path holding ';' is refused:
// unix.c cuts the command there (DELIMITER_ACTION). 1 for an app; 0, with `out` empty, for a file that
// is no app; -1, with `out` empty, when out of memory, so the scan can tell a short read from a skip.
int applist_parse_desktop(const char *path, const char *text, size_t length, const char *lang, AppItem *out)
{
    memset(out, 0, sizeof(*out));
    if (path == NULL || path[0] == '\0' || strchr(path, ';') != NULL || text == NULL)
        return 0;
    char locales[LOCALES][LOCALE_BYTES];
    int locale_count = locale_candidates(lang, locales);
    Slice type = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice name = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice localized = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice icon = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice exec = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice no_display = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice hidden = { NULL, 0 };
    Slice terminal = { NULL, 0 };
    int localized_rank = locale_count;
    bool in_entry = false;
    for (size_t at = 0; at < length;) {
        size_t end = at;
        while (end < length && text[end] != '\n')
            end++;
        Slice line = { text + at, end - at };
        at = end + 1;
        if (line.length > 0 && line.text[line.length - 1] == '\r')
            line.length--;
        if (line.length == 0 || line.text[0] == '#')
            continue;
        if (line.text[0] == '[') {
            in_entry = slice_is(line, "[Desktop Entry]");
            continue;
        }
        const char *equals = memchr(line.text, '=', line.length);
        if (!in_entry || equals == NULL)
            continue;
        Slice key = { line.text, (size_t) (equals - line.text) };
        while (key.length > 0 && key.text[key.length - 1] == ' ')
            key.length--;
        Slice value = { equals + 1, (size_t) (line.text + line.length - (equals + 1)) };
        while (value.length > 0 && value.text[0] == ' ') {
            value.text++;
            value.length--;
        }
        if (slice_is(key, "Type"))
            keep_first(&type, value);
        else if (slice_is(key, "Name"))
            keep_first(&name, value);
        else if (slice_is(key, "Icon"))
            keep_first(&icon, value);
        else if (slice_is(key, "Exec"))
            keep_first(&exec, value);
        else if (slice_is(key, "NoDisplay"))
            keep_first(&no_display, value);
        else if (slice_is(key, "Hidden"))
            keep_first(&hidden, value);
        else if (slice_is(key, "Terminal"))
            keep_first(&terminal, value);
        else {
            int rank = locale_rank(key, locales, locale_count);
            if (rank < localized_rank && value.length > 0) {
                localized = value;
                localized_rank = rank;
            }
        }
    }
    if (!slice_is(type, "Application") || slice_true(terminal) || slice_true(no_display) || slice_true(hidden) || exec.length == 0)
        return 0;
    Slice chosen = localized.text != NULL ? localized : name;
    if (chosen.text == NULL)
        return 0;
    out->name = unescaped(chosen);
    out->command = alloc_strdup(path);
    out->icon = icon.length > 0 ? unescaped(icon) : NULL;
    bool short_of_memory = out->name == NULL || out->command == NULL || (icon.length > 0 && out->icon == NULL);
    if (short_of_memory || out->name[0] == '\0') {
        applist_item_clear(out);
        return short_of_memory ? -1 : 0;
    }
    if (out->icon != NULL && out->icon[0] == '\0') {
        alloc_free(out->icon);
        out->icon = NULL;
    }
    return 1;
}

// A function to add a data folder: absolute only, as the XDG Base Directory Specification asks (a relative
// one is ignored), with `tail` after it, a trailing '/' dropped, once each. One that does not fit is left out.
static void add_data_dir(DirList *list, const char *dir, size_t length, const char *tail)
{
    while (length > 1 && dir[length - 1] == '/')
        length--;
    if (length == 0 || dir[0] != '/')
        return;
    char path[DIR_BYTES];
    int written = snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%.*s%s", (int) length, dir, tail);
    if (written < 0 || (size_t) written >= sizeof(path))
        return;
    for (int i = 0; i < list->count; i++) {
        if (strcmp(list->dirs[i], path) == 0)
            return;
    }
    size_t need = (size_t) written + 1;
    if (list->count >= list->max || list->used + need > list->size)
        return;
    memcpy(list->buffer + list->used, path, need);
    list->dirs[list->count++] = list->buffer + list->used;
    list->used += need;
}

// A function to list the data folders apps and their icons are found in (spec "Installed apps"), in the
// order a file in one shadows the same file in a later one: XDG_DATA_HOME when it is absolute, else
// ~/.local/share; each absolute entry of XDG_DATA_DIRS, else /usr/local/share and /usr/share when it is
// unset or empty; then the user's and the system's Flatpak exports, and Snap's. Each folder once, so one
// XDG_DATA_DIRS already names keeps its place there. The paths are packed into `buffer`; it fills at most
// `max` and returns how many it filled.
int applist_data_dirs(const char *data_home, const char *data_dirs, const char *home, char *buffer, size_t size,
                      const char **dirs, int max)
{
    static const char *const FLATPAK = "/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share";
    static const char *const SNAP = "/var/lib/snapd/desktop";
    DirList list = { buffer, size, 0, dirs, max, 0 };
    bool has_home = home != NULL && home[0] == '/';
    if (data_home != NULL && data_home[0] == '/')
        add_data_dir(&list, data_home, strlen(data_home), "");
    else if (has_home)
        add_data_dir(&list, home, strlen(home), "/.local/share");
    if (data_dirs == NULL || data_dirs[0] == '\0')
        data_dirs = "/usr/local/share:/usr/share";
    for (const char *at = data_dirs; *at != '\0';) {
        size_t length = strcspn(at, ":");
        add_data_dir(&list, at, length, "");
        at += length;
        if (*at == ':')
            at++;
    }
    if (has_home)
        add_data_dir(&list, home, strlen(home), "/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share");
    add_data_dir(&list, FLATPAK, strlen(FLATPAK), "");
    add_data_dir(&list, SNAP, strlen(SNAP), "");
    return list.count;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: The scan**

Create `src/appscan.h`:

```c
// Finding the installed apps for settings' Add > App page (spec "Installed apps"), on a thread of its own,
// once per settings visit: on Windows the shell's AppsFolder (Task 8), on Linux the .desktop files of the
// applications folders of the data folders applist_data_dirs() names. The thread fills an AppList, sorts
// it, and logs nothing; the main thread polls it each frame and takes the list once it is done.
#ifndef APPSCAN_H
#define APPSCAN_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include "applist.h"

typedef struct AppScan AppScan;

AppScan *appscan_start(void);                 // Its own thread; NULL when the thread could not start
bool appscan_poll(AppScan *scan, int *found); // True once done
AppList *appscan_take(AppScan *scan);         // After done; the caller owns the list
const char *appscan_why(const AppScan *scan); // Why it failed or found nothing, or NULL
void appscan_free(AppScan *scan);             // Joins the thread first

#endif
```

Create `src/appscan.c`:

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include "appscan.h"
#include "applist.h"
#include "fileio.h"
#include "alloc.h"
#include "test_hooks.h"

#define MAX_DEPTH 4               // An applications folder may hold folders (kde4/); no deeper than this
#define MAX_FOLDERS 32            // The applications folders a scan reads
#define FOLDER_TEXT_BYTES 8192    // Their paths, one after another
#define PATH_BYTES 4096
#define WHY_BYTES 1024
#define LANG_BYTES 64
#define DELAY_STEP_MS 10u         // The harness's delay looks for a stop this often

typedef enum { SCAN_HOOK_NONE, SCAN_HOOK_FAIL, SCAN_HOOK_EMPTY } ScanHook;

struct AppScan {
    SDL_Thread *thread;                 // NULL once it has been waited for
    SDL_AtomicInt done;
    SDL_AtomicInt found;                // Apps listed so far, for "Finding apps... (N)"
    SDL_AtomicInt stop;                 // appscan_free() asks the thread to stop at its next file
    AppList *list;                      // NULL once taken, or when the scan failed
    char why[WHY_BYTES];                // Why there are no apps; "" when there are
    char lang[LANG_BYTES];              // Linux: the locale the names are read in, found on the main thread
    char folder_text[FOLDER_TEXT_BYTES];
    size_t folder_used;
    const char *folders[MAX_FOLDERS];   // Linux: the applications folders, an earlier one's file shadowing a later one's
    int folder_count;
    char **ids;                         // Linux: the desktop file IDs read so far, the thread's own
    int id_count;
    int id_capacity;
    bool short_of_memory;               // An ID or a file's entry could not be kept: the list may be short
    Uint32 delay_ms;                    // Harness only: STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN's delay...
    ScanHook hook;                      // ...or its outcome, both read on the main thread
};

// A function to tell whether appscan_free() has asked the thread to stop
static bool stopping(AppScan *scan)
{
    return SDL_GetAtomicInt(&scan->stop) != 0;
}

#ifndef _WIN32
// A function to add an applications folder to the scan's list, `tail` after it; one that does not fit is
// left out
static void add_folder(AppScan *scan, const char *folder, size_t length, const char *tail)
{
    size_t tail_length = strlen(tail);
    size_t need = length + tail_length + 1;
    if (length == 0 || scan->folder_count >= MAX_FOLDERS || scan->folder_used + need > sizeof(scan->folder_text))
        return;
    char *at = scan->folder_text + scan->folder_used;
    memcpy(at, folder, length);
    memcpy(at + length, tail, tail_length + 1);
    scan->folders[scan->folder_count++] = at;
    scan->folder_used += need;
}

// A function to find the applications folders on the main thread, from the environment: each data
// folder's applications/ (applist_data_dirs()). The harness can name them instead.
static void list_folders(AppScan *scan)
{
#ifdef STREAMFLEX_TEST_HOOKS
    // Only the headless harness builds this: STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS names the applications folders
    // (colon-separated, an empty one skipped) in place of the data folders'
    const char *test_dirs = getenv("STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS");
    if (test_dirs != NULL) {
        for (const char *at = test_dirs; *at != '\0';) {
            size_t length = strcspn(at, ":");
            add_folder(scan, at, length, "");
            at += length;
            if (*at == ':')
                at++;
        }
        return;
    }
#endif
    char data_text[FOLDER_TEXT_BYTES];
    const char *dirs[MAX_FOLDERS];
    int count = applist_data_dirs(getenv("XDG_DATA_HOME"), getenv("XDG_DATA_DIRS"), getenv("HOME"), data_text,
                                  sizeof(data_text), dirs, MAX_FOLDERS);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
        add_folder(scan, dirs[i], strlen(dirs[i]), "/applications");
}

// A function to find the locale the apps' names are read in, on the main thread: the first of LC_ALL,
// LC_MESSAGES and LANG that is set and not empty, as POSIX picks a program's messages' language
static void read_locale(AppScan *scan)
{
    static const char *const NAMES[] = { "LC_ALL", "LC_MESSAGES", "LANG" };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(NAMES) / sizeof(NAMES[0]); i++) {
        const char *value = getenv(NAMES[i]);
        if (value == NULL || value[0] == '\0')
            continue;
        if (strlen(value) < sizeof(scan->lang))
            memcpy(scan->lang, value, strlen(value) + 1);
        return;
    }
}

// A function to tell whether this is the first file of its desktop file ID: the first is the one in force,
// so a user's copy that hides an app (Hidden=true, NoDisplay=true) hides the system's (Desktop Entry
// Specification, "Desktop File ID"). A new ID is kept; out of memory, the file is skipped and the scan
// marked short.
static bool first_of_id(AppScan *scan, const char *id)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < scan->id_count; i++) {
        if (strcmp(scan->ids[i], id) == 0)
            return false;
    }
    if (scan->id_count == scan->id_capacity) {
        int capacity = scan->id_capacity > 0 ? scan->id_capacity * 2 : 256;
        char **ids = alloc_realloc(scan->ids, (size_t) capacity * sizeof(char*));
        if (ids == NULL) {
            scan->short_of_memory = true;
            return false;
        }
        scan->ids = ids;
        scan->id_capacity = capacity;
    }
    char *copy = alloc_strdup(id);
    if (copy == NULL) {
        scan->short_of_memory = true;
        return false;
    }
    scan->ids[scan->id_count++] = copy;
    return true;
}

// A function to read one .desktop file into the list, unless an earlier file had its ID. A file that
// cannot be read, or is no app (applist_parse_desktop()'s 0), adds nothing; one read short of memory
// (its -1) marks the scan short, so finish() lets the list go, as it does for an add short of memory.
static void read_desktop_file(AppScan *scan, const char *path, const char *id)
{
    if (!first_of_id(scan, id))
        return;
    size_t length = 0;
    char *text = fileio_read_all(path, &length);
    if (text == NULL)
        return;
    AppItem item;
    int got = applist_parse_desktop(path, text, length, scan->lang, &item);
    if (got < 0)
        scan->short_of_memory = true;
    else if (got == 1) {
        if (applist_add(scan->list, item.name, item.command, item.icon))
            SDL_AddAtomicInt(&scan->found, 1);
        applist_item_clear(&item);
    }
    alloc_free(text);
}

// A function to tell whether a file's name is a .desktop file's
static bool is_desktop_file(const char *name)
{
    size_t length = strlen(name);
    return length > 8 && strcmp(name + length - 8, ".desktop") == 0;
}

// A function to note a folder that could not be listed because memory ran out (fileio's own reason, as
// fileio.c tells it): the list is short, so finish() lets it go, as it does for a file read short of
// memory. One that could not be listed for another reason (no permission) holds no apps, as a top folder
// that cannot be listed does while another can.
static void note_unlisted(AppScan *scan)
{
    if (strcmp(fileio_last_error(), "out of memory") == 0)
        scan->short_of_memory = true;
}

// A function to read the .desktop files in a folder and the folders under it. `prefix` is the desktop
// file ID's start for this folder: "" at the top, "kde4-" in kde4/. Regular files only, so a pipe named
// like one never holds the thread in its read; hidden ones skipped. False when the folder cannot be listed;
// a folder under it that cannot be listed for want of memory marks the scan short (note_unlisted()).
static bool scan_folder(AppScan *scan, const char *folder, const char *prefix, int depth)
{
    FileioEntry *entries = NULL;
    int count = fileio_list(folder, &entries);
    if (count < 0)
        return false;
    char path[PATH_BYTES];
    char id[PATH_BYTES];
    for (int i = 0; i < count && !stopping(scan); i++) {
        const FileioEntry *entry = &entries[i];
        if (entry->hidden)
            continue;
        int path_length = snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%s", folder, entry->name);
        int id_length = snprintf(id, sizeof(id), "%s%s%s", prefix, entry->name, entry->is_dir ? "-" : "");
        if (path_length < 0 || (size_t) path_length >= sizeof(path) || id_length < 0 || (size_t) id_length >= sizeof(id))
            continue;
        if (entry->is_dir && depth < MAX_DEPTH) {
            if (!scan_folder(scan, path, id, depth + 1))
                note_unlisted(scan);
        }
        else if (entry->is_file && is_desktop_file(entry->name))
            read_desktop_file(scan, path, id);
    }
    fileio_free_list(entries, count);
    return true;
}

// A function to read every applications folder, in order. A folder that is not there holds no apps; the
// scan fails only when none could be listed and one that is there could not be, and is short (let go)
// when one could not be listed for want of memory.
static void scan_folders(AppScan *scan)
{
    bool listed = false;
    char problem[512] = "";
    for (int i = 0; i < scan->folder_count && !stopping(scan); i++) {
        if (scan_folder(scan, scan->folders[i], "", 0)) {
            listed = true;
            continue;
        }
        char reason[256];
        snprintf(reason, sizeof(reason), "%s", fileio_last_error());   // fileio_present() replaces it
        note_unlisted(scan);
        if (fileio_present(scan->folders[i]))
            snprintf(problem, sizeof(problem), "%s: %s", scan->folders[i], reason);
    }
    if (!listed && problem[0] != '\0')
        snprintf(scan->why, sizeof(scan->why), "The apps could not be listed: %s", problem);
}
#endif

// A function to list the apps on the scan's thread, the platform's way. Windows' AppsFolder scan is
// Task 8's; until it lands, a Windows build lists none and says so.
static void list_apps(AppScan *scan)
{
#ifdef _WIN32
    snprintf(scan->why, sizeof(scan->why), "The apps could not be listed: this build does not list Windows apps yet");
#else
    scan_folders(scan);
#endif
}

// A function to end the scan on its thread: the IDs go; a list the scan could not keep whole is let go (a
// short list would misstate the apps, and the next visit lists them anew), as is one that failed; an empty
// one says so; the rest is sorted
static void finish(AppScan *scan)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < scan->id_count; i++)
        alloc_free(scan->ids[i]);
    alloc_free(scan->ids);
    scan->ids = NULL;
    scan->id_count = 0;
    scan->id_capacity = 0;
    if (scan->short_of_memory || applist_failed(scan->list))
        snprintf(scan->why, sizeof(scan->why), "Out of memory while listing the apps");
    if (scan->why[0] != '\0') {
        applist_free(scan->list);
        scan->list = NULL;
        return;
    }
    if (applist_count(scan->list) == 0)
        snprintf(scan->why, sizeof(scan->why), "No apps were found");
    applist_sort(scan->list);
}

// A function run on the scan's thread: list the apps, then say it is done. It logs nothing (output_log()
// is the main thread's).
static int scan_thread(void *data)
{
    AppScan *scan = data;
    bool decided = false;
#ifdef STREAMFLEX_TEST_HOOKS
    // Only the headless harness builds this: STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN holds the scan back (delay:<ms>,
    // which a stop ends at once), fails it (fail), or has it find nothing (empty), whatever the folders hold
    for (Uint32 waited = 0; waited < scan->delay_ms && !stopping(scan); waited += DELAY_STEP_MS)
        SDL_Delay(DELAY_STEP_MS);
    if (scan->hook == SCAN_HOOK_FAIL)
        snprintf(scan->why, sizeof(scan->why), "The apps could not be listed: the test hook failed it");
    decided = scan->hook != SCAN_HOOK_NONE;
#endif
    if (!decided && !stopping(scan))
        list_apps(scan);
    finish(scan);
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&scan->done, 1);
    return 0;
}

// A function to start listing the installed apps on a thread. Everything the thread reads from the
// environment is read here, on the main thread. NULL when it cannot start: out of memory, or no thread
// (the harness's STREAMFLEX_TEST_FAIL=appthread).
AppScan *appscan_start(void)
{
    AppScan *scan = alloc_calloc(1, sizeof(AppScan));
    AppList *list = scan != NULL ? applist_create() : NULL;
    if (list == NULL) {
        alloc_free(scan);
        return NULL;
    }
    scan->list = list;
#ifndef _WIN32
    read_locale(scan);
    list_folders(scan);
#endif
#ifdef STREAMFLEX_TEST_HOOKS
    const char *asked = getenv("STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN");
    if (asked != NULL && strncmp(asked, "delay:", 6) == 0)
        scan->delay_ms = (Uint32) strtoul(asked + 6, NULL, 10);
    else if (asked != NULL && strcmp(asked, "fail") == 0)
        scan->hook = SCAN_HOOK_FAIL;
    else if (asked != NULL && strcmp(asked, "empty") == 0)
        scan->hook = SCAN_HOOK_EMPTY;
#endif
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&scan->done, 0);
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&scan->found, 0);
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&scan->stop, 0);
    scan->thread = test_failing("appthread") ? NULL : SDL_CreateThread(scan_thread, "App scan", scan);
    if (scan->thread == NULL) {
        appscan_free(scan);
        return NULL;
    }
    return scan;
}

// A function to tell whether the scan is done, and how many apps it has listed so far. Once the thread
// says so it is waited for, which costs nothing (it has finished) and makes everything it wrote safe to
// read here, on any CPU: SDL_SetAtomicInt() alone does not order the thread's earlier writes on a weakly
// ordered one.
bool appscan_poll(AppScan *scan, int *found)
{
    if (found != NULL)
        *found = SDL_GetAtomicInt(&scan->found);
    if (scan->thread == NULL)
        return true;
    if (SDL_GetAtomicInt(&scan->done) == 0)
        return false;
    SDL_WaitThread(scan->thread, NULL);
    scan->thread = NULL;
    return true;
}

// A function to take the list once the scan is done, sorted: the caller frees it. NULL before then, once
// taken, and when the scan failed.
AppList *appscan_take(AppScan *scan)
{
    if (scan->thread != NULL)
        return NULL;
    AppList *list = scan->list;
    scan->list = NULL;
    return list;
}

// A function to say why the scan failed or found nothing, for the caption; NULL while it runs and when it
// found apps
const char *appscan_why(const AppScan *scan)
{
    return scan->thread == NULL && scan->why[0] != '\0' ? scan->why : NULL;
}

// A function to free the scan. A thread still running is asked to stop and waited for first, so nothing
// it fills is freed under it.
void appscan_free(AppScan *scan)
{
    if (scan == NULL)
        return;
    if (scan->thread != NULL) {
        SDL_SetAtomicInt(&scan->stop, 1);
        SDL_WaitThread(scan->thread, NULL);
    }
    applist_free(scan->list);
    alloc_free(scan);
}
```
