```c
// The installed apps, listed on their own thread at most once per visit, from its first Add > App (spec
// "Installed apps")
static AppScan *app_scan = NULL;         // From settings_apps_start() until the list is taken
static AppList *apps = NULL;             // The list, for Add > App; NULL before the start, while listing, or when there is none
static int apps_found = 0;               // Apps listed so far, while the scan runs
static char apps_why[1024] = "";         // Why there is no list, or it is empty
static Uint32 apps_started = 0;          // When the scan started, for the log

// A function to start listing the installed apps, unless this visit has started already: a scan under
// way, a list, or a reason there is none (see settings_screen.h). One that cannot start leaves Add's other
// choices working, and says why.
void settings_apps_start(void)
{
    if (app_scan != NULL || apps != NULL || apps_why[0] != '\0')
        return;
    apps_found = 0;
    apps_started = ticks_ms();
    app_scan = appscan_start();
    if (app_scan == NULL) {
        snprintf(apps_why, sizeof(apps_why), "The apps could not be listed: out of memory, or no thread");
        log_error("Apps: the apps cannot be listed: out of memory, or no thread");
        return;
    }
    log_debug("Apps: listing the installed apps");
}

// A function to see each frame whether the scan is done, and once it is, take its list and say what it
// found. The hook build lists each app, in the list's order.
static void poll_apps(void)
{
    if (app_scan == NULL || !appscan_poll(app_scan, &apps_found))
        return;
    apps = appscan_take(app_scan);
    const char *why = appscan_why(app_scan);
    snprintf(apps_why, sizeof(apps_why), "%s", why != NULL ? why : "");
    appscan_free(app_scan);
    app_scan = NULL;
    Uint32 took = ticks_ms() - apps_started;
    if (apps == NULL)
        log_error("Apps: none listed: %s (%u ms)", apps_why, took);
    else if (applist_count(apps) == 0)
        log_debug("Apps: none listed: %s (%u ms)", apps_why, took);
    else
        log_debug("Apps: found %i apps (%u ms)", applist_count(apps), took);
#ifdef STREAMFLEX_TEST_HOOKS
    // Only the headless harness builds this: each app, so a check can read the list
    for (int i = 0; apps != NULL && i < applist_count(apps); i++)
        log_debug("Test hook: app %i is %s, run by %s", i + 1, applist_item(apps, i)->name, applist_item(apps, i)->command);
#endif
}

// A function to let go of the apps as settings close: a scan under way is stopped and waited for before
// anything it fills is freed (appscan_free()), then the list goes
static void stop_apps(void)
{
    if (app_scan != NULL) {
        appscan_free(app_scan);
        app_scan = NULL;
        log_debug("Apps: stopped the app scan as settings closed (%u ms)", ticks_ms() - apps_started);
    }
    applist_free(apps);
    apps = NULL;
    apps_found = 0;
    apps_why[0] = '\0';
}

// A function to give the installed apps this visit's scan listed (see settings_screen.h)
const AppList *settings_apps(int *found, const char **why)
{
    if (found != NULL)
        *found = apps_found;
    if (why != NULL)
        *why = apps_why[0] != '\0' ? apps_why : NULL;
    return apps;
}
```

### Task 8: The Windows AppsFolder scan, its images, its launch command

**Files:**
- Create: `src/platform/appsfolder.h`, `src/platform/appsfolder_win32.c`
- Create: `tests/test_appsfolder.c`
- Modify: `src/platform/platform.h` (the Windows block `:29-48`, its first line `:30`)
- Modify: `src/platform/CMakeLists.txt` (`:5-7`)
- Modify: `src/applist.h`, `src/applist.c` (Task 7's; one function after `applist_data_dirs()`)
- Modify: `src/appscan.c` (Task 7's; its includes, and `list_apps()`)
- Modify: `tests/test_applist.c` (Task 7's; one test before `main()`, and `main()`)
- Modify: `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (a `WIN32` block after the `vulkan_fix` block `:169-178`)
- Modify: `src/CMakeLists.txt` (the launcher's Windows link line `:99-107`: `gdi32` and `user32`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 7's `AppList`, `applist_add()`, `applist_failed()`, `applist_count()`, `applist_item()`, `appscan_*`; `fileio_wide()`, `fileio_last_error()`; SDL3's surfaces, atomics and error string (per thread).
- Produces, declared in `src/platform/appsfolder.h`, which `src/platform/platform.h` includes in its Windows block, so the skeleton's "in `platform.h`" holds for every launcher file, while the CTest can include the two prototypes without `launcher.h`:
  ```c
  bool appsfolder_scan(AppList *list, SDL_AtomicInt *found, SDL_AtomicInt *stop);   // On the scan's thread; ends at the next item once *stop is set; false with SDL's error set
  SDL_Surface *appicon_image(const char *app_id, int size);    // ARGB8888, straight alpha, at most size x size; NULL with SDL's error set
  ```
  and, in `src/applist.h` (pure, so Linux CI tests it too), an addition:
  ```c
  bool applist_appsfolder_command(const char *app_id, char *out, size_t size);   // explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\<id>
  ```

**Decisions this task makes:**
- **A file of its own, `src/platform/appsfolder_win32.c`,** not `win32.c`: `win32.c` includes `launcher.h` and reads the launcher's `config`, `window_hwnd` and the exit hotkey's state, so a test that linked it would need the launcher. The scan and the image need only COM, GDI, SDL's surfaces and `applist.c`, so the CTest links them alone, as the unit tests link the pure modules.
- **The GUIDs are defined in the file**, from the SDK's own values (`knownfolders.h:348` `FOLDERID_AppsFolder` `{1E87508D-89C2-42F0-8A7E-645A0F50CA58}`; `shlguid.h:571` `BHID_EnumItems` `{94F60519-2850-4924-AA5A-D15E84868039}`; `propkey.h:8569` `PKEY_AppUserModel_ID` `{9F4C2855-9F79-4B39-A8D0-E1D42DE1D5F3}`, 5; read in Windows Kits 10.0.26100.0), so no `INITGUID` and no library has to carry them; the `IID_*` interface IDs come from `uuid.lib`, which `link_fileio()` and the launcher already link. `IShellItem2::GetString` is a COM method, so no `propsys.lib` is needed.
- **The command launches as written; `win32.c` does not change.** `parse_command()` (`win32.c:67-128`) skips leading spaces; the first character is not a quote, so the first space ends the file (`explorer.exe`), and everything after the spaces that follow is copied whole into `params` with `strdup(p)` (`:104-105`), spaces, backslashes, `!` and quotes included. `start_process()` (`:198-248`) passes the two as `lpFile` and `lpParameters` to `ShellExecuteExW()` with the verb `open`, which finds `explorer.exe` in the Windows folder, and explorer opens `shell:AppsFolder\<ID>`, which starts a Store app (`Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App`) or a desktop one (`MSEdge`) alike. One case needs care: a desktop app with no AppUserModelID of its own has an ID that is a path (`{6D809377-...}\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe`), and explorer.exe separates its own parameters at commas. So `applist_appsfolder_command()` writes the ID quoted (`explorer.exe "shell:AppsFolder\<ID>"`) when it holds a space or a comma, and as the spec writes it otherwise; `parse_command()` passes the quotes through to explorer.exe untouched, since the quote is not the command's first character. IDs holding `"`, `;` or a control character are left out (none is a valid AppUserModelID; `;` after a space would end the line's value in `config.ini`). The qa-harness rows for Calculator and Edge are the live proof.
- **`appicon_image()` runs on demand, on the caller's thread** (Task 13 calls it on the main thread for the one app whose Icon page opens), not on the scan thread for every app: `GetImage()` takes tens of milliseconds an app, and a 256 px image is 256 KiB, so imaging every app in a visit would cost seconds and tens of megabytes for icons nobody chose. Each call starts COM (apartment-threaded) and ends it when its own start succeeded, so it balances on any thread.
- **The bitmap is premultiplied; the surface is not.** `IShellItemImageFactory::GetImage()` gives a 32-bit DIB with premultiplied alpha (each color already multiplied by its alpha, as `AlphaBlend()` takes one). SDL surfaces and `IMG_SavePNG()` hold straight alpha, and Task 9's `plate_icon()` premultiplies a straight surface itself, so each pixel is divided by its alpha again on the way in (rounded, held to 255). An image whose alpha is 0 everywhere (an old icon with no alpha channel) is read as opaque. The CTest checks the premultiplied form on the runner's own bitmap: every color at most its alpha, in an image with partly transparent pixels.
- **COM on the scan's thread**: `appsfolder_scan()` starts COM apartment-threaded at its top and ends it before it returns, on the thread `appscan.c` made for it, which nothing else started COM on. **It reads the scan's `stop` before each item** (the skeleton's third argument, `appscan.c`'s `&scan->stop`): closing settings mid-scan ends the enumeration at its next item, as the Linux scan ends at its next file, and `appsfolder_scan()` returns true with what it listed, which `appscan_free()` then frees unread. One `IEnumShellItems_Next()` call is the longest a close waits.

```c
// The shell's AppsFolder on a real Windows (3c Task 8): the scan lists apps through COM, each with a
// name, an ID and the command that launches it; an app's image comes at 256 px or less as a straight-alpha
// surface, from a bitmap that is premultiplied as appicon_image() reads it; an ID the folder does not have
// gives no image and says why; a stop asked for before the first item lists nothing, and is no failure;
// and the whole scan runs on its own thread, COM started there, as settings run it. What the runner has
// installed is not known, so no app is named.
#define COBJMACROS
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include <shobjidl.h>
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include "check.h"
#include "applist.h"
#include "appscan.h"
#include "platform/appsfolder.h"

#define TRIES 40              // Apps whose image is asked for, at most, before the test gives up on one
#define HANG_GUARD_MS 120000  // The scan's thread, given up on as HUNG; a correct one takes a second or two

// A function to read one pixel of an ARGB8888 surface
static Uint32 pixel_at(const SDL_Surface *surface, int x, int y)
{
    return ((const Uint32 *) ((const Uint8 *) surface->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) surface->pitch))[x];
}

// A function to read the shell's own bitmap for an app, to check the form appicon_image() takes it in:
// 1 when every color is at most its alpha (premultiplied) in an image with partly transparent pixels, 0
// when a color is above its alpha (straight alpha), -1 when no image came, it has no alpha, or none of
// its pixels is partly transparent (the check would mean nothing)
static int premultiplied(const char *app_id)
{
    char text[1100];
    wchar_t path[1100];
    snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "shell:AppsFolder\\%s", app_id);
    if (MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, text, -1, path, (int) (sizeof(path) / sizeof(path[0]))) == 0)
        return -1;
    HRESULT started = CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);
    IShellItemImageFactory *factory = NULL;
    HBITMAP bitmap = NULL;
    if (SUCCEEDED(SHCreateItemFromParsingName(path, NULL, &IID_IShellItemImageFactory, (void **) &factory))) {
        SIZE want = { 256, 256 };
        if (FAILED(IShellItemImageFactory_GetImage(factory, want, SIIGBF_ICONONLY, &bitmap)))
            bitmap = NULL;
        IShellItemImageFactory_Release(factory);
    }
    int verdict = -1;
    BITMAP info;
    if (bitmap != NULL && GetObjectW(bitmap, (int) sizeof(info), &info) != 0 && info.bmWidth > 0 && info.bmHeight != 0) {
        int width = info.bmWidth;
        int height = info.bmHeight < 0 ? -info.bmHeight : info.bmHeight;
        size_t count = (size_t) width * (size_t) height;
        Uint32 *bits = malloc(count * sizeof(Uint32));
        BITMAPINFO header;
        memset(&header, 0, sizeof(header));
        header.bmiHeader.biSize = (DWORD) sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER);
        header.bmiHeader.biWidth = width;
        header.bmiHeader.biHeight = -height;
        header.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1;
        header.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32;
        header.bmiHeader.biCompression = BI_RGB;
        HDC screen = GetDC(NULL);
        if (bits != NULL && GetDIBits(screen, bitmap, 0, (UINT) height, bits, &header, DIB_RGB_COLORS) == height) {
            bool has_alpha = false;
            bool partial = false;
            bool above = false;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                Uint32 alpha = bits[i] >> 24;
                has_alpha = has_alpha || alpha != 0;
                partial = partial || (alpha > 0 && alpha < 255);
                above = above || ((bits[i] >> 16) & 0xFF) > alpha || ((bits[i] >> 8) & 0xFF) > alpha || (bits[i] & 0xFF) > alpha;
            }
            verdict = !has_alpha ? -1 : above ? 0 : partial ? 1 : -1;
        }
        ReleaseDC(NULL, screen);
        free(bits);
    }
    if (bitmap != NULL)
        DeleteObject(bitmap);
    if (SUCCEEDED(started))
        CoUninitialize();
    return verdict;
}

int main(void)
{
    // The scan, on this thread: apps, each with a name, an ID and the command made from it
    SDL_AtomicInt found;
    SDL_AtomicInt stop;
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&found, 0);
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&stop, 0);
    AppList *list = applist_create();
    CHECK(list != NULL);
    bool scanned = list != NULL && appsfolder_scan(list, &found, &stop);
    CHECK(scanned);
    if (!scanned)
        fprintf(stderr, "appsfolder_scan: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
    int count = list != NULL ? applist_count(list) : 0;
    printf("AppsFolder: %d apps\n", count);
    CHECK(count > 0);
    CHECK_INT(SDL_GetAtomicInt(&found), count);
    CHECK(list != NULL && !applist_failed(list));
    int bad = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const AppItem *item = applist_item(list, i);
        char command[1200];
        bool whole = item->name[0] != '\0' && item->icon != NULL &&
                     applist_appsfolder_command(item->icon, command, sizeof(command)) && strcmp(command, item->command) == 0;
        if (!whole && bad++ < 5)
            fprintf(stderr, "app %d: '%s' runs '%s' (ID '%s')\n", i, item->name, item->command, item->icon != NULL ? item->icon : "none");
        if (i < 5)
            printf("  %s: %s\n", item->name, item->command);
    }
    CHECK_INT(bad, 0);

    // Asked to stop before its first item, as closing settings asks mid-scan: it lists nothing, counts
    // nothing, and that is no failure
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&stop, 1);
    SDL_SetAtomicInt(&found, 0);
    AppList *stopped = applist_create();
    CHECK(stopped != NULL);
    CHECK(stopped != NULL && appsfolder_scan(stopped, &found, &stop));
    CHECK_INT(stopped != NULL ? applist_count(stopped) : -1, 0);
    CHECK_INT(SDL_GetAtomicInt(&found), 0);
    applist_free(stopped);

    // An image: the first app's whose image comes, at most 256 px a side, straight ARGB, not empty
    SDL_Surface *image = NULL;
    const AppItem *imaged = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < count && i < TRIES && image == NULL; i++) {
        imaged = applist_item(list, i);
        image = appicon_image(imaged->icon, 256);
    }
    CHECK(image != NULL);
    if (image != NULL) {
        printf("Image of %s: %d x %d\n", imaged->name, image->w, image->h);
        CHECK(image->format == SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
        CHECK(image->w > 0 && image->w <= 256 && image->h > 0 && image->h <= 256);
        bool seen = false;
        for (int y = 0; y < image->h && !seen; y++) {
            for (int x = 0; x < image->w && !seen; x++)
                seen = (pixel_at(image, x, y) >> 24) != 0;
        }
        CHECK(seen);
        SDL_DestroySurface(image);
    }

    // The shell's bitmap is premultiplied, as appicon_image() reads it
    int verdict = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < count && i < TRIES && verdict < 0; i++)
        verdict = premultiplied(applist_item(list, i)->icon);
    CHECK_INT(verdict, 1);

    // An ID the folder does not have: no image, and why
    SDL_ClearError();
    CHECK(appicon_image("StreamFlex.Test.NoSuchApp!App", 256) == NULL);
    CHECK(SDL_GetError()[0] != '\0');
    CHECK(appicon_image("", 256) == NULL);

    // The scan as settings run it: its own thread, COM started there, the list sorted and taken
    AppScan *scan = appscan_start();
    CHECK(scan != NULL);
    int listed = 0;
    bool hung = false;
    Uint64 began = SDL_GetTicks();
    while (scan != NULL && !appscan_poll(scan, &listed)) {
        if (SDL_GetTicks() - began > HANG_GUARD_MS) {
            fprintf(stderr, "HUNG: the app scan's thread had not finished after %d s, with %d apps listed\n",
                    HANG_GUARD_MS / 1000, listed);
            hung = true;
            break;
        }
        SDL_Delay(10);
    }
    CHECK(!hung);
    if (scan != NULL && !hung) {
        CHECK(appscan_why(scan) == NULL);
        AppList *taken = appscan_take(scan);
        CHECK(taken != NULL && applist_count(taken) == count);
        applist_free(taken);
        appscan_free(scan);
    }
    applist_free(list);
    return check_report();
}
```

```c
// The command that launches an AppsFolder app (Windows): explorer.exe opening shell:AppsFolder\<app ID>,
// the ID quoted when it holds a space or a comma. False for an ID that cannot be written so.
bool applist_appsfolder_command(const char *app_id, char *out, size_t size);
```

In `src/applist.c`, after `applist_data_dirs()`, add:

```c
// A function to write the command an AppsFolder app is launched by (spec "Installed apps"): explorer.exe
// opening shell:AppsFolder\<app ID>, which starts desktop and Store apps alike. win32.c's
// parse_command() ends the program at the command's first space and hands start_process() the rest as
// written, which ShellExecuteExW() gives explorer.exe as its parameters. The ID is quoted when it holds a
// space (a desktop app with no ID of its own has a path for one: "{GUID}\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe")
// or a comma (explorer.exe separates its own parameters at commas). False for an ID that is empty or
// holds a quote, a ';' (config.ini reads a ';' after a space as a comment) or a control character, and
// for a command that does not fit.
bool applist_appsfolder_command(const char *app_id, char *out, size_t size)
{
    if (app_id == NULL || app_id[0] == '\0' || strpbrk(app_id, "\";") != NULL)
        return false;
    for (const char *p = app_id; *p != '\0'; p++) {
        if ((unsigned char) *p < 0x20)
            return false;
    }
    int written = strpbrk(app_id, " ,") != NULL ? snprintf(out, size, "explorer.exe \"shell:AppsFolder\\%s\"", app_id)
                                               : snprintf(out, size, "explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\\%s", app_id);
    return written > 0 && (size_t) written < size;
}
```

```c
// The shell's AppsFolder on Windows (spec "Installed apps"): every app the Start menu lists, desktop and
// Store apps alike, and an app's own image (spec "Icons"). A file apart from win32.c, which needs the
// launcher, so the Windows unit test links these two alone.
#ifndef APPSFOLDER_H
#define APPSFOLDER_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include "../applist.h"

bool appsfolder_scan(AppList *list, SDL_AtomicInt *found, SDL_AtomicInt *stop);   // On the scan's thread; ends at the next item once *stop is set; false with SDL's error set
SDL_Surface *appicon_image(const char *app_id, int size);    // ARGB8888, straight alpha, at most size x size; NULL with SDL's error set

#endif
```

Create `src/platform/appsfolder_win32.c`:

```c
#define COBJMACROS   // IShellItem_GetDisplayName() and the rest, in C
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include <shobjidl.h>
#include <shlobj.h>
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include "appsfolder.h"
#include "../applist.h"
#include "../fileio.h"
#include "../alloc.h"

#define NAME_BYTES 1024
#define ID_BYTES 1024
#define COMMAND_BYTES 1200

// The AppsFolder known folder (knownfolders.h FOLDERID_AppsFolder), the handler that lists a folder's
// items (shlguid.h BHID_EnumItems) and the app's AppUserModelID (propkey.h PKEY_AppUserModel_ID), as the
// SDK defines them; defined here, so no INITGUID and no library has to carry them
static const GUID APPS_FOLDER = { 0x1E87508D, 0x89C2, 0x42F0, { 0x8A, 0x7E, 0x64, 0x5A, 0x0F, 0x50, 0xCA, 0x58 } };
static const GUID ENUM_ITEMS = { 0x94F60519, 0x2850, 0x4924, { 0xAA, 0x5A, 0xD1, 0x5E, 0x84, 0x86, 0x80, 0x39 } };
static const PROPERTYKEY APP_USER_MODEL_ID = { { 0x9F4C2855, 0x9F79, 0x4B39, { 0xA8, 0xD0, 0xE1, 0xD4, 0x2D, 0xE1, 0xD5, 0xF3 } }, 5 };

// A function to turn a UTF-16 string into UTF-8, into a buffer; false when it does not fit
static bool to_utf8(const wchar_t *wide, char *out, int size)
{
    return WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, wide, -1, out, size, NULL, NULL) > 0;
}

// A function to get an AppsFolder item's app ID: its AppUserModelID, else its name in the folder, which
// for an app with none is the ID Windows made for it. NULL when it has neither; CoTaskMemFree() frees it.
static wchar_t *app_id_of(IShellItem *item)
{
    wchar_t *id = NULL;
    IShellItem2 *item2 = NULL;
    if (SUCCEEDED(IShellItem_QueryInterface(item, &IID_IShellItem2, (void **) &item2))) {
        if (FAILED(IShellItem2_GetString(item2, &APP_USER_MODEL_ID, &id)))
            id = NULL;
        IShellItem2_Release(item2);
    }
    if (id != NULL && id[0] != L'\0')
        return id;
    CoTaskMemFree(id);
    id = NULL;
    if (FAILED(IShellItem_GetDisplayName(item, SIGDN_PARENTRELATIVEPARSING, &id)))
        id = NULL;
    return id;
}

// A function to add one AppsFolder item to the list: its display name, the command that launches it,
// and its app ID, which appicon_image() finds its image by. An item the list leaves out (an uninstaller,
// a document) or that cannot be written adds nothing; out of memory, the list says so itself.
static void add_item(AppList *list, IShellItem *item, SDL_AtomicInt *found)
{
    wchar_t *name = NULL;
    if (FAILED(IShellItem_GetDisplayName(item, SIGDN_NORMALDISPLAY, &name)))
        return;
    wchar_t *id = app_id_of(item);
    char name_text[NAME_BYTES];
    char id_text[ID_BYTES];
    char command[COMMAND_BYTES];
    if (id != NULL && to_utf8(name, name_text, (int) sizeof(name_text)) && to_utf8(id, id_text, (int) sizeof(id_text)) &&
        applist_appsfolder_command(id_text, command, sizeof(command)) && applist_add(list, name_text, command, id_text))
        SDL_AddAtomicInt(found, 1);
    CoTaskMemFree(name);
    CoTaskMemFree(id);
}

// A function to list the shell's AppsFolder into the list, on the scan's thread, counting each app added
// in `found` as it goes, and ending at the next item once `stop` is set (settings closed mid-scan), true
// with what it listed. COM is started here, apartment-threaded, and ended here: nothing else started it
// on this thread. False, with SDL's error saying why, when the folder cannot be opened or listed, or its
// listing fails part way (an error from Next(), not its S_FALSE at the end): a short list would misstate
// the apps, as appscan.c's finish() judges a Linux scan short of memory.
bool appsfolder_scan(AppList *list, SDL_AtomicInt *found, SDL_AtomicInt *stop)
{
    HRESULT started = CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);
    IShellItem *folder = NULL;
    IEnumShellItems *items = NULL;
    HRESULT hr = SHGetKnownFolderItem(&APPS_FOLDER, KF_FLAG_DEFAULT, NULL, &IID_IShellItem, (void **) &folder);
    if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
        hr = IShellItem_BindToHandler(folder, NULL, &ENUM_ITEMS, &IID_IEnumShellItems, (void **) &items);
        IShellItem_Release(folder);
    }
    if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
        IShellItem *item = NULL;
        HRESULT next = S_OK;   // Stays S_OK when a stop ends the loop before it asks again
        while (SDL_GetAtomicInt(stop) == 0 && (next = IEnumShellItems_Next(items, 1, &item, NULL)) == S_OK) {
            add_item(list, item, found);
            IShellItem_Release(item);
        }
        IEnumShellItems_Release(items);
        if (FAILED(next)) {
            hr = next;
            SDL_SetError("Windows could not list its apps folder (error 0x%08lX)", (unsigned long) next);
        }
    }
    else
        SDL_SetError("Windows could not open its apps folder (error 0x%08lX)", (unsigned long) hr);
    if (SUCCEEDED(started))
        CoUninitialize();
    return SUCCEEDED(hr);
}

// A function to divide a premultiplied color by its alpha again, rounded and held to 255
static Uint32 unmultiplied(Uint32 color, Uint32 alpha)
{
    Uint32 value = (color * 255 + alpha / 2) / alpha;
    return value > 255 ? 255 : value;
}

// A function to turn one of the shell's premultiplied pixels into a straight-alpha one; an image with no
// alpha at all is opaque
static Uint32 straight(Uint32 pixel, bool has_alpha)
{
    Uint32 alpha = has_alpha ? pixel >> 24 : 255;
    if (alpha == 0 || alpha == 255)
        return alpha << 24 | (pixel & 0xFFFFFFu);
    return alpha << 24 | unmultiplied((pixel >> 16) & 0xFF, alpha) << 16 | unmultiplied((pixel >> 8) & 0xFF, alpha) << 8 |
           unmultiplied(pixel & 0xFF, alpha);
}

// A function to copy the shell's 32-bit bitmap into a surface. The shell's image is premultiplied (each
// color already multiplied by its alpha, as AlphaBlend() takes one); a surface holds straight alpha, as
// plate_icon() and IMG_SavePNG() read it, so each color is divided by its alpha again. An image with no
// alpha at all (an old icon) is opaque. NULL, with SDL's error set, when it cannot be read.
static SDL_Surface *surface_of(HBITMAP bitmap)
{
    BITMAP info;
    if (GetObjectW(bitmap, (int) sizeof(info), &info) == 0 || info.bmWidth <= 0 || info.bmHeight == 0) {
        SDL_SetError("Windows gave an image that cannot be read");
        return NULL;
    }
    int width = info.bmWidth;
    int height = info.bmHeight < 0 ? -info.bmHeight : info.bmHeight;
    size_t count = (size_t) width * (size_t) height;
    Uint32 *bits = malloc(count * sizeof(Uint32));
    SDL_Surface *surface = bits != NULL ? SDL_CreateSurface(width, height, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888) : NULL;
    if (surface == NULL) {
        if (bits == NULL)
            SDL_OutOfMemory();
        free(bits);
        return NULL;
    }
    BITMAPINFO header;
    memset(&header, 0, sizeof(header));
    header.bmiHeader.biSize = (DWORD) sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER);
    header.bmiHeader.biWidth = width;
    header.bmiHeader.biHeight = -height;   // The top row first, as a surface holds its rows
    header.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1;
    header.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32;
    header.bmiHeader.biCompression = BI_RGB;
    HDC screen = GetDC(NULL);
    int rows = GetDIBits(screen, bitmap, 0, (UINT) height, bits, &header, DIB_RGB_COLORS);
    ReleaseDC(NULL, screen);
    if (rows != height) {
        free(bits);
        SDL_DestroySurface(surface);
        SDL_SetError("Windows could not copy the image's pixels");
        return NULL;
    }
    bool has_alpha = false;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count && !has_alpha; i++)
        has_alpha = (bits[i] >> 24) != 0;
    for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
        Uint32 *row = (Uint32 *) ((Uint8 *) surface->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) surface->pitch);
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            row[x] = straight(bits[(size_t) y * (size_t) width + (size_t) x], has_alpha);
    }
    free(bits);
    return surface;
}

// A function to get an AppsFolder app's own image (spec "Icons", choice 2), from its app ID: the icon at
// size x size or less (IShellItemImageFactory, icon only), as an ARGB8888 surface with straight alpha. Run
// on demand on the caller's thread, for the one app whose icon is being chosen; COM is started for the
// call and ended after it when this call started it. NULL, with SDL's error saying why, when there is none.
SDL_Surface *appicon_image(const char *app_id, int size)
{
    char path[ID_BYTES + 32];
    int written = app_id != NULL ? snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "shell:AppsFolder\\%s", app_id) : -1;
    if (app_id == NULL || app_id[0] == '\0' || written < 0 || (size_t) written >= sizeof(path) || size <= 0) {
        SDL_SetError("There is no app ID to get an image for");
        return NULL;
    }
    wchar_t *wide = fileio_wide(path);
    if (wide == NULL) {
        SDL_SetError("%s", fileio_last_error());
        return NULL;
    }
    HRESULT started = CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);
    IShellItemImageFactory *factory = NULL;
    HBITMAP bitmap = NULL;
    HRESULT hr = SHCreateItemFromParsingName(wide, NULL, &IID_IShellItemImageFactory, (void **) &factory);
    if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
        SIZE want = { size, size };
        hr = IShellItemImageFactory_GetImage(factory, want, SIIGBF_ICONONLY, &bitmap);
        IShellItemImageFactory_Release(factory);
    }
    SDL_Surface *image = NULL;
    if (SUCCEEDED(hr))
        image = surface_of(bitmap);
    else
        SDL_SetError("Windows has no image for %s (error 0x%08lX)", app_id, (unsigned long) hr);
    if (bitmap != NULL)
        DeleteObject(bitmap);
    if (SUCCEEDED(started))
        CoUninitialize();
    alloc_free(wide);
    return image;
}
```

### Task 9: Plating and saving app icons; the `icons/` folder; the Linux icon lookup

**Files:**
- Create: `src/plate.h`, `src/plate.c`, `src/iconfind.h`, `src/iconfind.c` (pure)
- Create: `tests/test_plate.c`, `tests/test_iconfind.c`

- Modify: `tests/test_alloc.c` (`#include "iconfind.h"`; one proof after Task 7's `prove_applist()`; `main()`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: SDL3's surfaces (`SDL_CreateSurface`, `SDL_ConvertSurface`, `SDL_DestroySurface`, `SDL_SetError`, `SDL_OutOfMemory`: all in SDL 3.2.0), SDL3_image's `IMG_SavePNG` (in SDL3_image 3.2.4's header (verified); `png_roundtrip` proves each build writes PNG); `fileio_make_dirs()`, `fileio_present()`, `fileio_remove()`, `fileio_list()`, `fileio_is_file()`, `fileio_is_separator()`, `fileio_lower()`; `launcher_config.h`'s `EXECUTABLE_TITLE`; util.c's `config.config_path` and `home_directory()`. (`iconfind_path()` takes its folders from its caller, so this task calls no `applist_data_dirs()`; Task 13b does.)
- Produces, in `src/plate.h`, the skeleton's four exactly, plus two additions and the plate's constants:
  ```c
  #define PLATE_SIZE 512         // The side a plated icon is saved at: the library's canvas
  #define PLATE_RADIUS 0.22      // libtools.py OUTLINE_RADIUS
  #define PLATE_GLYPH_BOX 0.60   // build-library.py GLYPH_BOX
  #define ICONS_NAME_MAX 48
  SDL_Surface *plate_icon(SDL_Surface *icon, int size);          // Centered on the library's square plate
  bool plate_save(SDL_Surface *plated, const char *path);         // IMG_SavePNG
  bool icons_dir(char *out, size_t size);                         // Beside config.ini; Linux ~/.config/streamflex/icons
  void icons_file_name(const char *app_name, char *out, size_t size);   // Safe file name, ".png"
  bool icons_dir_at(const char *config_path, const char *home, char *out, size_t size);   // Addition: icons_dir()'s rule, testable
  bool icons_new_path(const char *dir, const char *app_name, char *out, size_t size);     // Addition: a new file, -2, -3 on a clash
  ```
  and in `src/iconfind.h` (pure), the skeleton's exactly:
  ```c

  bool iconfind_path(const char *icon_value, const char *const *dirs, int dir_count, char *out, size_t size);   // pure
  ```
  Task 13 calls `iconfind_path()` with the data folders `applist_data_dirs(getenv("XDG_DATA_HOME"), getenv("XDG_DATA_DIRS"), home, ...)` gives, loads the file (`load_image_file()` reads PNG, SVG and XPM), plates it with `plate_icon(..., PLATE_SIZE)`, picks the path with `icons_new_path(dir, app_name, ...)` in the folder `icons_dir()` gives, and writes it with `plate_save()`.

**Decisions this task makes:**
- **The plate, read from the library's build** (`build-library.py`'s `CANVAS` `:22`, `RADIUS` `:23`, `GLYPH_BOX` `:24` and `GENERAL_HEX` `:29`; `libtools.py:16`): a square whose corners are rounded to **0.22** of its side (`RADIUS = round(512 * 0.22, 2)` = 112.64 on the 512 canvas), the icon fitted inside a centered box **0.60** of the side, its longer side filling the box and its aspect kept. The plate colors the library uses are `#07606C` for the general group (`GENERAL_HEX`, StreamFlex teal), `#5C646D` for system (LCh 42, 6, 260), `#4D7189` for devices (LCh 46, 18, 250), and a hue per icon for media, all computed with `plate_color()` from the build script. **An app's plate is the general group's `#07606C`**: it is the plate of the generic `apps` icon (`assets/icons/library/generic/apps.svg`, `group = general`) that an app with no icon of its own gets, so an app's plated icon and the fallback it replaces read as one family; a neutral system gray would set app tiles apart from the library's own.
- **Size:** saved at **512 px** (`PLATE_SIZE`), the library's canvas, so a plated icon is as sharp as a library icon at the largest button the layout draws; a 256 px Windows image is grown to the 307 px box.
- **How it is drawn, with SDL3 surface calls only** (no renderer, no math library): an `SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888` surface (straight alpha, which `IMG_SavePNG()` writes as PNG's own RGBA) is written row by row through its `pitch`. Rows and columns clear of the four corners are wholly inside the plate; each corner pixel is sampled at 4 x 4 points against the rounded square and given the share inside as its alpha, as `libtools.outline_mask()` draws at 4x and box-filters down. The plate's color is in every pixel, its alpha 0 outside the corners, so a renderer's linear filtering never blends another color into the edge.
- **The icon is scaled premultiplied, by area**: converted to ARGB8888 (`SDL_ConvertSurface()`, any format in), each color multiplied by its alpha, then resampled in two passes. Shrinking averages each output pixel over the input it covers, partial pixels weighed by their share; growing interpolates linearly between pixel centers. Premultiplied, the color under a transparent pixel adds nothing, so no edge rings with it; by area, a 512 px SVG raster shrunk to the 307 px box skips no pixel. SDL's own `SDL_ScaleSurface()` would interpolate straight alpha. The icon lies wholly inside the plate's opaque part (its box starts 0.20 of the side in; the corners' curves reach 0.22), so each of its pixels is its premultiplied color plus the plate's through what it leaves, opaque.
- **PNG saving needs no new vcpkg feature.** `vcpkg.json` asks `sdl3-image` for `png` (libpng), and `vcpkg-overlays/` holds only `sdl3` and `sdl3-ttf`, so the registry's port builds it; its portfile (read at `build/vcpkg/ports/sdl3-image`, 3.4.4) maps `png` to `SDLIMAGE_PNG` and passes no `SDLIMAGE_PNG_SAVE`, so SDL_image's own default for saving applies. `IMG_SavePNG` is in SDL3_image 3.2.4's header (verified); `png_roundtrip` proves each build writes PNG (the Linux images' SDL3_image and vcpkg's static one on the Windows leg), and a `PNG saving not supported`-style failure there is a stop-and-report, the fix being `SDLIMAGE_PNG_SAVE` in an overlay port.
- **The folder** (`icons_dir()`, in `util.c` because it reads the launcher's `config` and `home_directory()`; its rule is `icons_dir_at()` in `plate.c`, which the tests link): on Windows, `icons` in the folder `config.config_path` is in; on Linux, `<home>/.config/streamflex/icons`, beside the user's own `config.ini` that every Linux save writes (`settings_screen.c:928-934`). It is made with `fileio_make_dirs()`; false when it cannot be.
- **The file's name** (`icons_file_name()`): lower-case ASCII letters and digits kept; every other byte (a space, punctuation, each byte of a UTF-8 character) becomes `-`, a run of them one `-`, none at either end; at most 48 characters before `.png`; `app.png` when nothing is left (`日本`, `!!!`). **A clash is decided in `icons_new_path()`**, called right before the save: the first of `<name>.png`, `<name>-2.png` up to `<name>-999.png` with nothing at that path (`fileio_present()`), so StreamFlex never writes over a file, its own from another app or one the user put there. `plate_save()` removes a file its own failed save left half-written, and never one that was there before it.
- **The Linux lookup** (`iconfind_path()`, pure, over the folders it is given): an absolute `Icon=` value is used as it is when it is a regular file, else nothing; a value holding `/` or `\` otherwise is not a name, and finds nothing; a name may carry `.png`, `.svg` or `.xpm`, which is dropped (other dots stay: `org.gnome.Calculator`). In each folder's `icons/hicolor`, every `<N>x<N>` folder (square, digits only; `256x256@2` and `128x64` are not sizes) is looked in for `apps/<name>.png`, the largest across all folders kept (the first folder on a tie), and the first folder's `scalable/apps/<name>.svg`. **The PNG wins when it is at least 128 px** (`ICONFIND_GOOD_SIZE`); a smaller one loses to the SVG, which rasterizes sharp at any size; with no SVG, the largest PNG of any size. Then each folder's `pixmaps/<name>.png`, `.svg`, `.xpm`, folder by folder. The Flatpak export icon folders are searched as the data folders they are (`applist_data_dirs()` lists `exports/share`), so the spec's "then the Flatpak export icon folders" is that list's order.

Create `tests/test_plate.c`:

```c
// Plating an app's own icon (3c Task 9): the library's rounded square plate in #07606C, the icon centered
// in its 0.60 box, scaled premultiplied and by area; the file's name, a clash numbered, and the folder.
// Run as "test_plate png", it is the png_roundtrip test: a plated icon saved with IMG_SavePNG and read
// back with IMG_Load is the same, pixel for pixel, which proves the build's SDL3_image writes PNG.
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include <SDL3_image/SDL_image.h>
#include "check.h"
#include "plate.h"
#include "fileio.h"

#define DIR "plate-fixture"
#ifdef _WIN32
#define SEP "\\"
#else
#define SEP "/"
#endif
#define ARGB(a, r, g, b) ((Uint32) (a) << 24 | (Uint32) (r) << 16 | (Uint32) (g) << 8 | (Uint32) (b))
#define PLATE ARGB(0xFF, 0x07, 0x60, 0x6C)   // The library's general plate, opaque
#define CLEAR ARGB(0x00, 0x07, 0x60, 0x6C)   // Outside its corners: the plate's color at alpha 0
#define RED ARGB(0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00)
#define CHECK_PIXEL(surface, x, y, expected) check_pixel(surface, x, y, expected, __LINE__)

// A function to read one pixel of an ARGB8888 surface
static Uint32 pixel(const SDL_Surface *surface, int x, int y)
{
    return ((const Uint32 *) ((const Uint8 *) surface->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) surface->pitch))[x];
}

// A function to write one pixel of an ARGB8888 surface
static void put(SDL_Surface *surface, int x, int y, Uint32 value)
{
    ((Uint32 *) ((Uint8 *) surface->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) surface->pitch))[x] = value;
}

// A function to check one pixel, naming it and both values in hex when it differs
static void check_pixel(const SDL_Surface *surface, int x, int y, Uint32 expected, int line)
{
    Uint32 found = pixel(surface, x, y);
    check_count++;
    if (found != expected) {
        check_failures++;
        fprintf(stderr, "test_plate.c:%d: pixel %d,%d is %08X, expected %08X\n", line, x, y, (unsigned) found, (unsigned) expected);
    }
}

// A function to make an icon of one color (straight ARGB)
static SDL_Surface *solid(int width, int height, Uint32 color)
{
    SDL_Surface *surface = SDL_CreateSurface(width, height, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
    CHECK(surface != NULL);
    for (int y = 0; surface != NULL && y < height; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            put(surface, x, y, color);
    }
    return surface;
}

// A function to plate an icon at 100 px and free the icon; NULL (a failed check) when it could not
static SDL_Surface *plated_at_100(SDL_Surface *icon)
{
    SDL_Surface *plated = icon != NULL ? plate_icon(icon, 100) : NULL;
    CHECK(plated != NULL);
    SDL_DestroySurface(icon);
    return plated;
}

// A function to test the plate's shape on a 100 px plate: clear outside its corners, opaque along its
// edges and through its middle, the corners' curve partly covered and the same at all four; a 10 px red
// icon grown to fill the 60 px box at 20 to 79 on both axes; and the plate's color under every pixel the
// icon does not cover, whatever its alpha
static void test_shape(void)
{
    SDL_Surface *plated = plated_at_100(solid(10, 10, RED));
    if (plated == NULL)
        return;
    CHECK(plated->w == 100 && plated->h == 100 && plated->format == SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 0, 0, CLEAR);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 99, 0, CLEAR);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 0, 99, CLEAR);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 99, 99, CLEAR);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 0, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 0, 50, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 99, 50, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 99, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 10, 50, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 19, 50, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 19, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 20, 50, RED);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 20, RED);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 50, RED);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 79, 79, RED);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 80, 50, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 80, PLATE);
    int edge = (int) (pixel(plated, 6, 6) >> 24);
    CHECK(edge > 0 && edge < 255);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 93, 6, pixel(plated, 6, 6));
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 6, 93, pixel(plated, 6, 6));
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 93, 93, pixel(plated, 6, 6));
    int stray = 0;
    for (int y = 0; y < 100; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < 100; x++) {
            bool icon = x >= 20 && x < 80 && y >= 20 && y < 80;
            if (!icon && (pixel(plated, x, y) & 0xFFFFFFu) != 0x07606Cu)
                stray++;
        }
    }
    CHECK_INT(stray, 0);
    SDL_DestroySurface(plated);
}

// A function to test an icon's alpha over the plate: half-transparent white shows the plate through
// what it leaves, (255 x 128/255) + 0x07 x 127/255 and so on, rounded: 131, 176, 182, opaque
static void test_composite(void)
{
    SDL_Surface *plated = plated_at_100(solid(2, 2, ARGB(128, 255, 255, 255)));
    if (plated == NULL)
        return;
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 50, ARGB(0xFF, 131, 176, 182));
    SDL_DestroySurface(plated);
}

// A function to test that the color under transparent pixels never reaches the icon: 300 px, white in
// its first 152 columns, transparent red after, shrunk five to one. The output column over columns 150 to
// 154 holds two white and three transparent: a premultiplied average of 102, which over the plate is
// 106, 160, 167. A straight average would bring the red in (and 98 for green).
static void test_no_halo(void)
{
    SDL_Surface *icon = SDL_CreateSurface(300, 300, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
    CHECK(icon != NULL);
    for (int y = 0; icon != NULL && y < 300; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < 300; x++)
            put(icon, x, y, x < 152 ? ARGB(255, 255, 255, 255) : ARGB(0, 255, 0, 0));
    }
    SDL_Surface *plated = plated_at_100(icon);
    if (plated == NULL)
        return;
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 49, 50, ARGB(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF));
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 50, 50, ARGB(0xFF, 106, 160, 167));
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 51, 50, PLATE);
    SDL_DestroySurface(plated);
}

// A function to test that shrinking averages by area: a 300 px checkerboard of single black and white
// pixels, shrunk five to one, is gray everywhere (122 or 133); sampling a pixel per output pixel would
// give black and white
static void test_shrink_by_area(void)
{
    SDL_Surface *icon = SDL_CreateSurface(300, 300, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
    CHECK(icon != NULL);
    for (int y = 0; icon != NULL && y < 300; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < 300; x++)
            put(icon, x, y, (x + y) % 2 != 0 ? ARGB(255, 255, 255, 255) : ARGB(255, 0, 0, 0));
    }
    SDL_Surface *plated = plated_at_100(icon);
    if (plated == NULL)
        return;
    int outside = 0;
    for (int y = 20; y < 80; y++) {
        for (int x = 20; x < 80; x++) {
            Uint32 p = pixel(plated, x, y);
            Uint32 r = (p >> 16) & 0xFF;
            if (r < 115 || r > 140 || r != ((p >> 8) & 0xFF) || r != (p & 0xFF))
                outside++;
        }
    }
    CHECK_INT(outside, 0);
    SDL_DestroySurface(plated);
}

    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 19, 50, PLATE);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 20, 50, RED);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 79, 50, RED);
    CHECK_PIXEL(plated, 80, 50, PLATE);
    SDL_DestroySurface(plated);
}

}

// A function to give the file name icons_file_name() makes of an app's name
static const char *file_name(const char *app_name)
{
    static char out[64];
    icons_file_name(app_name, out, sizeof(out));
    return out;
}

// A function to test the file names: lower-case letters and digits, anything else one '-' however many
// there were and none at either end, 48 characters at most, "app" when nothing is left
static void test_file_names(void)
{
    CHECK_STR(file_name("Microsoft Edge"), "microsoft-edge.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name("VLC media player"), "vlc-media-player.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name("  GIMP 2.10 (64-bit)!"), "gimp-2-10-64-bit.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name("Caf\xC3\xA9 \xC3\x9Cnicode"), "caf-nicode.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name("\xE6\x97\xA5\xE6\x9C\xAC"), "app.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name("!!!"), "app.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name(""), "app.png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name(NULL), "app.png");

    char name[80];
    char expected[80];
    memset(name, 'A', 60);
    name[60] = '\0';
    memset(expected, 'a', ICONS_NAME_MAX);
    snprintf(expected + ICONS_NAME_MAX, sizeof(expected) - ICONS_NAME_MAX, ".png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name(name), expected);
    memset(name, 'a', 47);
    snprintf(name + 47, sizeof(name) - 47, " b");          // The '-' is the 48th: cut, and dropped
    memset(expected, 'a', 47);
    snprintf(expected + 47, sizeof(expected) - 47, ".png");
    CHECK_STR(file_name(name), expected);
}

// A function to test a new file's path: the name itself, then -2 and -3 as each before it is there;
// false when the path does not fit
static void test_new_path(void)
{
    static const char *const dir = DIR SEP "icons";
    CHECK(fileio_make_dirs(dir));
    fileio_remove(DIR SEP "icons" SEP "kodi.png");
    fileio_remove(DIR SEP "icons" SEP "kodi-2.png");
    fileio_remove(DIR SEP "icons" SEP "kodi-3.png");
    char path[256];
    CHECK(icons_new_path(dir, "Kodi", path, sizeof(path)));
    CHECK_STR(path, DIR SEP "icons" SEP "kodi.png");
    CHECK(fileio_write_all(path, "x", 1));
    CHECK(icons_new_path(dir, "KODI", path, sizeof(path)));
    CHECK_STR(path, DIR SEP "icons" SEP "kodi-2.png");
    CHECK(fileio_write_all(path, "x", 1));
    CHECK(icons_new_path(dir, "kodi", path, sizeof(path)));
    CHECK_STR(path, DIR SEP "icons" SEP "kodi-3.png");
    CHECK(!icons_new_path(dir, "Kodi", path, 10));
}

// A function to test the icons folder's rule, made as it is found: beside the config on Windows, in
// ~/.config/streamflex on Linux; none without a config (Windows) or a home (Linux); false when the path
// does not fit
static void test_icons_dir(void)
{
    char out[512];
#ifdef _WIN32
    CHECK(icons_dir_at(DIR "\\cfg\\config.ini", NULL, out, sizeof(out)));
    CHECK_STR(out, DIR "\\cfg\\icons");
    CHECK(fileio_is_dir(out));
    CHECK(!icons_dir_at(NULL, NULL, out, sizeof(out)));
    CHECK(!icons_dir_at("", NULL, out, sizeof(out)));
#else
    CHECK(icons_dir_at("/anywhere/config.ini", DIR "/home", out, sizeof(out)));
    CHECK_STR(out, DIR "/home/.config/streamflex/icons");
    CHECK(fileio_is_dir(out));
    CHECK(!icons_dir_at("/anywhere/config.ini", NULL, out, sizeof(out)));
    CHECK(!icons_dir_at("/anywhere/config.ini", "", out, sizeof(out)));
#endif
    CHECK(!icons_dir_at(DIR "\\cfg\\config.ini", DIR "/home", out, 8));
}

// A function to test that the build's SDL3_image writes PNG: a plated icon (partly transparent corners,
// an icon of many colors and alphas) saved and read back is the same, pixel for pixel (a clear pixel by
// its alpha alone); and a save into a folder that is not there is refused, saying why, with no file left
static void test_png_roundtrip(void)
{
    SDL_Surface *icon = SDL_CreateSurface(9, 7, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
    CHECK(icon != NULL);
    for (int y = 0; icon != NULL && y < 7; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < 9; x++)
            put(icon, x, y, ARGB(x * 28, y * 36, (x * y * 4) & 0xFF, 200));
    }
    SDL_Surface *plated = icon != NULL ? plate_icon(icon, 64) : NULL;
    SDL_DestroySurface(icon);
    CHECK(plated != NULL);
    if (plated == NULL)
        return;
    fileio_remove(DIR SEP "round.png");
    bool saved = plate_save(plated, DIR SEP "round.png");
    CHECK(saved);
    if (!saved)
        fprintf(stderr, "plate_save: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
    SDL_Surface *loaded = saved ? IMG_Load(DIR SEP "round.png") : NULL;
    CHECK(!saved || loaded != NULL);
    if (saved && loaded == NULL)
        fprintf(stderr, "IMG_Load: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
    SDL_Surface *read = loaded != NULL ? SDL_ConvertSurface(loaded, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888) : NULL;
    if (read != NULL) {
        CHECK(read->w == 64 && read->h == 64);
        int differ = 0;
        int partial = 0;
        for (int y = 0; y < 64 && read->w == 64 && read->h == 64; y++) {
            for (int x = 0; x < 64; x++) {
                Uint32 written = pixel(plated, x, y);
                Uint32 back = pixel(read, x, y);
                bool same = (written >> 24) == 0 ? (back >> 24) == 0 : written == back;
                differ += same ? 0 : 1;
                partial += (written >> 24) > 0 && (written >> 24) < 255 ? 1 : 0;
            }
        }
        CHECK_INT(differ, 0);
        CHECK(partial > 0);
        printf("png_roundtrip: 4096 pixels read back as written, %d of them partly transparent\n", partial);
    }
    SDL_DestroySurface(read);
    SDL_DestroySurface(loaded);

    SDL_ClearError();
    CHECK(!plate_save(plated, DIR SEP "missing" SEP "round.png"));
    CHECK(SDL_GetError()[0] != '\0');
    CHECK(!fileio_present(DIR SEP "missing" SEP "round.png"));
    SDL_DestroySurface(plated);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    if (!SDL_Init(0)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "SDL_Init: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
        return 1;
    }
    CHECK(fileio_make_dirs(DIR));
    if (argc > 1 && strcmp(argv[1], "png") == 0)
        test_png_roundtrip();
    else {
        test_shape();
        test_composite();
        test_no_halo();
        test_shrink_by_area();
        test_aspect();
        test_refused();
        test_file_names();
        test_new_path();
        test_icons_dir();
    }
    SDL_Quit();
    return check_report();
}
```

Create `src/plate.c`:

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include <SDL3_image/SDL_image.h>
#include <launcher_config.h>
#include "plate.h"
#include "fileio.h"
#ifdef _WIN32
#define SEPARATOR "\\"
#else
#define SEPARATOR "/"
#endif

#define PLATE_RED 0x07       // The general group's plate, #07606C (build-library.py GENERAL_HEX): the generic
#define PLATE_GREEN 0x60     // apps icon's, which an app with no icon of its own gets
#define PLATE_BLUE 0x6C
#define SAMPLES 4            // Points across and down a corner pixel is sampled at, as libtools.outline_mask()
                             // draws at 4x and box-filters down
#define MAX_CLASH 999        // name-2.png to name-999.png, then no new name

// A function to round a channel's value to a byte, held to 0 to 255
static Uint32 channel(double value)
{
    if (value <= 0.0)
        return 0;
    if (value >= 255.0)
        return 255;
    return (Uint32) (value + 0.5);
}

// A function to count the sample points of a pixel inside the plate: a square of side `size` whose corners
// are rounded to `radius`, sampled at SAMPLES x SAMPLES points
static int coverage(int size, double radius, int x, int y)
{
    int inside = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < SAMPLES; j++) {
        for (int i = 0; i < SAMPLES; i++) {
            double px = x + (i + 0.5) / SAMPLES;
            double py = y + (j + 0.5) / SAMPLES;
            double dx = px < radius ? radius - px : px > size - radius ? px - (size - radius) : 0.0;
            double dy = py < radius ? radius - py : py > size - radius ? py - (size - radius) : 0.0;
            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= radius * radius)
                inside++;
        }
    }
    return inside;
}

// A function to draw the plate: the library's rounded square in its color, row by row. The rows and the
// columns clear of the corners are wholly inside, so only the corners' pixels are sampled, each given the
// share of its points inside as its alpha, which smooths the curve as the library's own outline is
// smoothed. Every pixel has the plate's color, so filtering never blends another into the edge.
static void draw_plate(SDL_Surface *plated, int size)
{
    double radius = size * PLATE_RADIUS;
    int corner = (int) radius;
    if (corner < radius)
        corner++;
    const Uint32 color = (Uint32) PLATE_RED << 16 | (Uint32) PLATE_GREEN << 8 | (Uint32) PLATE_BLUE;
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++) {
        Uint32 *row = (Uint32 *) ((Uint8 *) plated->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) plated->pitch);
        bool clear_row = y >= corner && y < size - corner;
        for (int x = 0; x < size; x++) {
            bool clear = clear_row || (x >= corner && x < size - corner);
            int inside = clear ? SAMPLES * SAMPLES : coverage(size, radius, x, y);
            Uint32 alpha = (Uint32) ((inside * 255 + SAMPLES * SAMPLES / 2) / (SAMPLES * SAMPLES));
            row[x] = alpha << 24 | color;
        }
    }
}

// A function to read an icon into premultiplied channels, four floats a pixel (alpha, red, green, blue,
// each 0 to 255): scaled that way, a transparent pixel's color, whatever it is, adds nothing to its
// neighbors. NULL, with SDL's error set, when out of memory or the icon cannot be converted.
static float *premultiplied(SDL_Surface *icon)
{
    SDL_Surface *argb = SDL_ConvertSurface(icon, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
    if (argb == NULL)
        return NULL;
    float *out = malloc((size_t) argb->w * (size_t) argb->h * 4 * sizeof(float));
    if (out == NULL)
        SDL_OutOfMemory();
    for (int y = 0; out != NULL && y < argb->h; y++) {
        const Uint32 *row = (const Uint32 *) ((const Uint8 *) argb->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) argb->pitch);
        for (int x = 0; x < argb->w; x++) {
            float *p = out + ((size_t) y * (size_t) argb->w + (size_t) x) * 4;
            float alpha = (float) (row[x] >> 24);
            float share = alpha / 255.0F;
            p[0] = alpha;
            p[1] = (float) ((row[x] >> 16) & 0xFF) * share;
            p[2] = (float) ((row[x] >> 8) & 0xFF) * share;
            p[3] = (float) (row[x] & 0xFF) * share;
        }
    }
    SDL_DestroySurface(argb);
    return out;
}

// A function to resample one line of premultiplied pixels, four floats each and `in_step` or `out_step`
// pixels apart, from `from` pixels to `to`. Shrinking averages by area: each pixel made is the mean of
// the pixels it covers, one it covers in part weighed by that part, so none is skipped. Growing
// interpolates between the pixels' centers, the edge pixels held.
static void resample_line(const float *in, int from, int in_step, float *out, int to, int out_step)
{
    if (to < from) {
        double scale = (double) from / to;
        for (int o = 0; o < to; o++) {
            double start = o * scale;
            double end = start + scale;
            double sum[4] = { 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 };
            for (int i = (int) start; i < from && i < end; i++) {
                double left = i > start ? i : start;
                double right = i + 1 < end ? i + 1 : end;
                const float *p = in + (size_t) i * (size_t) in_step * 4;
                for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++)
                    sum[c] += (right - left) * p[c];
            }
            float *q = out + (size_t) o * (size_t) out_step * 4;
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++)
                q[c] = (float) (sum[c] / scale);
        }
        return;
    }
    for (int o = 0; o < to; o++) {
        double at = (o + 0.5) * from / to - 0.5;
        if (at < 0.0)
            at = 0.0;
        int i = (int) at;
        if (i > from - 1)
            i = from - 1;
        int next = i + 1 < from ? i + 1 : i;
        double t = at - i;
        const float *p = in + (size_t) i * (size_t) in_step * 4;
        const float *n = in + (size_t) next * (size_t) in_step * 4;
        float *q = out + (size_t) o * (size_t) out_step * 4;
        for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++)
            q[c] = (float) (p[c] * (1.0 - t) + n[c] * t);
    }
}

// A function to resample premultiplied pixels to a new size, across then down; NULL, with SDL's error
// set, when out of memory
static float *resample(const float *in, int width, int height, int to_width, int to_height)
{
    float *across = malloc((size_t) to_width * (size_t) height * 4 * sizeof(float));
    float *out = malloc((size_t) to_width * (size_t) to_height * 4 * sizeof(float));
    if (across == NULL || out == NULL) {
        free(across);
        free(out);
        SDL_OutOfMemory();
        return NULL;
    }
    for (int y = 0; y < height; y++)
        resample_line(in + (size_t) y * (size_t) width * 4, width, 1, across + (size_t) y * (size_t) to_width * 4, to_width, 1);
    for (int x = 0; x < to_width; x++)
        resample_line(across + (size_t) x * 4, height, to_width, out + (size_t) x * 4, to_height, to_width);
    free(across);
    return out;
}

// A function to put an app's own icon on the library's plate (spec "Icons", choice 2): a new ARGB8888
// surface, `size` square, the plate drawn by draw_plate() and the icon centered in its PLATE_GLYPH_BOX
// box, its longer side filling the box and its aspect kept, scaled premultiplied and by area. The box
// lies inside the plate's opaque part (it starts 0.20 of the side in; the corners' curves reach 0.22), so
// each of its pixels is the icon's color plus the plate's through what the icon leaves, opaque. NULL,
// with SDL's error set, for no icon, a plate too small to sample, or out of memory.
SDL_Surface *plate_icon(SDL_Surface *icon, int size)
{
    if (icon == NULL || icon->w <= 0 || icon->h <= 0 || size < SAMPLES) {
        SDL_SetError("There is no icon to put on a plate");
        return NULL;
    }
    int box = (int) (size * PLATE_GLYPH_BOX + 0.5);
    int longest = icon->w > icon->h ? icon->w : icon->h;
    int width = (int) ((double) icon->w * box / longest + 0.5);
    int height = (int) ((double) icon->h * box / longest + 0.5);
    if (width < 1)
        width = 1;
    if (height < 1)
        height = 1;
    float *pixels = premultiplied(icon);
    float *scaled = pixels != NULL ? resample(pixels, icon->w, icon->h, width, height) : NULL;
    free(pixels);
    SDL_Surface *plated = scaled != NULL ? SDL_CreateSurface(size, size, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888) : NULL;
    if (plated == NULL) {
        free(scaled);
        return NULL;
    }
    draw_plate(plated, size);
    int left = (size - width) / 2;
    int top = (size - height) / 2;
    for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
        Uint32 *row = (Uint32 *) ((Uint8 *) plated->pixels + (size_t) (top + y) * (size_t) plated->pitch);
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
            const float *p = scaled + ((size_t) y * (size_t) width + (size_t) x) * 4;
            double through = 1.0 - p[0] / 255.0;
            row[left + x] = 0xFF000000u | channel(p[1] + PLATE_RED * through) << 16 |
                            channel(p[2] + PLATE_GREEN * through) << 8 | channel(p[3] + PLATE_BLUE * through);
        }
    }
    free(scaled);
    return plated;
}

// A function to save a plated icon as a PNG (IMG_SavePNG, SDL3_image 3.2.4 and later), at a new file's
// path (icons_new_path()). False, with SDL's error saying why (a read-only folder, a full disk), when it
// could not; a file this save left half-written is removed, and never one that was there before it.
bool plate_save(SDL_Surface *plated, const char *path)
{
    bool was_there = fileio_present(path);
    if (plated != NULL && IMG_SavePNG(plated, path))
        return true;
    char why[512];
    snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "%s", plated != NULL ? SDL_GetError() : "There is no icon to save");
    if (!was_there)
        fileio_remove(path);
    SDL_SetError("%s", why);
    return false;
}

// A function to find the folder plated icons are saved in, and make it: on Windows, icons in the folder
// `config_path` is in; on Linux, <home>/.config/streamflex/icons, beside the user's own config.ini. False
// when there is no config path (Windows) or home (Linux), the path does not fit, or it cannot be made.
bool icons_dir_at(const char *config_path, const char *home, char *out, size_t size)
{
    int written;
#ifdef _WIN32
    (void) home;
    if (config_path == NULL || config_path[0] == '\0')
        return false;
    size_t folder = strlen(config_path);
    while (folder > 0 && !fileio_is_separator(config_path[folder - 1]))
        folder--;
    written = snprintf(out, size, "%.*sicons", (int) folder, config_path);
#else
    (void) config_path;
    if (home == NULL || home[0] == '\0')
        return false;
    written = snprintf(out, size, "%s/.config/" EXECUTABLE_TITLE "/icons", home);
#endif
    if (written < 0 || (size_t) written >= size)
        return false;
    return fileio_make_dirs(out);
}

// A function to make a file name from an app's name: lower-case ASCII letters and digits kept, every
// other byte (a space, punctuation, each byte of a UTF-8 character) a '-', a run of them one '-', none at
// either end, ICONS_NAME_MAX characters at most, then ".png"; "app.png" when nothing is left. `out` holds
// ICONS_NAME_MAX + 5 bytes.
void icons_file_name(const char *app_name, char *out, size_t size)
{
    char stem[ICONS_NAME_MAX + 1];
    size_t length = 0;
    bool dash = false;
    for (const char *p = app_name != NULL ? app_name : ""; *p != '\0' && length < ICONS_NAME_MAX; p++) {
        int c = fileio_lower(*p);
        if ((c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')) {
            stem[length++] = (char) c;
            dash = false;
        }
        else if (!dash && length > 0) {
            stem[length++] = '-';
            dash = true;
        }
    }
    while (length > 0 && stem[length - 1] == '-')
        length--;
    stem[length] = '\0';
    snprintf(out, size, "%s.png", length > 0 ? stem : "app");
}

// A function to give a new file's path in a folder for an app's plated icon: icons_file_name()'s name,
// or, while something is at that path, the name with -2, -3 and on up to -999 before ".png". False when
// none is free or the path does not fit.
bool icons_new_path(const char *dir, const char *app_name, char *out, size_t size)
{
    char file[ICONS_NAME_MAX + 5];
    icons_file_name(app_name, file, sizeof(file));
    int stem = (int) strlen(file) - 4;   // Without ".png"
    for (int n = 1; n <= MAX_CLASH; n++) {
        int written = n == 1 ? snprintf(out, size, "%s" SEPARATOR "%s", dir, file)
                             : snprintf(out, size, "%s" SEPARATOR "%.*s-%i.png", dir, stem, file, n);
        if (written < 0 || (size_t) written >= size)
            return false;
        if (!fileio_present(out))
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

```c
// every Linux save writes. False when it cannot be made.
bool icons_dir(char *out, size_t size)
```

- [ ] **Step 5: The lookup**

Create `src/iconfind.c`:

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "iconfind.h"
#include "fileio.h"

#define PATH_BYTES 4096
#define NAME_BYTES 256

// The extensions an Icon= name may carry, though the Desktop Entry Specification asks for none; the
// pixmaps folders are looked in for each, in this order
static const char *const EXTENSIONS[] = { ".png", ".svg", ".xpm", NULL };

// A function to tell whether a path is absolute: from the root, a share, or a drive
static bool is_absolute(const char *path)
{
    bool drive = ((path[0] >= 'A' && path[0] <= 'Z') || (path[0] >= 'a' && path[0] <= 'z')) && path[1] == ':' &&
                 fileio_is_separator(path[2]);
    return fileio_is_separator(path[0]) || drive;
}

// A function to tell whether snprintf() wrote its whole text: a path cut short names another file
static bool fits(int written, size_t size)
{
    return written >= 0 && (size_t) written < size;
}

// A function to copy a path found into the caller's buffer; false when it does not fit
static bool give(const char *path, char *out, size_t size)
{
    size_t length = strlen(path);
    if (length + 1 > size)
        return false;
    memcpy(out, path, length + 1);
    return true;
}

// A function to read a hicolor size folder's name, "<N>x<N>": N, or -1 for any other name (scalable, a
// HiDPI "256x256@2", a size that is not square)
static int square_size(const char *name)
{
    const char *p = name;
    int n = 0;
    int m = 0;
    if (*p < '0' || *p > '9')
        return -1;
    for (; *p >= '0' && *p <= '9'; p++) {
        if (n > 100000)
            return -1;
        n = n * 10 + (*p - '0');
    }
    if (*p != 'x' || p[1] < '0' || p[1] > '9')
        return -1;
    for (p++; *p >= '0' && *p <= '9'; p++) {
        if (m > 100000)
            return -1;
        m = m * 10 + (*p - '0');
    }
    return *p == '\0' && n == m && n > 0 ? n : -1;
}

// A function to drop an Icon= name's .png, .svg or .xpm, in any case; other dots stay (org.gnome.Calculator)
static void strip_extension(char *name)
{
    size_t length = strlen(name);
    for (int i = 0; EXTENSIONS[i] != NULL; i++) {
        size_t end = strlen(EXTENSIONS[i]);
        if (length <= end)
            continue;
        bool same = true;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < end && same; k++)
            same = fileio_lower(name[length - end + k]) == EXTENSIONS[i][k];
        if (same) {
            name[length - end] = '\0';
            return;
        }
    }
}

// A function to find the file a .desktop file's Icon= value names (see iconfind.h). In the hicolor theme
// the largest <N>x<N> PNG across the folders is kept (the first folder's on a tie) beside the first
// folder's scalable SVG; the PNG wins when it is ICONFIND_GOOD_SIZE or larger, else the SVG, else the PNG
// of any size. Then each folder's pixmaps, folder by folder, .png, .svg, then .xpm. False when nothing is
// found, or the path does not fit `out`.
bool iconfind_path(const char *icon_value, const char *const *dirs, int dir_count, char *out, size_t size)
{
    if (icon_value == NULL || icon_value[0] == '\0')
        return false;
    if (is_absolute(icon_value))
        return fileio_is_file(icon_value) && give(icon_value, out, size);
    size_t length = strlen(icon_value);
    if (strchr(icon_value, '/') != NULL || strchr(icon_value, '\\') != NULL || length >= NAME_BYTES)
        return false;
    char name[NAME_BYTES];
    memcpy(name, icon_value, length + 1);
    strip_extension(name);

    char png[PATH_BYTES] = "";
    char svg[PATH_BYTES] = "";
    char path[PATH_BYTES];
    int png_size = 0;
    for (int d = 0; d < dir_count; d++) {
        char theme[PATH_BYTES];
        if (!fits(snprintf(theme, sizeof(theme), "%s/icons/hicolor", dirs[d]), sizeof(theme)))
            continue;
        FileioEntry *entries = NULL;
        int count = fileio_list(theme, &entries);
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            int n = entries[i].is_dir ? square_size(entries[i].name) : -1;
            if (n > png_size && fits(snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%s/apps/%s.png", theme, entries[i].name, name), sizeof(path)) &&
                fileio_is_file(path)) {
                png_size = n;
                memcpy(png, path, strlen(path) + 1);
            }
        }
        fileio_free_list(entries, count > 0 ? count : 0);
        if (svg[0] == '\0' && fits(snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/scalable/apps/%s.svg", theme, name), sizeof(path)) &&
            fileio_is_file(path))
            memcpy(svg, path, strlen(path) + 1);
    }
    if (png_size >= ICONFIND_GOOD_SIZE || (png_size > 0 && svg[0] == '\0'))
        return give(png, out, size);
    if (svg[0] != '\0')
        return give(svg, out, size);
    for (int d = 0; d < dir_count; d++) {
        for (int e = 0; EXTENSIONS[e] != NULL; e++) {
            if (fits(snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/pixmaps/%s%s", dirs[d], name, EXTENSIONS[e]), sizeof(path)) &&
                fileio_is_file(path))
                return give(path, out, size);
        }
    }
    return false;
}
```

**The entry every way in uses** (Tasks 10a, 10b and 13 follow it):
- *A field* (a title, a name, a command, a path): `pickers_open_keyboard(label, initial, max_bytes, check, context, done)`. `done` runs once the keyboard has closed, so it may call `settings_menus_changed()` and open another picker.
- *A field the preview shows as it is typed*: then `pickers_keyboard_follow(changed, 300)`. `changed` hears the text once it has rested 300 ms after a change, and, if it heard one, hears the text the field opened with when the keyboard is canceled, so it can put the preview back.
- *A list that filters by typing* (the app list, the icon grid): while the list is open, `pickers_set_typing(open)`; `open(first)` opens the keyboard on the filter with `pickers_keyboard_follow(changed, 0)` (at once) and, when `first` is not NULL (a printing key on a real keyboard opened it), `pickers_keyboard_type(first)`. Up from the list's top row calls `open(NULL)`. `close_picker()` clears the opener. The list stays open under the keyboard and `changed` filters it in place (never by reopening it), so Back from the keyboard lands on the list.
- *A cancel* (Back with no change, Back twice after one, Esc likewise, Home, or a remade model) calls no `done`: it reaches the caller through its follower only, and only when the follower heard a change, which then hears the text the field opened with. A caller with no follower hears nothing (fix pass R5).

**What this task decides** (the spec leaves room, or the code forces it; each is pinned by a check):
- **Enter and Backspace are the remote's OK and Back** (`KEYBOARD_NOTE`: "OK (Enter) and Back (Backspace) always keep their own meaning"; the harness drives the remote with them). So a real keyboard's Enter is *Done* and its Backspace deletes **only once a printing key has been typed into this field from a real keyboard**; before that they are OK (type the highlighted key) and Back, as on the remote. The keypad's Enter is always Done. Esc is Back (asks first after a change), never a hotkey. Arrows always go the normal way. This is plan ruling 7, the user's answer of 2026-10-16.
- **The keyboard is a layer, not a picker kind.** It opens alone over a page (a title) or over a list it filters (the app list), which stays drawn in the column; `pickers_active()` is true while either is open, and the keyboard takes the remote's keys first.
- **Drawn across the right of the screen from 60% of its height down** (`KEYBOARD_TOP_RATIO`), over the preview and its caption, with its own label, field, cursor and note (why Done is off, *Back again to discard*, or the pad's shortcuts); the column keeps the page, the list or the browser. Key labels and the field's text go through `draw_text()`'s cache (ruling 7). **⌫, ◀ and ▶ are drawn as shapes**, not glyphs: the bundled Open Sans has none of U+232B, U+25C0, U+25B6, and a fallback font would fail check 90's "no run outside the fallback checks logged a fallback font" in every run that opens the keyboard.
- **The pad's X, Y and Start** act as pressed and are then held as swallowed (`pad_swallowed`, the capture's mechanism), so a Start held past Done never reaches `:settings`. They do not repeat.
- **Type… in the command picker is its last row**, so 3b's rows keep their places; *Type a path…* is the last row of every listing in a path row's browser, and its text starts as the folder on show with a separator. **A typed path's validator never reads the disk** (Fable review I6: it runs on every change, on the main thread, and a partial `\\nas\…` or a hung network mount can block for seconds): it keeps Done off only for an empty path or one config.ini cannot hold. **That it names what the row chooses is checked at Done** (a file; a folder for Folder, with 2 images or more; for Image an image StreamFlex shows that opens, its decode waited out as the browser's OK waits, Fable review M10); a path that fails reopens the keyboard on the same text with the reason in its note (kept while the text is unchanged), the browser still open under it. A typed command must be non-empty and fit config.ini (a binding's is weighed as a hotkey's `#4000003A;` line; the binding's own commit checks again with its real key).
- **`KeyboardLayout`** is `SET_ID_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT`, a `SET_TYPE_CHOICE` (`QWERTY`, `ABC`), the General page's last row (so 3b's checks' row counts down to Quit command hold). The keyboard opens in it, and pressing its layout key stores the new one as a change to that slot, which the save writes.
- **No OS keyboard:** `make_window()` stops text input on each window it makes and logs it; `tests/check-no-text-input.sh` runs from `tests/unit.sh` (on the copy, so a unit mutant that adds a call is caught), and so in CI's *Unit tests (ASan, UBSan)* job and every local unit run. It fails when there is no `src/` folder to read (a wrong root never passes), skips comment lines, those starting with `//`, `/*`, or a `*` followed by a space, a `/` or the line's end (a comment may name the calls it rules out; a line starting `*started = SDL_StartTextInput(w);` is code, Opus re-review m5), and keeps LF endings on a Windows checkout (`.gitattributes`, as `tests/unit.sh` has), since a CRLF copy would end its root in `\r` and read nothing (Fable review M11).
- **Logging for the checks:** `Settings: opened the keyboard for <label> (<layout>)`, `Settings: the keyboard reads '<text>' (cursor <n>)`, `Settings: the keyboard's highlight is on <key>`, `Settings: the keyboard says <note>`, `Settings: the keyboard typed '<c>' (scancode <name>)`, `Settings: Done is off: <why>`, `Settings: the keyboard finished with '<text>'`, `Settings: the keyboard was canceled`, `Settings: the pad's <label> <deletes|types a space|is Done>`, `Settings: the keyboard is drawn at <x>,<y>, <w> x <h>`, `Window: SDL text input is off for the window`.

```c
// A function to end every listing with a "Type a path..." row from now on (3c: a path row's way to the
// keyboard), the listing on show made again with it and the cursor kept. Out of memory, or with a folder
// that can no longer be listed, nothing is offered and the rows stay as they were.
void browser_offer_typing(Browser *browser)
{
    if (browser->typing)
        return;
    browser->typing = true;
    const BrowserRow *row = browser_row(browser, browser->cursor);
    char *selected = row != NULL ? alloc_strdup(row->path) : NULL;
    char *folder = browser->folder != NULL ? alloc_strdup(browser->folder) : NULL;
    bool ok = (row == NULL || selected != NULL) && (browser->folder == NULL || folder != NULL);
    if (ok)
        ok = folder != NULL ? load_folder(browser, folder, selected) == LOAD_DONE : load_places(browser, selected);
    if (!ok)
        browser->typing = false;
    alloc_free(selected);
    alloc_free(folder);
}
```

```c
static bool pad_shortcut(int label, OskCommand *out)
{
```
