```c
// A function to name a key as it shows now: a character key's shifted text while Shift or caps lock is on;
// the shapes' keys by what they stand for
static const char *key_face(const OskKey *key)
{
    if (key == NULL)
        return "";
    switch (key->kind) {
        case OSK_KEY_BACKSPACE:
            return "Backspace";
        case OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT:
            return "Cursor left";
        case OSK_KEY_CURSOR_RIGHT:
            return "Cursor right";
        case OSK_KEY_CHAR:
            return (osk_shift(keyboard) || osk_caps(keyboard)) && key->shifted != NULL ? key->shifted : key->label;
        default:
            return key->label;
    }
}

// A function to give the keyboard's note: "Back again to discard" while it asks, why Done is off, else
// the pad's shortcuts
static const char *keyboard_note(void)
{
    if (osk_asking(keyboard))
        return "Back again to discard";
    if (keyboard_why != NULL)
        return keyboard_why;
    return "X deletes" DOT "Y types a space" DOT "Start is Done";
}

// A function to log the keyboard as it changes: its text and cursor, the highlighted key, the note
static void log_keyboard(void)
{
    char text[sizeof(keyboard_logged)];
    snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "'%s' (cursor %i)", osk_text(keyboard), osk_cursor(keyboard));
    if (strcmp(text, keyboard_logged) != 0) {
        copy_string(keyboard_logged, text, sizeof(keyboard_logged));
        log_debug("Settings: the keyboard reads %s", text);
    }
    int row = 0;
    int column = 0;
    osk_highlight(keyboard, &row, &column);
    const char *face = key_face(osk_key(keyboard, row, column));
    if (strcmp(face, keyboard_key_logged) != 0) {
        copy_string(keyboard_key_logged, face, sizeof(keyboard_key_logged));
        log_debug("Settings: the keyboard's highlight is on %s", face);
    }
    const char *note = keyboard_note();
    if (strcmp(note, keyboard_note_logged) != 0) {
        copy_string(keyboard_note_logged, note, sizeof(keyboard_note_logged));
        log_debug("Settings: the keyboard says %s", note);
    }
}

// A function to let go of the keyboard, saying nothing to whoever opened it
static void close_keyboard(void)
{
    osk_free(keyboard);
    keyboard = NULL;
    keyboard_done = NULL;
    keyboard_context = NULL;
    keyboard_follower = NULL;
    keyboard_pending = false;
    keyboard_told = false;
    keyboard_typed = false;
    keyboard_why = NULL;
    keyboard_logged[0] = '\0';
    keyboard_key_logged[0] = '\0';
    keyboard_note_logged[0] = '\0';
}

// A function to remember the layout the keyboard shows as KeyboardLayout (spec "The choice is remembered"):
// a change to that setting, which the save writes
static void remember_layout(void)
{
    SettingSlot *layout = settings_slot(host.model, SET_ID_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT, -1);
    int now = osk_layout(keyboard) == OSK_ABC ? OSK_ABC : OSK_QWERTY;
    if (layout->value.number == now)
        return;
    SettingValue value = layout->value;
    value.number = now;
    SettingsEvent event = settings_choose_value(host.model, layout, &value);
    host.event(&event);
}

// A function to tell the follower the text now
static void tell_follower(void)
{
    keyboard_pending = false;
    if (keyboard_follower == NULL)
        return;
    keyboard_told = true;
    keyboard_follower(osk_text(keyboard), keyboard_context);
}

// A function to hand the text on at Done: the keyboard closes first, so `done` may open what it likes
static void finish_keyboard(void)
{
    char text[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    copy_string(text, osk_text(keyboard), sizeof(text));
    void (*done)(const char *text, void *context) = keyboard_done;
    void *context = keyboard_context;
    remember_layout();
    close_keyboard();
    log_debug("Settings: the keyboard finished with '%s'", text);
    if (done != NULL)
        done(text, context);
}

// A function to close the keyboard without its text: a follower that heard a change hears the text the
// field opened with, so the preview goes back
static void cancel_keyboard(const char *why)
{
    void (*follower)(const char *text, void *context) = keyboard_told ? keyboard_follower : NULL;
    void *context = keyboard_context;
    remember_layout();
    close_keyboard();
    log_debug("Settings: the keyboard was canceled%s", why);
    if (follower != NULL)
        follower(keyboard_initial, context);
}

// A function to act on what a key did: Done hands the text on, a cancel closes it, a change is followed,
// and Done refused says why in the log
static void keyboard_result(OskResult result, bool done_asked)
{
    switch (result) {
        case OSK_FINISHED:
            finish_keyboard();
            return;
        case OSK_CANCELED:
            cancel_keyboard("");
            return;
        case OSK_CHANGED:
            keyboard_why = osk_why(keyboard);
            keyboard_pending = true;
            keyboard_changed_at = ticks_ms();
            if (keyboard_rest == 0)
                tell_follower();
            break;
        case OSK_NONE:
            if (done_asked && keyboard_why != NULL)
                log_debug("Settings: Done is off: %s", keyboard_why);
            break;
        case OSK_MOVED:
        case OSK_ASKED:
            break;
    }
    if (keyboard != NULL) {
        remember_layout();
        log_keyboard();
    }
}

// A function to press one of the keyboard's commands: the remote's, or the pad's shortcuts
static void keyboard_key(OskCommand key)
{
    int row = 0;
    int column = 0;
    osk_highlight(keyboard, &row, &column);
    const OskKey *at = osk_key(keyboard, row, column);
    bool done_asked = key == OSK_DONE || (key == OSK_OK && at != NULL && at->kind == OSK_KEY_DONE);
    keyboard_result(osk_command(keyboard, key), done_asked);
}

// A function to act on one of the remote's keys while the keyboard is open
static void keyboard_command(const char *command)
{
    OskCommand key = OSK_BACK;
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_UP))
        key = OSK_UP;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_DOWN))
        key = OSK_DOWN;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_LEFT))
        key = OSK_LEFT;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_RIGHT))
        key = OSK_RIGHT;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_SELECT))
        key = OSK_OK;
    keyboard_key(key);
}

// A function to open the keyboard on a field (spec "The on-screen keyboard"): `label` names it ("Title for
// Kodi"), `initial` is its text, `max_bytes` its limit, and `check` its validator, whose reason the note
// gives while Done is off. It opens in the layout KeyboardLayout names, over the page or the list under it,
// which stays open. `done` gets the text at Done, once the keyboard has closed; Back with no change, or
// twice after one, closes it with nothing said. Out of memory it does not open, and says so: the keys stay
// with what is under it. The harness can make it fail (STREAMFLEX_TEST_FAIL=keyboard).
void pickers_open_keyboard(const char *label, const char *initial, int max_bytes, OskCheck check, void *context,
                           void (*done)(const char *text, void *context))
{
    close_keyboard();
    OskLayout layout = settings_slot(host.model, SET_ID_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT, -1)->value.number == OSK_ABC ? OSK_ABC : OSK_QWERTY;
    test_fail("keyboard", true);
    keyboard = osk_create(label, initial, max_bytes, check, context, layout);
    test_fail("keyboard", false);
    if (keyboard == NULL) {
        log_error("Settings: the keyboard cannot open: out of memory");
        return;
    }
    copy_string(keyboard_initial, initial != NULL ? initial : "", sizeof(keyboard_initial));
    keyboard_done = done;
    keyboard_context = context;
    keyboard_why = osk_why(keyboard);
    keyboard_drawn = false;
    log_debug("Settings: opened the keyboard for %s (%s)", label, layout == OSK_ABC ? "ABC" : "QWERTY");
    log_keyboard();
}

// A function to have the keyboard's text followed as it changes (see settings_pickers.h)
void pickers_keyboard_follow(void (*changed)(const char *text, void *context), unsigned int rest_ms)
{
    keyboard_follower = keyboard != NULL ? changed : NULL;
    keyboard_rest = rest_ms;
}

// A function to put text in at the cursor as a real keyboard's key does: from then on Enter is Done
void pickers_keyboard_type(const char *utf8)
{
    if (keyboard == NULL)
        return;
    keyboard_typed = true;
    keyboard_result(osk_insert(keyboard, utf8), false);
}

// A function to say the open picker filters by typing: a printing key on a real keyboard calls `open`,
// with the key's character, while the keyboard is closed. close_picker() clears it.
void pickers_set_typing(void (*open)(const char *first))
{
    typing_opens = open;
}

// A function to take a real keyboard's key while settings are open, before handle_keypress() (spec "A real
// keyboard types into the field"). The character is the layout's own for the key's place, with Shift, Caps
// Lock and AltGr applied (SDL_GetKeyFromScancode() with only those modifiers), never event.key.key, which
// SDL3 gives unshifted. While the keyboard is open, a printing key types it, Esc is Back and the keypad's
// Enter is Done; Enter and Backspace are the remote's OK and Back (KEYBOARD_NOTE) until a printing key has
// been typed into this field, and Done and delete after; every other key, the arrows always, goes on to
// handle_keypress(). While a picker that filters is open and the keyboard is not, a printing key opens it on
// the filter with that character. True when the key was taken.
bool pickers_text_key(SDL_Scancode scancode, SDL_Keymod mod, bool repeat)
{
    char typed[5];
    SDL_Keycode code = SDL_GetKeyFromScancode(scancode, mod & (SDL_KMOD_SHIFT | SDL_KMOD_CAPS | SDL_KMOD_MODE), false);
    bool printing = osk_key_char((unsigned int) code, typed);
    if (keyboard == NULL) {
        if (typing_opens == NULL || !printing || repeat)
            return false;
        log_debug("Settings: '%s' (scancode %s) opens the keyboard on the filter", typed, SDL_GetScancodeName(scancode));
        typing_opens(typed);
        return true;
    }
    switch (scancode) {
        case SDL_SCANCODE_ESCAPE:
            if (!repeat)
                keyboard_key(OSK_BACK);
            return true;
        case SDL_SCANCODE_KP_ENTER:
            if (!repeat)
                keyboard_key(OSK_DONE);
            return true;
        case SDL_SCANCODE_RETURN:
            if (!keyboard_typed)
                return false;
            if (!repeat)
                keyboard_key(OSK_DONE);
            return true;
        case SDL_SCANCODE_BACKSPACE:
            if (!keyboard_typed)
                return false;
            keyboard_key(OSK_BACKSPACE);   // Held, it deletes again, as any field's Backspace does
            return true;
        default:
            break;
    }
    if (!printing)
        return false;
    keyboard_typed = true;
    log_debug("Settings: the keyboard typed '%s' (scancode %s)", typed, SDL_GetScancodeName(scancode));
    keyboard_result(osk_insert(keyboard, typed), false);   // Held, it types again
    return true;
}

// A function to measure the bytes of a text from its start, in the keyboard's font
static int span_width(const char *text, size_t length)
{
    int w = 0;
    int h = 0;
    if (length > 0)
        TTF_GetStringSize(host.font_row, text, length, &w, &h);
    return w;
}

// A function to step from a byte offset past the UTF-8 character there
static size_t next_character(const char *text, size_t at)
{
    do {
        at++;
    } while (text[at] != '\0' && ((unsigned char) text[at] & 0xC0) == 0x80);
    return at;
}

// A function to draw the field: its text through the settings' text cache (plan ruling 7), scrolled so the
// cursor stays in view, and the cursor
static void draw_field(const SDL_Rect *field, int pad)
{
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, ALPHA_FIELD);
    fill_rect(renderer, field);
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, ALPHA_EDGE);
    outline_rect(renderer, field);
    const char *text = osk_text(keyboard);
    size_t cursor = (size_t) osk_cursor(keyboard);
    int room = field->w - 2 * pad;
    size_t start = 0;
    while (start < cursor && span_width(text + start, cursor - start) > room)
        start = next_character(text, start);
    int line = TTF_GetFontHeight(host.font_row);
    int text_y = field->y + (field->h - line) / 2;
    host.text(host.font_row, text + start, field->x + pad, text_y, room, 255, false);
    SDL_Rect caret = { field->x + pad + span_width(text + start, cursor - start), text_y, 2, line };
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF);
    fill_rect(renderer, &caret);
}

// A function to fill a triangle, for the cursor keys' faces
static void fill_triangle(float x1, float y1, float x2, float y2, float x3, float y3)
{
    SDL_FColor white = { 1.0F, 1.0F, 1.0F, 1.0F };
    SDL_Vertex corners[3] = {
        { { x1, y1 }, white, { 0.0F, 0.0F } }, { { x2, y2 }, white, { 0.0F, 0.0F } }, { { x3, y3 }, white, { 0.0F, 0.0F } }
    };
    SDL_RenderGeometry(renderer, NULL, corners, 3, NULL, 0);
}

// A function to draw a key's face: its text centered, or, for backspace and the text cursor's keys, a shape
// (the settings' font has no glyph for U+232B, U+25C0 or U+25B6, and a fallback font would be needed for one)
static void draw_key_face(const OskKey *key, const SDL_Rect *box)
{
    int cx = box->x + box->w / 2;
    int cy = box->y + box->h / 2;
    int half = box->h / 5;
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF);
    if (key->kind == OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT || key->kind == OSK_KEY_CURSOR_RIGHT) {
        float tip = (float) (key->kind == OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT ? cx - half : cx + half);
        float back = (float) (key->kind == OSK_KEY_CURSOR_LEFT ? cx + half : cx - half);
        fill_triangle(tip, (float) cy, back, (float) (cy - half), back, (float) (cy + half));
        return;
    }
    if (key->kind == OSK_KEY_BACKSPACE) {
        // An arrow-shaped outline pointing left, with an x in it
        int left = cx - half;
        int right = cx + 2 * half;
        int tip = cx - 2 * half;
        draw_line(renderer, tip, cy, left, cy - half);
        draw_line(renderer, left, cy - half, right, cy - half);
        draw_line(renderer, right, cy - half, right, cy + half);
        draw_line(renderer, right, cy + half, left, cy + half);
        draw_line(renderer, left, cy + half, tip, cy);
        int x = cx + half / 2;
        int arm = half / 2;
        draw_line(renderer, x - arm, cy - arm, x + arm, cy + arm);
        draw_line(renderer, x - arm, cy + arm, x + arm, cy - arm);
        return;
    }
    const char *face = key_face(key);
    int w = 0;
    int h = 0;
    TTF_GetStringSize(host.font_row, face, 0, &w, &h);
    host.text(host.font_row, face, box->x + (box->w - (w < box->w ? w : box->w)) / 2, cy - h / 2, box->w, 255, false);
}

// A function to measure a row of keys, in key widths
static float row_units(int row)
{
    float units = 0.0F;
    for (int c = 0; c < osk_row_length(keyboard, row); c++)
        units += osk_key(keyboard, row, c)->width;
    return units;
}

// A function to draw the keys: each row centered on the widest, as osk.c moves between them (so Up and
// Down land where they look to), the highlighted key filled and outlined, Shift filled while it is on and
// outlined while it is caps lock
static void draw_keys(int x, int y, int w, int h)
{
    int rows = osk_rows(keyboard);
    float widest = 0.0F;
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++)
        widest = row_units(r) > widest ? row_units(r) : widest;
    if (widest <= 0.0F || rows == 0 || h <= 0)
        return;
    float unit = (float) w / widest;
    int key_h = h / rows;
    int lit_row = 0;
    int lit_column = 0;
    osk_highlight(keyboard, &lit_row, &lit_column);
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
        float left = (float) x + (widest - row_units(r)) * unit / 2.0F;
        for (int c = 0; c < osk_row_length(keyboard, r); c++) {
            const OskKey *key = osk_key(keyboard, r, c);
            SDL_Rect box = { (int) left + 2, y + r * key_h + 2, (int) (key->width * unit) - 4, key_h - 4 };
            left += key->width * unit;
            bool lit = r == lit_row && c == lit_column;
            bool shift = key->kind == OSK_KEY_SHIFT && (osk_shift(keyboard) || osk_caps(keyboard));
            SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, lit || shift ? ALPHA_KEY_LIT : ALPHA_KEY);
            fill_rect(renderer, &box);
            if (lit || (key->kind == OSK_KEY_SHIFT && osk_caps(keyboard))) {
                SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, ALPHA_EDGE);
                outline_rect(renderer, &box);
            }
            draw_key_face(key, &box);
        }
    }
}

// A function to draw the keyboard over the bottom of the preview (spec "Where it appears"), in the
// rectangle the screen gives: the field's label, the field with its cursor, the note (why Done is off,
// "Back again to discard", or the pad's shortcuts), then the keys. The log says once where it is drawn.
void pickers_draw_keyboard(int x, int y, int w, int h)
{
    if (keyboard == NULL || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
        return;
    if (!keyboard_drawn) {
        keyboard_drawn = true;
        log_debug("Settings: the keyboard is drawn at %i,%i, %i x %i", x, y, w, h);
    }
    int pad = host.margin / 2;
    int small = TTF_GetFontHeight(host.font_small);
    int line = TTF_GetFontHeight(host.font_row);
    SDL_Rect panel = { x, y, w, h };
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, PANEL.r, PANEL.g, PANEL.b, PANEL.a);
    fill_rect(renderer, &panel);
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, ALPHA_PANEL_EDGE);
    outline_rect(renderer, &panel);
    int top = y + pad;
    host.text(host.font_small, osk_label(keyboard), x + pad, top, w - 2 * pad, ALPHA_LABEL, false);
    top += small + pad / 2;
    SDL_Rect field = { x + pad, top, w - 2 * pad, line + pad };
    draw_field(&field, pad);
    top += field.h + pad / 2;
    host.text(host.font_small, keyboard_note(), x + pad, top, w - 2 * pad, 255, false);
    top += small + pad;
    draw_keys(x + pad, top, w - 2 * pad, y + h - pad - top);
}

// A function to say why a typed command cannot be held by config.ini, or NULL when it can: a setting's is
// weighed under its own key, a binding's as a hotkey's line holds it (its commit checks again, under the
// key it gets)
static const char *check_command(const char *text, void *context)
{
    TypedCommand *typed = context;
    char value[BINDINGS_VALUE_MAX];
    if (text[0] == '\0')
        return "Type a command";
    if (typed->slot != NULL)
        snprintf(value, sizeof(value), "%s", text);
    else
        snprintf(value, sizeof(value), HOTKEY_PREFIX "%s", text);
    const char *why = inidoc_check(typed->key, value);
    if (why == NULL)
        return NULL;
    snprintf(typed->why, sizeof(typed->why), "config.ini can't hold this command: %s", why);
    return typed->why;
}

// A function to take a typed command, as the list picker takes a chosen one
static void command_typed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    TypedCommand *typed = context;
    if (typed->slot == NULL) {
        SettingsEvent event = settings_bind_command(host.model, text);
        host.event(&event);
        return;
    }
    SettingValue value = typed->slot->value;
    value.inherit = false;
    copy_string(value.text, text, sizeof(value.text));
    SettingsEvent event = settings_choose_value(host.model, typed->slot, &value);
    if (event.kind == SETTINGS_EVENT_NONE)
        log_debug("Settings: [%s] %s is unchanged", typed->slot->def->section, typed->slot->def->key);
    else
        host.event(&event);
}

// A function to open the keyboard on the command the list picker chooses for (a setting's, or the binding
// page's), in place of its rows (3c: "Type..."), the command as it is now to start
static void type_command(void)
{
    char label[96];
    char initial[BINDINGS_COMMAND_MAX];
    typed_command.slot = slot;
    if (slot != NULL) {
        snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "Command for %s", slot->def->label);
        copy_string(initial, slot->value.inherit ? "" : slot->value.text, sizeof(initial));
        copy_string(typed_command.key, slot->def->key, sizeof(typed_command.key));
    }
    else {
        snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "Command for the binding");
        copy_string(initial, settings_binding_command(host.model), sizeof(initial));
        copy_string(typed_command.key, "Hotkey99999", sizeof(typed_command.key));
    }
    close_picker();
    pickers_open_keyboard(label, initial, BINDINGS_COMMAND_MAX - 1, check_command, &typed_command, command_typed);
}
```

```c
// A function to act on a key while a picker or the keyboard is open. Home and the key that opened settings
// leave the keyboard without its text and the picker without choosing (the color picker puts its color back
// first, even from the hex editor, where Back would only leave the editor), then close settings as the
// pages would. The keyboard, open over a picker or alone, takes the other keys first.
void pickers_command(const char *command)
{
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_HOME) || MATCH(command, SCMD_SETTINGS)) {
        if (keyboard != NULL)
            cancel_keyboard(" as settings close");
        if (kind == PICKER_COLOR)
            put_color_back();
        close_picker();
        SettingsEvent event = settings_command(host.model, MATCH(command, SCMD_HOME) ? SETTINGS_HOME : SETTINGS_CLOSE);
        host.event(&event);
        return;
    }
    if (!MATCH(command, SCMD_UP) && !MATCH(command, SCMD_DOWN) && !MATCH(command, SCMD_LEFT) &&
        !MATCH(command, SCMD_RIGHT) && !MATCH(command, SCMD_SELECT) && !MATCH(command, SCMD_BACK)) {
        log_debug("Settings: ignoring '%s' while a picker is open", command);
        return;
    }
    if (keyboard != NULL)
        keyboard_command(command);
    else if (kind == PICKER_LIST || kind == PICKER_FONT)
        list_command(command);
    else if (kind == PICKER_COLOR)
        color_command(command);
}

// A function to close the keyboard and the picker on show as Back closes them at their top, the color
// picker putting its color back first; settings stay open on the page they opened from. A new screen size
// does this (they were measured when they opened), and so does a remade settings model.
void pickers_cancel(void)
{
    if (keyboard != NULL)
        cancel_keyboard("");
    if (kind == PICKER_COLOR)
        put_color_back();
    close_picker();
}
```

```c
void pickers_path(char *out, size_t size)
{

// A function to give the key hint for the picker on show, one line short enough for the column at

const char *pickers_hint(void)
{

        return "Arrows edit the digits" DOT "OK keeps" DOT "Back returns";

    if (kind == PICKER_FONT && list == NULL)
        return "Back cancels";
    return "Left and right page" DOT "OK chooses" DOT "Back cancels";
}
```

Before `handle_browser_command()` (`:1075`) add:

```c
static char path_why[320];                     // Why a typed path cannot be chosen, written for the keyboard's note
static char path_refused[BROWSER_PATH_MAX];    // The typed path Done last refused, which the keyboard reopened on...
static char path_refused_why[128];             // ...and why: its note says so until the text changes

// A function to say why a typed path cannot be chosen for a path row, or NULL when it can, as it is typed: it
// must not be empty, and config.ini must hold it, as the browser's rows are checked. It never reads the disk
// (Fable review I6): it runs on every change, on the main thread, where a partial network path's server or
// a hung mount could block for seconds; what the path names is checked at Done (path_typed()). The text
// Done just refused keeps its reason here until it is changed.
static const char *path_problem(const char *text, void *context)
{
    SettingSlot *slot = context;
    if (text[0] == '\0')
        return "Type a path";
    const char *why = check_path(text, slot);
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(path_why, sizeof(path_why), "config.ini can't hold this path: %s", why);
        return path_why;
    }
    return path_refused[0] != '\0' && strcmp(text, path_refused) == 0 ? path_refused_why : NULL;
}

// A function to say why a typed path names nothing the row can choose, or NULL when it does: a file; a
// folder of 2 images or more for Folder; for Image an image StreamFlex shows that opens, its decode asked
// for and waited out as the browser's OK waits for the one highlighted (Fable review M10). At Done only.
static const char *path_missing(const char *text, const SettingSlot *slot)
{
    if (slot->def->id == SET_ID_SLIDESHOW_DIRECTORY)
        return !fileio_is_dir(text) ? "No folder is there" : count_images(text) < 2 ? "A slideshow needs 2 or more images" : NULL;
    if (!fileio_is_file(text))
        return "No file is there";
    if (slot->def->id != SET_ID_BACKGROUND_IMAGE)
        return NULL;
    if (!browser_is_image(text))
        return "That is not an image StreamFlex shows (.jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp)";
    want_preview_image(text);
    if (decode_thread != NULL && strcmp(decode_path, text) != 0)
        poll_decode(true);   // Another image's decode first; this one's starts as it ends
    if (decode_thread != NULL && strcmp(decode_path, text) == 0) {
        log_debug("Settings: Done waited for the decode of %s", text);
        poll_decode(true);
    }
    return strcmp(text, broken_path) == 0 ? CANNOT_OPEN : NULL;
}

static void open_path_keyboard(SettingSlot *slot, const char *initial);

// A function to take a typed path as the browser takes a chosen one, once it names what the row chooses;
// else the keyboard reopens on the same text, its note saying why, over the browser still open
static void path_typed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    SettingSlot *slot = context;
    const char *why = path_missing(text, slot);
    if (why != NULL) {
        copy_string(path_refused, text, sizeof(path_refused));
        copy_string(path_refused_why, why, sizeof(path_refused_why));
        log_debug("Settings: the typed path %s is refused: %s", text, why);
        open_path_keyboard(slot, text);
        return;
    }
    path_refused[0] = '\0';
    close_browser();
    log_debug("Settings: chose %s", text);
    SettingsEvent event = settings_choose(model, slot, text);
    handle_event(&event);
}

// A function to open the keyboard on a path for a path row's setting, the browser staying open under it
static void open_path_keyboard(SettingSlot *slot, const char *initial)
{
    char label[96];
    snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "Path for %s", slot->def->label);
    pickers_open_keyboard(label, initial, BROWSER_PATH_MAX - 1, path_problem, slot, path_typed);
}

// A function to open the keyboard on a path for the browser's setting (3c, "Type a path..."), starting as
// the folder on show with a separator; the browser stays open under it until a path it takes
static void type_path(void)
{
    const BrowserRow *row = browser_row(browser, browser_cursor(browser));
    char initial[BROWSER_PATH_MAX] = "";
    if (row != NULL && row->path[0] != '\0') {
        size_t length = strlen(row->path);
        bool backslash = strchr(row->path, '\\') != NULL && strchr(row->path, '/') == NULL;
        bool ends = fileio_is_separator(row->path[length - 1]);
        snprintf(initial, sizeof(initial), "%s%s", row->path, ends ? "" : backslash ? "\\" : "/");
    }
    path_refused[0] = '\0';
    open_path_keyboard(browser_slot, initial);
}
```

`path_typed()` runs once the keyboard has closed (Task 12's `finish_keyboard()`), so it may open the keyboard again. `want_preview_image()`, `poll_decode()`, `decode_thread`, `decode_path`, `broken_path` and `CANNOT_OPEN` (`:129`) are master's, above `handle_browser_command()`; the typed image's decode shows it in the preview, as a highlighted row's does.

- [ ] **Step 9: The source check, in the unit run**

Create `tests/check-no-text-input.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# The no-OS-keyboard rule (spec, "No OS keyboard, ever"): StreamFlex never starts SDL's text input, which is
# what brings up GNOME's, KDE's and Windows' screen keyboards, and so has no handler for the text events only
# text input sends. This fails when any of them appears anywhere under src/ outside a comment line (one that
# starts with //, /*, or a * followed by a space, a / or the line's end, which may name the calls it rules
# out; a line such as *started = SDL_StartTextInput(w); is code), and when there is no src/ to read.
#   bash tests/check-no-text-input.sh [ROOT]   ROOT: the source tree; this file's parent folder by default
set -u
root=${1:-$(dirname "$0")/..}
if [ ! -d "$root/src" ]; then
    echo "NO SOURCE TREE: $root/src is not a folder, so nothing was checked"
    exit 1
fi
found=$(grep -rnE 'SDL_StartTextInput|SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT|SDL_EVENT_TEXT_EDITING' "$root/src" \
        | grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(//|/\*|\*([[:space:]/]|$))')
if [ -n "$found" ]; then
    echo "SDL TEXT INPUT FOUND: StreamFlex must never start text input (spec, \"No OS keyboard, ever\")"
    echo "$found"
    exit 1
fi
echo "No SDL text input in src/"
```

```bash
# The on-screen keyboard (3c, spec "The on-screen keyboard" and "No OS keyboard, ever"), through the ways in
# 3b's pages gain: the command picker's Type... (Startup command, Quit command) and a path row's Type a
# path... (Mappings file). Typing on its keys with the remote, on a real keyboard with Shift, and under a
# German layout with AltGr and a dead key; the pad's X, Y and Start; Back asking first after a change; Done
# off with the reason; the layout kept as KeyboardLayout; a keyboard that cannot open; and SDL's text input
# stopped on the window. The Tiles pages' ways in (titles, names, the app list's filter) are check 82's.
# Not timing-sensitive: every key waits for its frame, xdotool type's keys reach the launcher in order, and every result is read from the log's lines or the saved file, never from a clock

ARROW=$(printf ' \xE2\x80\xBA ')
K84_DOT=$(printf '\xC2\xB7')

K84_QUIT="Menu Return Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Return Right Right Right Return"

k84_type_semicolon() { xdotool type --delay 60 'a ;b'; }
k84_type_z() { xdotool type --delay 60 'z'; }
k84_type_new() { xdotool type --delay 60 'new.txt'; }
k84_type_gone() { xdotool type --delay 60 'gone.txt'; }
k84_altgr_q() { xdotool keydown ISO_Level3_Shift; xdotool key q; xdotool keyup ISO_Level3_Shift; }
k84_press() { : > /tmp/pad-k84; sleep 1; rm -f /tmp/pad-k84; sleep 1; }

# On its own keys: o (Right x8 from q), k (Down), then Down, Down, Right, Right to Done. The keyboard covers
# the bottom 40% (y = 648 of 1080), its hint is the keyboard's, and the window's text input is off

CFG=$cfg run_keys f84-osk $K84_STARTUP Right Right Right Right Right Right Right Right Return Down Return \

ok=1
log=$out/f84-osk.log

    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads 'o' (cursor 1)" "$log" \

grep -E "Settings: (opened the keyboard|the keyboard|the key hint)|Window: SDL text input" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# The ABC key switches the layout; the keyboard opens in it next time, and KeyboardLayout=ABC is saved
cfg=$(writable_config f84-keys)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f84-layout $K84_STARTUP Down Down Down Left Left Return BackSpace Return Right Right Right Return \
    BackSpace Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f84-layout.log
grep -qx 'KeyboardLayout=ABC' "$cfg" && grep -q 'Settings: \[General\] KeyboardLayout QWERTY -> ABC' "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: opened the keyboard for Command for Startup command (ABC)" "$log" \
    && ! grep -q '^StartupCmd' "$cfg" && ran_clean f84-layout && ok=0
result "keyboard: the ABC key switches the layout, which is kept as KeyboardLayout (exit $(cat "$out/f84-layout.code"))" $ok

# The pad (STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD holds the button STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD_BUTTON names while the file is there):
# Start is Done, and a Start held past Done never reaches :settings, which would close settings unsaved by
# this run's Menu; X deletes; Y types a space. OK on the q key types q; z comes from the real keyboard.
rm -f /tmp/pad-k84
cfg=$(writable_config f84-pad)
STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD=/tmp/pad-k84 STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD_BUTTON=start WAIT_FOR='Gamepad connected' CFG=$cfg \
    run_keys f84-padstart $K84_STARTUP Return +k84_press Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f84-padstart.log
grep -qx 'StartupCmd=q' "$cfg" && grep -q "Settings: the pad's ButtonStart is Done" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard finished with 'q'" "$log" && ! grep -q 'Gamepad ButtonStart detected' "$log" \
    && ran_clean f84-padstart && ok=0
result "keyboard: the pad's Start is Done, and never reaches :settings (exit $(cat "$out/f84-padstart.code"))" $ok

rm -f /tmp/pad-k84
cfg=$(writable_config f84-pad)
STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD=/tmp/pad-k84 STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD_BUTTON=x WAIT_FOR='Gamepad connected' CFG=$cfg \
    run_keys f84-padx $K84_STARTUP Return Return +k84_press +k84_type_z Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f84-padx.log
grep -qx 'StartupCmd=qz' "$cfg" && grep -q "Settings: the pad's ButtonX deletes" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads 'qq' (cursor 2)" "$log" && ran_clean f84-padx && ok=0
result "keyboard: the pad's X deletes (exit $(cat "$out/f84-padx.code"))" $ok

rm -f /tmp/pad-k84
cfg=$(writable_config f84-pad)
STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD=/tmp/pad-k84 STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD_BUTTON=y WAIT_FOR='Gamepad connected' CFG=$cfg \
    run_keys f84-pady $K84_STARTUP Return +k84_press +k84_type_z Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f84-pady.log
grep -qx 'StartupCmd=q z' "$cfg" && grep -q "Settings: the pad's ButtonY types a space" "$log" && ran_clean f84-pady && ok=0
result "keyboard: the pad's Y types a space (exit $(cat "$out/f84-pady.code"))" $ok
rm -f /tmp/pad-k84

# A path row's Type a path...: the browser's last row opens the keyboard on the folder on show, and a file
# typed there is chosen as one chosen in the list
rm -rf "$TESTER_HOME/k84"; mkdir -p "$TESTER_HOME/k84"
printf '# no mappings\n' > "$TESTER_HOME/k84/old.txt"; printf '# no mappings\n' > "$TESTER_HOME/k84/new.txt"
chown -R tester:tester "$TESTER_HOME/k84"
cfg=$(writable_config f84-paths)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f84-path Menu Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Return Down Return Down Down Return \
    Right Right Right Return +k84_type_new Return Menu BackSpace
ok=1
log=$out/f84-path.log
grep -qx 'ControllerMappingsFile=/home/tester/k84/new.txt' "$cfg" \
    && grep -q "Settings: opened the keyboard for Path for Mappings file" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads '/home/tester/k84/' (cursor 17)" "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: chose /home/tester/k84/new.txt' "$log" && ran_clean f84-path && ok=0
result "keyboard: Type a path... in a path row's browser types the path, which saves (exit $(cat "$out/f84-path.code"))" $ok

# A typed path that is not there: Done is on while it is typed (the validator reads no disk), Done refuses
# it, and the keyboard reopens on the same text with the reason, the browser under it; Esc then cancels at
# once (no change), and nothing is saved
cfg=$(writable_config f84-paths)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f84-pathgone Menu Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Return Down Return Down Down Return \
    Right Right Right Return +k84_type_gone Return Escape Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f84-pathgone.log
! grep -q 'Settings: Done is off: No file is there' "$log" \
    && grep -qx 'Settings: the typed path /home/tester/k84/gone.txt is refused: No file is there' "$log" \
    && [ "$(grep -c 'Settings: opened the keyboard for Path for Mappings file' "$log")" = 2 ] \
    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads '/home/tester/k84/gone.txt' (cursor 25)" "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: the keyboard says No file is there' "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: nothing changed' "$log" && cmp -s "$FX/f84-paths.ini" "$cfg" && ran_clean f84-pathgone && ok=0
result "keyboard: a typed path that is not there is refused at Done, the keyboard reopening on it with why (exit $(cat "$out/f84-pathgone.code"))" $ok

# A keyboard that cannot open (out of memory) says so, and the keys stay with the page
cfg=$(writable_config f84-keys)
STREAMFLEX_TEST_FAIL=keyboard CFG=$cfg run_keys f84-nomem $K84_STARTUP Down Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f84-nomem.log
grep -q 'Settings: the keyboard cannot open: out of memory' "$log" \
    && sed -n '/the keyboard cannot open/,$p' "$log" | grep -q "Settings: the cursor's row reads Quit command" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: nothing changed' "$log" && ran_clean f84-nomem && ok=0
result "keyboard: a keyboard that cannot open says so, and the page keeps the keys (exit $(cat "$out/f84-nomem.code"))" $ok
```

`text-input-started` is a unit-form entry the source check catches before ctest runs: unit.sh prints that line and exits 1. `text-input-starred` pins the check's comment filter (Opus re-review m5): its call sits on a code line that starts with `*&`, which a filter skipping every line that starts with `*` would pass over as a comment, and which this one finds, since only a `*` followed by a space, a `/` or the line's end marks a comment line; `no-text-input-control` is its control too. `browser_offer_typing()`'s early return when typing is already offered has no mutant: without it a second call only makes the same listing again (each listing is made whole, never appended to), so the mutant is equivalent; it saves a reload, nothing else. The real-keyboard character rule (`SDL_GetKeyFromScancode` with the three modifiers) has no mutant here: `xdotool type` cannot be expressed as `mutants.py` keys, and `f84-real` and `f84-german` pin it (dropping the mask types `k`, `3` and `1`; using `event.key.key` would type `y` for the German Y key). The pad's `pad_swallowed` after Start has no mutant either (its failure closes settings, which no expected line can tell from a run that saved): `f84-padstart`'s `! grep -q 'Gamepad ButtonStart detected'` pins it. Record both in the ledger as named survivors. A typed path's checks at Done are pinned only by check 84's `f84-pathgone` (the driver cannot type a path): dropping `path_typed()`'s refusal saves `gone.txt`, and a validator that read the disk again would log `Done is off: No file is there`; write them into the ledger as pinned by check 84. Unexercised by design: the typed Image path's decode wait and its `CANNOT_OPEN` refusal (no check types an Image path), and a typed folder with fewer than 2 images; named survivors.

### Task 10: Settings: the Tiles page, a tile's page, Add, Remove and its confirm page, rename, save and Discard

**Split in two, each ending green:**
- **Task 10a** (this section): the pages in the settings model (`SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES`, `_TILE`, `_ADD`, `_SPECIAL`, `_REMOVE_MENU`), a tile's title, a new submenu's name, the special commands, Remove and its confirm page, a submenu's rename with every binding and command that named it, the save through `config_save_with()` and Discard back to the snapshot.
- **Task 10b**: the app list picker over Task 7's scan, *Browse for a program ›* with its filter, and a tile's *Command ›*; check 81 (Task 7's scan, reached through *Add › App ›*) moves here.

**Order: Task 12 runs before Task 10a.** A tile's *Title* and *Submenu ›* open the keyboard (`pickers_open_keyboard()`), which Task 12 lands; Task 12's own ways in are 3b's (the command picker's and the path rows' *Type…*), so it is whole without the Tiles pages. The build's order becomes 1-9, **12, 10a, 10b, 11**, 13-18; nothing else moves.

**Where the pages' indexes come from.** A page's `menu` is the settings model's menu index (`state->names`); the menus model's menu is found by that name (`edit_index()`), never assumed to sit at the same index, though Task 4 keeps both lists in one order. A tile's index is the menus model's.

**What this task decides** (each pinned by a test):
- **The Menu page** of a menu gains *Tiles ›* (`N tiles`) after its three grid rows, before its note; only while the menus model was read. *All menus* has none.
- **The Tiles page:** *Add ›* first, then a row per tile in model order. A tile that opens a menu the model has is a link (›) whose value is its menu's tile count; any other tile is a row whose value is its command as 3b labels commands; OK on either opens the tile's page. An empty menu's only row is *Empty: Add ›*. Past 62 tiles the rest are counted in a note (*N more tiles have no room here: hold OK on one in the menu to edit it*, Task 14's way; 13a opens such a tile's page directly). The preview highlights the tile under the Tiles page's cursor (none on *Add ›*).
- **Where a new tile goes** (user ruling 2026-10-16, Fable review C3; spec "A new tile goes after the highlighted tile, or at the end"): **the Tiles page's *Add ›* puts it at the end; a tile's page has *Add after this tile ›*, which puts it right after that tile.** The Tiles page remembers no tile: a remote reaches *Add ›* only by passing every tile row above the one it left, so a remembered tile could only ever be the first.
- **A tile's page** has *Title*, *Add after this tile ›* and *Remove* here; Task 10b adds *Command ›* after Title, Task 11 *Move* and *Move to menu ›* before *Add after this tile ›*, Task 13 *Icon ›* after Title. Checks reach Remove as the last row (Down eight times) and *Add after this tile ›* one above it, so each later row leaves them as they are.
- **Add ›** has *Submenu ›* and *Special ›* here; Task 10b puts *App ›* and *Browse for a program ›* above them.
- **Special ›** lists Home, Back, Settings, Sleep, Restart, Shut down and Quit; each new tile takes that title, the library icon `home`, `back`, `settings`, `sleep`, `restart`, `power` or `quit`, and the command `:home`, `:back`, `:settings`, `:sleep`, `:restart`, `:shutdown` or `:quit` (`launcher.h:37-43`).
- **A new submenu** takes the library icon `folder`; its name is checked by `menuedit_check_name()` and its tile's line by `menuedit_check_tile()` before Done.
- **A submenu tile's title is its menu's name.** OK on *Title* renames the menu (`menuedit_rename_menu()`) and sets the tile's own title to the new name even when it had its own; every binding (`[Hotkeys]`, `[Gamepad]`) and the Startup and Quit commands holding exactly `:submenu <Old>` are rewritten through the bindings model and the slots (Known integration work 1). A plain tile's title is shown in the preview as it is typed, once it rests 300 ms; a submenu's rename waits for Done (it remakes the settings model, which would close the keyboard).
- **Remove:** a plain tile goes at once, back to the Tiles page on the tile now in its place. A tile that opens a menu the model has asks first: *Remove <Name> and its N tiles* (grayed with *The default menu can't be removed* for the default menu), and *Remove only this tile* only while another tile opens that menu.
- **Every change** reaches the launcher as `SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS`, which the screen answers with `settings_menus_changed()`; a rename's also re-applies the bindings and the Startup and Quit slots.
- **The save** passes `menuedit_apply()` to `config_save_with()` only when the menus model changed; its notes are logged as 3b's are (`Settings: not saved as asked: ...`), but a tile's "changed meanwhile" note without 3b's words on keys (*where two lines bind one key or button, the first in the file is the one that runs*): a tile written as a new line beside the hand's is one more tile, which the menu shows (Fable review M6). The screen tells the menus model's notes from the bindings' by the notes `menuedit_apply()` added. Nothing is written when nothing changed, menus included.
- **Discard** puts the menus model back to a copy of the snapshot taken as settings opened (after Task 4's hand-edit catch-up, before its test hook), before the slots are applied, then deletes every file Task 13 registered through `settings_note_plated()` that no tile uses. *Leave without saving* deletes nothing (spec: only Discard deletes).
- **Task 4's `test_remodel()`** hands the model a fake `MenuEdit` pointer; the Menu page now reads the menus model, so the test is given a real one (Step 1).

```c
// The menus the Tiles pages' tests start from: Main, with a submenu tile and a plain one, and Games
static const char *const TILES_TEXT =
    "[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[Main]\nEntry1=Games;games;:submenu Games\nEntry2=Kodi;kodi;kodi --standalone\n\n"
    "[Games]\nRows=3\nEntry1=Retro;emulators;:back\nEntry2=Pong;games;:back\n";

// A function to give a model the menus model of a config's text, with its default menu; the caller frees
// it after the model
static MenuEdit *with_menus(SettingsState *state, const char *text, const char *default_menu)
{
    IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, strlen(text));
    MenuEdit *edit = menuedit_load(doc, default_menu);
    inidoc_free(doc);
    CHECK(edit != NULL);
    settings_set_menus(state, edit);
    return edit;
}

// A function to open a menu's Tiles page from the top page: Menus, the menu, Tiles
static void open_tiles(SettingsState *state, const char *menu)
{
    open_page(state, "Menus");
    cursor_to(state, menu);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Tiles");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
}

// A function to get a tile of the menus model; NULL when there is none
static const MenuTile *tile_of(const MenuEdit *edit, const char *menu, int t)
{
    const MenuEditMenu *m = menuedit_menu(edit, menuedit_find(edit, menu));
    return m != NULL && t >= 0 && t < m->count ? &m->tiles[t] : NULL;
}

// A function to test the Tiles pages (3c): the Menu page's Tiles row; the Tiles page's rows, a submenu tile a
// link; the tile the preview highlights, the one under the cursor; the Tiles page's Add, at the end, through
// the Special page; a tile's page, its title and its removal
static void test_tiles_pages(void)
{
    SettingsState *state = open_model();
    MenuEdit *edit = with_menus(state, TILES_TEXT, "Main");
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    char path[256];
    char label[64];
    open_page(state, "Menus");
    cursor_to(state, "Main");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    const SettingsRow *tiles = row_labeled(state, rows, "Tiles");
    CHECK_INT(tiles->kind, SETTINGS_ROW_LINK);
    CHECK_STR(tiles->value, "2 tiles");
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 5);   // Rows, Columns, Largest button, Tiles, the note
    CHECK_INT(rows[4].kind, SETTINGS_ROW_NOTE);
    cursor_to(state, "Tiles");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "Main" ARROW "Tiles");
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 3);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Add");
    CHECK_INT(rows[0].kind, SETTINGS_ROW_LINK);
    CHECK_STR(rows[1].label, "Games");
    CHECK_INT(rows[1].kind, SETTINGS_ROW_LINK);
    CHECK_STR(rows[1].value, "2 tiles");
    CHECK_STR(rows[2].label, "Kodi");
    CHECK_INT(rows[2].kind, SETTINGS_ROW_ACTION);
    setting_command_label("kodi --standalone", label, sizeof(label));
    CHECK_STR(rows[2].value, label);

    // The preview shows Main, the tile under the cursor highlighted; Add is about none
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_menu(state), 0);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_tile(state), -1);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_DOWN);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_tile(state), 0);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_UP);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_tile(state), -1);

    // Add, Special, Sleep: the Tiles page's Add puts it at the end, wherever its cursor has been, with the
    // special's title, icon and command
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ADD);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "Main" ARROW "Tiles" ARROW "Add");
    cursor_to(state, "Special");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_SPECIAL);
    static const char *const specials[] = { "Home", "Back", "Settings", "Sleep", "Restart", "Shut down", "Quit" };
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 7);
    for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++)
        CHECK_STR(rows[i].label, specials[i]);
    cursor_to(state, "Sleep");
    SettingsEvent event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(event.menu, 0);
    CHECK_INT(event.tile, 2);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    const MenuTile *sleep = tile_of(edit, "Main", 2);
    CHECK(sleep != NULL && sleep->key == NULL);
    CHECK_STR(sleep->title, "Sleep");
    CHECK_STR(sleep->icon, "sleep");
    CHECK_STR(sleep->command, ":sleep");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 1)->title, "Kodi");
    settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    CHECK_STR(rows[settings_cursor(state)].label, "Sleep");
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_tile(state), 2);
    CHECK(settings_menus_edited(state));
    CHECK(!settings_any_changed(state));                           // The slots and bindings alone

    // The tile's page: its title through the keyboard's event, and Remove, back on the tile now in its place
    // (the last, Kodi)
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "Main" ARROW "Tiles" ARROW "Sleep");
    CHECK_STR(row_labeled(state, rows, "Title")->value, "Sleep");
    CHECK_INT(row_labeled(state, rows, "Add after this tile")->kind, SETTINGS_ROW_LINK);
    cursor_to(state, "Title");
    event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_TYPE_TITLE);
    CHECK_INT(event.menu, 0);
    CHECK_INT(event.tile, 2);
    CHECK_STR(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 2, "a;b"), "A title can't contain ;");
    CHECK(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 2, "Nap") == NULL);
    event = settings_set_title(state, 0, 2, "Nap");
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK(!event.rebind);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 2)->title, "Nap");
    event = settings_set_title(state, 0, 2, "");
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(settings_notice(state), "Type a title");
    cursor_to(state, "Remove");
    event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK(tile_of(edit, "Main", 2) == NULL);
    settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    CHECK_STR(rows[settings_cursor(state)].label, "Kodi");
    CHECK(!settings_menus_edited(state));                          // Back as it was read

    // The top page's Discard is enabled by a menus change alone
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Remove");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
        settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TOP);
    CHECK(row_labeled(state, rows, "Discard changes")->enabled);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}

// A function to test an empty menu's Tiles page, and a new submenu through the keyboard's events: its name
// checked, made where the Add page puts a tile (in an empty menu, the first), with the folder icon
static void test_empty_menu_and_new_submenu(void)
{
    SettingsState *state = open_model();
    MenuEdit *edit = with_menus(state, "[Main]\nEntry1=Kodi;kodi;kodi\n\n[Games]\n", "Main");
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    open_tiles(state, "Games");
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 1);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Empty: Add");
    CHECK_INT(rows[0].kind, SETTINGS_ROW_LINK);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ADD);
    cursor_to(state, "Submenu");
    SettingsEvent event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_TYPE_NAME);
    CHECK_STR(settings_name_problem(state, "Main"), "There's already a menu with that name");
    CHECK_STR(settings_name_problem(state, "main"), "There's already a menu with that name");
    CHECK_STR(settings_name_problem(state, "General"), "That name is kept for settings");
    CHECK_STR(settings_name_problem(state, "a]b"), "A name can't contain ]");
    CHECK(settings_name_problem(state, "Kids") == NULL);
    event = settings_add_submenu(state, "Kids");
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_count(edit), 3);
    const MenuTile *kids = tile_of(edit, "Games", 0);
    CHECK(kids != NULL);
    CHECK_STR(kids->title, "Kids");
    CHECK_STR(kids->icon, "folder");
    CHECK_STR(kids->command, ":submenu Kids");
    event = settings_add_submenu(state, "Kids");                    // Refused: the Add page is gone, and so is the name
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_count(edit), 3);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}

// A function to test Add after this tile (user ruling 2026-10-16, Fable review C3): a tile's page offers it,
// and the new tile goes right after that tile, here the third of four, back on the Tiles page on it; the
// Tiles page's own Add still puts one at the end, wherever its cursor has been
static void test_add_after_tile(void)
{
    static const char *const text = "[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:home\nEntry2=B;apps;:home\nEntry3=C;apps;:home\n"
                                    "Entry4=D;apps;:home\n";
    SettingsState *state = open_model();
    MenuEdit *edit = with_menus(state, text, "Main");
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    char path[256];
    open_tiles(state, "Main");
    cursor_to(state, "C");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    cursor_to(state, "Add after this tile");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ADD);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "Main" ARROW "Tiles" ARROW "C" ARROW "Add");
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_tile(state), 2);                     // The preview highlights the tile it goes after
    cursor_to(state, "Special");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Home");
    SettingsEvent event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(event.tile, 3);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);           // Under the tile's page, on the new tile
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 2)->title, "C");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 3)->title, "Home");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 4)->title, "D");
    settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    CHECK_STR(rows[settings_cursor(state)].label, "Home");

    // The Tiles page's Add, its cursor having passed B on the way up: at the end all the same
    cursor_to(state, "B");
    cursor_to(state, "Add");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Special");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Back");
    event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(event.tile, 5);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 5)->title, "Back");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 4)->title, "D");
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}

// The menus of the tests that weigh a tile in its own line: Main's one tile has a comment after it, 152 bytes
// in all, its comment 130 (Fable review M2)
static char commented_text[256];

// A function to make commented_text, and give a 60-byte value that fits a line of config.ini alone but not
// that tile's line with its comment
static const char *commented_menus(char long_value[61])
{
    snprintf(commented_text, sizeof(commented_text), "[Main]\nEntry1=A;apps;:home ; ");
    size_t used = strlen(commented_text);
    memset(commented_text + used, 'c', 130);
    snprintf(commented_text + used + 130, sizeof(commented_text) - used - 130, "\n");
    memset(long_value, 'a', 60);
    long_value[60] = '\0';
    return commented_text;
}

// A function to test that a tile's title is weighed in the tile's own line as config.ini has it (Task 3's
// menuedit_check_set(), Fable review M2): the comment after the line leaves less room, so Done is grayed for
// a title menuedit_check_tile() alone would pass, and the save never refuses it
static void test_title_weighed_in_its_line(void)
{
    char long_value[61];
    SettingsState *state = open_model();
    MenuEdit *edit = with_menus(state, commented_menus(long_value), "Main");
    CHECK(menuedit_check_tile(long_value, "apps", ":home") == NULL);   // Entry99999= + 60 + ;apps;:home: 82
    CHECK_STR(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 0, long_value),         // In its line: 7 + 60 + 11 + 3 + 130 = 211
              "It's too long for its line of config.ini with the comment there (199 bytes)");
    CHECK(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 0, "Nap") == NULL);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}

// A function to test a submenu tile's Remove: the confirm page's two rows, the second only while another
// tile opens the menu; Remove only this tile; Remove the menu with its tiles, and every tile that opens it;
// and the default menu, which cannot be removed
static void test_remove_submenu(void)
{
    static const char *const text = "[Main]\nEntry1=Games;games;:submenu Games\nEntry2=Play;games;:submenu Games\n"
                                     "Entry3=Kodi;kodi;kodi\n\n[Games]\nEntry1=Retro;emulators;:back\nEntry2=Pong;games;:back\n";
    SettingsState *state = open_model();
    MenuEdit *edit = with_menus(state, text, "Main");
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    char path[256];
    open_tiles(state, "Main");
    cursor_to(state, "Games");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Remove");
    CHECK_INT(settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK).kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_REMOVE_MENU);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "Main" ARROW "Tiles" ARROW "Games" ARROW "Remove?");
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 2);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Remove Games and its 2 tiles");
    CHECK(rows[0].enabled);
    CHECK_STR(rows[1].label, "Remove only this tile");
    cursor_to(state, "Remove only this tile");
    CHECK_INT(settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK).kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 0)->title, "Play");
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_find(edit, "Games"), 1);

    // Play is the only opener now: one row, and the menu goes with its tiles
    cursor_to(state, "Play");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Remove");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 1);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Remove Games and its 2 tiles");
    CHECK_INT(settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK).kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_find(edit, "Games"), -1);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 0)->title, "Kodi");
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);

    // The default menu's tile: the row is grayed with its reason, and OK on it changes nothing
    state = open_model();
    edit = with_menus(state, text, "Games");
    open_tiles(state, "Main");
    cursor_to(state, "Games");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    cursor_to(state, "Remove");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    CHECK(!rows[0].enabled);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].why, "The default menu can't be removed");
    CHECK_INT(settings_cursor(state), 0);
    CHECK_INT(settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK).kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_find(edit, "Games"), 1);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}

// A function to test a submenu tile's title, which renames its menu (spec "Renaming a submenu tile renames
// the submenu"): the name rules, the tile's own title following, and every binding and Startup or Quit
// command that holds exactly ":submenu <old>" rewritten (Known integration work 1), the rest left
static void test_rename_submenu(void)
{
    static const char *const text = "[Main]\nEntry1=Fun;games;:submenu Games\nEntry2=Kodi;kodi;kodi\n\n"
                                     "[Games]\nEntry1=Retro;emulators;:back\n";
    SettingsState *state = open_model();
    MenuEdit *edit = with_menus(state, text, "Main");
    Bindings *b = with_lines(state, "Hotkey1=#4000003A;:submenu Games\nHotkey2=#4000003B;:submenu Gamesx",
                             "ButtonX=:submenu Games", false);
    entry(state, SET_ID_STARTUP_CMD, ":submenu Games");
    entry(state, SET_ID_QUIT_CMD, ":submenu Gamesx");
    CHECK_STR(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 0, "Main"), "There's already a menu with that name");
    CHECK_STR(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 0, "a]b"), "A name can't contain ]");
    CHECK(settings_title_problem(state, 0, 0, "Play") == NULL);

    SettingsEvent refused = settings_set_title(state, 0, 0, "Main");
    CHECK_INT(refused.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(settings_notice(state), "There's already a menu with that name");
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_find(edit, "Games"), 1);

    SettingsEvent event = settings_set_title(state, 0, 0, "Play");
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK(event.rebind);
    CHECK_INT(menuedit_find(edit, "Play"), 1);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 0)->title, "Play");             // Its own title ("Fun") follows too
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Main", 0)->command, ":submenu Play");
    CHECK_STR(bindings_at(b, BINDINGS_KEYBOARD, 0)->command, ":submenu Play");
    CHECK_STR(bindings_at(b, BINDINGS_KEYBOARD, 1)->command, ":submenu Gamesx");
    CHECK_STR(bindings_at(b, BINDINGS_GAMEPAD, 0)->command, ":submenu Play");
    CHECK_STR(settings_slot(state, SET_ID_STARTUP_CMD, -1)->value.text, ":submenu Play");
    CHECK_STR(settings_slot(state, SET_ID_QUIT_CMD, -1)->value.text, ":submenu Gamesx");
    CHECK(settings_changed(settings_slot(state, SET_ID_STARTUP_CMD, -1)));
    CHECK(bindings_changed(b));
    settings_free(state);
    bindings_free(b);
    menuedit_free(edit);

    // A tile inside the menu it opens (written by hand: Move to menu forbids making one): the rename leaves
    // the settings' name for the menu the old one, so the tile is found again by the menus model's index
    // (Fable review I3), and takes the new name as its title
    state = open_model();
    edit = with_menus(state, "[Main]\nEntry1=Kodi;kodi;kodi\n\n[Games]\nEntry1=Loop;games;:submenu Games\n", "Main");
    event = settings_set_title(state, 1, 0, "Play");
    CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Play", 0)->command, ":submenu Play");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(edit, "Play", 0)->title, "Play");
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(edit);
}
```

```c
// A function to find the menus model's menu for a menu of the settings, by its name (the two lists keep one
// order, but a name is what both are sure of); -1 with no menus model, or no such menu
static int edit_index(const SettingsState *state, int menu)
{
    if (state->menus == NULL || menu < 0 || menu >= state->menu_count)
        return -1;
    return menuedit_find(state->menus, state->names[menu]);
}

// A function to get the menus model's menu for a menu of the settings; NULL when there is none
static const MenuEditMenu *edit_menu(const SettingsState *state, int menu)
{
    int e = edit_index(state, menu);
    return e >= 0 ? menuedit_menu(state->menus, e) : NULL;
}

// A function to get a tile; NULL when there is none
static const MenuTile *edit_tile(const SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile)
{
    const MenuEditMenu *m = edit_menu(state, menu);
    return m != NULL && tile >= 0 && tile < m->count ? &m->tiles[tile] : NULL;
}

// A function to find the menu a tile opens in the menus model; -1 for a tile that opens none, or one whose
// menu is gone (a tile like any other)
static int opened_menu(const SettingsState *state, const MenuTile *tile)
{
    const char *name = tile != NULL ? menuedit_submenu_of(tile) : NULL;
    return name != NULL ? menuedit_find(state->menus, name) : -1;
}

// A function to make a tile's row on the Tiles page: one that opens a menu is a link, showing its tile count;
// any other shows its command. OK on either opens the tile's page.
static SettingsRow tile_row(const SettingsState *state, int menu, int t)
{
    const MenuTile *tile = edit_tile(state, menu, t);
    int s = opened_menu(state, tile);
    SettingsRow row = s >= 0 ? link_row(tile->title, "", SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE, menu)
                             : action_row(tile->title, SETTINGS_ACTION_OPEN_TILE, true);
    row.menu = menu;
    row.tile = t;
    if (s >= 0) {
        int count = menuedit_menu(state->menus, s)->count;
        snprintf(row.value, sizeof(row.value), count == 1 ? "%d tile" : "%d tiles", count);
    }
    else
        setting_command_label(tile->command, row.value, sizeof(row.value));
    return row;
}

// A function to add the Tiles page's rows: Add (Empty: Add in an empty menu), which puts a new tile at the
// end (its row's tile is -1), then each tile in order. A page holds SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS rows: tiles past them
// are counted in a note, never cut off unseen.
static int tiles_rows(SettingsState *state, const PageRef *top, SettingsRow *rows, int n, int max)
{
    const MenuEditMenu *menu = edit_menu(state, top->menu);
    if (menu == NULL)
        return n;
    n = add_row(rows, n, max, link_row(menu->count == 0 ? "Empty: Add" : "Add", "", SETTINGS_PAGE_ADD, top->menu));
    int room = SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS - 2;
    int shown = menu->count <= room ? menu->count : room - 1;
    for (int t = 0; t < shown; t++)
        n = add_row(rows, n, max, tile_row(state, top->menu, t));
    if (shown < menu->count) {
        snprintf(state->more_tiles, sizeof(state->more_tiles),
            "%d more tiles have no room here: hold OK on one in the menu to edit it", menu->count - shown);
        n = add_row(rows, n, max, note_row(state->more_tiles));
    }
    return n;
}

// A function to add a submenu tile's Remove rows (spec "Decisions"): the menu with its tiles, grayed for the
// default menu, and the tile alone, only while another tile opens the menu too
static int remove_menu_rows(SettingsState *state, const PageRef *top, SettingsRow *rows, int n, int max)
{
    int s = opened_menu(state, edit_tile(state, top->menu, top->tile));
    if (s < 0)
        return n;
    const MenuEditMenu *submenu = menuedit_menu(state->menus, s);
    const char *default_menu = menuedit_default(state->menus);
    char label[128];
    snprintf(label, sizeof(label), submenu->count == 1 ? "Remove %s and its %d tile" : "Remove %s and its %d tiles",
        submenu->name, submenu->count);
    SettingsRow with = action_row(label, SETTINGS_ACTION_REMOVE_WITH_TILES, true);
    n = add_row(rows, n, max, grayed(with, default_menu != NULL && strcmp(default_menu, submenu->name) == 0, WHY_DEFAULT_MENU));
    if (menuedit_openers(state->menus, submenu->name) > 1)
        n = add_row(rows, n, max, action_row("Remove only this tile", SETTINGS_ACTION_REMOVE_ONLY_TILE, true));
    return n;
}
```

Replace `push_page()` (`:1570-1584`) with:

```c
// A function to open a page on top of the one on show; a Tiles page is about a tile (-1: none), which its
// rows are made for
static void open_page(SettingsState *state, SettingsPage page, int menu, int tile)
{
    if (state->depth + 1 >= SETTINGS_MAX_DEPTH)
        return;
    state->depth++;
    PageRef *top = &state->stack[state->depth];
    memset(top, 0, sizeof(*top));
    top->page = page;
    top->menu = menu;
    top->tile = tile;
    top->entry_mode = settings_slot(state, SET_ID_BACKGROUND_MODE, -1)->value.number;
    top->device = page == SETTINGS_PAGE_KEYBOARD ? BINDINGS_KEYBOARD
                : page == SETTINGS_PAGE_GAMEPAD ? BINDINGS_GAMEPAD : state->stack[state->depth - 1].device;
    fix_cursor(state);
}

// A function to open a page on top of the one on show
static void push_page(SettingsState *state, SettingsPage page, int menu)
{
    open_page(state, page, menu, -1);
}

// A function to go back to the Tiles page at `depth`, its cursor on tile `t`, or on the last tile when t is
// past the end now, or on Add when the menu is empty
static void back_to_tiles(SettingsState *state, int depth, int t)
{
    state->depth = depth;
    PageRef *page = &state->stack[depth];
    const MenuEditMenu *menu = edit_menu(state, page->menu);
    int count = menu != NULL ? menu->count : 0;
    page->cursor = (t < count ? t : count - 1) + 1;   // Add is the first row
    fix_cursor(state);
}

// A function to find the Tiles page an Add page at `add` was opened over: directly (the Tiles page's Add),
// or through a tile's page (its Add after this tile)
static int tiles_under(const SettingsState *state, int add)
{
    return state->stack[add - 1].page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE ? add - 2 : add - 1;
}

// A function to find the Add page under the page on show (it, or the Special page above it), over a Tiles
// page as tiles_under() finds it; -1 when there is none
static int adding_page(const SettingsState *state)
{
    for (int i = state->depth; i > 0; i--) {
        if (state->stack[i].page != SETTINGS_PAGE_ADD)
            continue;
        int under = tiles_under(state, i);
        return under >= 0 && state->stack[under].page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES ? i : -1;
    }
    return -1;
}

// A function to finish an addition the menus model made (`why` NULL) or refused: back on the Tiles page,
// the cursor on the new tile, or the reason in the caption
static SettingsEvent added(SettingsState *state, int add, int menu, int at, const char *why)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
        return event;
    }
    back_to_tiles(state, tiles_under(state, add), at);
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
    event.menu = menu;
    event.tile = at;
    return event;
}

// A function to add a tile to the Add page's menu: after the tile whose Add after this tile opened the page,
// or at the end from the Tiles page's Add; then back on the Tiles page, the cursor on it. The Special page,
// the app list and the program browser add through it. Refused with the menus model's reason in the caption.
SettingsEvent settings_add_tile(SettingsState *state, const char *title, const char *icon, const char *command)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_NONE;
    int add = adding_page(state);
    if (add < 0)
        return event;
    int menu = state->stack[add].menu;
    int after = state->stack[add].tile;
    int e = edit_index(state, menu);
    if (e < 0)
        return event;
    const char *why = menuedit_add(state->menus, e, after, title, icon, command);
    return added(state, add, menu, after < 0 ? menuedit_menu(state->menus, e)->count - 1 : after + 1, why);
}

// A function to make a submenu (spec "Submenu ›"): `[name]` and a tile that opens it, with the folder icon,
// where settings_add_tile() puts a tile. It gets no Back tile: Back and B go back.
SettingsEvent settings_add_submenu(SettingsState *state, const char *name)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    int add = adding_page(state);
    int menu = add >= 0 ? state->stack[add].menu : -1;
    int e = edit_index(state, menu);
    if (e < 0)
        return event;
    int after = state->stack[add].tile;
    const char *why = menuedit_add_submenu(state->menus, e, after, name, SUBMENU_ICON);
    return added(state, add, menu, after < 0 ? menuedit_menu(state->menus, e)->count - 1 : after + 1, why);
}

// A function to say why a new submenu's name cannot be written, or NULL: the name rules, then its tile's
// line, `name;folder;:submenu name`
const char *settings_name_problem(const SettingsState *state, const char *name)
{
    if (state->menus == NULL)
        return "The menus could not be read";
    const char *why = menuedit_check_name(state->menus, name, -1);
    if (why != NULL)
        return why;
    char command[INIDOC_MAX_LINE + 1];
    snprintf(command, sizeof(command), SUBMENU_COMMAND "%s", name);
    return menuedit_check_tile(name, SUBMENU_ICON, command);
}

// A function to say why a tile's title cannot be written, or NULL. A tile that opens a menu is renamed with
// its menu, so the name rules apply (its own name allowed in another case), then the tile's line with its
// command renamed. The line is weighed as it is in config.ini (Task 3's menuedit_check_set(): its comment
// and spacing count), so Done is grayed for a title the save would refuse.
const char *settings_title_problem(const SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile, const char *title)
{
    const MenuTile *t = edit_tile(state, menu, tile);
    if (t == NULL)
        return "The tile is gone";
    int e = edit_index(state, menu);
    int s = opened_menu(state, t);
    if (s < 0)
        return menuedit_check_set(state->menus, e, tile, title, t->icon, t->command);
    const char *why = menuedit_check_name(state->menus, title, s);
    if (why != NULL)
        return why;
    char command[INIDOC_MAX_LINE + 1];
    snprintf(command, sizeof(command), SUBMENU_COMMAND "%s", title);
    return menuedit_check_set(state->menus, e, tile, title, t->icon, command);
}

// A function to rewrite every command outside the menus that opens a renamed menu (Known integration work 1):
// each binding, keyboard or gamepad, and the Startup and Quit commands, holding exactly ":submenu <old>".
// True when one was rewritten.
static bool rename_commands(SettingsState *state, const char *old_name, const char *new_name)
{
    char before[BINDINGS_COMMAND_MAX];
    char after[BINDINGS_COMMAND_MAX];
    snprintf(before, sizeof(before), SUBMENU_COMMAND "%s", old_name);
    snprintf(after, sizeof(after), SUBMENU_COMMAND "%s", new_name);
    bool rewrote = false;
    for (int d = BINDINGS_KEYBOARD; state->bindings != NULL && d <= BINDINGS_GAMEPAD; d++) {
        for (int i = 0; i < bindings_count(state->bindings, (BindingsDevice) d); i++) {
            const Binding *binding = bindings_at(state->bindings, (BindingsDevice) d, i);
            if (binding->removed || strcmp(binding->command, before) != 0)
                continue;
            bindings_set(state->bindings, (BindingsDevice) d, i, binding->code, after);
            rewrote = true;
        }
    }
    static const SettingId commands[] = { SET_ID_STARTUP_CMD, SET_ID_QUIT_CMD };
    for (int i = 0; i < LENGTH(commands); i++) {
        SettingSlot *slot = settings_slot(state, commands[i], -1);
        if (slot->value.inherit || strcmp(slot->value.text, before) != 0)
            continue;
        snprintf(slot->value.text, sizeof(slot->value.text), "%s", after);
        rewrote = true;
    }
    return rewrote;
}

// A function to set a tile's title, as the keyboard typed it. A submenu tile's title is its menu's name: the
// menu is renamed (each tile opening it follows, and the default menu), the tile takes the new name as its
// own title, and so do the bindings and commands outside the menus (rename_commands()). Refused with the
// reason in the caption.
SettingsEvent settings_set_title(SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile, const char *title)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    state->notice[0] = '\0';
    int e = edit_index(state, menu);
    const MenuTile *t = edit_tile(state, menu, tile);
    if (t == NULL)
        return event;
    int s = opened_menu(state, t);
    const char *why = NULL;
    bool renamed = false;
    if (s < 0)
        why = menuedit_set(state->menus, e, tile, title, t->icon, t->command);
    else {
        char old_name[INIDOC_MAX_SECTION + 1];   // The menu's name goes with the rename
        snprintf(old_name, sizeof(old_name), "%s", menuedit_menu(state->menus, s)->name);
        why = menuedit_rename_menu(state->menus, s, title);
        if (why == NULL) {
            renamed = true;
            event.rebind = rename_commands(state, old_name, title);
            // The tile again, through the menus model's index: edit_tile() finds its menu by the settings'
            // name, which is still the old one, so a tile inside the menu it opens would not be found
            const MenuEditMenu *em = menuedit_menu(state->menus, e);
            t = em != NULL && tile < em->count ? &em->tiles[tile] : NULL;
            if (t != NULL && strcmp(t->title, title) != 0)
                why = menuedit_set(state->menus, e, tile, title, t->icon, t->command);
        }
    }
    if (why != NULL)
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
    if (why == NULL || renamed) {
        event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
        event.menu = menu;
        event.tile = tile;
    }
    return event;
}

// A function to remove the tile page's tile: one that opens a menu asks first (the confirm page); any other
// goes at once, back on the Tiles page on the tile now in its place
static SettingsEvent remove_tile(SettingsState *state)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    int menu = state->stack[state->depth].menu;
    int t = state->stack[state->depth].tile;
    const MenuTile *tile = edit_tile(state, menu, t);
    if (tile == NULL)
        return event;
    if (opened_menu(state, tile) >= 0) {
        open_page(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_REMOVE_MENU, menu, t);
        return event;
    }
    const char *why = menuedit_remove(state->menus, edit_index(state, menu), t);
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
        return event;
    }
    back_to_tiles(state, state->depth - 1, t);
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
    event.menu = menu;
    event.tile = -1;
    return event;
}

// A function to do what the confirm page chose for a submenu tile: the menu with its tiles (and every tile
// that opens it), or the tile alone; back on the Tiles page
static SettingsEvent remove_submenu(SettingsState *state, bool with_tiles)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    int menu = state->stack[state->depth].menu;
    int t = state->stack[state->depth].tile;
    const char *why = menuedit_remove_menu(state->menus, edit_index(state, menu), t, with_tiles);
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
        return event;
    }
    back_to_tiles(state, state->depth - 2, t);
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
    event.menu = menu;
    event.tile = -1;
    return event;
}
```
