```c
// A function to tell a page about a menu's tiles (3c), whose menu the preview shows
static bool tiles_page(SettingsPage page)
{
    return page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES || page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE || page == SETTINGS_PAGE_ADD ||
           page == SETTINGS_PAGE_SPECIAL || page == SETTINGS_PAGE_REMOVE_MENU;
}

// A function to say which menu the preview should show: the one a MENU or Tiles page is about, or the one
// highlighted on the Menus page; -1 for the menu settings were opened from
int settings_preview_menu(SettingsState *state)
{
    const PageRef *top = &state->stack[state->depth];
    if (top->page == SETTINGS_PAGE_MENU || tiles_page(top->page))
        return top->menu;
    if (top->page == SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS) {
        SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
        int count = settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
        if (top->cursor >= 0 && top->cursor < count && rows[top->cursor].kind == SETTINGS_ROW_LINK)
            return rows[top->cursor].menu;
    }
    return -1;
}

// A function to say which tile the preview highlights: on the Tiles page the one under its cursor (none on
// Add or the note), on the other Tiles pages the one they are about (the Add page's: the tile a new one goes
// after); -1 for none
int settings_preview_tile(SettingsState *state)
{
    const PageRef *top = &state->stack[state->depth];
    if (top->page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES) {
        SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
        int count = settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
        return top->cursor >= 0 && top->cursor < count ? rows[top->cursor].tile : -1;
    }
    return tiles_page(top->page) ? top->tile : -1;
}

// A function to tell whether the menus differ from how they were read: a tile or a menu added, removed,
// moved, renamed or changed
bool settings_menus_edited(const SettingsState *state)
{
    return state->menus != NULL && menuedit_changed(state->menus);
}
```

```c
// A function to select a tile of the menu on show, scrolled into view, as the settings preview highlights

    log_debug("Menu '%s': tile %i selected", current_menu->name, index);
}
```

```c
// A function to highlight in the preview the tile the page is about (settings_preview_tile())
static void select_preview_tile(void)
{

// A function to show in the preview the menu the page is about: a menu being edited or highlighted, its tile
// highlighted on a Tiles page, else the one settings opened over. An empty menu shows too, with its note
// (plan ruling 2). In the Menus list the preview waits for the cursor to rest (settings_draw() switches it),
// so moving down the list never waits for the icons of every menu on the way.
static void follow_preview(void)
{
    int index = settings_preview_menu(model);
    Menu *want = index >= 0 && index < menu_count ? menus[index] : origin;
    preview_wanted = NULL;
    if (want != current_menu) {
        if (settings_page(model) == SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS) {
            preview_wanted = want;
            preview_asked = ticks_ms();
            return;
        }
        show_preview(want);
    }
    select_preview_tile();
}
```

```c
static void handle_event(const SettingsEvent *event);

// A function to tell whether a tile of the menus model uses a file as its icon
static bool icon_in_use(const char *path)
{
    for (int m = 0; menu_edit != NULL && m < menuedit_count(menu_edit); m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *menu = menuedit_menu(menu_edit, m);
        for (int t = 0; t < menu->count; t++) {
            if (strcmp(menu->tiles[t].icon, path) == 0)
                return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to keep an icon file plated in this visit, which Discard deletes when no tile uses it (spec
// "Icons": StreamFlex deletes a plated file only so). Out of memory it is kept, and the log says so.
void settings_note_plated(const char *path)
{
    char **grown = realloc(plated, (size_t) (plated_count + 1) * sizeof(char*));
    char *copy = strdup(path);
    if (grown != NULL)
        plated = grown;
    if (grown == NULL || copy == NULL) {
        free(copy);
        log_error("Settings: out of memory, so Discard will not delete %s", path);
        return;
    }
    plated[plated_count++] = copy;
}

// A function to delete each icon file plated in this visit that no tile uses now
static void delete_unused_plated(void)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < plated_count; i++) {
        if (plated[i] == NULL || icon_in_use(plated[i]))
            continue;
        if (fileio_remove(plated[i]))
            log_debug("Settings: deleted %s, an icon plated in this visit that no tile uses", plated[i]);
        else
            log_error("Settings: could not delete %s: %s", plated[i], fileio_last_error());
        free(plated[i]);
        plated[i] = NULL;
    }
}

// A function to put the menus back as they were read, for Discard (spec "Saving and applying"): the menus
// model becomes a copy of the snapshot taken as settings opened, and the launcher and the settings follow it.
// Out of memory the menus stay as they are, and the log says so.
static void discard_menus(void)
{
    if (menu_edit != NULL && menu_snapshot != NULL && menuedit_changed(menu_edit)) {
        MenuEdit *copy = menuedit_copy(menu_snapshot);
        MenuEdit *now = menu_edit;
        if (copy == NULL) {
            log_error("Settings: out of memory, so Discard leaves the menus as they are");
            return;
        }
        menu_edit = copy;
        settings_set_menus(model, copy);
        if (!settings_menus_changed()) {
            menu_edit = now;
            settings_set_menus(model, now);
            menuedit_free(copy);
            return;   // settings_menus_changed() said why
        }
        menuedit_free(now);
        log_debug("Settings: the menus went back to how they were read");
    }
    delete_unused_plated();
}

// A function to put a change to the menus model into the launcher (settings_menus_changed()); after a
// submenu's rename, the bindings and the Startup and Quit commands the model rewrote too
static void menus_follow(bool rebind)
{
    if (!settings_menus_changed())
        return;
    log_debug("Settings: the menus changed");
    if (!rebind)
        return;
    if (bindings != NULL)
        apply_bindings(bindings);
    apply_slot(settings_slot(model, SET_ID_STARTUP_CMD, -1), false);
    apply_slot(settings_slot(model, SET_ID_QUIT_CMD, -1), false);
    log_debug("Settings: the bindings and the Startup and Quit commands follow the renamed menu");
}

// A function to say why a tile's title, as typed, cannot be written (the keyboard's validator)
static const char *title_problem(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    return settings_title_problem(model, typing.menu, typing.tile, text);
}

// A function to take a typed title
static void title_typed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    SettingsEvent event = settings_set_title(model, typing.menu, typing.tile, text);
    handle_event(&event);
}

// A function to show a plain tile's title in the preview as it is typed (spec "the preview updates as the
// user types"), once it has rested, and the title it had once the keyboard is canceled. A submenu tile's
// title is its menu's name, which changes at Done only: a rename makes the settings model again.
static void title_follows(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    if (typing.submenu || settings_title_problem(model, typing.menu, typing.tile, text) != NULL)
        return;
    SettingsEvent event = settings_set_title(model, typing.menu, typing.tile, text);
    if (event.kind == SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS && settings_menus_changed()) {
        log_debug("Settings: the preview shows the title '%s'", text);
        follow_preview();
    }
}

// A function to open the keyboard on a tile's title: "Title for <title>"; a submenu tile's is its menu's
// name, held to a section name's limit
static void open_title_keyboard(int menu, int tile)
{
    const MenuEditMenu *m = menu >= 0 && menu < menu_count && menu_edit != NULL
                          ? menuedit_menu(menu_edit, menuedit_find(menu_edit, menus[menu]->name)) : NULL;
    if (m == NULL || tile < 0 || tile >= m->count)
        return;
    const MenuTile *t = &m->tiles[tile];
    const char *opens = menuedit_submenu_of(t);
    typing.menu = menu;
    typing.tile = tile;
    typing.submenu = opens != NULL && menuedit_find(menu_edit, opens) >= 0;
    char label[MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX + 32];
    snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "Title for %s", t->title);
    pickers_open_keyboard(label, t->title, typing.submenu ? INIDOC_MAX_SECTION : MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX, title_problem,
                          NULL, title_typed);
    pickers_keyboard_follow(title_follows, PREVIEW_REST_MS);
}

// A function to say why a new submenu's name, as typed, cannot be written (the keyboard's validator)
static const char *name_problem(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    return settings_name_problem(model, text);
}

// A function to take a typed name: the submenu is made
static void name_typed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    SettingsEvent event = settings_add_submenu(model, text);
    handle_event(&event);
}
```

Create `tests/headless/checks/82-tiles.sh`:

```bash
# Editing a menu's tiles in settings (3c, spec "Pages and flows"): a special command added after a tile
# through its page's Add after this tile, its title typed on the on-screen keys and shown in the preview as
# typed; one added after the third of four tiles; a submenu made with a name typed on a real keyboard, at
# the end through the Tiles page's Add; a submenu removed with its tiles, and the confirm page's other
# choice; a submenu renamed, with every :submenu line, the default menu and the bindings that named it; a
# title config.ini cannot hold; Discard; and saves after a hand edit. Each saved config.ini is read line by
# line (its lines but the blank ones, in order).
# Not timing-sensitive: every key waits for its frame, xdotool type's keys reach the launcher in order, and every result is read from the log's lines or the saved file, never from a clock

ARROW=$(printf ' \xE2\x80\xBA ')
# The top page, Menus, the first menu, its Tiles row (after Rows, Columns and Largest button)
E82_TILES="Menu Down Down Return Down Return Down Down Down Return"
E82_LAST="Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down"   # The last row of a page: a tile's Remove, Add's Special
E82_AFTER="$E82_LAST Up"                              # A tile's Add after this tile, one above Remove
e82_type() { xdotool type --delay 60 "$1"; }
e82_type_kids() { e82_type Kids; }
e82_type_play() { e82_type Play; }
e82_type_semicolon() { e82_type ';x'; }
e82_type_x() { e82_type x; }
# A function to give the lines of a config but its blank ones, joined by '|', for a line-by-line comparison
e82_lines() { grep -v '^$' "$1" | tr '\n' '|'; }

# Games' page, Add after this tile, Special, Sleep: after Games; then its title on the on-screen keys:
# Right x5 to y, OK, then Down, Down, Down, Right x4 to Done. The preview follows the title as typed, and
# the new line is numbered above the section's highest and written before Bye's.
cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-special $E82_TILES Down Return $E82_AFTER Return $E82_LAST Return Down Down Down Return \
    Return Return Right Right Right Right Right Return Down Down Down Right Right Right Right Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-special.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Main]|Entry1=Games;games;:submenu Games|Entry3=Sleepy;sleep;:sleep|Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit|[Games]|Rows=2|Entry1=Retro;emulators;:back|Entry2=Arcade;games;:submenu Arcade|[Arcade]|Entry1=Pong;games;:back|' ] \
    && grep -qF "Settings: page Settings${ARROW}Menus${ARROW}Main${ARROW}Tiles${ARROW}Games${ARROW}Add${ARROW}Special" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 1 selected" "$log" \
    && in_range "$log" "Settings: opened the keyboard for Title for Sleep" "Settings: the keyboard finished with 'Sleepy'" \
        "Settings: the preview shows the title 'Sleepy'" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: the menus were written to ' "$log" && ran_clean f82-special && ok=0
result "tiles: a special command added after a tile from its page, its title typed on screen, saves (exit $(cat "$out/f82-special.code"))" $ok
grep -E "Settings: (page|the keyboard (reads|finished)|the preview shows the title|the menus)|tile [0-9]+ selected" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# Four tiles: Three's page, Add after this tile, Special, Home: after Three, before Four, numbered above
# the section's highest (user ruling 2026-10-16: a tile's page adds after that tile)
cfg=$(writable_config f82-four)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-after $E82_TILES Down Down Down Return $E82_AFTER Return $E82_LAST Return Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-after.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Main]|Entry1=One;apps;:home|Entry2=Two;apps;:home|Entry3=Three;apps;:home|Entry5=Home;home;:home|Entry4=Four;apps;:home|' ] \
    && grep -qF "Settings: page Settings${ARROW}Menus${ARROW}Main${ARROW}Tiles${ARROW}Three${ARROW}Add" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 3 selected" "$log" && ran_clean f82-after && ok=0
result "tiles: Add after this tile puts a new tile after the third of four (exit $(cat "$out/f82-after.code"))" $ok
grep -E "Settings: (page|the menus)|tile [0-9]+ selected" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# Add, Submenu: Kids typed on a real keyboard (Enter is Done once typed), at the end; then Games removed with
# its tiles from the confirm page, which offers nothing else (no other tile opens Games). Arcade stays.
cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-submenu $E82_TILES Return $E82_LAST Up Return +e82_type_kids Return Up Up Return \
    $E82_LAST Return Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-submenu.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Main]|Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit|Entry3=Kids;folder;:submenu Kids|[Arcade]|Entry1=Pong;games;:back|[Kids]|' ] \
    && grep -q "Settings: opened the keyboard for Name for the new submenu" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the cursor's row reads Remove Games and its 2 tiles" "$log" \
    && ! grep -q "Settings: the cursor's row reads Remove only this tile" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Menus: 'Games' is gone" "$log" && grep -q "Menus: 'Kids' is new" "$log" && ran_clean f82-submenu && ok=0
result "tiles: a submenu made with a typed name, and one removed with its tiles, save (exit $(cat "$out/f82-submenu.code"))" $ok
grep -E "Settings: (opened the keyboard|the cursor's row reads Remove)|Menus: '" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# Arcade opened from two menus: its tile's confirm page offers both, and Remove only this tile leaves the
# menu and its other opener
cfg=$(writable_config f82-two)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-two $E82_TILES Down Return $E82_LAST Return Down Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-two.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Main]|Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit|[Games]|Entry1=Arcade;games;:submenu Arcade|[Arcade]|Entry1=Pong;games;:back|' ] \
    && grep -q "Settings: the cursor's row reads Remove Arcade and its 1 tile" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the cursor's row reads Remove only this tile" "$log" && ran_clean f82-two && ok=0
result "tiles: a submenu opened twice offers Remove only this tile, which keeps the menu (exit $(cat "$out/f82-two.code"))" $ok

# Games renamed Play through its tile's title (settings opened over Games, the default menu): five Backspaces
# on the on-screen keys (Down x3 to the bottom row, Right x3 to the backspace key), then Play typed on a real
# keyboard. Its section, the tile that opens it, DefaultMenu, the hotkey and the gamepad button follow.
cfg=$(writable_config f82-rename)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-rename Menu Down Down Return Down Down Return Down Down Down Return Down Return Return \
    Down Down Down Right Right Right Return Return Return Return Return +e82_type_play Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-rename.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Play|[Hotkeys]|Hotkey1=#4000003A;:submenu Play|[Gamepad]|ButtonX=:submenu Play|[Play]|Entry1=Retro;emulators;:back|Entry2=Main;apps;:submenu Main|[Main]|Entry1=Play;games;:submenu Play|Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit|' ] \
    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads '' (cursor 0)" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Menus: 'Games' is now 'Play'" "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: the bindings and the Startup and Quit commands follow the renamed menu' "$log" \
    && ! grep -q "Settings: the preview shows the title" "$log" && ran_clean f82-rename && ok=0
result "tiles: a submenu renamed through its tile renames every :submenu line, DefaultMenu and the bindings (exit $(cat "$out/f82-rename.code"))" $ok
grep -E "Settings: (the keyboard (reads|finished)|the bindings)|Menus: '" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A title with ';' keeps Done off with the reason; Esc asks, Esc again discards; nothing is saved
cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-semicolon $E82_TILES Down Down Return Return +e82_type_semicolon Return Escape Escape Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-semicolon.log
grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads 'Bye;x' (cursor 5)" "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: the keyboard says A title can.t contain ;' "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: Done is off: A title can.t contain ;' "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: nothing changed' "$log" && cmp -s "$FX/f82-tiles.ini" "$cfg" && ran_clean f82-semicolon && ok=0
result "tiles: a title with ';' keeps Done off with the reason, and nothing is saved (exit $(cat "$out/f82-semicolon.code"))" $ok

# Discard after adding Home: the menus go back as they were read, the launcher with them, and nothing is
# written (Discard changes is the top page's last row)
cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-discard $E82_TILES Return $E82_LAST Return Return BackSpace BackSpace BackSpace \
    $E82_LAST Down Down Down Down Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-discard.log
grep -q 'Settings: discarded the changes' "$log" && grep -q 'Settings: the menus went back to how they were read' "$log" \
    && sed -n '/Settings: discarded the changes/,$p' "$log" | grep -q "Menus: the launcher's menus were made again from the menus model" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: nothing changed' "$log" && cmp -s "$FX/f82-tiles.ini" "$cfg" && ran_clean f82-discard && ok=0
result "tiles: Discard puts the menus back and writes nothing (exit $(cat "$out/f82-discard.code"))" $ok

# A hand edit meanwhile (Review Focus 1): Bye removed in settings while config.ini's Bye line is changed by
# hand, then Home added at the end through the Tiles page's Add. The removal is skipped with 3b's note, the
# hand's line stays, and Home is written after the section's last line
# (written over in place, as check 62's hand edits are, so the file keeps its owner and inode)
e82_hand_edit() {
    sed 's/^Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit$/Entry2=Ciao;quit;:quit/' "$e82_cfg" > "$out/f82-hand.edit"
    cat "$out/f82-hand.edit" > "$e82_cfg"
    sleep 0.5
}
e82_cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
CFG=$e82_cfg run_keys f82-hand $E82_TILES Down Down Return $E82_LAST Return +e82_hand_edit Up Return $E82_LAST \
    Return Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-hand.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$e82_cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Main]|Entry1=Games;games;:submenu Games|Entry2=Ciao;quit;:quit|Entry3=Home;home;:home|[Games]|Rows=2|Entry1=Retro;emulators;:back|Entry2=Arcade;games;:submenu Arcade|[Arcade]|Entry1=Pong;games;:back|' ] \
    && grep -q "Settings: not saved as asked: 'Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit' is not there any more, so its removal is skipped" "$log" \
    && ran_clean f82-hand && ok=0
result "tiles: a save after a hand edit skips what is gone, with a note, and writes the rest (exit $(cat "$out/f82-hand.code"))" $ok
grep -E 'Settings: (not saved as asked|saved|the menus were written)' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A tile's title changed in settings ("x" typed after Bye) while the hand changes its line: the change is
# written as a new line beside the hand's, and the note says so with no words on keys and buttons, which
# are the bindings' (Fable review M6)
e82_cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
CFG=$e82_cfg run_keys f82-meanwhile $E82_TILES Down Down Return Return +e82_hand_edit +e82_type_x Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-meanwhile.log
sed -n '/^\[Main\]/,/^$/p' "$e82_cfg" | grep -qx 'Entry2=Ciao;quit;:quit' \
    && sed -n '/^\[Main\]/,/^$/p' "$e82_cfg" | grep -qE '^Entry[0-9]+=Byex;quit;:quit$' \
    && grep -qx "Settings: not saved as asked: 'Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit' changed meanwhile, so its change is written as a new line" "$log" \
    && ran_clean f82-meanwhile && ok=0
result "tiles: a tile changed in settings and by hand is written as a new line, its note without the bindings' words (exit $(cat "$out/f82-meanwhile.code"))" $ok
grep -E 'Settings: (not saved as asked|the menus were written)' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'
```

`f82-discard`'s top page has General, Background, Menus, Titles, Highlight, Scroll indicators, Clock, Screensaver, Controls, a divider and Discard changes (no 3c task adds a top-page row): from Menus (where Back leaves the cursor), seven Downs reach Discard, the last row, and the five after them do nothing there (`settings_command()`'s Up and Down never wrap). **The run-order break this causes in Task 4's check 80.** From here on, closing settings saves a changed menus model, so the three check-80 runs whose test hook (`STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT`) changes it as settings open, then close them with Back, now write `config.ini`, and their `cmp -s "$FX/<fixture>.ini" "$cfg"` fails. Each instead asserts the file the save wrote, line by line (its lines but the blank ones), and the save's line. In `tests/headless/checks/80-menus-live.sh`:

  ```bash
  # the Tiles pages; since 3c Task 10a closing settings saves that change, which f80-remove, f80-rename and
  # f80-add read back line by line (the lines but the blank ones).
  ```

  ```bash
      && grep -q 'Settings: the menus were written to ' "$log" && ran_clean f80-remove && ok=0
  ```

- in `f80-rename`, replace `    && cmp -s "$FX/f80-rename.ini" "$cfg" && ran_clean f80-rename && ok=0` with:

(The removal takes Games' section and the tile that opened it, as `f82-submenu` does; the rename rewrites the section's header and `DefaultMenu`, as `f82-rename` does, and the hook's rename touches no binding (the hotkey runs `:home`); the new tile is numbered above the section's highest key, as `f87-add` reads it. `f80-empty`, `f80-default-empty`, `f80-stray`, `f80-caught-up` and `f80-no-menus` assert no file, so they stand: the first three change no model; `f80-caught-up`'s hook changes one, but the run asserts no file; `f80-no-menus` has no model to save, since settings open refuses one with no menu.)

`f82-hand`'s expected text for the note is Task 2's `REMOVAL_SKIPPED` wording (`config_save.c:222-225`), and `f82-meanwhile`'s is Task 3's `CHANGED_MEANWHILE` wording for a tile (`match_tiles()`), read whole with `grep -x` so 3b's words on keys and buttons would fail it; `f82-semicolon`'s greps match the apostrophe with `.` so the shell quoting stays simple. `E82_AFTER` reaches *Add after this tile ›* one above Remove on every tile's page, whatever rows Tasks 10b, 11 and 13a add above it.

Pinned only by check 82, with no `mutants.py` entry (its runs edit the file by hand mid-run, which the driver cannot): a tile's "changed meanwhile" note logged without 3b's words on keys (dropping `&& !from_menus` from `log_save_notes()` fails `f82-meanwhile`'s whole-line grep); write it into the ledger as pinned by check 82. **Smoke-row claims** (Task 17 writes the rows):
- `[All]` Settings › Menus › <menu> shows *Tiles ›* with the menu's tile count; its page lists *Add ›* then every tile in order, a submenu tile with ›; an empty menu shows *Empty: Add ›*.
- `[All]` Highlighting a tile on the Tiles page highlights it in the preview. The Tiles page's *Add ›* puts a new tile at the end; a tile's page has *Add after this tile ›*, which puts it right after that tile (the third of four included).
- `[All]` *Add › Special ›* adds Home, Back, Settings, Sleep, Restart, Shut down or Quit with its library icon, and it works at once.
- `[All]` *Add › Submenu ›* asks a name on the keyboard; a name in use, reserved, or with `]` keeps Done off with the reason; the new submenu opens, empty, from its tile.
- `[All]` A tile's *Title* opens the keyboard on it; the preview shows the title as it is typed; a `;` keeps Done off.
- `[All]` Renaming a submenu tile renames the menu: its tile, every tile that opens it, DefaultMenu, and any hotkey, gamepad button, Startup or Quit command that opened it follow; after a restart they all still work.
- `[All]` *Remove* takes a normal tile away at once; a submenu tile asks: *Remove <Name> and its N tiles*, and *Remove only this tile* only when another menu opens it too; the default menu's cannot be removed.
- `[All]` Closing settings saves the tiles; *Discard changes* puts every tile and menu back as it was, and nothing is written.
- `[All]` A hand edit to config.ini while settings are open: the save keeps the hand's lines and skips what is gone, and the menus still load; a tile changed both ways is written as a new line beside the hand's, and the log's note for it says nothing of keys or buttons.

**What this task decides:**
- **The app list** is a picker of its own kind (`PICKER_APPS`), with no slot, over Task 7's one scan (fix pass R1): the first *App ›* of a settings visit starts it (`settings_apps_start()`, which does nothing once this visit has started one), Task 7's `poll_apps()` follows it each frame, and its result (the list, or why there is none) is kept until settings close, where Task 7's `stop_apps()` stops the scan (joining its thread) and frees the list. So a second *App ›* in the visit opens at once on the same list. While it runs the column reads *Finding apps… (N)*; one that failed, could not start, or found nothing reads why (`settings_apps()`'s reason), the caption too, and Back returns to the Add page, whose other rows work as ever. The rows are made on the frame after the scan's list is in (`pickers_tick()`). Rows are the apps' names in the list's order; OK adds the app; Up from the top row, or a printing key on a real keyboard, opens the keyboard on the filter (Task 12's entry), which filters at once as it is typed. With nothing matching, one grayed row says so.
- **A new app's tile**: the app's name made a title (`settings_tile_title()`: `;` becomes `,`, control characters spaces, the edges trimmed of both, cut to `MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX` bytes on a character's edge; an empty one `App`); the command the app's (`AppItem.command`).
- **A new tile's icon, as it is added** (user ruling 2026-10-16, Fable review I5; the spec's order under "Icons", and "With no match and no icon of its own, an app gets the library's generic `apps` icon"): **the library's match for its title** (`iconmatch_find()` over `library_info()`); **else the app's own icon, plated** (as 13b's Icon page plates it: on Windows `appicon_image()` by the app ID `AppItem.icon` holds; on Linux the image its `Icon=` names, through `iconfind_path()` over `applist_data_dirs()`'s folders, read by `load_icon_surface()`), written then as a new PNG in `icons_dir()` at `icons_new_path(dir, title)` by `plate_save()` and listed for Discard (`settings_note_plated()`), when the tile's line can hold that path (`menuedit_check_tile()` first, so a refusal leaves no file); **else `apps`**. The app list's apps name their own icon (`AppItem.icon`); a program browsed is an app with an icon of its own only when it is a Linux `.desktop` file (its `Icon=`, read whatever its `NoDisplay` or `Hidden` say); a Windows `.exe` or `.lnk` has none (spec: the Windows own icon is an AppsFolder item's). An own icon that cannot be found, read, plated or written is not used, and the log says why. Task 13's Icon page offers every choice again later.
- **Browse for a program ›** opens the folder browser in file mode over a list function that hides every file that is not a program (`browser_is_program()`): on Windows `.exe` and `.lnk` in any case; on Linux a `.desktop` file (exactly, as `unix.c` launches one) or any file with its execute bit (scripts are run by it, so a script without it could not run). A hidden file is logged once per listing. The command written (`browser_program_command()`): on Windows the path, in double quotes when it holds a space (`win32.c`'s `parse_command()` splits at the first space otherwise); on Linux a `.desktop` path as it is, any other path as it is when the shell reads it as one word, else in single quotes. A path that cannot be written so (a `'` in a Linux path that needs quotes, a `;` in a `.desktop` path, which `unix.c` takes as its action separator) is a grayed row with its reason; so is one whose tile line config.ini could not hold, weighed as the line that would be written (Fable review M13): for a new tile, the title it would take with its library match or `apps` (an own icon's path is weighed again as it is written, and a line that cannot hold it takes `apps`); for a tile's *Command ›*, that tile's own title and icon. The title starts as the file's name without its extension. The browser opens on the program last chosen in this visit (its folder, with it highlighted: in file mode `browser_open()` takes any start as a file), else as the folder browser opens; a tile's *Command ›* browse opens on the tile's own program when its command names a file, as it is or inside the quotes `browser_program_command()` wrote round it (`browser_program_path()`, Fable review M18).
- **A tile's Command ›** opens a list: *App*, *Browse for a program*, the seven special commands (labeled as 3b labels them; never `:select`), and *Type…* last, with the cursor on the tile's command (pinned first as *Custom:* when no row gives it). *Type…* opens the keyboard on the command, checked by `menuedit_check_tile()`. A submenu tile's Command row is grayed: *A submenu tile's command is its menu's name: change it with Title*.

```c
// A function to test an app's or a file's name made a tile's title: ';' a comma, control characters spaces,
// the edges trimmed of both (a leading tab would be a leading space, which config.ini's line refuses), cut
// on a character's edge to the keyboard's limit; nothing left is "App"
static void test_tile_title(void)
{
    char title[MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX + 1];
    settings_tile_title("  Foo; Bar  ", title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_STR(title, "Foo, Bar");
    settings_tile_title("Line\tbreak\n", title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_STR(title, "Line break");
    settings_tile_title("\t \x7F" "Tab first", title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_STR(title, "Tab first");
    CHECK(menuedit_check_tile(title, "apps", ":home") == NULL);
    char name[200];
    memset(name, 'a', 70);
    name[70] = '\0';
    settings_tile_title(name, title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_INT((int) strlen(title), MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX);
    snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "a");
    for (int i = 0; i < 40; i++)
        strcat(name, "\xC3\xA9");                                   // e acute, two bytes each
    settings_tile_title(name, title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_INT((int) strlen(title), 63);                              // 64 would cut the 32nd in half
    settings_tile_title("", title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_STR(title, "App");
    settings_tile_title(" ; ", title, sizeof(title));
    CHECK_STR(title, ",");
}
```

```c
// A function to test reading a .desktop file's Icon= (3c): the [Desktop Entry] group's first, its spaces at
// either end dropped, whatever NoDisplay or Hidden say; another group's, a localized Icon[..], another key
// that starts with Icon, an empty one or none read as none
static void test_desktop_icon(void)
{

    CHECK_STR(out, "org.app");
    static const char *const other = "[Desktop Action New]\nIcon=action\n[Desktop Entry]\nIcon[de]=de\nIconic=no\n";
    CHECK(!browser_desktop_icon(other, strlen(other), out, sizeof(out)));
    CHECK_STR(out, "");
    static const char *const empty = "[Desktop Entry]\n# Icon=commented\nIcon=\n";
    CHECK(!browser_desktop_icon(empty, strlen(empty), out, sizeof(out)));
    static const char *const path = "[Desktop Entry]\nIcon=/opt/app/icon.png";
    CHECK(browser_desktop_icon(path, strlen(path), out, sizeof(out)));
    CHECK_STR(out, "/opt/app/icon.png");
    CHECK(!browser_desktop_icon(path, strlen(path), out, 8));          // No room
}
```

```c
// A function to set a tile's command, as its command list chose it or the keyboard typed it; refused with the
// reason in the caption
SettingsEvent settings_set_command(SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile, const char *command)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    state->notice[0] = '\0';
    const MenuTile *t = edit_tile(state, menu, tile);
    if (t == NULL)
        return event;
    const char *why = menuedit_set(state->menus, edit_index(state, menu), tile, t->title, t->icon, command);
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
        return event;
    }
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
    event.menu = menu;
    event.tile = tile;
    return event;
}

// A function to say why a tile cannot run a command, as typed, weighed in its line as config.ini has it
// (menuedit_check_set(): its comment and spacing count); NULL when it can
const char *settings_command_problem(const SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile, const char *command)
{
    const MenuTile *t = edit_tile(state, menu, tile);
    return t == NULL ? "The tile is gone"
                     : menuedit_check_set(state->menus, edit_index(state, menu), tile, t->title, t->icon, command);
}

// A function to make an app's or a file's name a tile's title: a ';' (which ends a title in config.ini)
// becomes a comma, a control character a space, the edges are trimmed of spaces and of what becomes one (a
// leading tab would be a leading space, which config.ini's line refuses), and it is cut on a character's
// edge to the keyboard's limit (MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX bytes) or `size`; with nothing left, "App"
void settings_tile_title(const char *name, char *out, size_t size)
{
    size_t limit = size - 1 < (size_t) MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX ? size - 1 : (size_t) MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX;
    while (*name != '\0' && ((unsigned char) *name <= 0x20 || *name == 0x7F))
        name++;
    size_t n = 0;
    for (; name[n] != '\0' && n < limit; n++) {
        unsigned char c = (unsigned char) name[n];
        out[n] = (char) (c == ';' ? ',' : c < 0x20 || c == 0x7F ? ' ' : c);
    }
    while (n > 0 && ((unsigned char) name[n] & 0xC0) == 0x80)   // The character the limit cut goes whole
        n--;
    while (n > 0 && out[n - 1] == ' ')
        n--;
    out[n] = '\0';
    if (n == 0)
        snprintf(out, size, "%s", APP_TITLE);
}
```

```c
#define DESKTOP_EXTENSION ".desktop"   // unix.c's EXT_DESKTOP: a .desktop file, matched exactly
// The bytes a shell reads as part of one word, unquoted: a Linux path of only these needs no quotes
#define SHELL_WORD "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789/._+,:@%=-"

// A function to tell whether a name ends with an extension, whatever its case
static bool ends_with_any_case(const char *name, const char *extension)
{
    size_t length = strlen(name);
    size_t extension_length = strlen(extension);
    if (length <= extension_length)
        return false;
    const char *tail = name + length - extension_length;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < extension_length; k++) {
        if (fileio_lower(tail[k]) != fileio_lower(extension[k]))
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to tell whether a file is a program the launcher can run, for the program browser: on
// Windows an .exe or an .lnk, whatever its case; on Linux a .desktop file (unix.c launches one by its
// exact extension) or a file with its execute bit (`executable`), a script included
bool browser_is_program(const char *name, bool executable, bool windows)
{
    if (windows)
        return ends_with_any_case(name, ".exe") || ends_with_any_case(name, ".lnk");
    size_t length = strlen(name);
    size_t desktop = strlen(DESKTOP_EXTENSION);
    return executable || (length > desktop && strcmp(name + length - desktop, DESKTOP_EXTENSION) == 0);
}

// A function to write the command that runs a program chosen in the program browser. On Windows: the path,
// in double quotes when it holds a space (win32.c's parse_command() ends the file at the first space
// otherwise). On Linux: a .desktop file's path as it is (unix.c reads it as a file, up to a ';'); any other
// path as it is when the shell reads it as one word, else in single quotes. False, with `out` empty, when
// it cannot be written so: a '"' in a Windows path, a '\'' in a Linux one that needs quotes, a ';' in a
// .desktop path, or no room.
bool browser_program_command(const char *path, bool windows, char *out, size_t size)
{
    out[0] = '\0';
    size_t length = strlen(path);
    bool quote;
    if (windows) {
        if (strchr(path, '"') != NULL)
            return false;
        quote = strchr(path, ' ') != NULL;
    }
    else if (browser_is_program(path, false, false)) {
        if (strchr(path, ';') != NULL)
            return false;
        quote = false;
    }
    else {
        quote = strspn(path, SHELL_WORD) != length;
        if (quote && strchr(path, '\'') != NULL)
            return false;
    }
    if (length + (quote ? 2 : 0) + 1 > size)
        return false;
    if (!quote)
        snprintf(out, size, "%s", path);
    else if (windows)
        snprintf(out, size, "\"%s\"", path);
    else
        snprintf(out, size, "'%s'", path);
    return true;
}

// A function to give the path a program's command names, the inverse of browser_program_command(): the text
// inside its quotes when it is quoted whole ('...' or "..."), else the command as it is (whether that is a
// file is the caller's question). False, with `out` empty, when it does not fit.
bool browser_program_path(const char *command, char *out, size_t size)
{
    out[0] = '\0';
    size_t length = strlen(command);
    bool quoted = length >= 2 && (command[0] == '"' || command[0] == '\'') && command[length - 1] == command[0] &&
                  memchr(command + 1, command[0], length - 2) == NULL;
    const char *start = quoted ? command + 1 : command;
    size_t kept = quoted ? length - 2 : length;
    if (kept + 1 > size)
        return false;
    memcpy(out, start, kept);
    out[kept] = '\0';
    return true;
}

// A function to give a program's file name without its extension, as its tile's title starts (a name
// whose only dot is its first keeps it: ".tool")
void browser_program_title(const char *path, char *out, size_t size)
{
    fileio_base_name(path, out, size);
    char *dot = strrchr(out, '.');
    if (dot != NULL && dot != out)
        *dot = '\0';
}

// A function to read the icon a .desktop file names, from its text: the [Desktop Entry] group's first Icon=,
// its spaces at either end dropped, as applist.c reads it. NoDisplay and Hidden are not read: a tile can run
// a file the app list leaves out, and its icon is its own all the same (Fable review M18). False, with `out`
// empty, for no Icon= there, an empty one, or one that does not fit.
bool browser_desktop_icon(const char *text, size_t length, char *out, size_t size)
{
    out[0] = '\0';
    bool in_entry = false;
    for (size_t at = 0; at < length;) {
        size_t end = at;
        while (end < length && text[end] != '\n')
            end++;
        const char *line = text + at;
        size_t line_length = end - at;
        at = end + 1;
        if (line_length > 0 && line[line_length - 1] == '\r')
            line_length--;
        if (line_length == 0 || line[0] == '#')
            continue;
        if (line[0] == '[') {
            in_entry = line_length == 15 && memcmp(line, "[Desktop Entry]", 15) == 0;
            continue;
        }
        if (!in_entry || line_length < 4 || memcmp(line, "Icon", 4) != 0)
            continue;
        size_t k = 4;
        while (k < line_length && line[k] == ' ')
            k++;
        if (k == line_length || line[k] != '=')
            continue;   // Icon[de]=, Iconic=: another key
        k++;
        while (k < line_length && line[k] == ' ')
            k++;
        size_t value_end = line_length;
        while (value_end > k && line[value_end - 1] == ' ')
            value_end--;
        if (value_end == k || value_end - k + 1 > size)
            return false;
        memcpy(out, line + k, value_end - k);
        out[value_end - k] = '\0';
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

```c
// A function to turn a remote's key into the list picker's
static ListPickCommand list_key(const char *command)
{
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_UP))
        return LISTPICK_UP;
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_DOWN))
        return LISTPICK_DOWN;
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_LEFT))
        return LISTPICK_PAGE_UP;
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_RIGHT))
        return LISTPICK_PAGE_DOWN;
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_SELECT))
        return LISTPICK_OK;
    return LISTPICK_BACK;
}

// A function to open a list the screen made (see settings_pickers.h)
void pickers_open_list(const char *label, ListPick *made, void (*chosen)(const char *value))
{
    close_picker();
    if (made == NULL) {
        log_error("Settings: the list cannot open: out of memory");
        return;
    }
    list = made;
    list_chosen = chosen;
    copy_string(list_label, label, sizeof(list_label));
    forget_list_log();
    kind = PICKER_LIST;
    log_debug("Settings: opened the list for %s (%i rows)", label, listpick_count(list));
}

// A function to make the app list's rows from the apps Task 7's scan found, as the filter leaves them, the
// cursor on the first; nothing matching is one grayed row that says so. While the scan runs, or with no
// apps, there are no rows. Out of memory the list closes, and says so.
static void make_app_list(void)
{
    listpick_free(list);
    list = NULL;
    const AppList *apps = settings_apps(NULL, NULL);
    apps_listed = apps != NULL;
    int count = apps != NULL ? applist_count(apps) : 0;
    if (count == 0)
        return;   // The column says why there is none, or that the apps are being found
    int *rows = calloc((size_t) count, sizeof(int));
    ListPick *made = rows != NULL ? listpick_create() : NULL;
    bool ok = made != NULL;
    int shown = ok ? applist_filter(apps, app_filter, rows, count) : 0;
    char value[16];
    for (int i = 0; ok && i < shown; i++) {
        snprintf(value, sizeof(value), "%d", rows[i]);
        ok = listpick_add(made, applist_item(apps, rows[i])->name, value, true, NULL);
    }
    if (ok && shown == 0)
        ok = listpick_add(made, "No app matches", "", false, "No app's name holds what was typed");
    free(rows);
    if (!ok) {
        listpick_free(made);
        log_error("Settings: the app list cannot be made: out of memory");
        close_picker();
        return;
    }
    list = made;
    forget_list_log();
    log_debug("Settings: the app list shows %i of %i apps%s%s", shown, count, app_filter[0] != '\0' ? " for " : "", app_filter);
}

// A function to follow the app list's filter as it is typed, at once
static void app_filter_changed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    copy_string(app_filter, text, sizeof(app_filter));
    if (kind == PICKER_APPS)
        make_app_list();
}

// A function to open the keyboard on the app list's filter (Task 12's way into it for a filtered list):
// `first` is the character a real keyboard's key typed to open it, or NULL (Up from the top row)
static void open_app_filter(const char *first)
{
    pickers_open_keyboard("Filter the apps", app_filter, MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX, NULL, NULL, app_filter_changed);
    pickers_keyboard_follow(app_filter_changed, 0);
    if (first != NULL)
        pickers_keyboard_type(first);
}

// A function to open the app list (see settings_pickers.h): Task 7's scan starts with its first opening in a
// visit (settings_apps_start() does nothing after that), and the rows come once it has found the apps
// (pickers_tick())
void pickers_open_apps(void (*chosen)(const AppItem *item))
{
    close_picker();
    settings_apps_start();
    app_chosen = chosen;
    app_filter[0] = '\0';
    kind = PICKER_APPS;
    pickers_set_typing(open_app_filter);
    make_app_list();
    log_debug("Settings: opened the app list");
}

// A function to act on a key in the app list: while the apps are found, or when there are none, Back alone
// closes it; Up from the top row opens the keyboard on its filter
static void apps_command(const char *command)
{
    if (list == NULL) {
        if (MATCH(command, SCMD_BACK))
            close_picker();
        return;
    }
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_UP) && listpick_cursor(list) == 0) {
        open_app_filter(NULL);
        return;
    }
    ListPickResult result = listpick_command(list, list_key(command), list_page);
    if (result == LISTPICK_CANCELED)
        close_picker();
    else if (result == LISTPICK_CHOSEN) {
        const AppItem *item = applist_item(settings_apps(NULL, NULL), atoi(listpick_chosen(list)));
        void (*chosen)(const AppItem *item) = app_chosen;
        close_picker();
        log_debug("Settings: chose the app %s", item != NULL ? item->name : "?");
        if (item != NULL && chosen != NULL)
            chosen(item);
    }
}

// A function to draw the app list: its rows, or "Finding apps... (N)" while the scan runs, or why there are none
static void draw_apps(int x, int top, int bottom)
{
    if (list != NULL) {
        draw_list(x, top, bottom);
        return;
    }
    int found = 0;
    const char *why = NULL;
    settings_apps(&found, &why);   // No reason while the scan runs: its count so far
    char text[300];
    if (why == NULL)
        snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "Finding apps\xE2\x80\xA6 (%i)", found);
    else
        snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%s", why);
    host.text(host.font_row, text, x + host.margin / 2, top, host.column_width - host.margin, 255, false);
}
```

```c
// A function to open the folder browser in a mode at a start, listing folders through `lister` and saying

static bool start_browser(BrowserMode mode, const char *start, BrowserList lister, BrowserCheck check, void *context)
{
    FileioPlace *places = NULL;

    BrowserPlace *list = calloc((size_t) (count > 0 ? count : 1), sizeof(BrowserPlace));

    test_fail("browser", true);
    browser = list != NULL ? browser_open(mode, start, list, count, lister, check, context, &why) : NULL;
    test_fail("browser", false);
    free(list);
    fileio_free_places(places, count);
    if (browser == NULL) {
        log_error("Settings: the folder browser cannot open: %s", why);
        return false;
    }
    browser_mode = mode;
    browser_first = 0;
    browser_note[0] = '\0';
    log_browsing();
    preview_highlighted();
    return true;
}

// A function to open the folder browser for an Image, Folder or Mappings file setting, at its current path
static void open_browser(SettingSlot *slot)
{
    // Paths are checked against config.ini as the save will find it; unread, by the key alone
    size_t length = 0;
    char *text = fileio_read_all(config.config_path, &length);
    browser_doc = text != NULL ? inidoc_parse(text, length) : NULL;
    alloc_free(text);
    BrowserMode mode = slot->def->id == SET_ID_BACKGROUND_IMAGE ? BROWSER_IMAGE
                     : slot->def->id == SET_ID_GAMEPAD_MAPPINGS ? BROWSER_FILE : BROWSER_FOLDER;
    if (!start_browser(mode, slot->value.text, list_folder, check_path, slot)) {
        inidoc_free(browser_doc);
        browser_doc = NULL;
        return;
    }
    browser_slot = slot;
    browser_offer_typing(browser);   // 3c: every listing ends with Type a path...
}

// A function to list a folder for the program browser: as the folder browser lists one, with every file that
// is not a program hidden (browser_is_program()), so its rows are folders and programs alone
static int list_programs(const char *folder, FileioEntry **entries, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    int count = fileio_list(folder, entries);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        FileioEntry *entry = &(*entries)[i];
        if (!entry->is_file || entry->hidden)
            continue;
        bool executable = false;
#ifndef _WIN32
        char path[BROWSER_PATH_MAX];
        snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%s", folder, entry->name);
        executable = access(path, X_OK) == 0;
#endif
        if (!browser_is_program(entry->name, executable, PROGRAM_WINDOWS)) {
            entry->hidden = true;
            log_debug("Settings: the program browser leaves out %s", entry->name);
        }
    }
    return count;
}

// A function to find the library icon a new tile's title matches (iconmatch.c); NULL for none, or when out of
// memory (the tile then takes its own icon or apps, and the Icon page offers the match later)
static const char *matched_icon(const char *title)
{
    int count = library_count();
    LibraryInfo *icons = count > 0 ? calloc((size_t) count, sizeof(LibraryInfo)) : NULL;
    for (int i = 0; icons != NULL && i < count; i++)
        icons[i] = *library_info(i);
    int found = icons != NULL ? iconmatch_find(title, icons, count) : -1;
    free(icons);
    return found >= 0 ? library_info(found)->name : NULL;
}

// A function to say why a program cannot be a tile's command, or NULL: its command cannot be written, or the
// line it would be written in would not fit config.ini (Fable review M13): a tile's Command keeps the tile's
// own title and icon; a new tile takes the file's name as its title and its library match or apps as its
// icon (an own icon's path is weighed again as it is written, and new_tile_icon() takes apps when the line
// cannot hold it). The reasons are the menus model's, which outlive the rows.
static const char *check_program(const char *path, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    char command[INIDOC_MAX_LINE + 1];
    char name[BROWSER_PATH_MAX];
    char title[MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX + 1];
    if (!browser_program_command(path, PROGRAM_WINDOWS, command, sizeof(command)))
        return PROGRAM_WINDOWS ? "This path can't be written as a command" : "A path with ' or ; can't be run from here";
    if (!choosing.adding)
        return settings_command_problem(model, choosing.menu, choosing.tile, command);
    browser_program_title(path, name, sizeof(name));
    settings_tile_title(name, title, sizeof(title));
    const char *match = matched_icon(title);
    return menuedit_check_tile(title, match != NULL ? match : LIBRARY_FALLBACK_ICON, command);
}

// A function to open the program browser (spec "Browse for a program ›"): file mode, programs alone, at
// `start` (a program's path, or a folder; "" as the folder browser opens)
static void open_program_browser(const char *start, void (*chosen)(const char *path))
{
    if (!start_browser(BROWSER_FILE, start, list_programs, check_program, NULL))
        return;
    browser_slot = NULL;
    browser_chose = chosen;
}
```

```c
// A function to get a tile of the menus model by the settings' menu and the tile's index; NULL for none
static const MenuTile *screen_tile(int menu, int tile)
{
    const MenuEditMenu *m = menu >= 0 && menu < menu_count && menu_edit != NULL
                          ? menuedit_menu(menu_edit, menuedit_find(menu_edit, menus[menu]->name)) : NULL;
    return m != NULL && tile >= 0 && tile < m->count ? &m->tiles[tile] : NULL;
}

#ifndef _WIN32
// A function to read the icon a Linux app's .desktop file names, from a tile's command: the file (any
// ";<action>" after it dropped, as unix.c launches it), read whole, its Icon= whatever its NoDisplay or
// Hidden say (browser_desktop_icon(), Fable review M18). False for a command that is no .desktop file, `why`
// left "", and for a file that cannot be read or names no icon, with why. 13b's Icon page reads it too.
static bool desktop_icon_name(const char *command, char *out, size_t size, char *why, size_t why_size)
{
    char file[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    snprintf(file, sizeof(file), "%s", command);
    file[strcspn(file, ";")] = '\0';
    size_t length = strlen(file);
    if (length <= 8 || strcmp(file + length - 8, ".desktop") != 0)
        return false;
    size_t text_length = 0;
    char *text = fileio_read_all(file, &text_length);
    if (text == NULL) {
        snprintf(why, why_size, "%s could not be read: %s", file, fileio_last_error());
        return false;
    }
    bool named = browser_desktop_icon(text, text_length, out, size);
    alloc_free(text);
    if (!named)
        snprintf(why, why_size, "%s names no icon", file);
    return named;
}
#endif

// A function to read an app's own icon by what names it (Windows: its AppsFolder app ID, appicon_image();
// Linux: its Icon= value, looked up as iconfind_path() does over the data folders applist_data_dirs() names:
// $XDG_DATA_HOME, else ~/.local/share; each of $XDG_DATA_DIRS, else /usr/local/share and /usr/share; then
// the Flatpak exports' and Snap's, in that order; an SVG read at 512 px by load_icon_surface(), so it plates
// sharp) and center it on the library's plate (plate_icon(), spec "Icons", choice 2), in memory: it is
// written to a file only when it is used. NULL, with why, when it cannot be found, read or plated (the test
// hook STREAMFLEX_TEST_FAIL=plate fails the plating, which 13b documents with check 85); icon_from says
// where it came from. 13b's Icon page reads its own icon through it too.
static SDL_Surface *plated_icon(const char *named, char *why, size_t size)
{
    SDL_Surface *image = NULL;
#ifdef _WIN32
    snprintf(icon_from, sizeof(icon_from), "the AppsFolder app %s", named);
    image = appicon_image(named, OWN_ICON_ASKED);
#else
    char path[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    char home[MAX_PATH_CHARS + 1];
    char folders[4 * SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    const char *dirs[ICON_DATA_DIRS];
    int count = applist_data_dirs(getenv("XDG_DATA_HOME"), getenv("XDG_DATA_DIRS"),
                                  home_directory(home, sizeof(home)) ? home : NULL, folders, sizeof(folders),
                                  dirs, ICON_DATA_DIRS);
    if (!iconfind_path(named, dirs, count < ICON_DATA_DIRS ? count : ICON_DATA_DIRS, path, sizeof(path))) {
        snprintf(why, size, "its icon %s is in none of the icon folders", named);
        return NULL;
    }
    snprintf(icon_from, sizeof(icon_from), "%s", path);
    image = load_icon_surface(path, PLATE_SIZE);
#endif
    if (image == NULL) {
        snprintf(why, size, "%s could not be read: %s", icon_from, SDL_GetError());
        return NULL;
    }
    bool failing = test_failing("plate");
    SDL_Surface *on_plate = failing ? NULL : plate_icon(image, PLATE_SIZE);
    if (on_plate == NULL)
        snprintf(why, size, "%s could not be put on a plate: %s", icon_from, failing ? "the test hook failed it" : SDL_GetError());
    SDL_DestroySurface(image);
    return on_plate;
}

// A function to choose a new tile's icon as it is added (user ruling 2026-10-16, Fable review I5; spec
// "Icons", in its order): the library icon its title matches; else the app's own icon, plated and written
// as a new PNG in the icons folder (named from the title, never over a file that is there) and listed for
// Discard, when the tile's line can hold its path (weighed first, so a refusal leaves no file); else the
// library's apps. `named` names the app's own icon (the app list's AppItem.icon: Linux its Icon= value,
// Windows its app ID), or is NULL to read it from a .desktop command (Linux: a browsed .desktop file; a
// Windows program browsed has none). `out` gets a library name or the PNG's path; the log says which, and
// why an own icon was not used.
static void new_tile_icon(const char *title, const char *named, const char *command, char *out, size_t size)
{
    const char *match = matched_icon(title);
    if (match != NULL) {
        snprintf(out, size, "%s", match);
        log_debug("Menus: the new tile '%s' takes the library icon %s, its match", title, match);
        return;
    }
    snprintf(out, size, "%s", LIBRARY_FALLBACK_ICON);
    char why[2 * SETTING_TEXT_MAX] = "";
    char value[SETTING_TEXT_MAX] = "";
    if (named != NULL)
        snprintf(value, sizeof(value), "%s", named);
#ifndef _WIN32
    else if (!desktop_icon_name(command, value, sizeof(value), why, sizeof(why)))
        value[0] = '\0';
#endif
    SDL_Surface *on_plate = value[0] != '\0' ? plated_icon(value, why, sizeof(why)) : NULL;
    if (on_plate != NULL) {
        char dir[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
        char path[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
        const char *refused = NULL;
        if (!icons_dir(dir, sizeof(dir)))
            snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "the icons folder could not be made: %s", fileio_last_error());
        else if (!icons_new_path(dir, title, path, sizeof(path)))
            snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "no new icon file could be named in %s", dir);
        else if ((refused = menuedit_check_tile(title, path, command)) != NULL)
            snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "its line could not hold %s: %s", path, refused);
        else if (!plate_save(on_plate, path))
            snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "it could not be saved to %s: %s", path, SDL_GetError());
        else {
            settings_note_plated(path);
            snprintf(out, size, "%s", path);
            log_debug("Menus: the new tile '%s' takes its own icon from %s, saved to %s", title, icon_from, path);
        }
        SDL_DestroySurface(on_plate);
        if (why[0] == '\0')
            return;
    }
    if (why[0] != '\0')
        log_debug("Menus: the new tile '%s' has no icon of its own: %s", title, why);
    log_debug("Menus: the new tile '%s' takes the generic icon %s", title, LIBRARY_FALLBACK_ICON);
}

// A function to take an app the app list chose: a new tile (its name the title; its library match, else
// its own icon, else apps, new_tile_icon()), or a tile's new command
static void app_chosen(const AppItem *item)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    if (choosing.adding) {
        char title[MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX + 1];
        char icon[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
        settings_tile_title(item->name, title, sizeof(title));
        new_tile_icon(title, item->icon, item->command, icon, sizeof(icon));
        event = settings_add_tile(model, title, icon, item->command);
    }
    else
        event = settings_set_command(model, choosing.menu, choosing.tile, item->command);
    handle_event(&event);
}

// A function to take a program the program browser chose: a new tile (its file's name the title, its icon
// as new_tile_icon() chooses it), or a tile's new command; the browser opens on it next time
static void program_chosen(const char *path)
{
    char command[INIDOC_MAX_LINE + 1];
    char name[BROWSER_PATH_MAX];
    char title[MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX + 1];
    char icon[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    copy_string(program_last, path, sizeof(program_last));
    if (!browser_program_command(path, PROGRAM_WINDOWS, command, sizeof(command)))
        return;   // check_program() refused every such row
    SettingsEvent event;
    if (choosing.adding) {
        browser_program_title(path, name, sizeof(name));
        settings_tile_title(name, title, sizeof(title));
        new_tile_icon(title, NULL, command, icon, sizeof(icon));
        event = settings_add_tile(model, title, icon, command);
    }
    else
        event = settings_set_command(model, choosing.menu, choosing.tile, command);
    handle_event(&event);
}

// A function to say why a tile cannot run a command as typed (the keyboard's validator)
static const char *command_problem(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    return settings_command_problem(model, choosing.menu, choosing.tile, text);
}

// A function to take a typed command
static void command_typed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    SettingsEvent event = settings_set_command(model, choosing.menu, choosing.tile, text);
    handle_event(&event);
}

// A function to act on the row a tile's command list chose: the app list, the program browser (at the
// tile's own program when its command names a file, as it is or inside the quotes a browsed path was
// written in), the keyboard, or a special command
static void tile_command_chosen(const char *value)
{
    const MenuTile *tile = screen_tile(choosing.menu, choosing.tile);
    if (tile == NULL)
        return;
    if (strcmp(value, CHOOSE_APP) == 0)
        pickers_open_apps(app_chosen);
    else if (strcmp(value, CHOOSE_PROGRAM) == 0) {
        char path[BROWSER_PATH_MAX];
        bool own = browser_program_path(tile->command, path, sizeof(path)) && fileio_is_file(path);
        open_program_browser(own ? path : program_last, program_chosen);
    }
    else if (strcmp(value, CHOOSE_TYPED) == 0) {
        char label[MENUEDIT_TITLE_MAX + 32];
        snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "Command for %s", tile->title);
        pickers_open_keyboard(label, tile->command, INIDOC_MAX_LINE, command_problem, NULL, command_typed);
    }
    else {
        SettingsEvent event = settings_set_command(model, choosing.menu, choosing.tile, value);
        handle_event(&event);
    }
}

// A function to open a tile's command list (spec "Command ›"): the app list, a browse, the special
// commands (never :select, which no tile may run), then Type...; the cursor on the tile's command, pinned
// first as Custom when no row gives it
static void open_tile_commands(int menu, int tile)
{
    static const char *const specials[] = { SCMD_HOME, SCMD_BACK, SCMD_SETTINGS, SCMD_SLEEP, SCMD_RESTART,
                                            SCMD_SHUTDOWN, SCMD_QUIT };
    const MenuTile *t = screen_tile(menu, tile);
    if (t == NULL)
        return;
    choosing.adding = false;
    choosing.menu = menu;
    choosing.tile = tile;
    char label[LISTPICK_TEXT_MAX];
    ListPick *made = listpick_create();
    bool ok = made != NULL && listpick_add(made, "App", CHOOSE_APP, true, NULL) &&
              listpick_add(made, "Browse for a program", CHOOSE_PROGRAM, true, NULL);
    for (size_t i = 0; ok && i < sizeof(specials) / sizeof(specials[0]); i++) {
        setting_command_label(specials[i], label, sizeof(label));
        ok = listpick_add(made, label, specials[i], true, NULL);
    }
    ok = ok && listpick_add(made, "Type" ELLIPSIS, CHOOSE_TYPED, true, NULL);
    snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "Custom: %s", t->command);
    ok = ok && listpick_select(made, t->command, label);
    if (!ok) {
        listpick_free(made);
        made = NULL;
    }
    pickers_open_list("Command", made, tile_command_chosen);
}
```

In `src/image.c`, after `rasterize_svg()` (`:605-608`), add:

```c
// A function to read an icon file whole, on the main thread (its rasterizer is the main thread's): an
// SVG rasterized `size` px wide, its height in proportion, so an app's own icon plates sharp and a
// library icon fills a button; any other image decoded at its own size. NULL, with SDL's error set, when
// it cannot be read.
SDL_Surface *load_icon_surface(const char *path, int size)
{
    size_t length = strlen(path);
    if (length <= 4 || SDL_strcasecmp(path + length - 4, ".svg") != 0)
        return load_image_file(path);
    char *buffer = SDL_LoadFile(path, NULL);
    if (buffer == NULL)
        return NULL;
    char error[256];
    int width = 0, height = 0;
    unsigned char *pixels = rasterize_pixels(rasterizer, buffer, size, -1, &width, &height, error, sizeof(error));
    SDL_free(buffer);
    if (pixels == NULL) {
        SDL_SetError("%s", error);
        return NULL;
    }
    // nanosvg writes R, G, B, A bytes in memory order: SDL_PIXELFORMAT_RGBA32
    SDL_Surface *surface = SDL_CreateSurface(width, height, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_RGBA32);
    if (surface != NULL) {
        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++)
            SDL_memcpy((Uint8 *) surface->pixels + y * surface->pitch, pixels + y * 4 * width, (size_t) (4 * width));
    }
    free(pixels);
    return surface;
}
```

```bash
    Return Menu

log=$out/f82-scanfail.log
grep -q '^Apps: none listed: ' "$log" && sed -n '/^\[Main\]/,/^$/p' "$cfg" | grep -qx 'Entry3=Home;home;:home' \
    && ran_clean f82-scanfail && ok=0
result "tiles: a failed app scan says why, and Special still adds (exit $(cat "$out/f82-scanfail.code"))" $ok
grep -E '^Apps:|Settings: the note under the preview' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# (Settings closed while the scan runs, Review Focus 4, is check 81's f81-closed: the one scan is Task 7's.)

# A tile's Command, Browse for a program: it opens at the tile's own program, lists programs alone (the
# README without its execute bit is left out), and run-kodi.sh becomes the command. Then the Tiles page's
# Add, Browse for a program, which opens on the program last chosen: Up to old-tool.sh, added at the end,
# titled by its file's name, with the generic icon (no library match, and a script names no icon of its own).
rm -rf "$TESTER_HOME/progs82"; mkdir -p "$TESTER_HOME/progs82"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$TESTER_HOME/progs82/old-tool.sh"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$TESTER_HOME/progs82/run-kodi.sh"
printf 'not a program\n' > "$TESTER_HOME/progs82/readme.txt"
chmod 755 "$TESTER_HOME/progs82/old-tool.sh" "$TESTER_HOME/progs82/run-kodi.sh"
chmod 644 "$TESTER_HOME/progs82/readme.txt"
chown -R tester:tester "$TESTER_HOME/progs82"
cfg=$(writable_config f82-progs)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-browse $E82_TILES Down Return Down Return Down Down Return Down Return BackSpace Up Return \
    Down Return Up Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-browse.log
[ "$(e82_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Main]|Entry1=Tool;apps;/home/tester/progs82/run-kodi.sh|Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit|Entry3=old-tool;apps;/home/tester/progs82/old-tool.sh|' ] \
    && grep -q 'Settings: the program browser leaves out readme.txt' "$log" \
    && grep -qx "Menus: the new tile 'old-tool' takes the generic icon apps" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the list's cursor reads Custom: /home/tester/progs82/old-tool.sh" "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: chose /home/tester/progs82/run-kodi.sh' "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: chose /home/tester/progs82/old-tool.sh' "$log" && ran_clean f82-browse && ok=0
result "tiles: Browse for a program lists programs alone, sets a command and adds a tile (exit $(cat "$out/f82-browse.code"))" $ok
grep -E 'Settings: (the program browser|chose|browsing|opened the list)' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A tile's Command, Type...: the keyboard opens on its command; " now" typed on a real keyboard after it
cfg=$(writable_config f82-tiles)
e82_type_now() { e82_type ' now'; }
CFG=$cfg run_keys f82-command $E82_TILES Down Down Return Down Return Right Right Right Return +e82_type_now Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f82-command.log
sed -n '/^\[Main\]/,/^$/p' "$cfg" | grep -qx 'Entry2=Bye;quit;:quit now' \
    && grep -q "Settings: opened the keyboard for Command for Bye" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the keyboard reads ':quit now' (cursor 9)" "$log" && ran_clean f82-command && ok=0
result "tiles: a tile's command typed on the keyboard saves (exit $(cat "$out/f82-command.code"))" $ok
```

`f82-browse`'s keys: Tool's page (Down, OK), Command (Down, OK); the list opens on *Custom: …old-tool.sh*, pinned first, so Down Down is *Browse for a program*; OK; the browser opens in `progs82` on `old-tool.sh`; Down to `run-kodi.sh`, OK; Back to the Tiles page, Up to Add, OK; Down to *Browse for a program*, OK; the browser opens in `progs82` on `run-kodi.sh`, the program last chosen; Up to `old-tool.sh`, OK. `f82-command`'s list opens on *Quit StreamFlex* (`:quit`, a special row), and Right pages to its last row, *Type…*. Task 13a adds the tile page's *Icon ›* row between Title and Command, and with it one `Down` before Command in each of these two runs (fix pass R3); every other run reaches its row from the page's bottom.

**Task 7's hooks, as these runs use them:** `STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS` is a list of applications folders, `:` between them, read in place of the XDG, Flatpak and Snap ones; `STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=fail` makes the scan fail with the reason `appscan_why()` gives (`The apps could not be listed: the test hook failed it`), `empty` makes it find nothing (`No apps were found`), and `delay:<ms>` holds it that long before it finishes (a close of settings stops it at once). Its log lines are `Apps: listing the installed apps`, `Apps: found <N> apps (<ms> ms)`, `Apps: none listed: <why> (<ms> ms)` and `Apps: stopped the app scan as settings closed (<ms> ms)` (fix pass R1: the one vocabulary, which checks 81, 82 and 87 read).

Create `tests/headless/checks/81-apps.sh`:

```bash
# The installed apps (3c, spec "Installed apps"): the first Add > App of a settings visit starts listing them
# on a thread of their own (Task 7's scan), here over the fixture applications folders (the harness build's
# STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS stands in for the XDG folders, the Flatpak exports and Snap's). The log gives the
# count and the time, and the hook build each app in the list's order; a scan that fails or finds nothing
# says why; a folder that is not there holds no apps, and one that cannot be read fails the scan; closing
# settings while it runs stops it and waits for its thread; and a thread that cannot start leaves settings
# working. The list on screen, "Finding apps... (N)" included, is check 82's.
# Not timing-sensitive: every wait ends on a log line (20 s) or a key's frame (60 s); the scan held by
# STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=delay:600000 is stopped by the close however late the close comes, and a close
# that waited it out would miss its frame's 60 s; no result reads a duration

A81=$FX/apps
A81_DIRS=$A81/user:$A81/system:$A81/flatpak:$A81/system
A81_CFG=$FX/f81-apps.ini
A81_ARROW=$(printf ' \xE2\x80\xBA ')
# The top page, Menus, Main, its Tiles row, Add, App: the app list, whose first opening starts the scan
A81_APP="Menu Down Down Return Down Return Down Down Down Return Return Return"
a81_found() { wait_line 'Apps: found' "$2"; }
a81_none() { wait_line 'Apps: none listed' "$2"; }

# A function to list a run's apps as the hook build logged them, joined with |
a81_apps() { grep -o '^Test hook: app [0-9]* is .*' "$1" | sed 's/^Test hook: app [0-9]* is //' | tr '\n' '|'; }

# Every rule at once, in German: the user's Kodi by its German name; the system's Firefox hidden by the
# user's copy (Hidden=true, the same desktop file ID, in an earlier folder); GIMP by its de_DE name;
# NoDisplay, a Link, an uninstaller, a readme, a hidden file and a text file left out; a subfolder's VLC
# and the Flatpak's VLC both listed (two installs: two commands); the system folder named twice adds
# nothing the second time, every file's ID having been read
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$A81_DIRS LC_ALL= LC_MESSAGES= LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-apps $A81_APP +a81_found Menu
log=$out/f81-apps.log
a81_list=$(a81_apps "$log")
a81_want="GIMP Bildbearbeitung, run by $A81/system/gimp.desktop|Kodi Mediencenter, run by $A81/user/kodi.desktop|"
a81_want+="Steam, run by $A81/system/steam.desktop|VLC media player, run by $A81/flatpak/org.videolan.VLC.desktop|"
a81_want+="VLC media player, run by $A81/system/sub/vlc.desktop|"
ok=1
grep -qE '^Apps: found 5 apps \([0-9]+ ms\)$' "$log" && precedes "$log" 'Apps: listing the installed apps' 'Apps: found 5 apps' \
    && precedes "$log" "Settings: page Settings${A81_ARROW}Menus${A81_ARROW}Main${A81_ARROW}Tiles${A81_ARROW}Add" 'Apps: listing the installed apps' \
    && [ "$a81_list" = "$a81_want" ] && ran_clean f81-apps && ok=0
result "apps: settings list every folder's apps by the rules, in the system's language (exit $(cat "$out/f81-apps.code"))" $ok
echo "      ${a81_list:-no apps listed}"
grep -E '^Apps:' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A folder with no .desktop files, and one that is not there: no apps, and that is no failure
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$A81/empty:$TESTER_HOME/a81-not-there UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-empty $A81_APP +a81_none Menu
ok=1
grep -qE '^Apps: none listed: No apps were found \([0-9]+ ms\)$' "$out/f81-empty.log" \
    && ! grep -q '^Test hook: app ' "$out/f81-empty.log" && ran_clean f81-empty && ok=0
result "apps: folders with no apps say none were found (exit $(cat "$out/f81-empty.code"))" $ok

# A folder that is there but cannot be read, beside one that is not there: the scan fails, and says
# which folder and why; settings still close as usual
rm -rf "$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked"
mkdir -p "$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked"
cp "$A81/system/steam.desktop" "$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked/"
chmod 000 "$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked"
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked:$TESTER_HOME/a81-not-there UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-locked $A81_APP +a81_none Menu
chmod 755 "$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked"
rm -rf "$TESTER_HOME/a81-locked"
ok=1
grep -qE "^Apps: none listed: The apps could not be listed: $TESTER_HOME/a81-locked: .+ \([0-9]+ ms\)$" "$out/f81-locked.log" \
    && grep -q '^Settings closed$' "$out/f81-locked.log" && ran_clean f81-locked && ok=0
result "apps: a folder that cannot be read fails the scan, saying which and why (exit $(cat "$out/f81-locked.code"))" $ok
grep -E '^Apps:' "$out/f81-locked.log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# The hook's two outcomes over folders that hold apps: a failure, and nothing found
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$A81_DIRS STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=fail UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-fail $A81_APP +a81_none Menu
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$A81_DIRS STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=empty UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-hookempty $A81_APP +a81_none Menu
ok=1
grep -qE '^Apps: none listed: The apps could not be listed: the test hook failed it \([0-9]+ ms\)$' "$out/f81-fail.log" \
    && grep -qE '^Apps: none listed: No apps were found \([0-9]+ ms\)$' "$out/f81-hookempty.log" \
    && ! grep -q '^Test hook: app ' "$out/f81-fail.log" "$out/f81-hookempty.log" \
    && ran_clean f81-fail && ran_clean f81-hookempty && ok=0
result "apps: a scan that fails or finds nothing says so, and lists nothing (exits $(cat "$out/f81-fail.code"), $(cat "$out/f81-hookempty.code"))" $ok

# Settings closed while the scan runs (held for ten minutes; Review Focus 4): the close stops it and waits
# for its thread before the list it fills is freed, the leak pass finds nothing left, and no verdict is logged
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$A81_DIRS STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=delay:600000 UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-closed $A81_APP Menu
log=$out/f81-closed.log
ok=1
grep -qE '^Apps: stopped the app scan as settings closed \([0-9]+ ms\)$' "$log" \
    && precedes "$log" 'Apps: listing the installed apps' 'Apps: stopped the app scan as settings closed' \
    && precedes "$log" 'Apps: stopped the app scan as settings closed' 'Settings closed' \
    && ! grep -qE '^Apps: (found|none listed)' "$log" && ran_clean f81-closed && ok=0
result "apps: closing settings mid-scan stops the scan and waits for it (exit $(cat "$out/f81-closed.code"))" $ok
grep -E '^(Apps:|Settings closed)' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A thread that cannot start: settings say why, and work as before
CFG=$A81_CFG STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_DIRS=$A81_DIRS STREAMFLEX_TEST_FAIL=appthread UNTIL='Settings closed' \
    run_keys f81-nothread $A81_APP Menu
log=$out/f81-nothread.log
ok=1
grep -q '^Test hook: appthread fails$' "$log" \
    && grep -q '^Apps: the apps cannot be listed: out of memory, or no thread$' "$log" \
    && ! grep -q '^Apps: listing the installed apps' "$log" && grep -q '^Settings closed$' "$log" \
    && ran_clean f81-nothread && ok=0
result "apps: a scan thread that cannot start leaves settings working (exit $(cat "$out/f81-nothread.code"))" $ok
```

`f81-apps`'s `precedes` from the Add page's path line to `Apps: listing the installed apps` pins the lazy start (fix pass R1, Known integration work 4): a scan started as settings open would list before the Add page opened. **What this task decides** (each pinned by a test):
- **Move** is a mode of the tile's page, not a page: OK on *Move* picks the tile up; while it is up, the arrows move it, OK drops it, Back puts it back where it was picked up and ends the mode (staying on the tile's page), and Home or the key that opened settings drop it where it is and close as they would. The key hint reads *Arrows move it · OK drops it · Back puts it back*.
- **The arrows move it as the launcher's own arrows move the highlight** (`settings_move_target()`, `layout_move()`'s rule at `layout.c:293-339`; Fable review M17), in the grid the preview lays the menu out in now (`layout.rows`/`layout.columns`, handed over before each key): in a grid, Left and Right step within the tile's row and stop at its ends, and Up and Down go to the row above or below, keeping the column, onto the last tile of a shorter last row, stopping at the first and last rows; in a one-row strip Left and Right step along it to either end, and Up and Down do nothing. No wrapping, whatever *Wrap around* says: a tile moved past an end would land at the other.
- **Each step** is a `menuedit_move()`, put into the launcher as `SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS` (`settings_menus_changed()`, which lays the menu out again); the preview then selects the tile (`select_entry()`) and outlines it (`outline_entry()`: a white frame round its button, `layout.button / 32` px wide, at least 2). The tile's page and the Tiles page under it follow the tile to its new place.
- **Move to menu ›** lists every other menu in the settings' order. A submenu tile cannot go into the menu it opens (*This tile opens that menu*) nor into any menu that menu leads to through its submenus, however deep (*That menu is inside the one this tile opens*): it would be the only way to a menu that is then only reachable through itself. Those rows are grayed with the reason; when memory runs out working that out, a row is grayed rather than offered. Moving appends the tile to the other menu (Task 3: it gets a new line there) and goes back to the Tiles page.
