```c
// A function to tell whether a menu leads to another through its submenu tiles, however deep; true when out
// of memory, so a move that could not be ruled out is refused
static bool reaches(const MenuEdit *edit, int from, int target)
{
    int count = menuedit_count(edit);
    int *queue = alloc_calloc((size_t) count, sizeof(int));
    bool *seen = alloc_calloc((size_t) count, sizeof(bool));
    bool found = queue == NULL || seen == NULL;
    int head = 0;
    int tail = 0;
    if (!found) {
        queue[tail++] = from;
        seen[from] = true;
    }
    while (!found && head < tail) {
        const MenuEditMenu *menu = menuedit_menu(edit, queue[head++]);
        for (int t = 0; t < menu->count && !found; t++) {
            const char *name = menuedit_submenu_of(&menu->tiles[t]);
            int next = name != NULL ? menuedit_find(edit, name) : -1;
            if (next == target)
                found = true;
            else if (next >= 0 && !seen[next]) {
                seen[next] = true;
                queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
    }
    alloc_free(queue);
    alloc_free(seen);
    return found;
}

// A function to add Move to menu's rows: every other menu. A submenu tile's own menu, and every menu inside
// it, are grayed with the reason: the tile would be the only way to them, inside them.
static int move_to_rows(SettingsState *state, const PageRef *top, SettingsRow *rows, int n, int max)
{
    const MenuTile *tile = edit_tile(state, top->menu, top->tile);
    if (tile == NULL)
        return n;
    int s = opened_menu(state, tile);
    for (int k = 0; k < state->menu_count; k++) {
        if (k == top->menu)
            continue;
        int e = edit_index(state, k);
        SettingsRow row = action_row(state->names[k], SETTINGS_ACTION_MOVE_TO, e >= 0);
        row.menu = k;
        if (s >= 0 && e == s)
            row = grayed(row, true, WHY_OPENS_IT);
        else if (s >= 0 && e >= 0 && reaches(state->menus, s, e))
            row = grayed(row, true, WHY_INSIDE_IT);
        n = add_row(rows, n, max, row);
    }
    return n;
}
```

```c
// A function to give the model the preview's grid as laid out now, which Move steps a tile through
void settings_set_grid(SettingsState *state, int rows, int columns)
{
    state->grid_rows = rows;
    state->grid_columns = columns;
}

// A function to give the tile Move picked up; -1 for none
int settings_moving_tile(const SettingsState *state)
{
    return state->move.active ? state->move.at : -1;
}

// A function to work out where an arrow sends a picked-up tile (spec "Move"), as the launcher's arrows move
// the highlight (layout_move(), layout.c:293-339): in a grid, Left and Right within the tile's row, stopping
// at its ends, Up and Down to the row above or below keeping the column, onto the last tile of a shorter
// last row, stopping at the first and last rows; in a one-row strip (or a grid with no columns) Left and
// Right along it, Up and Down nothing. The launcher's wrap-around is not followed: a tile moved past an end
// would land at the other.
int settings_move_target(int index, int count, int rows, int columns, SettingsCommand command)
{
    if (count <= 0)
        return index;
    index = index < 0 ? 0 : index >= count ? count - 1 : index;
    if (rows <= 1 || columns <= 0) {
        if (command == SETTINGS_RIGHT)
            return index < count - 1 ? index + 1 : index;
        if (command == SETTINGS_LEFT)
            return index > 0 ? index - 1 : index;
        return index;
    }
    int row = index / columns;
    int column = index % columns;
    int last_row = (count - 1) / columns;
    int length = count - row * columns < columns ? count - row * columns : columns;
    if (command == SETTINGS_RIGHT)
        return column < length - 1 ? index + 1 : index;
    if (command == SETTINGS_LEFT)
        return column > 0 ? index - 1 : index;
    int target = command == SETTINGS_DOWN && row < last_row ? row + 1 : command == SETTINGS_UP && row > 0 ? row - 1 : -1;
    if (target < 0)
        return index;
    int target_length = count - target * columns < columns ? count - target * columns : columns;
    return target * columns + (column < target_length - 1 ? column : target_length - 1);
}
```

After Task 10a's `remove_submenu()` add:

```c
// A function to follow a moved tile with the pages: the tile's page is about it at its new place, and the
// Tiles page under it has its cursor on it there
static void moved_to(SettingsState *state, int at)
{
    state->move.at = at;
    state->stack[state->depth].tile = at;
    if (state->depth > 0 && state->stack[state->depth - 1].page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES)
        state->stack[state->depth - 1].cursor = at + 1;   // Add is the first row
}

// A function to act on a key while a tile is picked up (spec "Move"): the arrows move it (settings_move_target(),
// one menuedit_move() a step, which the screen lays out at once); OK drops it; Back puts it back where it was
// picked up. Either ends the mode on the tile's page. Home and the key that opened settings drop it where it
// is, then close settings as they would.
static SettingsEvent move_command(SettingsState *state, SettingsCommand command)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_NONE;
    int e = edit_index(state, state->move.menu);
    const MenuEditMenu *menu = e >= 0 ? menuedit_menu(state->menus, e) : NULL;
    int to = state->move.at;
    switch (command) {
        case SETTINGS_LEFT:
        case SETTINGS_RIGHT:
        case SETTINGS_UP:
        case SETTINGS_DOWN:
            if (menu != NULL)
                to = settings_move_target(state->move.at, menu->count, state->grid_rows, state->grid_columns, command);
            break;
        case SETTINGS_BACK:
            to = state->move.from;
            break;
        case SETTINGS_OK:
        case SETTINGS_HOME:
        case SETTINGS_CLOSE:
            break;
    }
    if (menu != NULL && to != state->move.at) {
        const char *why = menuedit_move(state->menus, e, state->move.at, to);
        if (why != NULL) {
            snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
            return event;
        }
        moved_to(state, to);
        event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
        event.menu = state->move.menu;
        event.tile = to;
    }
    if (command == SETTINGS_OK || command == SETTINGS_BACK || command == SETTINGS_HOME || command == SETTINGS_CLOSE) {
        state->move.active = false;
        if (event.kind == SETTINGS_EVENT_NONE)
            event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    }
    if (command == SETTINGS_HOME || command == SETTINGS_CLOSE)
        event.kind = command == SETTINGS_HOME ? SETTINGS_EVENT_CLOSE_HOME : SETTINGS_EVENT_CLOSE;
    return event;
}

// A function to move the tile page's tile to the end of another menu, back on the Tiles page on the tile now
// in its place
static SettingsEvent move_to_menu(SettingsState *state, int to_menu)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    int menu = state->stack[state->depth].menu;
    int t = state->stack[state->depth].tile;
    const char *why = menuedit_move_to_menu(state->menus, edit_index(state, menu), t, edit_index(state, to_menu));
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
        return event;
    }
    back_to_tiles(state, state->depth - 2, t);
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
    event.menu = menu;
    event.tile = -1;
    return event;
}
```

```c
static int outlined = -1;   // The tile the settings preview outlines while Move has it up; -1: none

// A function to outline a tile of the menu on show in the settings preview while Move has it picked up
// (spec "Move": the preview outlines it); -1 for none. The log says when it changes.
void outline_entry(int index)
{
    if (index == outlined)
        return;
    outlined = index;
    if (index < 0)
        log_debug("Settings: no tile outlined");
    else
        log_debug("Menu '%s': tile %i outlined", current_menu != NULL ? current_menu->name : "?", index);
}

// A function to draw the outline round a picked-up tile's button: white, a thirty-second of the button wide
// and never under 2 px, so it reads over the highlight
static void draw_outline(const SDL_Rect *button)
{
    int width = layout.button / 32 > 2 ? layout.button / 32 : 2;
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF);
    for (int i = 1; i <= width; i++) {
        SDL_Rect box = { button->x - i, button->y - i, button->w + 2 * i, button->h + 2 * i };
        outline_rect(renderer, &box);
    }
}
```

```bash
# Moving tiles (3c, spec "Move"): OK on Move picks a tile up and the preview outlines it; the arrows move it
# through Main's 2 x 2 grid while the preview lays the menu out again; OK drops it, Back puts it back; and
# Move to menu, which a submenu tile cannot use to go into its own menu or a menu inside it. Each saved
# config.ini is read line by line.
# Not timing-sensitive: every key waits for its frame, and every result is read from the log's lines or the saved file, never from a clock

E83_TILES="Menu Down Down Return Down Return Down Down Down Return"   # Main's Tiles page
E83_MOVE="Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Up Up Up"          # A tile's page: Move, three above Remove
E83_MOVE_TO="Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Down Up Up"          # Move to menu, two above Remove
e83_lines() { grep -v '^$' "$1" | tr '\n' '|'; }

# One picked up, Right, Right (the row's end: it stays), Down, dropped: Two, Three, Games, One, each line
# keeping its key; the second Right moves nothing, as the launcher's own highlight stops at a row's end
cfg=$(writable_config f83-move)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f83-move $E83_TILES Down Return $E83_MOVE Return Right Right Down Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f83-move.log
[ "$(sed -n '/^\[Main\]/,/^$/p' "$cfg" | grep -v '^$' | tr '\n' '|')" = '[Main]|Entry2=Two;apps;:home|Entry3=Three;apps;:home|Entry4=Games;games;:submenu Games|Entry1=One;apps;:home|' ] \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 0 outlined" "$log" && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 1 outlined" "$log" \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 3 outlined" "$log" && ! grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 2 outlined" "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: no tile outlined' "$log" \
    && grep -q "Settings: the key hint reads Arrows move it $(printf '\xC2\xB7') OK drops it $(printf '\xC2\xB7') Back puts it back" "$log" \
    && in_range "$log" "Menu 'Main': tile 0 outlined" 'Settings: no tile outlined' "Menus: the launcher's menus were made again" \
    && ran_clean f83-move && ok=0
result "move: a tile picked up, moved right to its row's end and down, and dropped, saves in its place (exit $(cat "$out/f83-move.code"))" $ok
grep -E "outlined|Settings: (the key hint|the menus changed)" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# Two picked up, Down a row (two columns): One, Three, Games, Two
cfg=$(writable_config f83-move)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f83-down $E83_TILES Down Down Return $E83_MOVE Return Down Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f83-down.log
[ "$(sed -n '/^\[Main\]/,/^$/p' "$cfg" | grep -v '^$' | tr '\n' '|')" = '[Main]|Entry1=One;apps;:home|Entry3=Three;apps;:home|Entry4=Games;games;:submenu Games|Entry2=Two;apps;:home|' ] \
    && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 3 outlined" "$log" && grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 3 selected" "$log" \
    && ran_clean f83-down && ok=0
result "move: Down moves a tile a row of the grid (exit $(cat "$out/f83-down.code"))" $ok

# Three picked up, Left (the row's start: it stays), Up (the first), then Back: put back where it was, and
# nothing saved

CFG=$cfg run_keys f83-cancel $E83_TILES Down Down Down Return $E83_MOVE Return Left Up BackSpace Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f83-cancel.log
grep -q "Menu 'Main': tile 0 outlined" "$log" && grep -q 'Settings: no tile outlined' "$log" \
    && grep -q 'Settings: nothing changed' "$log" && cmp -s "$FX/f83-move.ini" "$cfg" && ran_clean f83-cancel && ok=0
result "move: Back puts a moved tile back, and nothing is saved (exit $(cat "$out/f83-cancel.code"))" $ok

# Two moved to Arcade: at its end, with a new line there
cfg=$(writable_config f83-move)
CFG=$cfg run_keys f83-moveto $E83_TILES Down Down Return $E83_MOVE_TO Return Down Return Menu
ok=1
log=$out/f83-moveto.log
[ "$(e83_lines "$cfg")" = '[General]|DefaultMenu=Main|[Layout]|Rows=2|Columns=2|[Main]|Entry1=One;apps;:home|Entry3=Three;apps;:home|Entry4=Games;games;:submenu Games|[Games]|Entry1=Arcade;games;:submenu Arcade|[Arcade]|Entry1=Pong;games;:back|Entry2=Two;apps;:home|' ] \
```

### Task 13: The Icon page

Task 13 is split in two, each a commit of its own with its own implementer and reviewer: **13a** is the pure half (the library grid's model, the AppsFolder ID read back from a command, the Icon page's rows and events in `settings.c`, and opening the pages at a tile), proven by CTest; **13b** is the SDL half (the grid picker, the app's own icon read and plated, the preview, the Icon page's choices on screen) and headless check 85. 13b needs 13a's commit.

**What 13a and 13b take from Tasks 10-12** (as `tasks-10-12.md` defines them; Known integration work 8):
- Task 10a's pages are `SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES` (one menu's tiles: *Add ›*, then one row per tile, labeled by its title) and `SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE` (one tile: *Title*, Task 10b's *Command ›*, Task 11's *Move* and *Move to menu ›*, *Add after this tile ›* and *Remove*; 13a adds *Icon ›* after Title, the spec's order); `PageRef` gains `int tile` and `SettingsRow` gains `int tile`; the Menu page's *Tiles ›* row is `link_row(..., SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES, m)`. On the Tiles page **a submenu tile's row is a `SETTINGS_ROW_LINK` to `SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE` and every other tile's an ACTION row (`SETTINGS_ACTION_OPEN_TILE`)**, each with `menu = m` and `tile = t` (`tile_row()`). Pages open through Task 10a's static `open_page(state, page, menu, tile)` (its `push_page()` is a two-line wrapper over it), and a link row's OK calls `open_page(state, row->target, row->menu, row->tile)`. **Decisions this task makes** (where the spec and the skeleton leave room; each is pinned by a test):
- **The Icon page is a settings page whose choices the screen finds.** Which library icon matches, and whether the app has an icon of its own, take the library and the platform, which the pure model cannot reach. The page opens with *Library ›* and *Browse for an image ›* alone (`ready` false); the screen looks, as the page opens, and hands its findings over with `settings_set_icon_choices()`, which puts the cursor on the first row. The rows are then, in the spec's order: **the library icon offered first** (the match, labeled by the icon's title, valued *Library match*; with no match and no icon of its own, the generic `apps`, valued *Generic icon*), ***Its own icon***, ***Library ›*** and ***Browse for an image ›***. The first row that applies is the one the cursor rests on: that is the spec's preselection.
- **OK on a row never sets the icon by itself.** OK on any of the four rows gives `SETTINGS_EVENT_ICON` with the row's action, and the page stays: the screen writes a file or opens a picker, sets the icon it chose with `settings_set_icon()` (the twin of Task 10b's `settings_set_command()`: `SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS` for the screen's `handle_event()`, or `MOVED` with the reason as the notice when the tile's line could not hold it), then calls `settings_icon_done()`, with `NULL` (chosen: back to the tile's page) or the reason it could not (the page stays, the reason in the caption until the next key).
- **The Icon page knows its tile from the row that opens it**: the tile page's *Icon ›* row carries the tile (`icon.tile = top->tile`), which Task 10a's `open_page()` gives the Icon page, and opening it empties the choices, so each opening looks again.
- **The preview follows the tile's menu and highlights its tile** on the Icon page, as on the other Tiles pages: 13a adds `SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON` to Task 10a's `tiles_page()`, which `settings_preview_menu()` and `settings_preview_tile()` read.
- **`settings_show_tile()` opens the pages at a tile** by the remote's own route: on each page it puts the cursor on the row that leads on (*Menus*, the menu's row, *Tiles ›*, the tile's row: a link for a submenu tile, an `OPEN_TILE` action row for any other) and presses OK there, so Back walks up the same pages, each with its cursor where it was. Tile -1 stops at the Tiles page; a tile or menu that is not there stops at the last page that opened. **A menu or tile its page has no row for** (past the rows the Menus page or the Tiles page has room for, which the page's note counts; the Tiles page's sends the user to hold OK on such a tile, Fable review I4) **has its page opened directly** (`open_page()`), the page under it keeping its cursor where it opened (the Tiles page's on *Add ›*), so Back still walks up the same pages. Task 14's hold-OK shortcut opens settings with it, and 13b's test hook does too.
- **`handle_event()` names the new event kind from this commit on** (Fable review C2): the launcher builds with `-Wall -Wextra` (`-Wswitch`) and `handle_event()` has a case for every kind and no `default:`, so 13a adds `case SETTINGS_EVENT_ICON: break;` (nothing on screen acts on it yet), which 13b replaces with the Icon page's case.
- **The library grid** (`icongrid.c`): every library icon, in groups, the groups in the order the manifest first names each and each group's icons in the manifest's order; an icon with no group in the group `""`, which the screen names *Other*. **Filtering** keeps the icons whose title, name or one of whose `match =` aliases holds what was typed, ASCII letters compared in either case (as the app list's filter compares), a group with none left out, and the cursor on its icon while that is still shown. **The arrows**: Left and Right step through the icons in the grid's order, across the headers; Up and Down go to the same column of the next row, of the next group's first row or of the group above's last row, or to a shorter row's last icon; Up from the first row asks for the keyboard (`ICONGRID_FILTER`), which is how the grid is filtered by typing; nothing moves past either end. OK with no icon shown does nothing and says *No icon matches what was typed*.
- **The AppsFolder ID** (`applist_appsfolder_id()`) reads back either form Task 8 writes (`explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\<ID>`, and the ID quoted when it holds a space or a comma), the two words in any case, since a config written by hand may spell them otherwise. Any other command is no AppsFolder app, and gets no Windows image.

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "check.h"
#include "icongrid.h"

// A library as the manifest lists one: groups first named in a mixed order, Kodi with an alias
static const char *const KODI_ALIASES[] = { "xbmc" };
static const LibraryInfo ICONS[] = {
    { "power", "Power", "system", NULL, 0 },
    { "kodi", "Kodi", "servers", KODI_ALIASES, 1 },
    { "restart", "Restart", "system", NULL, 0 },
    { "plex", "Plex", "servers", NULL, 0 },
    { "netflix", "Netflix", "streaming", NULL, 0 },
    { "sleep", "Sleep", "system", NULL, 0 },
    { "jellyfin", "Jellyfin", "servers", NULL, 0 },
    { "emby", "Emby", "servers", NULL, 0 },
    { "apps", "Apps", "general", NULL, 0 },
    { "settings", "Settings", "system", NULL, 0 },
    { "vlc", "VLC", "servers", NULL, 0 }
};
#define ICON_COUNT ((int) (sizeof(ICONS) / sizeof(ICONS[0])))

// A function to name the icon under the cursor; "(none)" when no icon is shown
static const char *at_cursor(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    const LibraryInfo *icon = icongrid_icon(grid, icongrid_cursor(grid));
    return icon != NULL ? icon->name : "(none)";
}

// A function to list the icons shown, group by group: "system: power restart | servers: kodi"
static const char *listed(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    static char out[512];
    out[0] = '\0';
    for (int g = 0; g < icongrid_groups(grid); g++) {
        size_t used = strlen(out);
        snprintf(out + used, sizeof(out) - used, "%s%s:", g == 0 ? "" : " | ", icongrid_group(grid, g));
        for (int s = icongrid_group_first(grid, g); s < icongrid_group_first(grid, g) + icongrid_group_size(grid, g); s++) {
            used = strlen(out);
            snprintf(out + used, sizeof(out) - used, " %s", icongrid_icon(grid, s)->name);
        }
    }
    return out;
}

// A function to test the groups: each named once, in the order the manifest first names it, its icons
// in the manifest's order; the cursor on the first icon; and the accessors' answers past the end
static void test_groups(void)
{
    IconGrid *grid = icongrid_create(ICONS, ICON_COUNT);
    CHECK(grid != NULL);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_count(grid), 11);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_groups(grid), 4);
    CHECK_STR(listed(grid), "system: power restart sleep settings | servers: kodi plex jellyfin emby vlc | "
                            "streaming: netflix | general: apps");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_first(grid, 1), 4);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_size(grid, 1), 5);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_of(grid, 8), 1);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_of(grid, 9), 2);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_cursor(grid), 0);
    CHECK_STR(icongrid_query(grid), "");
    CHECK(icongrid_group(grid, 4) == NULL);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_first(grid, -1), -1);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_size(grid, 4), 0);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_of(grid, 11), -1);
    CHECK(icongrid_icon(grid, 11) == NULL);
    CHECK(icongrid_icon(grid, -1) == NULL);
    CHECK(icongrid_chosen(grid) == NULL);
    icongrid_free(grid);
}

// A function to test the arrows three icons wide: Left and Right through the icons across the headers,
// Down and Up to the same column, a shorter row's last icon, the next group's first row and the last
// group's last row; Up from the first row asks for the keyboard; nothing moves past either end
static void test_moves(void)
{
    IconGrid *grid = icongrid_create(ICONS, ICON_COUNT);
    // system: [power restart sleep] [settings]; servers: [kodi plex jellyfin] [emby vlc];
    // streaming: [netflix]; general: [apps]
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_LEFT, 3), ICONGRID_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_RIGHT, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "restart");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "settings");                 // Its row is shorter: its last icon
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "kodi");                     // The next group's first row
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "emby");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_RIGHT, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "vlc");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "netflix");                  // Column 1 of a group of one: its only icon
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "apps");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_RIGHT, 3), ICONGRID_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "netflix");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "emby");                     // The group above's last row
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "kodi");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_LEFT, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "settings");                 // Left crosses the header
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 3), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "power");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 3), ICONGRID_FILTER);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "power");

    // Four wide, system is one row: Down from restart goes to the servers' column 1, Up from plex back
    CHECK(icongrid_select(grid, "restart"));
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 4), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "plex");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 4), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "restart");

    // A width under one is one: Down is the next icon
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 0), ICONGRID_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "sleep");
    icongrid_free(grid);
}

// A function to test filtering: by an alias, in any case; by a part of a title or name, the groups
// with none left out; the cursor kept on its icon while it is shown; and a query nothing matches, where
// OK says why and Up still asks for the keyboard
static void test_filter(void)
{
    IconGrid *grid = icongrid_create(ICONS, ICON_COUNT);
    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, "XBMC"));
    CHECK_STR(listed(grid), "servers: kodi");
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "kodi");
    CHECK_STR(icongrid_query(grid), "XBMC");
    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, icongrid_query(grid)));      // Its own query, given back
    CHECK_STR(icongrid_query(grid), "XBMC");
    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, ""));
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_count(grid), 11);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "kodi");                     // Still shown: the cursor stays on it

    CHECK(icongrid_select(grid, "plex"));
    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, "e"));
    CHECK_STR(listed(grid), "system: power restart sleep settings | servers: plex jellyfin emby | streaming: netflix");
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "plex");
    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, "Ix"));
    CHECK_STR(listed(grid), "streaming: netflix");
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "netflix");                  // Plex is not shown: the first icon

    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, "zzz"));
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_count(grid), 0);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_groups(grid), 0);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_cursor(grid), -1);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_OK, 3), ICONGRID_NONE);
    CHECK_STR(icongrid_why(grid), "No icon matches what was typed");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_DOWN, 3), ICONGRID_NONE);
    CHECK(icongrid_why(grid) == NULL);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_UP, 3), ICONGRID_FILTER);
    CHECK(icongrid_filter(grid, NULL));
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_count(grid), 11);
    CHECK_STR(at_cursor(grid), "power");
    icongrid_free(grid);
}

// A function to test choosing: OK on the icon the cursor was put on by name, a name not shown leaving
// the cursor where it was, and Back
static void test_choose(void)
{
    IconGrid *grid = icongrid_create(ICONS, ICON_COUNT);
    CHECK(icongrid_select(grid, "jellyfin"));
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_cursor(grid), 6);
    CHECK(!icongrid_select(grid, "nope"));
    CHECK(!icongrid_select(grid, NULL));
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_cursor(grid), 6);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_OK, 3), ICONGRID_CHOSEN);
    CHECK_STR(icongrid_chosen(grid)->name, "jellyfin");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_BACK, 3), ICONGRID_CANCELED);
    icongrid_free(grid);

    // An icon with no group is in the group "", which the screen names; an empty library shows nothing
    static const LibraryInfo loose[] = { { "a", "A", NULL, NULL, 0 }, { "b", "B", "", NULL, 0 } };
    grid = icongrid_create(loose, 2);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_groups(grid), 1);
    CHECK_STR(icongrid_group(grid, 0), "");
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_group_size(grid, 0), 2);
    icongrid_free(grid);
    grid = icongrid_create(NULL, 0);
    CHECK(grid != NULL);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_count(grid), 0);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_RIGHT, 3), ICONGRID_NONE);
    CHECK_INT(icongrid_command(grid, ICONGRID_BACK, 3), ICONGRID_CANCELED);
    icongrid_free(grid);
    icongrid_free(NULL);
}

int main(void)
{
    test_groups();
    test_moves();
    test_filter();
    test_choose();
    return check_report();
}
```

```c
    static const char *const text = "[General]\nDefaultMenu=Main\n\n[Main]\nEntry1=Kodi;kodi;kodi\n"
                                     "Entry2=Games;games;:submenu Games\nEntry3=Bye;quit;:quit\n\n"
                                     "[Games]\nEntry1=Retro;emulators;retro\nEntry2=Steam;steam;steam\n";
    SettingsState *state = settings_create(names, 2);
    IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, strlen(text));
    *menus = doc != NULL ? menuedit_load(doc, "Main") : NULL;
    inidoc_free(doc);
    CHECK(state != NULL && *menus != NULL);
    settings_set_menus(state, *menus);
    return state;
}

// A function to name the row under the cursor on the page on show
static const char *cursor_label(SettingsState *state)
{
    static SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    int count = settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    int cursor = settings_cursor(state);
    return cursor >= 0 && cursor < count ? rows[cursor].label : "(no row)";
}

// A function to test opening the pages at a tile (the hold-OK shortcut's way in, and the harness's):
// Menus, the menu, its Tiles page and the tile's page, each opened from the row that leads on, so Back
// walks up them with each cursor where it was; tile -1 stops at the Tiles page; a tile or a menu that is
// not there stops at the last page that opened
static void test_show_tile(void)
{
    MenuEdit *menus = NULL;
    SettingsState *state = tiles_model(&menus);
    settings_show_tile(state, 1, 1);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK_STR(cursor_label(state), "Steam");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_MENU);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_menu(state), 1);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS);
    CHECK_STR(cursor_label(state), "Games");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TOP);
    CHECK_STR(cursor_label(state), "Menus");

    settings_show_tile(state, 0, -1);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_menu(state), 0);
    settings_show_tile(state, 0, 7);              // Main has no tile 7: its Tiles page
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    settings_show_tile(state, 5, 0);              // No menu 5: the Menus page
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(menus);
}

// A function to open a model over `count` menus named in `names`, with the menus model of `text`; the
// caller frees the menus model after the model
static SettingsState *text_model(const char *const *names, int count, const char *text, MenuEdit **menus)
{
    SettingsState *state = settings_create(names, count);
    IniDoc *doc = inidoc_parse(text, strlen(text));
    *menus = doc != NULL ? menuedit_load(doc, names[0]) : NULL;
    inidoc_free(doc);
    CHECK(state != NULL && *menus != NULL);
    settings_set_menus(state, *menus);
    return state;
}

// A function to test opening the pages at a tile the pages have no row for (Fable review I4): the 66th tile
// of a 70-tile menu, past the Tiles page's rows (its note counts it), and the one tile of the 66th of 70
// menus, past the Menus page's; each page opens all the same, and Back walks up the pages as ever
static void test_show_tile_past_rows(void)
{
    static const char *const main_name[] = { "Main" };
    char text[4096] = "[Main]\n";
    for (int t = 0; t < 70; t++) {
        size_t used = strlen(text);
        snprintf(text + used, sizeof(text) - used, "Entry%d=T%d;apps;:home\n", t + 1, t);
    }
    MenuEdit *menus = NULL;
    SettingsState *state = text_model(main_name, 1, text, &menus);
    char path[256];
    settings_show_tile(state, 0, 65);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "Main" ARROW "Tiles" ARROW "T65");
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_tile(state), 65);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES);
    CHECK_STR(cursor_label(state), "Add");                   // No row leads to T65: the cursor where it opened
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(menus);

    static char labels[70][8];
    const char *names[70];
    text[0] = '\0';
    for (int m = 0; m < 70; m++) {
        snprintf(labels[m], sizeof(labels[m]), "M%d", m);
        names[m] = labels[m];
        size_t used = strlen(text);
        snprintf(text + used, sizeof(text) - used, "[M%d]\nEntry1=Only%d;apps;:home\n", m, m);
    }
    state = text_model(names, 70, text, &menus);
    settings_show_tile(state, 65, 0);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    CHECK_STR(path, "Settings" ARROW "Menus" ARROW "M65" ARROW "Tiles" ARROW "Only65");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_MENU);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_menu(state), 65);
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(menus);
}

// A function to test the Icon page (spec "Icons"): opened from a tile's page, about that tile; until the
// screen has looked, Library and Browse alone; then the choices in the spec's order with the cursor on
// the first that applies (the library match, else its own icon, else the generic icon); OK on each row
// hands the screen that row, the page staying; a choice made goes back to the tile's page, and one
// refused stays with why
static void test_icon_page(void)
{
    MenuEdit *menus = NULL;
    SettingsState *state = tiles_model(&menus);
    settings_show_tile(state, 1, 1);              // Games' Steam
    cursor_to(state, "Icon");
    CHECK_INT(settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK).kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON);
    int menu = -1;
    int tile = -1;
    CHECK(settings_icon_tile(state, &menu, &tile));
    CHECK_INT(menu, 1);
    CHECK_INT(tile, 1);
    CHECK_INT(settings_preview_menu(state), 1);
    char path[512];
    settings_path(state, path, sizeof(path));
    size_t length = strlen(path);
    CHECK(length > strlen(ARROW "Icon") && strcmp(path + length - strlen(ARROW "Icon"), ARROW "Icon") == 0);
    CHECK(!settings_icon_choices(state)->ready);
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 2);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Library");
    CHECK_STR(rows[1].label, "Browse for an image");
    CHECK_INT(settings_cursor(state), 0);

    // A match and its own icon: the match first, and the cursor put back on it
    SettingsIconChoices choices;
    memset(&choices, 0, sizeof(choices));
    snprintf(choices.suggested, sizeof(choices.suggested), "steam");
    snprintf(choices.suggested_title, sizeof(choices.suggested_title), "Steam");
    choices.matched = true;
    choices.own = true;
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_DOWN);
    settings_set_icon_choices(state, &choices);
    CHECK(settings_icon_choices(state)->ready);
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 4);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Steam");
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].value, "Library match");
    CHECK_STR(rows[1].label, "Its own icon");
    CHECK_STR(rows[2].label, "Library");
    CHECK_STR(rows[3].label, "Browse for an image");
    CHECK_INT(settings_cursor(state), 0);
    static const SettingsAction actions[] = { SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_SUGGESTED, SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_OWN,
                                             SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_GRID, SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_BROWSE };
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        SettingsEvent event = settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
        CHECK_INT(event.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_ICON);
        CHECK_INT(event.action, actions[i]);
        CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON);   // The screen acts; the page waits for it
        settings_command(state, SETTINGS_DOWN);
    }

    // The screen sets the icon it chose through the model (a library name or an image's path), as a tile's
    // command is set: one the tile's line cannot hold is refused with the reason, the tile as it was
    SettingsEvent set = settings_set_icon(state, 1, 1, "kodi");
    CHECK_INT(set.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS);
    CHECK_INT(set.menu, 1);
    CHECK_INT(set.tile, 1);
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(menus, "Games", 1)->icon, "kodi");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(menus, "Games", 1)->title, "Steam");
    set = settings_set_icon(state, 1, 1, "");
    CHECK_INT(set.kind, SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED);
    CHECK_STR(settings_notice(state), "Choose an icon");
    CHECK_STR(tile_of(menus, "Games", 1)->icon, "kodi");
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON);       // The page is the screen's to leave

    // Refused: the page stays, its reason in the caption until the next key; chosen: the tile's page
    settings_icon_done(state, "Couldn't save its icon");
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON);
    CHECK_STR(settings_notice(state), "Couldn't save its icon");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_UP);
    CHECK_STR(settings_notice(state), "");
    settings_icon_done(state, NULL);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    CHECK(!settings_icon_tile(state, &menu, &tile));
    settings_icon_done(state, NULL);              // Not on the Icon page: nothing happens
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);

    // Opened again, the screen looks again. Its own icon alone comes first; with neither, the generic icon
    cursor_to(state, "Icon");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
    CHECK(!settings_icon_choices(state)->ready);
    memset(&choices, 0, sizeof(choices));
    choices.own = true;
    settings_set_icon_choices(state, &choices);
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 3);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Its own icon");
    snprintf(choices.suggested, sizeof(choices.suggested), "apps");
    snprintf(choices.suggested_title, sizeof(choices.suggested_title), "Apps");
    choices.own = false;
    settings_set_icon_choices(state, &choices);
    CHECK_INT(settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS), 3);
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].label, "Apps");
    CHECK_STR(rows[0].value, "Generic icon");
    settings_command(state, SETTINGS_BACK);
    CHECK_INT(settings_page(state), SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE);
    settings_free(state);
    menuedit_free(menus);
}
```

```c
// A function to prove that the library grid fails cleanly: made, or NULL with nothing left allocated;
// a filter refused leaves the grid as it was (its icons, its query and its cursor), or is done
static void prove_icongrid(void)
{
    static const char *const aliases[] = { "xbmc" };
    static const LibraryInfo icons[] = {
        { "power", "Power", "system", NULL, 0 }, { "kodi", "Kodi", "servers", aliases, 1 },
        { "plex", "Plex", "servers", NULL, 0 }, { "apps", "Apps", "general", NULL, 0 }
    };
    for (int n = 1;; n++) {
        arm(n);
        IconGrid *grid = icongrid_create(icons, 4);
        bool selected = grid != NULL && icongrid_select(grid, "plex");
        bool filtered = grid != NULL && icongrid_filter(grid, "XBMC");
        disarm();
        if (grid == NULL)
            CHECK_RUN(failed, n);
        else if (!filtered) {
            CHECK_RUN(failed && selected, n);
            CHECK_RUN(icongrid_count(grid) == 4 && strcmp(icongrid_query(grid), "") == 0 && icongrid_cursor(grid) == 2, n);
        }
        else
            CHECK_RUN(icongrid_count(grid) == 1 && strcmp(icongrid_icon(grid, 0)->name, "kodi") == 0, n);
        icongrid_free(grid);
        runs = n;
        if (!no_leak(__LINE__, n) || !failed)
            break;
    }
    report("the library grid");
}
```

```c
// The library grid's model (spec "Icons", choice 3): every library icon, grouped by the manifest's
// group with a header for each, filtered by what is typed, and moved through with the four arrows. Pure:
// no SDL, no globals; memory comes from alloc.h. settings_pickers.c draws it.
#ifndef ICONGRID_H
#define ICONGRID_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include "library.h"

#define ICONGRID_QUERY_MAX 64   // The longest filter kept, with its terminator: the keyboard's limit is one less

typedef enum {
    ICONGRID_UP,
    ICONGRID_DOWN,
    ICONGRID_LEFT,
    ICONGRID_RIGHT,
    ICONGRID_OK,
    ICONGRID_BACK
} IconGridCommand;

typedef enum {
    ICONGRID_NONE,
    ICONGRID_MOVED,      // The cursor is on another icon: the preview shows it
    ICONGRID_CHOSEN,     // icongrid_chosen() gives the icon
    ICONGRID_CANCELED,
    ICONGRID_FILTER      // Up from the first row: the keyboard opens to filter the icons
} IconGridResult;

typedef struct IconGrid IconGrid;

IconGrid *icongrid_create(const LibraryInfo *icons, int count);   // Borrowed icons; NULL when out of memory
void icongrid_free(IconGrid *grid);
bool icongrid_filter(IconGrid *grid, const char *query);   // False when out of memory, with the grid as it was
const char *icongrid_query(const IconGrid *grid);
int icongrid_count(const IconGrid *grid);                  // The icons shown
int icongrid_groups(const IconGrid *grid);                 // The groups shown, each with an icon at least
const char *icongrid_group(const IconGrid *grid, int group);       // As the manifest names it; "" for none
int icongrid_group_first(const IconGrid *grid, int group);         // Its first icon among those shown
int icongrid_group_size(const IconGrid *grid, int group);
int icongrid_group_of(const IconGrid *grid, int shown);            // The group an icon shown is in; -1 past them
const LibraryInfo *icongrid_icon(const IconGrid *grid, int shown); // NULL past the icons shown
int icongrid_cursor(const IconGrid *grid);                 // -1 when no icon is shown
bool icongrid_select(IconGrid *grid, const char *name);    // The cursor to that icon, when it is shown
IconGridResult icongrid_command(IconGrid *grid, IconGridCommand command, int columns);
const LibraryInfo *icongrid_chosen(const IconGrid *grid);
const char *icongrid_why(const IconGrid *grid);            // Why the last OK did nothing, or NULL

#endif
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The grid, the ID and the Icon page**

Create `src/icongrid.c`:

```c
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "icongrid.h"
#include "alloc.h"

static const char *const NO_MATCH = "No icon matches what was typed";

struct IconGrid {
    const LibraryInfo *icons;   // Borrowed: the library's, in the manifest's order
    int count;
    int *group_of;              // Each icon's group, an index into `names`
    const char **names;         // The groups, in the order the manifest first names each ("" for none)
    int group_count;
    int *shown;                 // The icons shown, group by group, each group in the manifest's order
    int shown_count;
    int *firsts;                // Each group shown: its first icon in `shown`...
    int *sizes;                 // ...how many icons it shows...
    int *groups;                // ...and which of `names` it is
    int shown_groups;
    int cursor;                 // An index into `shown`; -1 when nothing is shown
    char query[ICONGRID_QUERY_MAX];
    const LibraryInfo *chosen;  // The icon OK chose
    const char *why;            // Why the last OK did nothing; NULL otherwise
};

// A function to fold an ASCII capital to lower case, as the app list's filter folds; any other byte
// stays as it is
static char fold(char c)
{
    return c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' ? (char) (c - 'A' + 'a') : c;
}

// A function to tell whether a text holds the query, ASCII letters compared in either case; an empty
// query is in every text
static bool holds(const char *text, const char *query)
{
    size_t length = strlen(query);
    if (length == 0)
        return true;
    for (const char *at = text != NULL ? text : ""; *at != '\0'; at++) {
        size_t k = 0;
        while (k < length && at[k] != '\0' && fold(at[k]) == fold(query[k]))
            k++;
        if (k == length)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to tell whether an icon is shown for a query: its title, its name or one of its aliases
// holds it
static bool shown_for(const LibraryInfo *icon, const char *query)
{
    if (holds(icon->title, query) || holds(icon->name, query))
        return true;
    for (int a = 0; a < icon->match_count; a++) {
        if (holds(icon->match[a], query))
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to find a group among those named so far; -1 for a new one
static int group_named(const IconGrid *grid, const char *name)
{
    for (int g = 0; g < grid->group_count; g++) {
        if (strcmp(grid->names[g], name) == 0)
            return g;
    }
    return -1;
}

// A function to make the grid over the library's icons (borrowed: they must outlive it), every icon
// shown, the cursor on the first; NULL when out of memory
IconGrid *icongrid_create(const LibraryInfo *icons, int count)
{
    IconGrid *grid = alloc_calloc(1, sizeof(IconGrid));
    if (grid == NULL)
        return NULL;
    grid->icons = icons;
    grid->count = icons != NULL && count > 0 ? count : 0;
    grid->cursor = -1;
    size_t room = (size_t) (grid->count > 0 ? grid->count : 1);
    grid->group_of = alloc_calloc(room, sizeof(int));
    grid->names = alloc_calloc(room, sizeof(char*));
    if (grid->group_of == NULL || grid->names == NULL) {
        icongrid_free(grid);
        return NULL;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < grid->count; i++) {
        const char *name = icons[i].group != NULL ? icons[i].group : "";
        int g = group_named(grid, name);
        if (g < 0) {
            g = grid->group_count++;
            grid->names[g] = name;
        }
        grid->group_of[i] = g;
    }
    if (!icongrid_filter(grid, "")) {
        icongrid_free(grid);
        return NULL;
    }
    return grid;
}

// A function to free the grid
void icongrid_free(IconGrid *grid)
{
    if (grid == NULL)
        return;
    alloc_free(grid->group_of);
    alloc_free(grid->names);
    alloc_free(grid->shown);
    alloc_free(grid->firsts);
    alloc_free(grid->sizes);
    alloc_free(grid->groups);
    alloc_free(grid);
}

// A function to show only the icons whose title, name or an alias holds the query (ASCII letters in
// either case; "" or NULL shows them all), group by group, a group with none left out. The cursor
// stays on its icon while that is still shown, else goes to the first. False when out of memory, with
// the grid as it was.
bool icongrid_filter(IconGrid *grid, const char *query)
{
    char wanted[ICONGRID_QUERY_MAX];   // A copy: the query may be the grid's own (icongrid_query())
    snprintf(wanted, sizeof(wanted), "%s", query != NULL ? query : "");
    size_t icons = (size_t) (grid->count > 0 ? grid->count : 1);
    size_t groups = (size_t) (grid->group_count > 0 ? grid->group_count : 1);
    int *shown = alloc_calloc(icons, sizeof(int));
    int *firsts = alloc_calloc(groups, sizeof(int));
    int *sizes = alloc_calloc(groups, sizeof(int));
    int *which = alloc_calloc(groups, sizeof(int));
    if (shown == NULL || firsts == NULL || sizes == NULL || which == NULL) {
        alloc_free(shown);
        alloc_free(firsts);
        alloc_free(sizes);
        alloc_free(which);
        return false;
    }
    int count = 0;
    int made = 0;
    for (int g = 0; g < grid->group_count; g++) {
        int first = count;
        for (int i = 0; i < grid->count; i++) {
            if (grid->group_of[i] == g && shown_for(&grid->icons[i], wanted))
                shown[count++] = i;
        }
        if (count > first) {
            firsts[made] = first;
            sizes[made] = count - first;
            which[made] = g;
            made++;
        }
    }
    int was = grid->cursor >= 0 ? grid->shown[grid->cursor] : -1;
    int cursor = count > 0 ? 0 : -1;
    for (int s = 0; s < count; s++) {
        if (shown[s] == was)
            cursor = s;
    }
    alloc_free(grid->shown);
    alloc_free(grid->firsts);
    alloc_free(grid->sizes);
    alloc_free(grid->groups);
    grid->shown = shown;
    grid->firsts = firsts;
    grid->sizes = sizes;
    grid->groups = which;
    grid->shown_count = count;
    grid->shown_groups = made;
    grid->cursor = cursor;
    snprintf(grid->query, sizeof(grid->query), "%s", wanted);
    grid->why = NULL;
    return true;
}

// A function to get the query the icons are filtered by; "" for none
const char *icongrid_query(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    return grid->query;
}

// A function to count the icons shown
int icongrid_count(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    return grid->shown_count;
}

// A function to count the groups shown: each holds at least one icon
int icongrid_groups(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    return grid->shown_groups;
}

// A function to name a group shown, as the manifest names it ("" for icons with no group); NULL past
// the groups shown
const char *icongrid_group(const IconGrid *grid, int group)
{
    return group >= 0 && group < grid->shown_groups ? grid->names[grid->groups[group]] : NULL;
}

// A function to give a group's first icon among those shown; -1 past the groups shown
int icongrid_group_first(const IconGrid *grid, int group)
{
    return group >= 0 && group < grid->shown_groups ? grid->firsts[group] : -1;
}

// A function to count a group's icons shown; 0 past the groups shown
int icongrid_group_size(const IconGrid *grid, int group)
{
    return group >= 0 && group < grid->shown_groups ? grid->sizes[group] : 0;
}

// A function to give the group shown an icon shown is in; -1 past the icons shown
int icongrid_group_of(const IconGrid *grid, int shown)
{
    for (int g = 0; shown >= 0 && shown < grid->shown_count && g < grid->shown_groups; g++) {
        if (shown < grid->firsts[g] + grid->sizes[g])
            return g;
    }
    return -1;
}

// A function to give an icon shown, in the grid's order; NULL past the icons shown
const LibraryInfo *icongrid_icon(const IconGrid *grid, int shown)
{
    return shown >= 0 && shown < grid->shown_count ? &grid->icons[grid->shown[shown]] : NULL;
}

// A function to give the icon under the cursor, as an index among those shown; -1 when none is shown
int icongrid_cursor(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    return grid->cursor;
}

// A function to put the cursor on the icon of a name, when it is shown; false (the cursor where it
// was) when it is not
bool icongrid_select(IconGrid *grid, const char *name)
{
    for (int s = 0; name != NULL && s < grid->shown_count; s++) {
        if (strcmp(grid->icons[grid->shown[s]].name, name) == 0) {
            grid->cursor = s;
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to act on one key, the grid `columns` icons wide (at least one). Left and Right step
// through the icons in the grid's order, across the groups' headers; Up and Down go to the same column
// of the row above or below, or of the next group's first row or the group above's last row, or to a
// shorter row's last icon. Up from the first row asks for the keyboard (ICONGRID_FILTER), as it does with
// no icon shown. OK chooses the icon under the cursor, and does nothing, saying why, when none is shown;
// Back cancels.
IconGridResult icongrid_command(IconGrid *grid, IconGridCommand command, int columns)
{
    grid->why = NULL;
    if (columns < 1)
        columns = 1;
    if (command == ICONGRID_BACK)
        return ICONGRID_CANCELED;
    if (grid->cursor < 0) {
        if (command == ICONGRID_UP)
            return ICONGRID_FILTER;
        if (command == ICONGRID_OK)
            grid->why = NO_MATCH;
        return ICONGRID_NONE;
    }
    if (command == ICONGRID_OK) {
        grid->chosen = &grid->icons[grid->shown[grid->cursor]];
        return ICONGRID_CHOSEN;
    }
    int g = icongrid_group_of(grid, grid->cursor);
    int place = grid->cursor - grid->firsts[g];
    int row = place / columns;
    int column = place % columns;
    int to = grid->cursor;
    switch (command) {
        case ICONGRID_LEFT:
            to = grid->cursor - 1;
            break;
        case ICONGRID_RIGHT:
            to = grid->cursor + 1;
            break;
        case ICONGRID_DOWN:
            if ((row + 1) * columns < grid->sizes[g]) {
                int next = (row + 1) * columns + column;
                to = grid->firsts[g] + (next < grid->sizes[g] ? next : grid->sizes[g] - 1);
            }
            else if (g + 1 < grid->shown_groups)
                to = grid->firsts[g + 1] + (column < grid->sizes[g + 1] ? column : grid->sizes[g + 1] - 1);
            break;
        case ICONGRID_UP:
            if (row > 0)
                to = grid->firsts[g] + (row - 1) * columns + column;
            else if (g > 0) {
                int last = (grid->sizes[g - 1] - 1) / columns * columns + column;
                to = grid->firsts[g - 1] + (last < grid->sizes[g - 1] ? last : grid->sizes[g - 1] - 1);
            }
            else
                return ICONGRID_FILTER;
            break;
        case ICONGRID_OK:
        case ICONGRID_BACK:
            break;
    }
    if (to < 0 || to >= grid->shown_count || to == grid->cursor)
        return ICONGRID_NONE;
    grid->cursor = to;
    return ICONGRID_MOVED;
}

// A function to give the icon OK chose; NULL before one was
const LibraryInfo *icongrid_chosen(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    return grid->chosen;
}

// A function to say why the last OK did nothing; NULL when it did something, or no OK came
const char *icongrid_why(const IconGrid *grid)
{
    return grid->why;
}
```

In `src/applist.c`, after Task 8's `applist_appsfolder_command()`, add:

```c
// A function to tell whether a text starts with a prefix written in lower case, ASCII letters compared
// in either case
static bool starts_folded(const char *text, const char *prefix)
{
    for (; *prefix != '\0'; text++, prefix++) {
        if (fileio_lower(*text) != *prefix)
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// A function to read an AppsFolder app's ID back out of its tile's command, in either form
// applist_appsfolder_command() writes (the words in any case, as a config written by hand may have
// them): the Icon page finds the app's own image by it. False for any other command, for an empty ID or
// one holding a quote, and for an ID that does not fit.
bool applist_appsfolder_id(const char *command, char *out, size_t size)
{
    static const char program[] = "explorer.exe ";
    static const char folder[] = "shell:appsfolder\\";
    if (command == NULL || !starts_folded(command, program))
        return false;
    const char *at = command + strlen(program);
    bool quoted = *at == '"';
    if (quoted)
        at++;
    if (!starts_folded(at, folder))
        return false;
    at += strlen(folder);
    size_t length = strlen(at);
    if (quoted) {
        if (length == 0 || at[length - 1] != '"')
            return false;
        length--;
    }
    if (length == 0 || length >= size || memchr(at, '"', length) != NULL)
        return false;
    memcpy(out, at, length);
    out[length] = '\0';
    return true;
}
```

(`applist.c` already includes `fileio.h` for `fileio_lower()`, Task 7's Consumes; the walk stops at the text's end, where `fileio_lower('\0')` is 0 and no prefix byte is.)

```c
// A function to set a tile's icon, as the Icon page chose it (a library name, or an image's or a plated
// file's path): the twin of settings_set_command(). Refused with the reason as the notice, which the Icon
// page's caption shows.
SettingsEvent settings_set_icon(SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile, const char *icon)
{
    SettingsEvent event;
    memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MOVED;
    state->notice[0] = '\0';
    const MenuTile *t = edit_tile(state, menu, tile);
    if (t == NULL)
        return event;
    const char *refused = menuedit_set(state->menus, edit_index(state, menu), tile, t->title, icon, t->command);
    if (refused != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", refused);   // The Icon page's caption says it
        return event;
    }
    event.kind = SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS;
    event.menu = menu;
    event.tile = tile;
    return event;
}
```

(`menuedit_set()` copies what it is given before it frees the tile's old strings, so passing the tile's own title and command is safe.)

```c
// A function to give the Icon page what the screen found for its tile, and put the cursor on the first
// row: the first choice that applies, which the spec preselects
void settings_set_icon_choices(SettingsState *state, const SettingsIconChoices *choices)
{
    state->icon = *choices;
    state->icon.ready = true;
    if (state->stack[state->depth].page == SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON) {
        state->stack[state->depth].cursor = 0;
        fix_cursor(state);
    }
}

// A function to give what the Icon page offers; `ready` false until the screen has looked
const SettingsIconChoices *settings_icon_choices(const SettingsState *state)
{
    return &state->icon;
}

// A function to tell whether the Icon page is on show, and which tile it is about: its menu's index and
// the tile's place in it
bool settings_icon_tile(const SettingsState *state, int *menu, int *tile)
{
    const PageRef *top = &state->stack[state->depth];
    if (top->page != SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON)
        return false;
    *menu = top->menu;
    *tile = top->tile;
    return true;
}

// A function to end the Icon page's choice: chosen (`why` NULL), back to the tile's page; refused, the
// page stays and the caption says why until the next key. Nothing happens off the Icon page.
void settings_icon_done(SettingsState *state, const char *why)
{
    if (state->stack[state->depth].page != SETTINGS_PAGE_ICON)
        return;
    if (why != NULL) {
        snprintf(state->notice, sizeof(state->notice), "%s", why);
        return;
    }
    state->depth--;
    fix_cursor(state);
}

// A function to put the cursor on the page's row that leads to `page` for `menu` (and, for a tile's page,
// that `tile`; -1 for any) and press OK on it, as the remote would: a link row to it, or on the Tiles page
// an ordinary tile's row, an OPEN_TILE action (Task 10a's tile_row() makes only a submenu tile's a link).
// False when the page has no such row or the page did not open.
static bool open_row(SettingsState *state, SettingsPage page, int menu, int tile)
{
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    int count = settings_rows(state, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        bool leads = rows[i].kind == SETTINGS_ROW_LINK ? rows[i].target == page
                   : page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE && rows[i].kind == SETTINGS_ROW_ACTION &&
                     rows[i].action == SETTINGS_ACTION_OPEN_TILE;
        if (leads && rows[i].menu == menu && (tile < 0 || rows[i].tile == tile)) {
            state->stack[state->depth].cursor = i;
            settings_command(state, SETTINGS_OK);
            return settings_page(state) == page;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to open the pages at a tile, as the remote opens them from the top: Menus, the menu, its
// Tiles page and the tile's page, each from the row that leads on, so Back walks up the same pages with
// each cursor where it was. Tile -1 stops at the Tiles page (an empty menu's way in), and a menu or tile
// that is not there stops at the last page that opened. A menu or tile its page has no row for (past the
// rows the page has room for: its note counts it) has its page opened directly, the page under it keeping
// its cursor where it opened (Fable review I4): the hold reaches what the remote cannot.
void settings_show_tile(SettingsState *state, int menu, int tile)
{
    state->depth = 0;
    fix_cursor(state);
    if (!open_row(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_MENUS, -1, -1))
        return;
    if (!open_row(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_MENU, menu, -1)) {
        if (menu < 0 || menu >= state->menu_count)
            return;
        open_page(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_MENU, menu, -1);
    }
    if (!open_row(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES, menu, -1) || tile < 0)
        return;
    if (!open_row(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE, menu, tile) && edit_tile(state, menu, tile) != NULL)
        open_page(state, SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE, menu, tile);
}
```

**Decisions this task makes:**
- **What is looked at as the page opens.** The library match is `iconmatch_find()` on the tile's title, which starts as the app's name and is what the user calls it. The app's own icon is read and plated in memory there and then, since the preview shows it the moment its row is highlighted, through Task 10b's `plated_icon()` (which a new tile's icon is chosen with as it is added): on Windows for a tile whose command `applist_appsfolder_id()` reads (an AppsFolder app), `appicon_image(id, 256)`; on Linux for a tile whose command is a `.desktop` file (any `;<action>` after it dropped, as `unix.c` launches it), its `Icon=` (10b's `desktop_icon_name()`, read whatever the file's `NoDisplay` or `Hidden` say, since a tile may run a file the app list leaves out: Fable review M18) through `iconfind_path()` over the data folders `applist_data_dirs()` names (`$XDG_DATA_HOME`, else `~/.local/share`; each of `$XDG_DATA_DIRS`, else `/usr/local/share` and `/usr/share`; then the Flatpak exports' and Snap's, in that order), read by `load_icon_surface()` (an SVG rasterized at 512 px, so it plates sharp) and centered by `plate_icon(..., PLATE_SIZE)`. A tile that is neither has no icon of its own. **An icon that cannot be read or plated is not offered**, and the log says why: the first row is then the library match, else `apps` (spec, Errors and limits).
- **The file is written only when the row is chosen**: in `icons_dir()`, at `icons_new_path(dir, title)`, by `plate_save()`, once `menuedit_check_set()` (through `icon_problem()`) has said the tile's line, as config.ini has it, can hold that path (Fable review M15: a refusal leaves no file behind, which only Discard would delete); the tile's icon becomes that path (`settings_set_icon()`), and the path joins Task 10a's Discard list (`settings_note_plated()`). A path the line cannot hold, or a file that cannot be written (a read-only folder), keeps the tile's icon as it was; the caption says why (*Couldn't save its icon to <path>: <reason>*).
- **A tile that already shows its plated own icon keeps that file** (the controller's ruling, 2026-10-16): since Task 10b plates an app's own icon as it is added (Fable review I5), Calculator's tile already reads `icons\calculator.png`, and choosing *Its own icon* again would otherwise write `calculator-2.png` beside it. When the tile's icon is that icon's file, a file directly in `icons_dir()` (`icon_in_folder()`: only an own icon is ever written there) that holds the same plated picture the page read (`holds_own_icon()`: its size and every pixel, a clear one by its alpha alone, as Task 9's `png_roundtrip` proves a PNG reads back), choosing *Its own icon* writes nothing, changes nothing and goes back to the tile's page, logging `Menus: '<title>' in '<menu>' keeps its own icon <path>, written already`. A file there that holds another picture is not this icon (Opus re-review P3): the tile's *Command ›* changed since it was written (10b keeps the icon), the app's own icon changed, or the tile was given another tile's file through *Browse for an image ›*. Then choosing *Its own icon* writes a new file (`<name>-2.png` when `<name>.png` is there), as it would with no file, so the tile gets the icon the page showed.
- **The preview** (spec: "The preview shows each highlighted icon on the tile"): as the Icon page opens, the menu's highlight moves to the tile (it is the menu on show, `settings_preview_menu()`), so the tile is in view. The live entry's icon texture is replaced by the highlighted icon's (a library icon rendered at the button's size, the plated surface, or the browsed image as the preview thread decodes it), its selected icon dropped so it draws under the highlight too. Leaving the page renders the menu's buttons again from its entries; choosing remakes the launcher's menus (`settings_set_icon()`'s event, through `handle_event()` and Task 10a's `menus_follow()`), the new icon with them. Library and Browse rows show the tile's own icon until the grid's or the folder's cursor rests on one.
- **The library grid** is a picker (`PICKER_ICONS`) four icons across the column, each icon with its title under it, under a header per group (the group's name with a capital, *Other* for none). Its textures are made once a settings visit at the cell's size, all the library's icons decoded on the icon threads at once (`iconload_batch()`, as a menu's are), and let go with the renderer or as settings close. **Filtering**, as Task 10b's app list filters: Up from the grid's first row, or a printing key on a real keyboard (`pickers_set_typing()`, which then types that key), opens Task 12's keyboard (*Filter the icons*, 63 bytes at most) over the grid, which stays open under it (fix pass R5); each change filters the open grid at once (`pickers_keyboard_follow(..., 0)`, `icongrid_filter()` in place), the cursor kept on its icon while it is shown; *Done* keeps the filter; Back after a change puts back the filter the grid had (the follower hears the text the keyboard opened with), and Back with none leaves the grid as it is; either way Back lands on the grid.
- **Browse for an image ›** is 3a's folder browser in image mode, opened through Task 10b's `start_browser()` with no slot (fix pass R2), at the tile's icon when that is an image's path (its folder, the image highlighted), else at the first place; each row is checked with `menuedit_check_set()` (`icon_problem()`: the tile's own line, its comment and spacing counted, Fable review M2), so a path the line could not hold says why on its row. OK waits for the image's decode, as the Image setting's browser does, and an image that cannot be opened keeps the browser open with its note (`CANNOT_OPEN`, as the Image setting's); one that opens goes to the tile through Task 10b's `browser_chose`.

```c
// A function to let go of the library grid's textures, before the renderer that made them goes or as
// settings close; how many it destroyed, for a lost device's count. The grid makes them again when it
// next draws.
int pickers_drop_icon_textures(void)
{
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < icon_texture_count; i++) {
        if (icon_textures[i] != NULL) {
            SDL_DestroyTexture(icon_textures[i]);
            count++;
        }
    }
    free(icon_textures);
    icon_textures = NULL;
    icon_texture_count = 0;
    icon_size = 0;
    return count;
}

// A function to make every library icon's texture at `size` px for the grid, decoded on the icon threads
// as a menu's icons are (iconload_batch()): once a settings visit, and again only at another size. An
// icon that cannot be read shows its title alone, and is logged.
static void load_icon_textures(int size)
{
    if (icon_textures != NULL && size == icon_size)
        return;
    pickers_drop_icon_textures();
    int count = library_count();
    Uint64 start = SDL_GetPerformanceCounter();
    icon_textures = calloc((size_t) (count > 0 ? count : 1), sizeof(SDL_Texture*));
    IconJob *jobs = calloc((size_t) (count > 0 ? count : 1), sizeof(IconJob));
    int *from = calloc((size_t) (count > 0 ? count : 1), sizeof(int));
    if (icon_textures == NULL || jobs == NULL || from == NULL) {
        free(icon_textures);
        free(jobs);
        free(from);
        icon_textures = NULL;
        log_error("Settings: the library grid's icons cannot be made: out of memory, so it shows their titles");
        return;
    }
    icon_texture_count = count;
    icon_size = size;
    int work = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const char *path = library_lookup(library_info(i)->name);
        if (path == NULL || fileio_not_a_file(path))
            continue;
        size_t length = strlen(path);
        jobs[work].path = path;
        jobs[work].size = size;
        jobs[work].svg = length > 4 && SDL_strcasecmp(path + length - 4, ".svg") == 0;
        from[work++] = i;
    }
    iconload_batch(jobs, work, iconload_workers(), decode_icon_job, icon_worker_start, icon_worker_end);
    int made = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < work; j++) {
        if (jobs[j].surface == NULL) {
            log_error("Settings: the library grid cannot show %s: %s", library_info(from[j])->name, jobs[j].error);
            continue;
        }
        icon_textures[from[j]] = load_texture(jobs[j].surface);   // Frees the surface
        made += icon_textures[from[j]] != NULL ? 1 : 0;
    }
    free(jobs);
    free(from);
    log_debug("Settings: the library grid made %i of %i icons at %i px in %u ms", made, count, size,
        timing_ms(SDL_GetPerformanceCounter() - start));
}

// A function to tell the screen which icon is under the grid's cursor, for the preview, and log it
static void tell_shown(void)
{
    const LibraryInfo *icon = icongrid_icon(icon_grid, icongrid_cursor(icon_grid));
    if (icon == NULL)
        return;
    log_debug("Settings: the library grid's cursor is on %s", icon->name);
    if (icon_shown != NULL)
        icon_shown(icon->name);
}

// A function to open the library grid over the library's icons, filtered by `query`, the cursor on the
// icon `at` when it is shown (else the first). Out of memory it does not open, and says so.
static bool open_grid(const char *at, const char *query)
{
    close_picker();
    icon_grid = icongrid_create(library_info(0), library_count());
    if (icon_grid == NULL || !icongrid_filter(icon_grid, query)) {
        icongrid_free(icon_grid);
        icon_grid = NULL;
        log_error("Settings: the library grid cannot open: out of memory");
        return false;
    }
    if (at != NULL)
        icongrid_select(icon_grid, at);
    icon_first_line = 0;
    kind = PICKER_ICONS;
    return true;
}

// A function to filter the open library grid in place as the keyboard's text changes (Task 12's follower,
// at once), the cursor kept on its icon while that is still shown; a cancel after a change gives it the
// text the keyboard opened with, which puts the old filter back. It never opens the grid again: the grid
// stays open under the keyboard, so Back lands on it. Out of memory the grid closes, and says so.
static void icons_filter_changed(const char *text, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    if (kind != PICKER_ICONS || icon_grid == NULL)
        return;
    if (!icongrid_filter(icon_grid, text)) {
        log_error("Settings: the library grid cannot be filtered: out of memory");
        close_picker();
        return;
    }
    log_debug("Settings: the library grid shows %i icons for '%s'", icongrid_count(icon_grid), icongrid_query(icon_grid));
    tell_shown();
}

// A function to open the keyboard on the library grid's filter, over the grid (Task 12's way into it for a
// filtered list, as Task 10b's app list does): `first` is the character a real keyboard's key typed to
// open it, or NULL (Up from the grid's first row). Done keeps the filter, already applied as it was typed.
static void open_icon_filter(const char *first)
{
    log_debug("Settings: the keyboard filters the library grid");
    pickers_open_keyboard("Filter the icons", icongrid_query(icon_grid), ICONGRID_QUERY_MAX - 1, NULL, NULL,
                          icons_filter_changed);
    pickers_keyboard_follow(icons_filter_changed, 0);
    if (first != NULL)
        pickers_keyboard_type(first);
}

// A function to open the library grid for a tile's icon (spec "Icons", choice 3): every library icon with
// its title, grouped, the cursor on `current` when it names one. Typing on a real keyboard opens its filter.
void pickers_open_icons(const char *current, void (*shown)(const char *name), void (*done)(const char *name))
{
    icon_shown = shown;
    icon_done = done;
    if (!open_grid(current, ""))
        return;
    pickers_set_typing(open_icon_filter);   // After open_grid(): its close_picker() clears the opener
    log_debug("Settings: opened the library grid: %i icons in %i groups", icongrid_count(icon_grid), icongrid_groups(icon_grid));
    tell_shown();
}

// A function to act on a key in the library grid: the arrows move (Up from the first row opens the
// keyboard to filter it), OK chooses and Back leaves, each telling the screen
static void icons_command(const char *command)
{
    IconGridCommand key;
    if (MATCH(command, SCMD_UP))
        key = ICONGRID_UP;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_DOWN))
        key = ICONGRID_DOWN;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_LEFT))
        key = ICONGRID_LEFT;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_RIGHT))
        key = ICONGRID_RIGHT;
    else if (MATCH(command, SCMD_SELECT))
        key = ICONGRID_OK;
    else
        key = ICONGRID_BACK;
    IconGridResult result = icongrid_command(icon_grid, key, ICONS_COLUMNS);
    void (*done)(const char *name) = icon_done;
    if (result == ICONGRID_MOVED)
        tell_shown();
    else if (result == ICONGRID_FILTER)
        open_icon_filter(NULL);
    else if (result == ICONGRID_CANCELED) {
        close_picker();
        if (done != NULL)
            done(NULL);
    }
    else if (result == ICONGRID_CHOSEN) {
        char name[LIBRARY_NAME_MAX + 1];   // Copied: the grid goes before `done` runs
        snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%s", icongrid_chosen(icon_grid)->name);
        close_picker();
        log_debug("Settings: chose the library icon %s", name);
        if (done != NULL)
            done(name);
    }
}

// A function to name a group for its header: its name with a capital first letter; "Other" for none
static void group_label(const char *group, char *out, size_t size)
{
    if (group == NULL || group[0] == '\0') {
        snprintf(out, size, "Other");
        return;
    }
    snprintf(out, size, "%s", group);
    if (out[0] >= 'a' && out[0] <= 'z')
        out[0] = (char) (out[0] - 'a' + 'A');
}

// A function to tell whether the grid's line `line` is a group's header (else a row of its icons)
static bool header_line(int line)
{
    for (int g = 0, at = 0; g < icongrid_groups(icon_grid); g++) {
        if (line == at)
            return true;
        at += 1 + (icongrid_group_size(icon_grid, g) + ICONS_COLUMNS - 1) / ICONS_COLUMNS;
        if (line < at)
            return false;
    }
    return false;
}

// A function to draw one icon of the grid in its cell: the icon, its title under it, and an outline round
// the cell under the cursor
static void draw_icon_cell(int shown, int x, int y, int cell, int title_height)
{
    const LibraryInfo *icon = icongrid_icon(icon_grid, shown);
    bool cursor = shown == icongrid_cursor(icon_grid);
    int pad = host.margin / 2;
    int index = (int) (icon - library_info(0));
    SDL_Rect box = { x + pad / 2, y + pad / 2, cell - pad, cell - pad };
    if (index >= 0 && index < icon_texture_count && icon_textures[index] != NULL)
        draw_texture(renderer, icon_textures[index], NULL, &box);
    host.text(host.font_small, icon->title, x + 2, y + cell - pad / 2, cell - 4, (Uint8) (cursor ? 255 : ALPHA_GRID_TEXT), false);
    if (!cursor)
        return;
    SDL_Rect outline = { x, y, cell, cell + title_height };
    SDL_SetRenderDrawColor(renderer, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, ALPHA_MARK);
    outline_rect(renderer, &outline);
    SDL_Rect inner = { outline.x + 1, outline.y + 1, outline.w - 2, outline.h - 2 };
    outline_rect(renderer, &inner);
}

// A function to draw the library grid: each group's header, then its icons four across, each with its
// title, the one under the cursor outlined; scrolled so the cursor's row (with its group's header, for a
// group's first row) is on show. With no icon shown it says so.
static void draw_icons(int x, int top, int bottom)
{
    int pad = host.margin / 2;
    int cell = (host.column_width - 2 * pad) / ICONS_COLUMNS;
    int title_height = TTF_GetFontHeight(host.font_small);
    int row_height = cell + title_height;
    load_icon_textures(cell - pad);
    int cursor = icongrid_cursor(icon_grid);
    if (cursor < 0) {
        host.text(host.font_row, "No icon matches. Up types another filter.", x + pad, top, host.column_width - 2 * pad, 255, false);
        return;
    }

    // The cursor's line: each group a header, then its rows
    int groups = icongrid_groups(icon_grid);
    int cursor_group = icongrid_group_of(icon_grid, cursor);
    int cursor_place = cursor - icongrid_group_first(icon_grid, cursor_group);
    int cursor_line = 0;
    for (int g = 0; g < cursor_group; g++)
        cursor_line += 1 + (icongrid_group_size(icon_grid, g) + ICONS_COLUMNS - 1) / ICONS_COLUMNS;
    cursor_line += 1 + cursor_place / ICONS_COLUMNS;
    int from = cursor_place < ICONS_COLUMNS ? cursor_line - 1 : cursor_line;   // A first row shows its header
    if (from < icon_first_line)
        icon_first_line = from;
    for (;;) {
        int y = top;
        for (int line = icon_first_line; line <= cursor_line; line++)
            y += header_line(line) ? host.row_height : row_height;
        if (y <= bottom || icon_first_line >= cursor_line)
            break;
        icon_first_line++;
    }

    int y = top;
    int line = 0;
    for (int g = 0; g < groups && y < bottom; g++) {
        int first = icongrid_group_first(icon_grid, g);
        int size = icongrid_group_size(icon_grid, g);
        int rows = (size + ICONS_COLUMNS - 1) / ICONS_COLUMNS;
        if (line >= icon_first_line) {
            if (y + host.row_height > bottom)
                break;
            char label[64];
            group_label(icongrid_group(icon_grid, g), label, sizeof(label));
            host.text(host.font_row, label, x + pad, y + (host.row_height - TTF_GetFontHeight(host.font_row)) / 2,
                      host.column_width - 2 * pad, ALPHA_GRID_TEXT, false);
            y += host.row_height;
        }
        line++;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++, line++) {
            if (line < icon_first_line)
                continue;
            if (y + row_height > bottom) {
                y = bottom;
                break;
            }
            for (int c = 0; c < ICONS_COLUMNS && r * ICONS_COLUMNS + c < size; c++)
                draw_icon_cell(first + r * ICONS_COLUMNS + c, x + pad + c * cell, y, cell, title_height);
            y += row_height;
        }
    }
}
```
