```c
// A function to give the Icon page's tile, in the menus model, found by its menu's name (Task 10b's
// screen_tile(): a name is what the settings and the menus model are both sure of); NULL while no Icon page
// is open
static const MenuTile *icon_page_tile(void)
{
    return icon_menu >= 0 ? screen_tile(icon_menu, icon_tile) : NULL;
}

// A function to give the launcher's menu the Icon page's tile is in, which the preview shows; NULL when
// there is none
static Menu *icon_page_menu(void)
{
    if (icon_page_tile() == NULL)
        return NULL;
    return menu_for(menuedit_menu(menu_edit, menuedit_find(menu_edit, menus[icon_menu]->name)));
}

// A function to show an icon on the Icon page's tile in the preview without choosing it (spec "Icons":
// the preview shows each highlighted icon on the tile): the launcher's entry gets a texture of it, its
// selected icon dropped so this one draws under the highlight too, until the menu's buttons are rendered
// again. `what` names it for the log; the surface stays the caller's.
static void show_on_tile(SDL_Surface *surface, const char *what)
{
    Menu *menu = icon_page_menu();
    if (menu == NULL || surface == NULL || icon_tile >= (int) menu->num_entries)
        return;
    SDL_Texture *texture = surface_texture(surface);
    if (texture == NULL) {
        log_error("Settings: the preview cannot show %s: %s", what, SDL_GetError());
        return;
    }
    Entry *entry = menu->items[icon_tile];
    if (entry->icon != NULL)
        SDL_DestroyTexture(entry->icon);
    if (entry->icon_selected != NULL)
        SDL_DestroyTexture(entry->icon_selected);
    entry->icon = texture;
    entry->icon_selected = NULL;
    log_debug("Menus: the preview shows %s on '%s'", what, entry->title);
}

// A function to show the tile's own icon in the preview again: the menu's buttons are rendered again from
// the launcher's entries, at once when it is on show, else when it next is
static void restore_tile_icon(void)
{
    if (icon_previewed[0] == '\0')
        return;
    icon_previewed[0] = '\0';
    Menu *menu = icon_page_menu();
    if (menu == NULL)
        return;
    menu->rendered_size = 0;
    if (menu == current_menu)
        refresh_layout();
}

// A function to show a library icon on the tile in the preview, rendered from the library's file at the
// button's size
static void preview_library_icon(const char *name)
{
    char key[SETTING_TEXT_MAX + 8];
    snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "library:%s", name);
    if (strcmp(key, icon_previewed) == 0)
        return;
    const char *file = library_lookup(name);
    SDL_Surface *surface = file != NULL ? load_icon_surface(file, layout.button > 0 ? layout.button : PLATE_SIZE) : NULL;
    if (surface == NULL) {
        log_error("Settings: the preview cannot show the library icon %s: %s", name,
            file != NULL ? SDL_GetError() : "the library has no such icon");
        return;
    }
    char what[96];
    snprintf(what, sizeof(what), "the library icon %s", name);
    show_on_tile(surface, what);
    SDL_DestroySurface(surface);
    snprintf(icon_previewed, sizeof(icon_previewed), "%s", key);
}

// A function to show in the preview the icon of the Icon page's row under the cursor: the library icon
// it offers, or the app's own icon; on Library and Browse, the tile's own icon, until the grid's or the
// folder's cursor rests on one
static void preview_icon_row(void)
{
    SettingsRow rows[SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS];
    int count = settings_rows(model, rows, SETTINGS_MAX_ROWS);
    int cursor = settings_cursor(model);
    SettingsAction action = cursor >= 0 && cursor < count ? rows[cursor].action : SETTINGS_ACTION_NONE;
    if (action == SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_SUGGESTED)
        preview_library_icon(settings_icon_choices(model)->suggested);
    else if (action == SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_OWN && strcmp(icon_previewed, "own") != 0) {
        show_on_tile(icon_plated, "its own icon");
        snprintf(icon_previewed, sizeof(icon_previewed), "own");
    }
    else if (action != SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_OWN)
        restore_tile_icon();
}

// A function to find a library icon by its name; NULL when the library has none of that name
static const LibraryInfo *library_named(const char *name)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < library_count(); i++) {
        if (strcmp(library_info(i)->name, name) == 0)
            return library_info(i);
    }
    return NULL;
}

// A function to read a tile's app's own icon and put it on the library's plate (spec "Icons", choice 2),
// in memory: it is written to a file only when it is chosen. What names it comes from the tile's command:
// on Windows the app ID an AppsFolder command launches (applist_appsfolder_id()); on Linux the Icon= of
// the .desktop file it runs, whatever its NoDisplay or Hidden say (Task 10b's desktop_icon_name()). Task
// 10b's plated_icon() then finds, reads and plates it, as it does for a new tile. NULL for a tile that is
// no such app, `why` left "", and for an icon that cannot be found, read or plated, with why. icon_from
// says where it came from.
static SDL_Surface *own_icon(const MenuTile *tile, char *why, size_t size)
{
    char named[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!applist_appsfolder_id(tile->command, named, sizeof(named)))
        return NULL;
#else
    if (!desktop_icon_name(tile->command, named, sizeof(named), why, size))
        return NULL;
#endif
    return plated_icon(named, why, size);
}

// A function to leave the Icon page: the preview's tile shows its own icon again, and its own icon on the
// plate, never chosen, goes. Nothing happens with no Icon page open.
static void close_icon_page(void)
{
    if (icon_menu < 0)
        return;
    restore_tile_icon();
    if (icon_plated != NULL)
        SDL_DestroySurface(icon_plated);
    icon_plated = NULL;
    icon_menu = -1;
    icon_tile = -1;
}

// A function to find what the Icon page offers for its tile as it opens (spec "Icons"): the library icon
// its title matches (iconmatch_find()), its app's own icon on a plate, and with neither the library's
// generic icon. The model's rows follow, the cursor on the first. The preview's highlight goes to the
// tile, so it is in view while its icons are tried on it. `menu` is the settings' index, as
// settings_icon_tile() gives it.
static void open_icon_page(int menu, int tile)
{
    close_icon_page();
    icon_menu = menu;
    icon_tile = tile;
    const MenuTile *at = icon_page_tile();
    if (at == NULL) {
        icon_menu = -1;
        icon_tile = -1;
        return;
    }
    const char *menu_name = menus[menu]->name;
    char why[2 * SETTING_TEXT_MAX] = "";
    icon_plated = own_icon(at, why, sizeof(why));
    int found = iconmatch_find(at->title, library_info(0), library_count());
    const LibraryInfo *offered = found >= 0 ? library_info(found)
                               : icon_plated == NULL ? library_named(LIBRARY_FALLBACK_ICON) : NULL;
    SettingsIconChoices choices;
    memset(&choices, 0, sizeof(choices));
    choices.own = icon_plated != NULL;
    choices.matched = found >= 0;
    if (offered != NULL) {
        snprintf(choices.suggested, sizeof(choices.suggested), "%s", offered->name);
        snprintf(choices.suggested_title, sizeof(choices.suggested_title), "%s", offered->title);
    }
    if (found >= 0)
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s': the library match is %s", at->title, menu_name, offered->name);
    else
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s': no library match", at->title, menu_name);
    if (icon_plated != NULL)
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s': its own icon is %s", at->title, menu_name, icon_from);
    else if (why[0] != '\0')
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s': its own icon cannot be used: %s", at->title, menu_name, why);
    if (found < 0 && icon_plated == NULL && offered != NULL)
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s': no match and no icon of its own, so the generic %s is offered", at->title,
            menu_name, offered->name);
    settings_set_icon_choices(model, &choices);
    Menu *live = icon_page_menu();
    if (live != NULL && live == current_menu && tile < (int) live->num_entries && live->position.selected != tile) {
        live->position.selected = tile;
        refresh_layout();   // apply_layout() scrolls the tile into view
    }
}

// A function to give the Icon page's tile an icon (a library name or an image's path) and go back to its
// page, through the model (13a's settings_set_icon(), fix pass R12): its MENUS event goes to handle_event(),
// whose Task 10a case puts the change into the launcher (settings_menus_changed()), so the preview shows it
// from its file; nothing here calls settings_menus_changed() again. One its line in config.ini could not
// hold is refused: the page stays, and the caption says why (settings_icon_done()). `source` names where it
// came from, for the log.
static bool set_tile_icon(const char *icon, const char *source)
{
    const MenuTile *tile = icon_page_tile();
    if (tile == NULL)
        return false;
    // Copies: `icon` may be the model's, and the tile's strings go when the model changes
    char chosen[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    char title[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    char menu_name[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    snprintf(chosen, sizeof(chosen), "%s", icon);
    snprintf(title, sizeof(title), "%s", tile->title);
    snprintf(menu_name, sizeof(menu_name), "%s", menus[icon_menu]->name);
    SettingsEvent event = settings_set_icon(model, icon_menu, icon_tile, chosen);
    if (event.kind != SETTINGS_EVENT_MENUS) {
        char why[SETTING_TEXT_MAX + 512];   // A copy: settings_icon_done() writes the notice it is given
        snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "%s", settings_notice(model));
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s' cannot take the icon %s: %s", title, menu_name, chosen, why);
        settings_icon_done(model, why);
        return false;
    }
    log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s' now has the icon %s, from %s", title, menu_name, chosen, source);
    icon_previewed[0] = '\0';   // The launcher's menus are made again from the model, this icon with them
    handle_event(&event);
    if (model != NULL)
        settings_icon_done(model, NULL);
    return true;
}

// A function to say why the Icon page's tile cannot take `icon`, or NULL: its line weighed as config.ini has
// it, its comment and spacing counted (Task 3's menuedit_check_set(), Fable review M2), so a row the save
// would refuse is refused before anything is written
static const char *icon_problem(const MenuTile *tile, const char *icon)
{
    return menuedit_check_set(menu_edit, menuedit_find(menu_edit, menus[icon_menu]->name), icon_tile, tile->title, icon,
        tile->command);
}

// A function to tell whether a tile's icon is a plated icon already written to the icons folder `dir`: a
// file there, directly in it, where only an app's own icon is ever written
static bool icon_in_folder(const char *icon, const char *dir)
{
    size_t length = strlen(dir);
    if (strncmp(icon, dir, length) != 0 || (icon[length] != '/' && icon[length] != '\\'))
        return false;
    const char *name = icon + length + 1;
    return name[0] != '\0' && strpbrk(name, "/\\") == NULL && fileio_is_file(icon);
}

// A function to tell whether an image file holds the own icon the Icon page plated as it opened, pixel for
// pixel: its size, and each pixel's color and alpha, a clear pixel by its alpha alone, as Task 9's
// png_roundtrip reads a plated icon back from its PNG (plate_icon() makes ARGB8888). A file that cannot be
// read, or holds another picture (the tile's Command changed since it was written, the app's icon changed,
// or the tile was given another tile's file), does not.
static bool holds_own_icon(const char *path)
{
    if (icon_plated == NULL || icon_plated->format != SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888)
        return false;
    SDL_Surface *loaded = load_image_file(path);
    SDL_Surface *argb = loaded != NULL ? SDL_ConvertSurface(loaded, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888) : NULL;
    SDL_DestroySurface(loaded);
    bool same = argb != NULL && argb->w == icon_plated->w && argb->h == icon_plated->h;
    for (int y = 0; same && y < argb->h; y++) {
        const Uint32 *on_file = (const Uint32 *) ((const Uint8 *) argb->pixels + (size_t) y * (size_t) argb->pitch);
        const Uint32 *on_page = (const Uint32 *) ((const Uint8 *) icon_plated->pixels +
                                                  (size_t) y * (size_t) icon_plated->pitch);
        for (int x = 0; same && x < argb->w; x++)
            same = (on_page[x] >> 24) == 0 ? (on_file[x] >> 24) == 0 : on_file[x] == on_page[x];
    }
    SDL_DestroySurface(argb);
    return same;
}

// A function to write the tile's own icon, plated as the page opened it, as a new PNG in the icons folder
// (named from its title, never over a file that is there), list it for Discard, and make it the tile's
// icon. A tile whose icon is already that icon's file (a file directly in that folder holding the same
// plated picture: written as the tile was added, or chosen here before) keeps it: nothing is written and
// nothing changes (the controller's ruling, 2026-10-16). A file there holding another picture is not this
// icon, so a new file is written (Opus re-review P3). A path the tile's line could not hold is refused
// before anything is written (Fable review M15: a file left behind would wait for Discard), and a file
// that cannot be written leaves the tile's icon as it was; the caption says why.
static void save_own_icon(void)
{
    const MenuTile *tile = icon_page_tile();
    char dir[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    char path[SETTING_TEXT_MAX];
    char why[SETTING_TEXT_MAX + 512];
    const char *refused = NULL;
    if (tile == NULL || icon_plated == NULL)
        return;
    if (!icons_dir(dir, sizeof(dir)))
        snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "Couldn't make the icons folder: %s", fileio_last_error());
    else if (icon_in_folder(tile->icon, dir) && holds_own_icon(tile->icon)) {
        log_debug("Menus: '%s' in '%s' keeps its own icon %s, written already", tile->title, menus[icon_menu]->name,
            tile->icon);
        settings_icon_done(model, NULL);
        return;
    }
    else if (!icons_new_path(dir, tile->title, path, sizeof(path)))
        snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "Couldn't name a new icon file in %s", dir);
    else if ((refused = icon_problem(tile, path)) != NULL)
        snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "Couldn't use %s as its icon: %s", path, refused);
    else if (!plate_save(icon_plated, path))
        snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "Couldn't save its icon to %s: %s", path, SDL_GetError());
    else {
        log_debug("Menus: saved the own icon of '%s' to %s", tile->title, path);
        settings_note_plated(path);
        set_tile_icon(path, "its own icon");
        return;
    }
    log_debug("Menus: %s", why);
    settings_icon_done(model, why);
}

// The library grid's cursor moved: its icon on the tile in the preview
static void icon_grid_shown(const char *name)
{
    preview_library_icon(name);
}

// The library grid closed: the icon chosen becomes the tile's; none (Back) leaves the Icon page as it was
static void icon_grid_done(const char *name)
{
    if (name != NULL)
        set_tile_icon(name, "the library");
}

// A function to tell the folder browser whether the Icon page's tile can take an image's path as its
// icon: the rule its line in config.ini must keep (icon_problem())
static const char *check_icon_path(const char *path, void *context)
{
    UNUSED(context);
    const MenuTile *tile = icon_page_tile();
    return tile != NULL ? icon_problem(tile, path) : NULL;
}

// The Icon page's folder browser chose an image (Task 10b's browser_chose, called once the browser has
// closed, after handle_browser_command() waited for its decode): it becomes the tile's icon
static void icon_browser_chose(const char *path)
{
    set_tile_icon(path, "an image file");
}

// A function to open the folder browser for the Icon page's tile (*Browse for an image ›*), in image mode,
// at its icon when that is an image's path, else at the first place; each image the cursor rests on is
// shown on the tile in the preview. Task 10b's start_browser() opens it with no slot (fix pass R2): it sets
// the mode, logs the folder and previews the highlighted image.
static void open_icon_browser(void)
{
    const MenuTile *tile = icon_page_tile();
    const char *start = tile != NULL && !library_is_name(tile->icon) ? tile->icon : NULL;
    browsing_icon = true;   // Before it opens: the first image it highlights goes on the tile
    if (!start_browser(BROWSER_IMAGE, start, list_folder, check_icon_path, NULL)) {
        browsing_icon = false;
        return;
    }
    browser_slot = NULL;
    browser_chose = icon_browser_chose;
}

// A function to act on the Icon page's row chosen: the library icon it offers and the app's own icon
// become the tile's; Library and Browse open the grid or the folder browser over the page
static void choose_icon(SettingsAction action)
{
    const SettingsIconChoices *choices = settings_icon_choices(model);
    const MenuTile *tile = icon_page_tile();
    if (action == SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_SUGGESTED)
        set_tile_icon(choices->suggested, choices->matched ? "the library match" : "the library's generic icon");
    else if (action == SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_OWN)
        save_own_icon();
    else if (action == SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_GRID)
        pickers_open_icons(tile != NULL ? tile->icon : NULL, icon_grid_shown, icon_grid_done);
    else if (action == SETTINGS_ACTION_ICON_BROWSE)
        open_icon_browser();
}

// A function to keep the Icon page's tile in step with the pages after every key: the page opened (find
// what it offers), its cursor moved (its row's icon on the tile), or the page left (the tile's own icon
// again, its own icon on the plate let go). While the grid or the browser is open over the page, they
// show their own icons on the tile.
static void follow_icon_page(void)
{
    int menu = -1;
    int tile = -1;
    if (model == NULL || !settings_icon_tile(model, &menu, &tile)) {
        close_icon_page();
        return;
    }
    if (menu != icon_menu || tile != icon_tile || !settings_icon_choices(model)->ready)
        open_icon_page(menu, tile);
    if (!pickers_active() && browser == NULL)
        preview_icon_row();
}
```

```c
// A function only the headless harness builds: STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE=<menu>:<tile> opens the pages at
// that tile's page as settings open (tile -1: the menu's Tiles page), as the hold-OK shortcut opens them,

static void test_open_tile(void)
{
    const char *given = getenv("STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE");
    if (given == NULL)
        return;
    char name[256];
    snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%s", given);

                menu = m;
        }

    if (menu < 0) {
        log_debug("Test hook: no menu for STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE=%s", given);
        return;
    }
    settings_show_tile(model, menu, atoi(colon + 1));
    follow_preview();
    log_path();
    log_debug("Test hook: settings opened at tile %s of menu '%s'", colon + 1, name);
}
```

```bash
# The Icon page (3c Task 13, spec "Icons"): the choices in the spec's order with the first that applies
# preselected; an app's own icon found through its .desktop file's Icon= in a hicolor theme, plated, and
# written as a PNG under ~/.config/streamflex/icons only when it is chosen; the library match; the generic
# icon for an app with neither; the library grid filtered on the keyboard; an image chosen in the folder
# browser; a read-only icons folder; an icon that cannot be plated; Discard deleting the plated file
# nothing uses; and its own icon chosen again once the app's icon changed, written as a new file rather
# than the old one kept. STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE opens settings at a tile's page, where Down and OK open
# Icon.
# Not timing-sensitive: every key waits for its frame, the filter's letters are typed into the keyboard
# that opened a frame before, and every result is read from the log, config.ini and the PNG file

I85_SHARE=/work/tests/headless/fixtures/icons85/share
I85_DATA=$I85_SHARE:/usr/local/share:/usr/share
I85_ICONS=$TESTER_HOME/.config/streamflex/icons
I85_PNG=$I85_ICONS/sf85-tool.png
I85_SVG=$I85_SHARE/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/sf85-tool.svg
I85_DESKTOP=$I85_SHARE/applications
I85_BACK="BackSpace BackSpace BackSpace BackSpace BackSpace"   # The tile's page up to the top, then saved and closed

# A function to start each run with no icons folder, so a file it writes is its own
i85_clean() { chmod -R u+w "$TESTER_HOME/.config/streamflex" 2> /dev/null; rm -rf "$TESTER_HOME/.config/streamflex"; }

# A function to read a PNG's width, height, color type and its first pixel's alpha: "512 512 6 0". The
# first pixel of the first row reads as stored whatever the row's filter: each filter adds only what lies
# left of it or above it, which is nothing there.
i85_png() {
    python3 - "$1" <<'EOF'
import struct, sys, zlib
data = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
width, height, depth, kind = struct.unpack('>IIBB', data[16:26])
at, idat = 8, b''
while at < len(data):
    length, name = struct.unpack('>I4s', data[at:at + 8])
    if name == b'IDAT':
        idat += data[at + 8:at + 8 + length]
    at += 12 + length
raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
print(width, height, kind, raw[4] if kind == 6 and depth == 8 else 'none')
EOF
}

# SF85 Tool, an app with no library match: its own icon comes first and is highlighted, shown on the tile
# as it is; chosen, it is written as a 512 px PNG with clear corners, and saved as the tile's icon. Its
# .desktop file says NoDisplay=true, which keeps it out of the app list but not its icon from its tile.
# Chosen again from the Icon page opened once more (the tile's page keeps its cursor on Icon), the tile
# already shows that file, so it keeps it and nothing more is written (the controller's ruling, 2026-10-16).
i85_clean
cfg=$(writable_config f85-icons)
XDG_DATA_DIRS=$I85_DATA STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE=Main:0 CFG=$cfg run_keys f85-own Menu Down Return Return Return Return \
    $I85_BACK
log=$out/f85-own.log
ok=1
grep -qx "Menus: 'SF85 Tool' in 'Main': no library match" "$log" \
    && grep -qx "Menus: 'SF85 Tool' in 'Main': its own icon is $I85_SVG" "$log" \
    && grep -q "^Settings: the cursor's row reads Its own icon" "$log" \
    && grep -qx "Menus: the preview shows its own icon on 'SF85 Tool'" "$log" \
    && precedes "$log" "Menus: the preview shows its own icon on 'SF85 Tool'" "Menus: saved the own icon of 'SF85 Tool' to $I85_PNG" \
    && grep -qx "Menus: 'SF85 Tool' in 'Main' now has the icon $I85_PNG, from its own icon" "$log" \
    && [ "$(grep -c '^Menus: saved the own icon of ' "$log")" = 1 ] \
    && precedes "$log" "Menus: saved the own icon of 'SF85 Tool' to $I85_PNG" "Menus: 'SF85 Tool' in 'Main' keeps its own icon $I85_PNG, written already" \
    && [ "$(ls -A "$I85_ICONS")" = sf85-tool.png ] \
    && grep -qx "Entry1=SF85 Tool;$I85_PNG;$I85_DESKTOP/sf85-tool.desktop" "$cfg" \
    && [ "$(i85_png "$I85_PNG" 2> /dev/null)" = "512 512 6 0" ] && ran_clean f85-own && ok=0
result "icons: an app's own icon is offered first, shown on its tile, written as a 512 px PNG when chosen, and kept, not written again, when chosen again (exit $(cat "$out/f85-own.code"))" $ok
echo "      $(i85_png "$I85_PNG" 2>&1)"
grep -E "^Menus:|the cursor's row reads" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# Kodi, which the library matches: the match comes before its own icon and is highlighted; chosen, no

i85_clean

# icon changes (the SVG written again in blue) and the Icon page is opened once more: its own icon is now
# another picture than the tile's file holds, so choosing it writes a new file, sf85-swap-2.png, which the
# tile takes; the old file is kept only when it holds the same plated picture (Opus re-review P3)
I85_SWAP_SVG=/tmp/sf85-swap.svg
i85_swap_svg() {
    printf '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="128" height="128" viewBox="0 0 128 128"><rect x="8" y="8" width="112" height="112" rx="24" fill="%s"/></svg>\n' "$1" > "$I85_SWAP_SVG"
}
i85_swap_blue() { i85_swap_svg '#2850C8'; }
i85_clean
i85_swap_svg '#C83228'
cfg=$(writable_config f85-icons)
XDG_DATA_DIRS=$I85_DATA STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE=Main:4 CFG=$cfg run_keys f85-changed Menu Down Return Return \
    +i85_swap_blue Return Return $I85_BACK
log=$out/f85-changed.log
ok=1
grep -qx "Menus: 'SF85 Swap' in 'Main': its own icon is $I85_SWAP_SVG" "$log" \
    && precedes "$log" "Menus: saved the own icon of 'SF85 Swap' to $I85_ICONS/sf85-swap.png" \
        "Menus: saved the own icon of 'SF85 Swap' to $I85_ICONS/sf85-swap-2.png" \
    && grep -qx "Menus: 'SF85 Swap' in 'Main' now has the icon $I85_ICONS/sf85-swap-2.png, from its own icon" "$log" \
    && ! grep -q "^Menus: 'SF85 Swap' in 'Main' keeps its own icon " "$log" \
    && [ -f "$I85_ICONS/sf85-swap.png" ] && [ "$(ls -A "$I85_ICONS" | wc -l)" = 2 ] \
    && grep -qx "Entry5=SF85 Swap;$I85_ICONS/sf85-swap-2.png;$I85_DESKTOP/sf85-swap.desktop" "$cfg" \
    && ran_clean f85-changed && ok=0
result "icons: its own icon chosen again once the app's icon changed is written as a new file, not the old one kept (exit $(cat "$out/f85-changed.code"))" $ok
grep -E "^Menus:" "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'
rm -f "$I85_SWAP_SVG"
i85_clean
```

`icons-own-written-again` writes the own icon a second time when it is chosen again (the controller's ruling, 2026-10-16): the tile's icon becomes `sf85-tool-2.png`, and the line that it keeps its file is never logged. Its `&& false` keeps `icon_in_folder()` and `holds_own_icon()` called, so the build has no unused function.

`icons-own-kept-when-changed` keeps any file in the icons folder, whatever picture it holds (Opus re-review P3): the second choice, made after `+write` gave the app's icon another color, logs that the tile keeps `sf85-swap.png` (or the `-N` the folder's leftovers gave the first), so the second `saved` line is missing and the absent line is there. `(… || true)` keeps `holds_own_icon()` called. The pair's first `+write` puts the red SVG in place before Menu opens anything, so every run starts from the same picture; the SVG in `/tmp` is outside the tree, which no later entry reads. The first choice may be `-N` when earlier entries left files (the pattern allows it); the second is always a `-N`, since the first is in the folder.

`icon-set-not-applied` drops the hand-over of `settings_set_icon()`'s event (fix pass R12): the model takes the icon and the page goes back, but the launcher's menus are never made again from it, so the preview and the menu would keep the old icon until the next change. Pinned only by check 85, with no `mutants.py` entry, since its runs need what the driver cannot give (a read-only folder made before the run, Pictures from `make_images.py`, text typed into the keyboard): the read-only folder's caption (`f85-readonly`), the browser's image on the tile and OK's decode wait and broken-image check in Task 10b's no-slot branch (`f85-browse`, `poll_decode()`'s `browsing_icon` branch: a mutant dropping `browser_chose = icon_browser_chose;` would leave the tile's icon as it was, which `f85-browse`'s `now has the icon …green.png` line catches), the grid's filter in place under the keyboard (`f85-grid`: dropping `pickers_keyboard_follow(icons_filter_changed, 0);` loses its `shows … for 'kod'` line), and Discard's deletion (`f85-discard`, Task 10a's code over `settings_note_plated()`). Write them into the ledger as pinned by check 85. Named survivors, unexercised by design: `load_icon_textures()`'s, `open_grid()`'s and `icons_filter_changed()`'s out-of-memory returns (SDL-side allocations outside `test_alloc`'s seam), `draw_icons()`'s scrolling past a column's height (the harness's 1920 x 1080 column fits the fixture library's groups; qa-harness rows below look at it), `restore_tile_icon()` for a menu not on show (the Icon page's menu is always the one on show), `set_tile_icon()`'s refusal (no fixture tile's line is too long for an icon; 13a's `test_icon_page()` pins `settings_set_icon()`'s refusal and `settings_icon_done()`'s caption), `icon_in_folder()`'s refusal of a file in a folder under the icons folder or of a file that is gone (no fixture tile names one), `holds_own_icon()`'s refusal of a file that cannot be read or holds a picture of another size, and of a plated icon not in ARGB8888 (`f85-changed`'s two pictures differ in their pixels alone, and `plate_icon()` makes ARGB8888 only), the `SETTINGS_EVENT_ICON` case's return under an open grid or browser (its absence only makes the preview follow the page once more under them, which no line tells apart), the grid's filter opened by a printing key (`pickers_set_typing(open_icon_filter)`: `f85-grid` opens it with Up; the app list's `f82-app` pins the same Task 12 route), and the Windows half of `own_icon()` (proven by Task 8's `appsfolder` CTest and the qa-harness rows).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: 13a's `settings_show_tile()`; Task 4's `nothing_to_select()`; Task 12's `SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN` statement (`settings_text_key()` first); `execute_command()`'s `:settings` branch (every way into settings but the hold's); `settings_open()`, `settings_page()`, `follow_preview()`, `log_path()`, `show_menu()`, `ControlHold`, `derive_repeat_due()`, `gamepad_controls_version()`, `window_id`, and the pad test hooks (`STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD`, `_BUTTON`, `_FRAMES`).
- Produces, the skeleton's, in `src/derive.h` and `src/settings_screen.h`:
  ```c
  #define HOLD_OK_MS 800
  bool derive_hold_fired(unsigned int now, unsigned int pressed_at);   // unsigned int, as the skeleton has it: derive.h is SDL-free
  void settings_open_at_tile(const char *menu, int tile);              // tile -1: the menu's Tiles page
  ```
- Produces, additions (fix pass, the hold-OK rulings): `ControlHold` gains `bool ok;` (`launcher.h`: a press taken as OK in the menus, which never repeats until let go); the test hooks `STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD_UNPLUG=<frames>` and `STREAMFLEX_TEST_UNFOCUS=<frames>` (both counted from `STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD`'s button's first press). The launcher's own OK functions are static; the one that selects is `select_highlighted()`, beside Task 10a's public `select_entry(int)` (fix pass R8).

**Decisions this task makes:**
- **Which presses are OK.** In the launcher's menus (settings closed), OK is the built-in Return, any hotkey whose command is `:select` (read by its first word, as `execute_command()` reads it), and any gamepad control whose command is `:select` (the pad's A by default). The mouse's click stays at once (mouse use is out of the spec's scope). Inside settings each of them acts on its press, as before.
- **The press is timed from its event.** A key's press and release are each timed by their events' own timestamps (`SDL_NS_TO_MS(event.key.timestamp)`, SDL's ticks), so a frame drawn late cannot turn a hold into a tap: a release whose time is `HOLD_OK_MS` or more after its press opens settings as the hold would have. While the key is held, each frame checks `derive_hold_fired(ticks_ms(), pressed_at)` and fires the hold on the frame it is due. The pad has no events, so its press and release are timed by the frame that polled them, as its repeat is. `derive_hold_fired()` reads a press stamped after `now` (an event read against a clock read before it) as a hold of no time, not of 49 days: a difference past half the ticks' range is.
- **Only the first press counts; nothing repeats.** A second OK pressed while one is held (Return held, then a `:select` hotkey, or the pad's A) does nothing, and so do its repeats, until it is let go: in the menus, and in the settings the first one's hold opened (a key's through `ok_ignored_key`, a pad control's through its `ControlHold.ok`). OK's own repeats (the keyboard's, and the pad's) never act either: not in the menus, and not in the settings its hold opened, until it is let go. A Return pressed again with no release between (its release lost to another window) starts a new press.
- **A hold the launcher loses track of is canceled** (no select, no settings), so the next OK is a press of its own: the window losing the keyboard (`SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_FOCUS_LOST`; and a release of OK's key that SDL sends just before it, as SDL lets every held key go when the window loses the keyboard, which `ok_key_up()` tells by the focus event queued behind it), and a pad pulled out while its control holds OK (`SDL_EVENT_JOYSTICK_REMOVED`; with no pad left the pad is not polled at all, so its release would never come and the hold would fire on its own).
- **Settings opened another way during a press cancel it** (user ruling 2026-10-16, Fable review M16). Every other way in (the Menu key, a `:settings` hotkey, pad control or tile) goes through `execute_command()`'s `:settings` branch, which cancels a held press, key or pad, as it opens them (`ok_settings_opened()`): the hold never fires, not even on the frame settings close with OK still down, and the release does nothing. A held key's repeats are then ignored until it is let go (`ok_ignored_key`), and a held pad control's by its `ControlHold.ok`, so none reaches the settings it did not open. (A keyboard repeats only the last key pressed, on X and on Windows alike, so the Menu key that opens them ends Return's repeat; a key's repeats reach those settings only when a pad control or another device opens them, which `f86-padopened` pins.)
- **A pad's hold or release after its controls were made again does nothing** (Fable review C1). The hold notes `gamepad_controls_version()` at its press; when it differs, the press it began is not the one going on: `ok_tick()` never fires it, and its release neither selects nor opens settings. Master makes the controls again only in settings (`apply_bindings()`: Discard, a binding's change, a submenu's rename) and as StreamFlex quits (`cleanup()`), and settings opened another way cancel the press first, so these two checks are the second line behind that cancel: a hold left over by any way in that does not pass `execute_command()` still cannot fire on the frame settings close. `poll_gamepad()`'s release path also stops its loop when the release's command made the controls again, as its press path does.
- **What the hold opens.** The tile highlighted when the hold fires; in an empty menu, its Tiles page (tile -1). `settings_open_at_tile()` opens settings over that menu and walks the pages to the tile's page with 13a's `settings_show_tile()`: Menus, the menu, *Tiles ›*, the tile, each from its row, so Back goes to the Tiles page, then the menu's page, Menus and the top, and Back there saves and closes as always.
- **Closing lands on the tile.** The menu keeps its `LayoutPosition` through settings: the preview shows that menu with its highlight, `show_menu()` keeps a menu's place, and `close_settings()` shows `origin`, the menu the hold opened them over. The Icon page moves the highlight only to the same tile (13b). A tile removed meanwhile leaves the highlight where `layout_clamp()` puts it.
- **The checks are two files.** The holds run against the 800 ms and the X server's key repeat, which a loaded box could stretch or shorten, so they are `86-hold-ok-timing.sh`, marked `# Timing-sensitive` and pinned in `timing_pinned` as `run.sh` requires; the taps and the press inside settings are `86-hold-ok.sh`, in the rest set.
- **Check 48's launch case changes.** It held A, which launched at its press, through the launch's gap in polling. A now launches only as it is let go, so it cannot be held through its own launch: Y (bound to `:up`, which a one-row menu does nothing with) is held instead, and Return launches.

```c
// A function to say when a hold first reaches HOLD_OK_MS, frame by frame at `fps` (ms after its press),
// or -1 when a hold of `hold_ms` never does; each pressed at its own time across the ticks' wrap
static int hold_fires_at(int fps, int hold_ms)
{
    unsigned int pressed = next_start;
    next_start += 7;
    for (int frame = 1;; frame++) {
        int held = frame * 1000 / fps;
        if (held > hold_ms)
            return -1;
        if (derive_hold_fired(pressed + (unsigned int) held, pressed))
            return held;
    }
}

// A function to test the hold that opens settings at OK's tile (plan ruling 1): due at HOLD_OK_MS to the
// millisecond, across the ticks' wrap, within a frame of it at 30, 60 and 144 fps, and never for a hold a
// millisecond shorter; a press stamped a little after `now` (an event's time, read against a clock read
// before it) is a hold of no time, not one of 49 days
static void test_hold_ok(void)
{
    CHECK(!derive_hold_fired(1000 + HOLD_OK_MS - 1, 1000));
    CHECK(derive_hold_fired(1000 + HOLD_OK_MS, 1000));
    CHECK(derive_hold_fired(1000 + 60000, 1000));
    CHECK(!derive_hold_fired(0xFFFFFF00u + HOLD_OK_MS - 1, 0xFFFFFF00u));
    CHECK(derive_hold_fired(0xFFFFFF00u + HOLD_OK_MS, 0xFFFFFF00u));
    CHECK(!derive_hold_fired(1000, 1003));
    CHECK(!derive_hold_fired(5, 14));
    static const int rates[] = { 30, 60, 144 };
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        int fired = hold_fires_at(rates[i], 1000);
        CHECK(fired >= HOLD_OK_MS && fired <= HOLD_OK_MS + frame_ms(rates[i]));
        CHECK_INT(hold_fires_at(rates[i], HOLD_OK_MS - 1), -1);
    }
}
```

```c
// A function to decide whether OK, pressed at `pressed_at`, has been held long enough by `now` to open
// settings at its tile (plan ruling 1): HOLD_OK_MS or more. The times are SDL's ticks, so the subtraction
// is unsigned and holds across their wrap. A press stamped after `now` (an event's time, read against a
// clock read just before it) is a hold of no time, not one of 49 days: any difference past half the
// ticks' range is.
bool derive_hold_fired(unsigned int now, unsigned int pressed_at)
{
    unsigned int held = now - pressed_at;
    return held >= HOLD_OK_MS && held < 0x80000000u;
}
```

```c
// OK in the launcher's menus (plan ruling 1): the press of the key or the pad control that runs :select,
// until it is let go. Let go before HOLD_OK_MS it selects; held that long it opens settings at its tile,
// and its release then does nothing. Only the first press counts, and it never repeats.
typedef struct {
    bool held;             // A press is held
    bool fired;            // It was held HOLD_OK_MS and opened settings
    Uint32 pressed_at;     // When it was pressed, in SDL's ticks: a key's event's time, a pad's poll
    SDL_Keycode key;       // The key (its stored code); 0 for a pad control
    const char *pad;       // The pad control (its label, from the labels' table); NULL for a key
    unsigned int version;  // gamepad_controls_version() at the press: a pad's release after another does nothing
} OkHold;
static OkHold ok_hold = { false, false, 0, 0, NULL, 0 };
static SDL_Keycode ok_ignored_key = 0;   // A second OK key pressed while one was held: its repeats do nothing
                                         // until it is let go, in the menus or the settings the hold opened

// A function to tell whether a command is :select, read by its first word as execute_command() reads it
static bool runs_select(const char *command)
{
    size_t length = strlen(SCMD_SELECT);
    return strncmp(command, SCMD_SELECT, length) == 0 && (command[length] == '\0' || command[length] == ' ');
}

// A function to tell whether OK's press is held by this key (`pad` NULL) or by this pad control
static bool ok_holds(SDL_Keycode key, const char *pad)
{
    if (!ok_hold.held)
        return false;
    if (pad != NULL || ok_hold.pad != NULL)
        return pad != NULL && ok_hold.pad != NULL && strcmp(pad, ok_hold.pad) == 0;
    return key == ok_hold.key;
}

// A function to select the tile on show, as OK does once it is let go: its command runs, or nothing in
// an empty menu, which says so (Task 10a's select_entry(int) only moves the highlight, for the preview)
static void select_highlighted(void)
{
    if (nothing_to_select())
        return;
    log_debug("Selected Entry:\n"
        "Title: %s\n"
        "Icon Path: %s\n"
        "Command: %s",
        current_entry->title,
        current_entry->icon_path,
        current_entry->cmd
    );
    execute_command(current_entry->cmd);
}

// A function to start OK's press: nothing runs yet. A press while one is held is not counted, nor are its
// repeats until it is let go (a key's here; a pad control's by its ControlHold.ok, poll_gamepad()).
static void ok_press(SDL_Keycode key, const char *pad, Uint32 at)
{
    if (ok_hold.held) {
        if (key != 0)
            ok_ignored_key = key;
        log_debug("Hold OK: a second OK while the first is held does nothing");
        return;
    }
    ok_hold = (OkHold) { true, false, at, key, pad, gamepad_controls_version() };
}

// A function to forget OK's press without selecting or opening anything, as the launcher loses track of it
// (the window lost the keyboard, or a pad was pulled out, while it was held), so the next OK is a press of
// its own. Nothing happens with no press held.
static void ok_cancel(const char *why)
{
    if (!ok_hold.held)
        return;
    ok_hold.held = false;
    log_debug("Hold OK: %s, so the hold is canceled", why);
}

// A function to cancel OK's press as settings open another way during it (the Menu key, or a :settings
// hotkey, pad control or tile; user ruling 2026-10-16): the hold never fires, not even as those settings
// close with OK still down, and its release does nothing. A held key's repeats are ignored until it is let
// go, as a second OK's are, so none reaches the settings it did not open; a pad control's ControlHold.ok
// already keeps its own from repeating.
static void ok_settings_opened(void)
{
    if (!ok_hold.held)
        return;
    if (ok_hold.pad == NULL)
        ok_ignored_key = ok_hold.key;
    ok_cancel("settings opened another way");
}

// A function to open settings at the tile OK was held on (spec "The hold-OK shortcut"), or at an empty
// menu's Tiles page: the tile highlighted when the hold came due
static void ok_fire(Uint32 held)
{
    ok_hold.fired = true;
    int tile = current_menu->num_entries > 0 ? current_menu->position.selected : -1;
    log_debug("Hold OK: held %u ms, so settings open at tile %i of menu '%s'", (unsigned int) held, tile, current_menu->name);
    settings_open_at_tile(current_menu->name, tile);
}

// A function to run each frame while no app is in front: OK held HOLD_OK_MS opens settings at its tile on
// the frame it comes due. Settings opened another way cancel the press as they open (ok_settings_opened());
// a pad's press whose controls were made again since never fires (Fable review C1: the press it began is
// not the one going on).
static void ok_tick(void)
{
    Uint32 now = ticks_ms();
    if (ok_hold.held && !ok_hold.fired && !settings_is_open() && derive_hold_fired(now, ok_hold.pressed_at) &&
        (ok_hold.pad == NULL || gamepad_controls_version() == ok_hold.version))
        ok_fire(now - ok_hold.pressed_at);
}

// A function to end OK's press as its key or control is let go (`at`: the release's time): held under
// HOLD_OK_MS it selects; held longer (a frame drawn late saw it only now), it opens settings as the hold
// would have; after the hold opened them, nothing. Only the key or control that pressed it ends it; a pad's
// release after its controls were made again does nothing (the press it began is not the one ending); and
// with settings open, opened by a way that did not cancel the press, nothing is selected under them.
static void ok_release(SDL_Keycode key, const char *pad, Uint32 at)
{
    if (!ok_holds(key, pad))
        return;
    OkHold was = ok_hold;
    ok_hold.held = false;
    if (was.fired) {
        log_debug("Hold OK: let go after the hold opened settings, so it does nothing");
        return;
    }
    if (was.pad != NULL && gamepad_controls_version() != was.version) {
        log_debug("Hold OK: the pad's controls were made again during the hold, so its release does nothing");
        return;
    }
    if (settings_is_open())
        return;
    Uint32 held = at - was.pressed_at;
    if (derive_hold_fired(at, was.pressed_at)) {
        ok_fire(held);
        return;
    }
    log_debug("Hold OK: let go after %u ms, so it selects", held < 0x80000000u ? (unsigned int) held : 0u);
    select_highlighted();
}

// A function to end OK's press as a key is let go. SDL lets every held key go just before it says the
// window lost the keyboard (its focus event comes right behind, in the same batch): such a release is no
// one's choice, so the hold is canceled, as that focus event would cancel it, and nothing is selected.
static void ok_key_up(SDL_Keycode key, Uint32 at)
{
    if (key == ok_ignored_key)
        ok_ignored_key = 0;
    SDL_Event next;
    if (ok_holds(key, NULL) &&
        SDL_PeepEvents(&next, 1, SDL_PEEKEVENT, SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_FOCUS_LOST, SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_FOCUS_LOST) == 1 &&
        next.window.windowID == window_id) {
        ok_cancel("the window lost the keyboard");
        return;
    }
    ok_release(key, NULL, at);
}
```

```c
// A function only the headless harness builds: the window loses the keyboard as SDL reports a real focus
// change (Xvfb has no window manager to move it, and an X focus change may never reach SDL there): each key
// held is let go first, as SDL's own keyboard reset sends it, then the focus event, both queued before
// the next events are read. test_pad_update() gives it back the frame after.
static void test_unfocus(void)
{
    int count = 0;
    const bool *keys = SDL_GetKeyboardState(&count);
    log_debug("Test hook: the window loses the keyboard");
    for (int code = 0; code < count; code++) {
        if (!keys[code])
            continue;
        SDL_Event release;
        SDL_zero(release);
        release.type = SDL_EVENT_KEY_UP;
        release.key.windowID = window_id;
        release.key.scancode = (SDL_Scancode) code;
        release.key.key = SDL_GetKeyFromScancode((SDL_Scancode) code, SDL_KMOD_NONE, false);
        if (!SDL_PushEvent(&release))
            log_error("Test hook: a key's release was not pushed\n%s", SDL_GetError());
    }
    SDL_Event focus;
    SDL_zero(focus);
    focus.type = SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_FOCUS_LOST;
    focus.window.windowID = window_id;
    if (!SDL_PushEvent(&focus))
        log_error("Test hook: the focus event was not pushed\n%s", SDL_GetError());
    test_unfocused = true;
}
```

```c
        test_pad_after = atoi(unplug != NULL ? unplug : unfocus);
    if (test_pad_after == 0) {
        test_pad_after = -2;
        if (unfocus != NULL)
            test_unfocus();
        if (unplug != NULL && test_pad != NULL) {
            SDL_CloseJoystick(test_pad);
            SDL_DetachVirtualJoystick(test_pad_id);
            test_pad = NULL;
            test_pad_id = 0;
            test_pad_gone = true;
            log_debug("Test hook: the pad is pulled out, its button held");
            return;
        }
    }
    else if (test_pad_after > 0)
        test_pad_after--;
```

(`test_pad_stop()` already copes with no pad attached. `SDL_DetachVirtualJoystick()` sends `SDL_EVENT_JOYSTICK_REMOVED`, as `test_pad_plug()`'s pulling out does.)

```c
// For the hold-OK shortcut: settings open over the menu named, at its tile's page (tile -1: its Tiles

```

In `src/settings_screen.c`, after 13b's `test_open_tile()` and its `#endif`, before `settings_open()`, add:

```c
// A function to open settings at a tile's page, for OK held on it in the launcher's menus (spec "The
// hold-OK shortcut"): over the menu named, through Menus, the menu and its Tiles page to the tile's page
// (settings_show_tile()), so Back goes to the Tiles page and then up through settings as usual; tile -1
// (an empty menu) opens the menu's Tiles page. The menu keeps its highlight through settings (the preview
// shows it, and show_menu() keeps a menu's place), so closing settings lands on the tile.
void settings_open_at_tile(const char *menu, int tile)
{
    char name[256];   // A copy: settings_open() may make the launcher's menus again, the name with them
    snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%s", menu);
    for (Menu *over = config.first_menu; over != NULL; over = over->next) {
        if (strcmp(over->name, name) == 0 && over != current_menu)
            show_menu(over);
    }
    settings_open();
    if (model == NULL)
        return;   // settings_open() said why
    int index = -1;
    for (int m = 0; m < menu_count && index < 0; m++) {
        if (strcmp(menus[m]->name, name) == 0)
            index = m;
    }
    if (index < 0) {
        log_debug("Hold OK: the menu '%s' is not in config.ini any more, so settings open at their top", name);
        return;
    }
    settings_show_tile(model, index, tile);
    follow_preview();
    log_path();
    // The page that opened, not the one asked for (Fable review I4): a menu with no menus model stops short
    SettingsPage page = settings_page(model);
    log_debug("Hold OK: settings opened at %s of menu '%s'", page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILE ? "a tile's page"
              : page == SETTINGS_PAGE_TILES ? "the Tiles page" : page == SETTINGS_PAGE_MENU ? "the menu's page"
              : "the Menus page", name);
}
```

Create `tests/headless/checks/86-hold-ok.sh`:

```bash
# OK in the launcher's menus (3c Task 14, plan ruling 1): it acts as it is let go, not as it is pressed.
# A tap of Return, and of a hotkey bound to :select, selects on its release; in an empty menu it selects
# nothing; inside settings OK still acts on its press. The holds are 86-hold-ok-timing.sh's.
# Not timing-sensitive: a tap's press and release come in one xdotool call, 800 ms short of a hold, and
# the press inside settings is read in the log before its release is sent

P86_ARROW=$(printf ' \xE2\x80\xBA ')

# Return tapped on Bye: its release selects it, and StreamFlex quits
CFG=$FX/f86-hold.ini run_keys f86-tap Right Return
log=$out/f86-tap.log
ok=1
precedes "$log" 'Key Return (#D) detected' 'Hold OK: let go after' \
    && grep -qE '^Hold OK: let go after [0-9]+ ms, so it selects$' "$log" \
    && grep -qx 'Title: Bye' "$log" && grep -q '^Quitting program' "$log" && ! grep -q 'Settings opened' "$log" \
    && ran_clean f86-tap && ok=0
result "hold-ok: Return tapped selects as it is let go (exit $(cat "$out/f86-tap.code"))" $ok
grep -E '^(Key Return|Hold OK|Title:)' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'

# A hotkey bound to :select (F6) is OK too
CFG=$FX/f86-hold.ini run_keys f86-hotkey Right F6
log=$out/f86-hotkey.log
ok=1
precedes "$log" 'Key F6 (#4000003F) detected' 'Hold OK: let go after' \
    && grep -qx 'Title: Bye' "$log" && ran_clean f86-hotkey && ok=0
result "hold-ok: a hotkey bound to :select selects as it is let go (exit $(cat "$out/f86-hotkey.code"))" $ok

# An empty menu: OK let go there selects nothing, and says so
CFG=$FX/f86-hold.ini run_keys f86-empty Return Return BackSpace
log=$out/f86-empty.log
ok=1
in_range "$log" "Loading menu 'Kids'" "Loading menu 'Main'" "Menu 'Kids' is empty: there is no tile to select" \
    && ! grep -q 'Settings opened' "$log" && ran_clean f86-empty && ok=0
result "hold-ok: OK let go in an empty menu selects nothing (exit $(cat "$out/f86-empty.code"))" $ok

# Inside settings OK acts as it is pressed: the General page opens while Return is still held
p86_press_in_settings() {
    xdotool keydown Return
    wait_line "Settings: page Settings${P86_ARROW}General" "$2" && echo 'pressed yes' >> "$out/$1.seen"
    xdotool keyup Return; sleep 1
}
rm -f "$out/f86-inside.seen"
CFG=$FX/f86-hold.ini run_keys f86-inside Menu +p86_press_in_settings BackSpace BackSpace
ok=1
grep -qx 'pressed yes' "$out/f86-inside.seen" 2> /dev/null && ! grep -q '^Hold OK:' "$out/f86-inside.log" \
    && ran_clean f86-inside && ok=0
result "hold-ok: inside settings OK acts as it is pressed (exit $(cat "$out/f86-inside.code"))" $ok
```

```bash
# The hold-OK shortcut (3c Task 14, spec "The hold-OK shortcut"): Return and the pad's A held past 0.8 s
# open settings at the tile's page, the key's repeats doing nothing in the menu or in settings; Back walks
# up to the top and closing lands on the tile; an empty menu's hold opens its Tiles page; a press let go
# before 0.8 s selects; a second OK during a press is not counted, nor are its repeats in the settings the
# first one's hold opened; a hold canceled by a pad pulled out or by the window losing the keyboard (the
# pad's A, and Return, whose release SDL sends just before it says so) opens nothing, and the next OK
# selects; settings opened by Menu during a hold (the pad's A, or Return) cancel it, so closing them
# with OK still down opens nothing, and its release does nothing; and settings opened by the pad's Y
# (:settings) during Return's hold cancel it, and Return's repeats, going on inside them, press nothing
# Timing-sensitive: 1 s and 0.5 s key and button holds against the 800 ms hold and the X server's key
# repeat, and keys that must come inside the hold's 800 ms

T86_ARROW=$(printf ' \xE2\x80\xBA ')
T86_TILES="Settings${T86_ARROW}Menus${T86_ARROW}Main${T86_ARROW}Tiles"
t86_hold_return() { xdotool keydown Return; sleep 1; xdotool keyup Return; sleep 0.5; }
t86_short_return() { xdotool keydown Return; sleep 0.5; xdotool keyup Return; sleep 1; }

# Return held 1 s on Bye: settings open at Bye's page, its repeats (it came more than once) do nothing,

    && grep -qF "Settings: page $T86_TILES$T86_ARROW" "$log" \

    && sed -n '/^Settings closed/,$p' "$log" | grep -qx 'Title: Bye' && ran_clean f86-hold && ok=0
result "hold-ok: Return held on a tile opens its page, Back walks up, and closing lands on it (exit $(cat "$out/f86-hold.code"))" $ok
grep -E '^(Hold OK|Settings: page|Settings (opened|closed)|Title:)' "$log" | sed 's/^/      /'
echo "      Return came $(grep -c 'Key Return (#D) detected' "$log") times"

# Return held 0.5 s, under the hold: its release selects
CFG=$FX/f86-hold.ini run_keys f86-short Right +t86_short_return
log=$out/f86-short.log

grep -qE '^Hold OK: let go after [0-9]+ ms, so it selects$' "$log" && grep -qx 'Title: Bye' "$log" \

result "hold-ok: OK held in an empty menu opens its Tiles page (exit $(cat "$out/f86-holdempty.code"))" $ok

t86_second() { xdotool keydown Return; sleep 0.1; xdotool key F6; xdotool keyup Return; sleep 1; }
```

In `tests/headless/checks/48-pad-repeat.sh`, replace `:48-68` (the launch case, from its comment through its last `grep ... | sed`) with:

```bash
# A control held through a gap in polling does not repeat the moment polling resumes: Y is held, then
# Return launches `sleep 1` as it is let go (A, which selects as it is let go since 3c, cannot be held
# through its own launch); the launcher does not poll the pad until the launch's 3 s timeout, and Y is
# held on through it. Its hold is timed again from the resume, which the test hook logs, and Y is let go
# 0.1 s after that line (wait_line sees it up to 0.2 s late, so 0.1-0.3 s after the resume), short of the
# next repeat, 500 ms after the resume. Timed from the press, as it was, it would have repeated at once.
# Y's repeats before the launch are its own: only those after the resume count.
p48_launch() {
    : > /tmp/pad-y
    wait_line 'Gamepad ButtonY detected' "$2" && xdotool key Return
    wait_line 'Test hook: pad ButtonY held through a gap in polling' "$2" && sleep 0.1
    rm -f /tmp/pad-y; sleep 1
}
rm -f /tmp/pad-y
STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD=/tmp/pad-y STREAMFLEX_TEST_PAD_BUTTON=y WAIT_FOR='Gamepad connected' CFG=$FX/f48-gap.ini \
    run_keys f48-launchhold +p48_launch
rm -f /tmp/pad-y
ok=1
[ "$(p48_count f48-launchhold 'Gamepad ButtonY detected')" = 1 ] \
    && grep -q 'Test hook: pad ButtonY held through a gap in polling, timed from now' "$out/f48-launchhold.log" \
    && [ "$(sed -n '/Test hook: pad ButtonY held through a gap in polling/,$p' "$out/f48-launchhold.log" | grep -c 'Test hook: pad ButtonY repeated')" = 0 ] \
    && ran_clean f48-launchhold && ok=0
result "pad: Y held through a launch's timeout is timed again from the resume, and does not repeat at once (pressed $(p48_count f48-launchhold 'Gamepad ButtonY detected') times, repeated after the resume $(sed -n '/Test hook: pad ButtonY held through a gap in polling/,$p' "$out/f48-launchhold.log" | grep -c 'Test hook: pad ButtonY repeated') times; exit $(cat "$out/f48-launchhold.code"))" $ok
grep -E 'Test hook: pad ButtonY|Gamepad ButtonY|Hold OK' "$out/f48-launchhold.log" | sed 's/^/      /'
```

`hold-only-at-release` leaves the hold to the release, which still opens settings as the hold would have (the release comes a second after the press), but never says it was let go after the hold opened them: the line that tells a hold that fired while held from one found at its release. `pad-repeats-into-settings` drops `ControlHold.ok`'s swallow, so A's own repeats reach the settings its hold opened. The three new pairs are the hold-OK rulings: a pad pulled out mid-hold (`unplug-keeps-hold`: the hold fires on its own 0.8 s after the press, and settings open), the window losing the keyboard mid-hold (`unfocus-keeps-hold`, the same), and settings opened another way mid-hold (user ruling 2026-10-16, `other-open-keeps-hold`: Menu opens settings inside the hold's 0.8 s and the press is not canceled, so the cancel's line is missing and, once Discard has made the controls again, A let go at its three-hundredth frame logs that its controls were made again; it replaces the first pass's `pad-rebuilt-release-acts`, whose release check the cancel now goes before). Pinned only by `86-hold-ok-timing.sh`, with no `mutants.py` entry, since the driver cannot hold a key: the repeat swallow inside settings for OK's own key (`ok_holds(key, NULL)` with `repeat`; `f86-hold`, counting the `Settings: page` lines between the hold and the first Back), a second OK key's repeats (dropping `    if (repeat && key != 0 && key == ok_ignored_key)\n        return;\n` lets F6's repeats press OK on the tile's page, which opens the keyboard on its Title: `f86-secondheld`), and SDL's release of a held Return just before the window loses the keyboard (dropping `ok_key_up()`'s `SDL_PeepEvents()` branch makes that release select Bye before the focus event: `f86-unfocuskey`). A held key's repeats inside settings opened another way (dropping `ok_settings_opened()`'s `ok_ignored_key = ok_hold.key;` lets Return's repeats open General: `f86-padopened`, whose pad button opens settings with no key pressed after Return, so Return keeps repeating; from the keyboard alone the Menu key ends Return's repeat, so `f86-keyopened` pins the cancel only) is pinned the same way. Write them into the ledger as pinned by check 86. Named survivors, unexercised by design, each a second line behind `ok_settings_opened()`, which every way into settings but the hold's passes first: `ok_tick()`'s controls-version condition and `ok_release()`'s (master makes the controls again only in settings and at quit, Fable review C1), and `ok_release()`'s `settings_is_open()` return.

**Smoke-row claims** (for Task 17):
- `[All]` In a menu, OK (Return, or the pad's A) selects the highlighted tile as it is let go, not as it is pressed; a quick press feels the same as before.
- `[All]` Holding OK on a tile for about a second opens settings at that tile's page; letting go then does nothing.
- `[All]` From that page, Back goes to the menu's Tiles page, then up through settings; closing settings lands on the tile that was held.
- `[All]` Holding OK in an empty menu opens its Tiles page.
- `[All]` Holding OK on a tile the Tiles page has no row for (a menu of more than 62 tiles, whose page counts the rest in its note) opens that tile's page; Back goes to the Tiles page.
- `[All]` OK held down never launches a tile twice, nor acts on the page the hold opened; a second OK held with it does nothing there either.
- `[All]` Switching away from StreamFlex (or pulling out the gamepad) while OK is held neither launches the tile nor opens settings, and the next OK works as ever.
- `[All]` Opening settings with Menu while OK is held (before its second is up) drops the hold: closing them with OK still down opens nothing, and letting OK go selects nothing.
- `[All]` Opening settings with a gamepad button bound to `:settings` while Return is held (before its second is up) drops the hold too, and Return's repeats, which go on while no other key is pressed, press nothing in them.
- `[Win]` The same holds with an Xbox controller's A.

- **The save's own lines** (3a/3b, kept): `Settings saved <N> change(s) to <path> (backup: <path>)`, and one `Settings: not saved as asked: <note>` for each note Task 2's and Task 3's skipped edits give; a tile's "changed meanwhile" note without 3b's words on keys and buttons, which are the bindings' (10a, Fable review M6).

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/settings_screen.c` (Task 4's statics after `menu_edit`; Task 4's `load_menus()`; `free_screen()`; `save_changes()` `:888`; Task 4's `settings_menus_changed()`; the two log functions after Task 4's `menus_in_step()`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 3's `menuedit_copy()`, `menuedit_free()`, `menuedit_changed()`, `menuedit_count()`, `menuedit_menu()`; Task 4's `menu_edit`, `load_menus()`, `settings_menus_changed()` and its `STREAMFLEX_TEST_MENU_EDIT` hook; Task 7's `STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN` and its `Apps: none listed: <why> (<ms> ms)` line; 13b's `STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE`; Task 10b's Add page (*App ›* first, *Browse for a program ›* second) and its app list, whose first opening in a visit starts Task 7's scan (`settings_apps_start()`) and which, with no apps, gives `settings_apps()`'s reason in its column and as its note (the caption), Back returning to the Add page.
- Produces: no function another task calls. The log lines, each exactly:
  - every menu edit, tile by tile, in `settings_menus_changed()`: `Menus: '<menu>': tile <t> added: <title>;<icon>;<command>`, `Menus: '<menu>': tile <t> removed: <title>`, `Menus: '<menu>': tile <t> is now <title>;<icon>;<command>, was <title>;<icon>;<command>`;
  - each save step for the menus, before the save: `Menus: saving: [<menu>] is removed`, `Menus: saving: [<old>] is renamed [<new>]`, `Menus: saving: [<menu>] is added, with <N> tile(s)`, `Menus: saving: [<menu>]'s tiles are written again, <N> of them`.

**Decisions this task makes:**
- **Edits are logged by what changed, not where they were made.** Tasks 10, 11, 13 and 14 each put a change into the model and then call `settings_menus_changed()`; it compares the model with the state the log last described (a copy, `menuedit_copy()`) and logs each place in a menu whose tile was added, removed or is now another, then keeps a new copy. So every edit is logged once, from whichever page (or Discard, or the test hook) made it, and no page has to remember to. A menu is matched across the two states by the section it was read from, or by its name when it was made in settings; a menu's coming, going or renaming is the rebuild's own line. A move shows as the places whose tiles changed.
- **The save's steps are logged as the save is asked to take them**, before `save_changes()` writes: against a copy of the model as settings opened, each menu removed, renamed or added, and each whose tiles are written again.
```c
// A function to find the menu a menus model's menu is in another state of the model: the one read from
// the same section, or for a menu made in settings (read from none) the one of its name; -1 for none
static int same_menu(const MenuEdit *in, const MenuEditMenu *menu)
{
    for (int m = 0; in != NULL && m < menuedit_count(in); m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *other = menuedit_menu(in, m);
        bool same = menu->original_name != NULL
                    ? other->original_name != NULL && strcmp(other->original_name, menu->original_name) == 0
                    : other->original_name == NULL && strcmp(other->name, menu->name) == 0;
        if (same)
            return m;
    }
    return -1;
}

// A function to tell whether two tiles say the same: their title, icon and command
static bool same_tile(const MenuTile *a, const MenuTile *b)
{
    return strcmp(a->title, b->title) == 0 && strcmp(a->icon, b->icon) == 0 && strcmp(a->command, b->command) == 0;
}

// A function to log every change to the menus model since the log last described it (spec, Errors and
// limits: every menu edit), place by place: each tile added, removed or now another. A menu that came,
// went or was renamed the rebuild logs itself (menus_apply()). The model as it is now is then the one the
// next change is logged against.
static void log_menu_edits(void)
{
    for (int m = 0; menus_logged != NULL && m < menuedit_count(menu_edit); m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *now = menuedit_menu(menu_edit, m);
        int at = same_menu(menus_logged, now);
        const MenuEditMenu *was = at >= 0 ? menuedit_menu(menus_logged, at) : NULL;
        int was_count = was != NULL ? was->count : 0;
        for (int t = 0; t < now->count || t < was_count; t++) {
            const MenuTile *a = t < was_count ? &was->tiles[t] : NULL;
            const MenuTile *b = t < now->count ? &now->tiles[t] : NULL;
            if (a == NULL)
                log_debug("Menus: '%s': tile %i added: %s;%s;%s", now->name, t, b->title, b->icon, b->command);
            else if (b == NULL)
                log_debug("Menus: '%s': tile %i removed: %s", now->name, t, a->title);
            else if (!same_tile(a, b))
                log_debug("Menus: '%s': tile %i is now %s;%s;%s, was %s;%s;%s", now->name, t, b->title, b->icon,
                    b->command, a->title, a->icon, a->command);
        }
    }
    menuedit_free(menus_logged);
    menus_logged = menuedit_copy(menu_edit);
    if (menus_logged == NULL)
        log_error("Menus: out of memory, so the next menu edit goes unlogged");
}

// A function to log the steps the save is asked to take for the menus (spec, Errors and limits: each save
// step), against the model as settings opened: each menu removed, renamed or added, and each whose tiles
// are written again. What the save could not do as asked it logs itself, a line a note.
static void log_menu_save(void)
{
    if (menu_edit == NULL || menus_opened == NULL || !menuedit_changed(menu_edit))
        return;
    for (int m = 0; m < menuedit_count(menus_opened); m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *was = menuedit_menu(menus_opened, m);
        if (same_menu(menu_edit, was) < 0)
            log_debug("Menus: saving: [%s] is removed", was->name);
    }
    for (int m = 0; m < menuedit_count(menu_edit); m++) {
        const MenuEditMenu *now = menuedit_menu(menu_edit, m);
        int at = same_menu(menus_opened, now);
        const MenuEditMenu *was = at >= 0 ? menuedit_menu(menus_opened, at) : NULL;
        if (was == NULL) {
            log_debug("Menus: saving: [%s] is added, with %i tile(s)", now->name, now->count);
            continue;
        }
        if (strcmp(was->name, now->name) != 0)
            log_debug("Menus: saving: [%s] is renamed [%s]", was->name, now->name);
        bool changed = was->count != now->count;
        for (int t = 0; !changed && t < now->count; t++)
            changed = !same_tile(&was->tiles[t], &now->tiles[t]);
        if (changed)
            log_debug("Menus: saving: [%s]'s tiles are written again, %i of them", now->name, now->count);
    }
}
```

```bash
    && grep -qx "Menus: saving: [Main]'s tiles are written again, 1 of them" "$log" \

# A submenu removed with its tiles: its opener is logged removed, and the save removes the section

STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=fail STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE=Main:-1 CFG=$FX/f87-menus.ini \
    run_keys f87-scanfail Menu Return Return +i87_scanned BackSpace Down Return Menu
log=$out/f87-scanfail.log

grep -qE "^Apps: none listed: $i87_why \([0-9]+ ms\)$" "$log" \

result "menus log: an app scan that fails says why where the app list would be, and Browse for a program still works (exit $(cat "$out/f87-scanfail.code"))" $ok

i87_why='No apps were found'
STREAMFLEX_TEST_APP_SCAN=empty STREAMFLEX_TEST_OPEN_TILE=Main:-1 CFG=$FX/f87-menus.ini \

log=$out/f87-scanempty.log

    && grep -qxF "Settings: the note under the preview says $i87_why" "$log" \

result "menus log: an app scan that finds nothing says why where the app list would be, and Browse for a program still works (exit $(cat "$out/f87-scanempty.code"))" $ok
```

### Task 16: The mutants, gathered and run

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/mutants/menu-editing.json` (every mutant Tasks 1-15 list, unit and headless, with this task's resolutions)
- Modify: `tests/mutants/mutants.py` (unit entries through `tests/unit.sh`; `--controls`, `--kind`, `--find-only`)
- Modify: `tests/unit.sh` (`MUTANT_FIND`, `MUTANT_REPLACE`, `MUTANT_COUNT`; a mutant's own warnings no longer stop its tests)
- Modify: `CONTRIBUTING.md` (`:9`, the sentence on `tests/unit.sh`'s header)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: each task's mutant list, from the ledger's `## Task N mutants` sections (Tasks 1-15; Task 6's Python checks and Task 8's COM code have none, by their tasks' notes); `tests/unit.sh` as Task 12 leaves it (its `check-no-text-input.sh` line after the mutant block); `tests/mutants/mutants.py` as PR #62 left it (the SDL3 plan's Task 1.3 driver, plus #62's key steps: `step()` with `+write`, `+wait`, `+stop`, `+cont` and `+sleep`, multi-key words, and `SIGCONT` before the end); the fixtures `f50-empty`, `f80-*`, `f81-apps`, `f82-tiles`, `f83-move`, `f84-keys`, `f85-icons`, `f86-hold`, `f87-menus`.
- Produces:
  ```
  python3 /src/tests/mutants/mutants.py [--controls] [--kind unit|headless] [--find-only] <list>.json
  # a unit entry:     {"name", "unit": "<ctest -R regex>", ["targets": "<cmake targets>"], "file", "find", "replace", ["count"], "expect", "verdict"}
  # a headless entry: as before (fixture, keys, env, wait, seconds, file, find, replace, count, expect, absent, exit, verdict)
  # tests/unit.sh:    MUTANT_FILE with MUTANT_FIND, MUTANT_REPLACE and MUTANT_COUNT (exact text), beside MUTANT_FILE with MUTANT_SED
  ```

**What this task decides:**
- **`mutants.py` runs the unit entries, through `tests/unit.sh`.** One list, one command, one place for the verdict rules, and the unit entries keep the sanitized build CI's unit job runs (several entries expect `heap-use-after-free` or `heap-buffer-overflow`, which only that build reports). Not `MUTANT_SED`: the drafted finds are exact text, many spanning lines (`\n`), full of `\`, quotes, `[`, `*` and `$`, which a sed program would need escaped entry by entry, by hand, where one slip makes a pattern match a second place in silence. So `unit.sh` gains the exact-text form `mutants.py` already applies to headless entries: the text must be there `MUTANT_COUNT` times (once by default), or the run stops `MUTANT NOT APPLIED`.
- **Unit entries run first.** `unit.sh` makes `/work` afresh, and `/work` is also the tree `mutants.py` builds the launcher in, so every unit entry runs before that tree is made. `--kind unit` and `--kind headless` run one kind each, in two containers (each with its own `/work`), so the two halves run at once.
- **How a unit entry is judged.** `holds`: `unit.sh` exits 0 and every expectation is in its output. `caught`: it exits non-zero and every expectation is in its output; the expectations name the failure a test must report (`CHECK failed: ...`, `... is X, expected Y`, a sanitizer's report, or the source check's `SDL TEXT INPUT FOUND`), so a run that failed some other way is `WRONG`, never a kill. A run that stopped before its tests (`MUTANT NOT APPLIED`, `CONFIGURE FAILED`, `BUILD FAILED`) is `NOT-RUN`. Each verdict prints ctest's count of failed tests beside it, or `ctest never ran`.
- **A mutant's own warnings do not stop it.** `unit.sh` stops at a warning outside `src/external` (exit 1) before ctest. Several mutants leave something unused (`if (0)` in place of a call leaves a static function or a variable behind: `-Wunused-function`, `-Wunused-but-set-variable`), so they would never reach their tests. In a mutant's build the warnings are printed and ctest runs; a run with no mutant stops as before, so CI's job and every control keep the rule.
- **Every mutant is judged against its unmutated control (`--controls`).** For each `caught` or `fires` entry the driver also runs the same setup with nothing mutated (for a unit entry its filter and targets; for a headless one its fixture, keys, env, wait and seconds), once per setup, kept for every entry that shares it; an unmutated `holds` entry with that setup is that run. A `caught` headless entry's control must hold that entry's own expectations; a `fires` entry's control must not; a unit entry's control must exit 0 with none of the entry's expectations in its output. Otherwise the entry is `CONTROL-FAILED`, which is wrong whatever the mutant did: a caught verdict means only "the expectations held unmutated and failed mutated", and without the control the first half is an assumption (a driver broken on its own path, or an expectation no run ever meets, scores as a kill). The list's explicit `holds` entries stay, as the readable record of each setup; every caught headless entry here has one with its exact setup, so `--controls` adds no headless run.
- **Without `--controls` the driver behaves as it did**, so the SDL3 plan's `task-1.3.json` and `task-1.4.json` and PR #62's `sdl3-minors.json` run as they were written (the first two's `gamepad-sdl2-form` judges a fault branch's lines that no unmutated run prints, which a control could never hold; `sdl3-minors.json`'s keys are #62's `+` steps and multi-key words, which `launch()` keeps).
- **`--find-only`** counts each entry's find in `/src` and runs nothing: the cheap first pass before an hours-long run.
- **Resolutions, where the drafted entries collide or cannot run as drafted:**
  1. **One control per unit filter.** `settings-control` replaces Task 4's `settings-remodel-control`, Task 10a's `tiles-control`, Task 11's `move-control` and Task 13a's `icon-page-control` (four names for one unmutated `^settings$` run); `applist-control` (Task 7's) also stands for Task 8's `appsfolder-command-control` and Task 13a's `appsfolder-id-control`; `browser-control` replaces Task 10b's `programs-control` and Task 12's `browser-type-control` and `no-text-input-control`, carrying both expectations (`^No SDL text input in src/$` and the pass line).
  2. **Task 9's control ran three tests** (`^(plate|png_roundtrip|iconfind)$`) while its mutants run `^plate$` or `^iconfind$`: it becomes `plate-control` (`^plate$`) and `iconfind-control` (`^iconfind$`). `png_roundtrip` has no mutant, so no control.
  3. **`alloc-control` is added:** Task 7's `applist-oom-unmarked` and Task 13a's `icongrid-filter-frees-first` run `^alloc$`, and no entry ran it unmutated.
  4. **Task 7's six headless entries are Task 10b's** (fix pass R1: they move with check 81, since each needs *Add › App ›* to start the scan), and the list holds them in Task 10b's group: `apps-control` and `apps-close-control` with its controls, the four mutants after them. Task 7's own list keeps its unit entries only. They are re-keyed for Known integration work 4: the scan starts at the first *App ›* of a visit, not as settings open, so their keys go on to *Add › App ›* by Task 10b's route (`E82_TILES`, then OK on *Add ›* and *App ›*), and the closing ones then key Menu. Their `wait` (`Settings opened over menu`) is dropped: in `mutants.py` a keyed entry's `wait` is the line its first key waits for, and that line comes only after the first key, so as drafted none of them would ever press a key (`NOT-RUN` every time). Their finds are in Task 7's code (`appscan.c`, and `settings_screen.c`'s `free_screen()`).
  5. **Task 13b's `icons-saved-not-set`** finds `settings_note_plated(path);`, Known integration work 5's one name, not `plated_add(path);`.
  6. **Task 13b's expectations name `/root/.config/streamflex/icons/`**, not `/home/tester/...`: `mutants.py` runs the launcher as the container's user, root (the image sets no `USER`), where check 85 runs it as `tester`.
  7. **No two entries share a name.** Task 14's `derive-hold-future-press` and `derive-hold-a-ms-late` share a find with different replacements; each runs alone from a fresh copy, so they do not collide.
  8. **Order:** unit entries by filter, each filter's control first; headless entries by task, each task's controls before its mutants (Task 10a drafted `control-tiles-save` and `control-preview-tile` after the entries they cover).
