- [ ] **Step 1: `tests/unit.sh` takes an exact-text mutant**

Replace the whole of `tests/unit.sh` (as Task 12 leaves it) with:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# The unit tests as CI's "Unit tests (ASan, UBSan)" job runs them: that job (unit_sanitizers in
# .github/workflows/build.yml) runs this file in the Debian image, and it runs in either harness
# image (streamflex-test or streamflex-test-fedora): a copy of /src built with ASan, UBSan and the
# extra warnings, as the user tester, then ctest. The repository is mounted read-only and never
# written; everything happens in the copy at /work.
#   bash /src/tests/unit.sh [CTEST-REGEX]   CTEST-REGEX: ctest's -R filter; none runs every test
# UNIT_TARGETS, when set, builds only those targets (space-separated), as before the launcher builds.
# MUTANT_FILE and MUTANT_SED, when set, apply one sed program to that file in the copy only: a unit
# mutant. MUTANT_FIND and MUTANT_REPLACE, set in MUTANT_SED's place, replace that exact text, which
# must be in the file MUTANT_COUNT times (once when unset), as tests/mutants/mutants.py does. A mutant
# that changes nothing, or a configure or build that fails, stops the run before ctest (exit 2), so
# none counts as a kill. A warning outside src/external stops the run too (exit 1), but in a mutant's
# build it is printed and ctest runs: a mutant that leaves a variable unused is still judged by its
# tests. It runs tests/check-no-text-input.sh on the copy first, which stops the run (exit 1) when
# src/ starts SDL's text input.
set -u
rm -rf /work; mkdir -p /work
tar -C /src --exclude=./build --exclude=./.git --exclude=./headless-out --exclude=./.superpowers -cf - . | tar -C /work -xf -
if [ -n "${MUTANT_FILE:-}" ]; then
    if [ -n "${MUTANT_FIND:-}" ]; then
        python3 - "/work/$MUTANT_FILE" <<'EOF' || exit 2
import os
import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
want = int(os.environ.get("MUTANT_COUNT") or "1")
found = text.count(os.environ["MUTANT_FIND"])
if found != want:
    print(f"MUTANT NOT APPLIED to {os.environ['MUTANT_FILE']}: the text is there {found} times, not {want}")
    sys.exit(2)
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(text.replace(os.environ["MUTANT_FIND"], os.environ.get("MUTANT_REPLACE", "")))
EOF
    else
        sed -i -e "$MUTANT_SED" "/work/$MUTANT_FILE"
    fi
    cmp -s "/src/$MUTANT_FILE" "/work/$MUTANT_FILE" && { echo "MUTANT NOT APPLIED to $MUTANT_FILE"; exit 2; }
    echo "MUTANT applied to $MUTANT_FILE:"; diff "/src/$MUTANT_FILE" "/work/$MUTANT_FILE"
fi
# The no-OS-keyboard rule, on the copy (a mutant's change included): CI's unit job runs this file
bash /work/tests/check-no-text-input.sh /work || exit 1
chown -R tester /work
flags="-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
su tester -c "cmake -S /work -B /work/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS='$flags' -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined' -DEXTRA_WARNINGS=ON" > /tmp/configure.log 2>&1 \
    || { echo "CONFIGURE FAILED"; tail -30 /tmp/configure.log; exit 2; }
targets=
[ -z "${UNIT_TARGETS:-}" ] || targets="--target $UNIT_TARGETS"
su tester -c "cmake --build /work/build -j$(nproc) $targets" > /tmp/build.log 2>&1 \
    || { echo "BUILD FAILED"; grep -E 'error' /tmp/build.log | head -30; tail -10 /tmp/build.log; exit 2; }
ours=$(grep -iE 'warning:' /tmp/build.log | grep -vE '^g?make(\[[0-9]+\])?: ' | grep -v '^/work/src/external/')
if [ -n "$ours" ]; then
    echo "WARNINGS OUTSIDE src/external"; echo "$ours"
    [ -n "${MUTANT_FILE:-}" ] || exit 1
    echo "MUTANT: the warnings above are the mutant's build's; its tests run"
fi
filter=
[ -z "${1:-}" ] || filter="-R '$1'"
su tester -c "UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 setarch $(uname -m) -R ctest --test-dir /work/build --output-on-failure $filter"
```

- [ ] **Step 2: `mutants.py` runs unit entries, and judges each mutant against its control**

Replace the whole of `tests/mutants/mutants.py` with:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The mutant driver (plan Task 1.3; unit entries and controls, 3c Task 16). For each entry of a JSON list
it puts one mutation into a copy of the source and judges a run of it. It runs in the streamflex-test
image: /src the repository (read-only; the lists are in /src/tests/mutants), /out the logs and the verdicts.
    python3 /src/tests/mutants/mutants.py [--controls] [--kind unit|headless] [--find-only] /src/tests/mutants/<list>.json
A list with unit entries needs the seccomp profile off (docker run --security-opt seccomp=unconfined), as
tests/unit.sh does.

A headless entry (one with no "unit") builds the launcher with the harness's test hooks (no sanitizers, for
speed), runs it on a fixture under Xvfb with -d, presses the entry's keys a second apart, ends it (TERM,
then KILL 10 s later), and judges its log.

verdict "holds": an unmutated control, whose expectations all hold. "fires": a failure forced, whose
failure branch's expectations all hold. "caught": the old form put back, whose expectations (the
check's) must NOT all hold: the check catches the mutant. A run that never got far enough to be
judged is NOT-RUN, which is wrong whatever its verdict: one with no log at all, one with keys to press
whose wait line never came, and one whose entry sets wait when that line is not in its log. A "caught"
entry's expectations cannot show that the launcher reached the site, as one failing is enough, so a
"caught" entry with no keys must set wait to a line the run prints only if it reached the site: at the
site, or just past it on the path the mutated form takes, or just before it when nothing at or past it
is printed; never a line only the success path the old form skips prints. A mutant that stops the
launcher before then is NOT-RUN, never caught. One that sets no wait is wrong, and not run. A keyed
entry's wait is the line its first key waits for (Begin program loop by default).
Each verdict is followed by every expectation, and whether it held.

A key is an X key name, pressed a second before the next. Words with spaces between them ("Left Right")
are pressed in one xdotool call, as fast as it sends them. A key starting with + is a step instead,
followed by no second's wait: "+write PATH TEXT" puts TEXT and a newline in PATH in one step (a rename),
for a hook's file; "+wait LINE" waits up to 30 s for LINE in the log, and a LINE that never comes ends
the keys and makes the run NOT-RUN, so a +wait names only a line a correct run and its mutant both
print; "+stop" and "+cont" stop the launcher and let it go on, so the keys between reach it in one
pass of its loop; "+sleep S" waits S seconds.

A unit entry ("unit": a ctest -R regex) runs tests/unit.sh with that filter, building only the tests it
names ("targets", or test_<name> for each name in the regex), its find put into unit.sh's copy through
MUTANT_FIND and MUTANT_REPLACE, and judges unit.sh's output. "holds": unit.sh exits 0 and every
expectation is in its output. "caught" (or "fires"): unit.sh exits non-zero and every expectation, the
failure a test must report, is in its output; a run that failed another way is WRONG. A run that stopped
before its tests (MUTANT NOT APPLIED, CONFIGURE FAILED, BUILD FAILED) is NOT-RUN. Each verdict gives
ctest's count of failed tests. Every unit entry runs before the first headless one, since unit.sh makes
/work afresh.

--controls: each "caught" or "fires" entry is also judged against its control, the same run with nothing
mutated (for a unit entry its filter and targets; for a headless one its fixture, keys, env, wait and
seconds), which runs once for each setup and is kept; an unmutated "holds" entry with that setup is that
run. A "caught" headless entry's control must hold the entry's own expectations, a "fires" entry's must
not, and a unit entry's control must exit 0 with none of the entry's expectations in its output;
otherwise the entry is CONTROL-FAILED, which is wrong whatever the mutant did, since its verdict could
then be the driver's or the expectation's, not the check's.
--kind runs only that kind of entry, so the two kinds can run at once in two containers.
--find-only counts each entry's find in /src and runs nothing: a find that is not there "count" times
(1 when unset) is wrong."""
import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

SRC, WORK, OUT = "/src", "/work", "/out"
LOG = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/streamflex/streamflex.log")
STOPPED = ("MUTANT NOT APPLIED", "CONFIGURE FAILED", "BUILD FAILED")   # unit.sh's lines for a run that never tested
SETUP = ("fixture", "keys", "env", "wait", "seconds")                  # What a headless entry's control shares


def tree():
    shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(WORK)
    tar = subprocess.Popen(["tar", "-C", SRC, "--exclude=./build", "--exclude=./.git", "--exclude=./headless-out",
                            "--exclude=./.superpowers", "-cf", "-", "."], stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-C", WORK, "-xf", "-"], stdin=tar.stdout, check=True)
    tar.wait()
    subprocess.run(["cmake", "-S", WORK, "-B", f"{WORK}/build", "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug",
                    "-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-DSTREAMFLEX_TEST_HOOKS"], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def mutate(entry):
    if entry.get("find") is None:
        return True
    path = f"{WORK}/{entry['file']}"
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    found = text.count(entry["find"])
    if found != entry.get("count", 1):
        print(f"MUTANT NOT APPLIED {entry['name']}: the text is in {entry['file']} {found} times")
        return False
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(text.replace(entry["find"], entry["replace"]))
    return True


def log_text():
    return open(LOG, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read() if os.path.exists(LOG) else ""


def step(key, process):
    """Runs a + step of a key list (see above); False when a +wait's line never came"""
    verb, _, rest = key[1:].partition(" ")
    if verb == "write":
        path, _, text = rest.partition(" ")
        with open(f"{path}.new", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as hook:
            hook.write(text + "\n")
        os.replace(f"{path}.new", path)
    elif verb == "wait":
        end = time.time() + 30
        while time.time() < end and process.poll() is None and rest not in log_text():
            time.sleep(0.2)
        return rest in log_text()
    elif verb == "stop":
        process.send_signal(signal.SIGSTOP)
    elif verb == "cont":
        process.send_signal(signal.SIGCONT)
    elif verb == "sleep":
        time.sleep(float(rest))
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown step {key!r}")
    return True


def launch(entry, env):
    """Runs the entry; returns its exit code and whether the line its keys wait for came (True with no keys)"""
    fixture = entry["fixture"]
    source = fixture if fixture.startswith("/") else f"{WORK}/tests/headless/fixtures/{fixture}.ini"
    config = f"/tmp/{entry['name']}.ini"
    shutil.copyfile(source, config)   # A settings save writes here, never into /src
    if os.path.exists(LOG):
        os.remove(LOG)
    keys = entry.get("keys", [])
    with open(f"{OUT}/{entry['name']}.err", "w") as err:
        process = subprocess.Popen([f"{WORK}/build/streamflex", "-c", config, "-d"], env=env,
                                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=err)
        end = time.time() + entry.get("seconds", 20)
        wait = entry.get("wait", "Begin program loop")
        while time.time() < end and process.poll() is None and wait not in log_text():
            time.sleep(0.2)
        pressed = not keys or wait in log_text()
        for key in keys if pressed else []:
            if process.poll() is not None:
                break
            if key.startswith("+"):
                if not step(key, process):
                    pressed = False
                    break
                continue
            if re.fullmatch(r"F\d+", key):
                subprocess.run(["python3", f"{WORK}/tests/headless/key.py", "key", key], env=env)
            else:
                subprocess.run(["xdotool", "key", *key.split()], env=env)
            time.sleep(1)
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.send_signal(signal.SIGCONT)   # A run left stopped would never read its TERM
        time.sleep(2)
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.terminate()
            try:
                process.wait(10)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                process.kill()
                process.wait()
    shutil.copyfile(LOG, f"{OUT}/{entry['name']}.log") if os.path.exists(LOG) else open(f"{OUT}/{entry['name']}.log", "w").close()
    return process.returncode, pressed


def find_only(entries):
    """Counts each entry's find in /src; returns how many are not there exactly as often as they must be"""
    wrong = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if entry.get("find") is None:
            continue
        path = f"{SRC}/{entry['file']}"
        found = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().count(entry["find"]) if os.path.isfile(path) else -1
        ok = found == entry.get("count", 1)
        wrong += 0 if ok else 1
        where = f"{entry['file']} is missing" if found < 0 else f"{entry['file']} holds the text {found} times"
        print(f"{'OK     ' if ok else 'WRONG  '} {entry['name']}: {where}")
    return wrong


def unit_targets(entry):
    return entry.get("targets") or " ".join(f"test_{name}" for name in re.findall(r"\w+", entry["unit"]))


def unit_run(entry, name):
    """Runs tests/unit.sh for the entry, its mutation put in unless it has none; returns its exit code and output"""
    env = dict(os.environ, UNIT_TARGETS=unit_targets(entry))
    if entry.get("find") is not None:
        env.update(MUTANT_FILE=entry["file"], MUTANT_FIND=entry["find"], MUTANT_REPLACE=entry["replace"],
                   MUTANT_COUNT=str(entry.get("count", 1)))
    run = subprocess.run(["bash", f"{SRC}/tests/unit.sh", entry["unit"]], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, errors="replace")
    with open(f"{OUT}/{name}.unit.log", "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
        out.write(run.stdout)
    return run.returncode, run.stdout


def failed_tests(text):
    """ctest's count of failed tests in a unit.sh output, or None when ctest never summed up"""
    found = re.findall(r"tests passed, (\d+) tests? failed out of \d+", text)
    return int(found[-1]) if found else None


def run_units(entries, controls):
    wrong, kept = 0, {}

    def control_of(entry):
        key = (entry["unit"], unit_targets(entry))
        if key not in kept:
            kept[key] = unit_run(dict(entry, find=None), entry["name"] if entry.get("find") is None else f"control.{entry['name']}")
        return kept[key]

    for entry in entries:
        code, text = control_of(entry) if entry.get("find") is None else unit_run(entry, entry["name"])
        expects = [(rx, re.search(rx, text, re.M) is not None) for rx in entry.get("expect", [])]
        held = all(ok for _, ok in expects)
        stopped = next((line for line in STOPPED if line in text), None)
        control = None
        if controls and entry["verdict"] != "holds":
            c_code, c_text = control_of(entry)
            control = (c_code == 0 and not any(line in c_text for line in STOPPED)
                       and not any(re.search(rx, c_text, re.M) for rx, _ in expects))
        if stopped:
            ok, mark = False, "NOT-RUN"
        elif control is False:
            ok, mark = False, "CONTROL-FAILED"
        else:
            ok = (code == 0 and held) if entry["verdict"] == "holds" else (code != 0 and held)
            mark = "OK     " if ok else "WRONG  "
        wrong += 0 if ok else 1
        failed = failed_tests(text)
        tests = f"{failed} test(s) failed" if failed is not None else "ctest never ran"
        print(f"{mark} {entry['name']} ({entry['verdict']}): exit {code}, {tests}" + (f", {stopped}" if stopped else ""))
        for rx, ok in expects:
            print(f"        expect {'held  ' if ok else 'FAILED'} {rx}")
        if control is not None:
            print(f"        control {'held  ' if control else 'FAILED'} {entry['unit']} unmutated: exit 0, and none of the expectations")
    return wrong


def setup_of(entry):
    return json.dumps({key: entry.get(key) for key in SETUP}, sort_keys=True)


def judged(entry, code, pressed, text):
    """A headless run's log against the entry's expectations: (held, reached, expects, absents, exited)"""
    expects = [(rx, re.search(rx, text, re.M) is not None) for rx in entry.get("expect", [])]
    absents = [(rx, re.search(rx, text, re.M) is None) for rx in entry.get("absent", [])]
    exited = "exit" not in entry or code == entry["exit"]
    held = all(ok for _, ok in expects + absents) and exited
    reached = bool(text) and pressed and ("wait" not in entry or entry["wait"] in text)
    return held, reached, expects, absents, exited


def run_headless(entries, controls):
    tree()
    xvfb = subprocess.Popen(["Xvfb", ":99", "-screen", "0", "1920x1080x24", "-ac"],
                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    # lavapipe's ICD, as run.sh finds it (Debian names it lvp_icd.json, Fedora lvp_icd.<arch>.json)
    icd = [path for path in ("/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.json", f"/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.{platform.machine()}.json")
           if os.path.exists(path)]
    if not icd:
        print("NO LAVAPIPE FOUND")
        sys.exit(2)
    env = dict(os.environ, DISPLAY=":99", VK_DRIVER_FILES=icd[0])
    for _ in range(100):
        if subprocess.run(["xdotool", "getdisplaygeometry"], env=env, capture_output=True).returncode == 0:
            break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    wrong, touched, kept = 0, set(), {}

    def run(entry, name):
        """Builds the entry's mutation (none when its find is None) and runs it: (code, pressed, log), or None"""
        for path in touched:   # Every file an earlier entry mutated goes back first
            shutil.copyfile(f"{SRC}/{path}", f"{WORK}/{path}")
        if entry.get("find") is not None:
            touched.add(entry["file"])
        if not mutate(entry):
            return None
        if subprocess.run(["cmake", "--build", f"{WORK}/build", "-j", str(os.cpu_count())],
                          capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
            print(f"BUILD FAILED {name}")
            return None
        code, pressed = launch(dict(entry, name=name), dict(env, **entry.get("env", {})))
        return code, pressed, open(f"{OUT}/{name}.log", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

    def control_of(entry):
        key = setup_of(entry)
        if key not in kept:
            kept[key] = run(dict(entry, find=None), entry["name"] if entry.get("find") is None else f"control.{entry['name']}")
        return kept[key]

    for entry in entries:
        if entry["verdict"] == "caught" and not entry.get("keys") and "wait" not in entry:
            print(f"NO WITNESS {entry['name']} (caught): no keys, and no wait line to show the run reached its site")
            wrong += 1
            continue
        result = control_of(entry) if entry.get("find") is None else run(entry, entry["name"])
        if result is None:
            wrong += 1
            continue
        code, pressed, text = result
        held, reached, expects, absents, exited = judged(entry, code, pressed, text)
        control = None
        if controls and entry["verdict"] != "holds":
            ran = control_of(entry)
            if ran is None:
                control = False
            else:
                c_held, c_reached = judged(entry, *ran)[:2]
                control = c_reached and (c_held if entry["verdict"] == "caught" else not c_held)
        if not reached:
            ok, mark = False, "NOT-RUN"
        elif control is False:
            ok, mark = False, "CONTROL-FAILED"
        else:
            ok = held if entry["verdict"] in ("holds", "fires") else not held
            mark = "OK     " if ok else "WRONG  "
        wrong += 0 if ok else 1
        why = "no log" if not text else f"no line '{entry.get('wait', 'Begin program loop')}'" + ("" if pressed else ", so its keys were never pressed")
        print(f"{mark} {entry['name']} ({entry['verdict']}): exit {code}" + ("" if mark != "NOT-RUN" else f", {why}"))
        for rx, ok in expects:
            print(f"        expect {'held  ' if ok else 'FAILED'} {rx}")
        for rx, ok in absents:
            print(f"        absent {'held  ' if ok else 'FAILED'} {rx}")
        if "exit" in entry:
            print(f"        exit   {'held  ' if exited else 'FAILED'} {entry['exit']}")
        if control is not None:
            what = "held its expectations" if entry["verdict"] == "caught" else "did not hold them"
            print(f"        control {'held  ' if control else 'FAILED'} the same run unmutated {what}")
    xvfb.terminate()
    return wrong


def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)   # Each verdict shows as it comes, through docker's pipe
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Each entry's mutation, run and judged (see the docstring).")
    parser.add_argument("list", help="the JSON list of entries")
    parser.add_argument("--controls", action="store_true", help="judge each caught or fires entry against its unmutated run")
    parser.add_argument("--kind", choices=("unit", "headless"), help="run only that kind of entry")
    parser.add_argument("--find-only", action="store_true", help="count each find in /src, and run nothing")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    entries = json.load(open(args.list, encoding="utf-8"))
    if args.kind:
        entries = [entry for entry in entries if ("unit" in entry) == (args.kind == "unit")]
    if args.find_only:
        wrong = find_only(entries)
    else:
        units = [entry for entry in entries if "unit" in entry]
        shows = [entry for entry in entries if "unit" not in entry]
        wrong = run_units(units, args.controls) if units else 0
        wrong += run_headless(shows, args.controls) if shows else 0
    print(f"{len(entries)} entries, {wrong} wrong")
    sys.exit(1 if wrong else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

[

- [ ] **Step 7: A verdict that is not OK**

Each is a finding about the task the entry came from, never a reason to loosen the entry:
- **`WRONG` on a `caught` unit entry, a test failed:** the test reports the failure in other words than the entry's `expect`. Read the entry's `.unit.log` in `/out`: when the failing test is the one the entry names and its message is the same defect, correct the `expect` to the message as printed, and say so in the ledger. Any other failure is a finding for the owning task.
- **`WRONG` on a `caught` entry, nothing failed:** a branch no test pins. Add the test to the owning task's test file (the test the entry's `expect` names), run that task's unit command, and run this entry again alone (a one-entry list in the scratch folder).
- **`CONTROL-FAILED`:** the unmutated run does not do what the entry's expectations say: either the test or check is red on its own (run the task's unit command or its check), or the expectation names something no run prints. Fix the cause; never drop the control.
- **`NOT-RUN`:** the run never reached its tests or its keys (a find that moved, a build that failed, a wait line that never came); Step 4 catches the first, the `.unit.log` or `.err` file names the others.

After any fix, run the list again from Step 6 (both halves, all entries) and record the new last lines.

- [ ] **Step 8: The named survivors**

Write into the ledger under `## Task 16 survivors`, each with its owning task and why no mutant runs it:
- Task 3: `reordered()`'s `r == read->count` guard (every tile with a line as read was matched in `mark_held()`), `format_value()`'s truncation (every written value passed `tile_problem()`), and `room_key()`'s cut to `size - 1` (a hand-written key longer than a line inih reads).
- Task 4: `menus_apply()`'s fallback when the default menu is gone (the model refuses to remove it) and `add_empty_menus()`'s out-of-memory line; the pointers `menus_apply()` lets go of are the ASan and leak passes' (`f80-remove`); `make_menu()`'s section, pinned by check 80's `f80-caught-up` alone (its `+f80_hand_add` writes config.ini while StreamFlex runs, which `mutants.py` cannot); `load_menus()`'s refusal of a model with no menu, pinned by check 80's `f80-no-menus` alone (its `+f80_hand_empty` does the same), and `settings_menus_changed()`'s like guard, which only a hand-written corner reaches once the load refuses (a lone menu holding a tile that opens itself, removed with its tiles).
- Task 5: `osk_key_char()`'s `(keycode & OSK_SCANCODE_MASK) != 0`, equivalent (every masked keycode is past 0x10FFFF).
- Task 6: `build-library.py`'s alias checks, pinned by its Python tests in the Icon library job.

**Three new sections**, after the *list pickers* paragraph (`:213`) and before `### Key and button bindings`:

```markdown
### The on-screen keyboard
A title, a submenu's name, a command, a path, and the filters of the app list and the icon grid are typed on StreamFlex's own keyboard. It opens across the bottom 40% of the screen, beside the settings column and over the preview, with the field's label and the field itself above its keys; the preview stays in view above it, and follows a tile's title as you type it.

- **Layouts.** *QWERTY*, the default, has a number row, three letter rows and a bottom row of *ABC*, *?123*, *àé*, *Shift*, *Space*, *⌫*, *◀* *▶* (the text cursor) and *Done*. *ABC* is the alphabet in a grid seven keys wide, with the same bottom row. *?123* is a page of digits and symbols, and *àé* a page of accents: à á â ä ã å æ ç è é ê ë ì í î ï ñ ò ó ô ö õ ø œ ù ú û ü ý ÿ ß. The *ABC* key (*QWERTY* on the alphabetical grid) switches the layout, and the keyboard opens in the one you used last, which is saved as [KeyboardLayout](#keyboardlayout).
- **The remote.** Left and Right step between keys, wrapping within a row; Up and Down go to the key in the next row nearest the one you are on. OK types the highlighted key. *Shift* capitalizes the next letter; pressed twice, it turns on caps lock until it is pressed again.
- **A gamepad.** X deletes, Y types a space, and Start is *Done*.
- **Back** closes the keyboard at once when nothing was changed. After a change, the first Back shows *Back again to discard*, and the second throws the change away.
- **Done** stays grayed while the text cannot be written, and the keyboard's note says why: a title with `;` (which would split `title;icon;command`), an empty title, a name taken by another menu, or a line too long for the config file.
- **A real keyboard** types into the field too, from the keys themselves: each printing key types the character your keyboard layout gives it, with Shift, Caps Lock and AltGr. Many remotes send Enter for OK and Backspace for Back, so Enter types the highlighted key and Backspace backs out, as everywhere in settings, until you type a character into the field on the keyboard; from then on, in that field, Enter is *Done* and Backspace deletes. The keypad's Enter is always *Done*, and Esc is always Back. The arrows always move the keyboard's highlight. A held key types again as it repeats.
- **Limits.** A dead key types its own character (`^`, `` ` ``, `~`) and does not combine with the next letter, and an input method is bypassed, so a Japanese or Chinese layout types Latin letters; the *àé* page has the European accents. Layouts that need no input method, such as Greek or Cyrillic, type their own letters.
- **No other keyboard appears.** StreamFlex never turns on the system's text input, which is what brings up Windows' touch keyboard, GNOME's screen keyboard and KDE's virtual keyboard, so none of them covers the screen, whatever their settings.

### Editing menus
Each menu's tiles are edited on its **Tiles page**: *Menus ›*, the menu, *Tiles ›*. A tile is one entry of the menu's section (see [Creating Menus](#creating-menus)), and a submenu is a section of its own, opened by a tile that runs `:submenu <its name>`.

- **The Tiles page** lists *Add ›*, then each tile in the menu's order: a tile that opens a submenu shows that menu's tile count and ›, and any other tile its command. The preview highlights the tile the cursor is on. An empty menu's page holds only *Empty: Add ›*. A menu of more than 62 tiles lists 61 and counts the rest in a note; to edit one of those, hold OK on it in the launcher, which opens its page all the same.
- **Add ›** on the Tiles page puts the new tile at the end; *Add after this tile ›* on a tile's page (below) puts it right after that tile. Either offers:
  - *App ›*: one of your installed apps (see [Installed apps](#installed-apps)).
  - *Browse for a program ›*: the [folder browser](#the-folder-browser), listing folders and programs only: on Windows `.exe` and `.lnk` files; on Linux `.desktop` files and files with their execute bit set (a script without it could not run). The tile is titled by the file's name without its extension. A path with a space is written in quotes, double on Windows and single on Linux, so it runs as one path.
  - *Submenu ›*: a name, typed on the keyboard. It makes the section `[<name>]` at the end of your config file, empty, and a tile that runs `:submenu <name>` with the library's `folder` icon. A new submenu gets no Back tile: Back, and the pad's B, already go back.
  - *Special ›*: *Home*, *Back*, *Settings*, *Sleep*, *Restart*, *Shut down* or *Quit*, each with its library icon.
- **A tile's page:**
  - *Title*: opens the keyboard on it. The preview shows it as you type. A submenu tile's title is its menu's name, so changing it renames the menu (below).
  - *Icon ›*: see [Icons](#icons).
  - *Command ›*: an installed app, a program browsed to, a special command, or *Type…* for a `:fork` line or any other command. `:select` is never offered, as a menu entry cannot use it. A submenu tile's command is grayed: renaming its title changes it.
  - *Move*: OK picks the tile up, and the preview outlines it. The arrows move it through the grid as they move the highlight in a menu, Left and Right along its row, stopping at the row's ends, and Up and Down a row, keeping the column, the preview laying the menu out again at each step; OK drops it there, and Back puts it back where it was.
  - *Move to menu ›*: the other menus; the tile goes to the end of the one you choose. A submenu tile cannot go into its own menu, or into a menu inside it, and those rows say why.
  - *Add after this tile ›*: the Add page, whose new tile goes right after this one.
  - *Remove*: a tile goes at once; *Discard changes* is the undo, as everywhere in settings. A submenu tile asks first: *Remove <name> and its N tiles*, or *Remove only this tile*, which is offered only when another tile also opens that menu. The default menu cannot be removed.
- **Renaming a submenu** renames its section, every tile in every menu whose command is exactly `:submenu <old name>`, `DefaultMenu` when it names it, and every hotkey, gamepad control, startup command and quit command that is exactly `:submenu <old name>`.
- **A menu's name** is 1 to 49 bytes, holds no `]` and no `;` (it is also its tile's title), does not start or end with a space, and is neither a reserved section's (General, Layout, Background, Titles, Highlight, Scroll Indicators, Clock, Screensaver, Hotkeys, Gamepad) nor another menu's. Names that differ only in case count as the same, since they would look the same on screen; a menu may change the case of its own name.
- **A tile** needs a title, an icon and a command; its title holds no `;`, and its whole line must fit one line of the config file (199 bytes), with any comment or spacing that line already has. Until it does, *Done* stays grayed, with the reason.
- **Leaving settings** lands on the menu they were opened over, or on the default menu if that menu was removed; after the [hold-OK shortcut](#the-hold-ok-shortcut), on the tile that was held.

#### Installed apps
*App ›* lists the apps installed, alphabetically. It looks for them the first time you open it after settings open, showing *Finding apps… (N)* meanwhile, and keeps what it found until settings close; Back works while it looks, and closing settings stops it at once. Up from the list's top row, or a printing key on a real keyboard, opens the keyboard to filter the list as you type.

- **On Windows,** the list is the Start menu's: the shell's AppsFolder, desktop and Store apps alike, leaving out uninstallers and help or readme shortcuts. A tile runs its app with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\<app ID>`, or `explorer.exe "shell:AppsFolder\<app ID>"` when the ID holds a space or a comma, so Explorer reads it as one argument.
- **On Linux,** the list is read from the `.desktop` files in each `applications` folder of `$XDG_DATA_DIRS`, in `~/.local/share/applications`, in Flatpak's exports (`/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications` and `~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications`) and in `/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications`. An app is named in your language (`Name[<language>]`, from `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES` or `LANG`), or by its `Name`. Files with `NoDisplay=true` or `Hidden=true`, a `Type` other than `Application` or no `Exec` are left out, as are apps with `Terminal=true` (StreamFlex runs an app with no terminal, so one would show nothing), uninstallers and readmes, and a file in your own folder hides one of the same name in the system's. A tile runs the app's `.desktop` file.
- **When no list comes** (the search failed, or found nothing), *App ›* says why in the note under the preview, and *Browse for a program ›*, *Submenu ›* and *Special ›* still add tiles.

A new app's tile gets, as it is added, the library's icon for it when the library has one; else its own icon, put on the plate and saved in the `icons` folder as [Icons](#icons) says (*Discard changes* deletes it); else the generic *apps* icon. Its *Icon ›* page offers every choice again.

#### Icons
A tile's *Icon ›* lists, in this order, and puts the cursor on the first that applies:
1. **A library match:** the library icon whose name, title or one of whose aliases matches the tile's title, compared in lower case, without punctuation and without vendor words such as *Microsoft*, *Google*, *Apple* or *Valve* (the aliases are the manifest's `match =` lines; see the [Icon Library](icons)). With no match and no icon of its own, this row offers the generic *apps* icon.
2. ***Its own icon***, for an app: on Windows the image the Start menu shows for it, at 256 px; on Linux its `.desktop` file's `Icon=`, as a path, or looked up by name in the hicolor theme (its largest PNG when that is at least 128 px, else its SVG, else its largest PNG), in `/usr/share/pixmaps`, and in Flatpak's exported icons. It is centered on the library's square teal plate (`#07606C`) and saved as a 512 px PNG named after the app (its letters and digits in lower case, each run of anything else one `-`, or `app` when none is left; `-2`, `-3` and on for a name already taken) in an `icons` folder: beside `config.ini` on Windows, and `~/.config/streamflex/icons` on Linux. An icon that cannot be read or put on its plate is not offered. One that cannot be saved (a folder you cannot write, for example) leaves the tile's icon as it was, and the note says why. A tile that already shows its own icon's file keeps it (the same picture) when you choose *Its own icon* again: no second file is written. Once the app's icon or the tile's command has changed, a new file is written.
3. ***Library ›***: every library icon with its title, under its group's heading. Up from the top row, or a printing key on a real keyboard, opens the keyboard to filter the grid by title, name or alias.
4. ***Browse for an image ›***: the [folder browser](#the-folder-browser).

The preview shows each icon on the tile as the cursor reaches it. StreamFlex only ever writes files in the `icons` folder; *Discard changes* deletes the ones written in that visit that no tile uses, and nothing else ever deletes one.

#### The hold-OK shortcut
In the launcher's menus, OK selects a tile as it is let go, not as it is pressed, so a quick press feels as it always has. Held for 0.8 s, it opens settings at that tile's page instead, and letting go then does nothing; in an empty menu, it opens the menu's Tiles page. Back from the tile's page goes to the Tiles page, then up through the settings as usual, and closing settings lands on the tile you held.

OK is Return, any hotkey whose command is `:select`, and any gamepad control whose command is `:select` (the pad's A by default). Only the first press counts: a second OK while one is held does nothing, and a held OK's repeats never act, in the menus or in the settings its hold opened. Opening settings another way while OK is held (Menu, or a `:settings` hotkey or button) cancels the hold: it never fires, and letting go does nothing. A mouse click still selects at once. Inside settings, OK acts as it is pressed.
```

Then, under `## [Unreleased]`, after the SDL2 notice, add:

```markdown
### Added
- **Editing menus from the remote.** Settings › Menus › *<menu>* › Tiles adds, removes, moves and renames a menu's tiles and submenus, and chooses their icons, with no config file to edit. *Add* takes an installed app, a program browsed to, a new submenu or a special command (Home, Back, Settings, Sleep, Restart, Shut down, Quit), at the end of the menu, or, from a tile's page, right after that tile. A tile's page changes its title, icon and command, moves it through the grid as the arrows move the highlight, with the preview following, or to another menu, and removes it. Renaming a submenu renames its section and every tile, hotkey, gamepad control, `DefaultMenu`, startup and quit command that opens it; removing one asks first, and the default menu cannot be removed. The save keeps the settings screen's rules: only what changed is written, comments and order stay, a hand edit made meanwhile is kept, and *Discard changes* puts every tile back.
- **An on-screen keyboard.** StreamFlex's own keyboard types titles, menu names, commands, paths and filters with the remote's arrows and OK, or a gamepad (X deletes, Y types a space, Start is Done). It has a QWERTY layout and an alphabetical one, remembered as `[General] KeyboardLayout` and set on the General page too, with a page of digits and symbols and one of accents. A real keyboard types into it in its own layout, with Shift, Caps Lock and AltGr; Enter and Backspace stay the remote's OK and Back until something is typed on it, then are Done and delete. The command picker gains *Type…*, and the image, folder and mappings-file browsers *Type a path…*, where a typed path is looked for when it is done, and the keyboard opens again on it with the reason when it is not there. No operating system's on-screen keyboard ever appears: StreamFlex never turns on text input, so Windows' touch keyboard, GNOME's screen keyboard and KDE's virtual keyboard stay hidden.
- **The installed apps list.** *Add › App* lists the installed apps: on Windows the Start menu's, desktop and Store apps alike (a tile runs `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\<app ID>`, with the argument in double quotes when the ID holds a space or a comma); on Linux the `.desktop` files of the system, the user, Flatpak and Snap, named in the system's language, without what the desktop's own menu hides, apps that run in a terminal, uninstallers or readmes. It is found on a thread of its own the first time it opens in a visit, with a count as it goes, and is filtered by typing.
- **Icons for tiles.** A tile's *Icon* page offers the library icon matching its title (the library's manifest gains `match =` aliases), the app's own icon on the library's teal plate, saved as a 512 px PNG in an `icons` folder (beside `config.ini` on Windows, `~/.config/streamflex/icons` on Linux), the whole library in a grid by group with a typed filter, or an image file, and the preview shows each on the tile. A new app's tile gets the library's icon when there is one, else its own icon, plated and saved as it is added, else the generic one.
- **The hold-OK shortcut.** Holding OK (Return, or the pad's A) on a tile for 0.8 s opens settings at that tile's page, and closing them lands back on the tile; in an empty menu it opens the menu's Tiles page. Opening settings another way while OK is held cancels the hold.

### Changed
- **OK selects a tile as it is let go** in the launcher's menus, so that holding it can open the tile's page; a quick press feels the same. Return, hotkeys and gamepad controls bound to `:select` all work this way; inside settings OK still acts as it is pressed, and a mouse click still selects at once.
- **A menu with no entries is shown.** A section with no entries (a header alone, or only comments) is a menu: it shows *This menu is empty. Hold OK to add tiles.* in the launcher and in the settings preview, and `DefaultMenu` may name one. Before, such a menu could not be shown, and a `DefaultMenu` naming it stopped StreamFlex at start.
- **Entry lines in no section are ignored.** Lines before the first `[section]`, or under an empty `[]` header, used to make a menu with no name; now they are in no menu, and the log says how many were ignored.
- The headless harness gains checks 80 to 87 for menu editing, and the mutant driver runs unit mutants through `tests/unit.sh` and judges every mutant against its unmutated control.
- The smoke doc gains module 18, *Menu editing*, and retires row 6.17 for 18.6.

### Known limits
- A real keyboard's dead key types its own character and does not combine with the next letter, and an input method is bypassed, so a Japanese or Chinese layout types Latin letters; the keyboard's accents page covers the European accents.
```
